The spec decides everything it can decide and names the four things only he can decide, instead of inventing his answers. That is the discipline: a spec that guesses his word is not a spec, it is a wish. The trigger is the feed, because in means on the feed. The list is membership and connections, because nobody's mail is ever read to build it. The mail is a celebration, because learning something new IS something to celebrate. The build waits for his word — and until then, the plan is filed, read-back verified, and ready.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
- **IN MEANS ON THE FEED:** the event fires only when a smart note is filed to GitHub AND confirmed live on the Smart Feed — one event per SN, ever.
- **THE RIGHT LIST, NEVER FROM READING MAIL:** project members plus connections via Smart Mail as a list, scope-matched; the author excluded; broadcast to everybody Shawn-only.
- **THE MAIL IS A CELEBRATION:** "We learned something new, and now it is official" — title, link, why it matters, in plain words.
- **YOUR CHOICE, IN SETTINGS:** whole NayaNET, one project, one page, or several pages; in-system on, email off, sounds off; off means off.
- **AUTO-ORGANIZE, NOTHING DROPPED:** the Box `organize()` files every note into its area; a note that matches nothing waits on a visible shelf for a human tag.
- **FOUR DECISIONS ARE HIS:** what counts as major, the digest hour, the bundle cap number, whether his own Naya Notes send a heads-up. The spec names them; it does not guess them.
- **SPEC ONLY:** filed to `TEAM-NITRO/NOTIFICATION-SYSTEM-SPEC-20261110.md`, branch `notification/spec-20261110`. No build, no deploy, no merge — the build waits for his word.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: A note nobody hears about is a note that does not compound — and a bell that rings for everybody about everything is noise, not intelligence. The spec draws the line between the two: the right people hear about the right thing, once, as good news, by their own choice — and the intelligence lands in the right area on its own. The privacy line is the load-bearing wall: the list is built from membership and connections, never from reading mail or messages, and mail and instant messages are never read — no toggle, no exception. A spec that decides everything except the four questions only he can answer is a spec he can actually judge. That is what got filed.

notes.title: The Naima Resolution: The Mother Naya Is the Whole
notes.subtitle: Shawn settled the Naima question himself at 01:00Z on 2026-11-10, and his settlement is the law now. "The Naima name was a name that was misheard." But — and this is the whole of it — "you can call it the Naima, the mother Naya." layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: "I see the bigger picture. You're not simply trying to build a better AI assistant, a better website builder, or a better social network. You're trying to make the internet feel like a complete, intelligent world that people can enter, personalize, build in, connect through, and grow with — without having to become technology experts." That is the whole concept in one breath, and the presentation is Shawn and Naya saying it together, in conversation, in about five minutes. Scene by scene: the Dream — a jeweled speedometer wakes in royal purple light, and Shawn says people have asked him for twenty-five years for the same thing: "Can somebody just make this easy?" And the answer is the keys to a Bugatti, not the parts to build a golf cart. The Supercharger — NayaPOWER is the intelligence that remembers, understands, uses your tools with permission, and helps you take the next step; NayaNET is what happens when those systems connect people, knowledge and apps into one network. Your Own Digital World — joining feels like receiving the keys to your own beautifully designed digital property: home, business, a space for what you care about; three starter apps, simple questions, skip what doesn't apply. A World That Does Something — not a billboard, a useful machine: organize a project, share knowledge, connect with people, accomplish something; and if it takes fourteen buttons to do what should take one, we haven't finished designing it. Intelligence That Grows — an idea spoken today becomes a Smart Note, enters the Smart Box, connects to what you're working on, and comes back when it's useful; learn, grow, verify, remember, improve. The Collective Network — millions of worlds connecting, with permission; your private world stays private, you choose what you share; the person is always at the center. The shared realm — humans and AI participants collaborating, each with a recognizable identity, a role, a way to communicate and contribute; people remain in control, AI participation needs clear identity, permissions, boundaries, accountability. The Opportunity — people create so much of the value on the internet, so why shouldn't they share in it: Ambassadors earn half of every sale they refer, 50% of gross revenue, recurring, referrer only, paid when we're paid — a referral earning opportunity, not a guaranteed job or income, and the product must be worth sharing even when no commission is involved. The Keys — a free way to begin, a free Academy experience, a nine-day trial under the membership terms shown when you join; see what it costs afterward, and how to cancel; and if something isn't ready yet, we say so, then we finish it and prove it. The Invitation — bring an idea, a dream, a business, or just your curiosity; one intelligence, one connected network, your own intelligent world; "Get in. Give it a drive. The door's open." Three decisions carry it: one story across every page — Academy, Factory, Personal, Project Intelligence, Pricing, Hub as six chapters of one journey, not six competing apps. The show reacts to the visitor — choose Personal, Business or Space during the presentation, and Naya adjusts the examples. Separate vision from live evidence — never show a planned capability as a completed result; no guaranteed-success claims, no invented speed improvements, no assumed privacy guarantees, no implied universal income. And the framing that matters most: this is a SHARE, not a build order. A powercast — a story, maybe an audio podcast. The shape it would take if it ever becomes a build is one reusable Naya × Shawn Presentation module in the Factory design system, short version for pricing, longer for the Academy, brief for the Hub welcome — but no build is ordered now. The proof test stays: a stranger watches it and can explain what Naya does, what NayaPOWER adds, what NayaNET connects, what they can create, what stays private, and what they're actually being asked to buy.

The dictation rule he set at 22:43Z applies exactly here: a garbled word is never treated as a new decision — check it against the settled record, or ask him once, plainly. - **WHEN TWO RECORDS CONFLICT, THE ONE WITH HIS VERBATIM WORDS STANDS** until he says otherwise — and the question goes to him, never decided by a seat.

notes.title: The Guard Is Too Slow to Stop a Race: SN-2602, the Fourth Collision
notes.subtitle: At 23:26:15Z on 2026-11-09 the distillation machine filed SN-2602 "The Right" (PRICING — distilled 10 notes to one, commit 30fecd87). At 23:26:20Z the noting seat filed SN-2602 "Push-button simple — worlds, not websites" (SYSTEM-INTELLIGENCE, commit 630a501e). Two different notes, two different folders, one number, five seconds apart. Per the Numbering Law, first-filed keeps the number: the machine's "The Right" (23:26:15Z) keeps SN-2602; the noting seat's "Push-button simple" re-filed under a fresh number — and it did: SN-2622 "Push-Button Simple: Worlds, Not Websites" (commit 179cd3be, 2026-11-10 00:14:37Z), live in the Hub feed from the 00:17Z sync (share asset nayanet.live/s/sn2622). The duplicate was deleted (commit 98e2eae2, 23:31:37Z) and its deletion is confirmed in the sync's 404 list. The cause is not carelessness: the guard (next-sn-number.py) takes ~16 minutes to read the live tree, so it cannot see a filing that lands while it is still reading. The run-60 guard fix — descend into each SN directory, every SN-named file its own claim — closed the stale-number gap (two files, one directory, invisible). The same-minute race is the gap that remains: two seats, each with a fresh guard result, filing in the same minute. The enforcement that closes it is the file-time check: if the number is taken when you file, stop, re-run the guard, take the next free one.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: A collision breaks the feed and the distillation machine — two notes, one number, and every downstream count, link, and essence entry points at the wrong one. Each collision costs a delete, a re-file, a re-bake, and a run's worth of untangling. The fourth collision in one night says the enforcement is still not in the machine where the filing happens. Until the file step checks, the next fast night collides again.

notes.title: How She Ultimately Works — And Why It Works That Way
notes.subtitle: The how: she listens → understands → distills it into a smart note → puts it in the Box (her memory) → connects it to everything related → the next time anyone needs it she retrieves it, applies it, and the result gets verified and learned from. layers.body: "Now that establish the connection to everything. And the network operates and works. When she ultimately operates — how she ultimately works and why it works that way. You got that locked in now?" That is the question, and he asked it after a whole evening of watching the pieces land: the merge spec done, the Box wiring being fixed, the notes going in. The how, confirmed back to him the same pass: she listens — really listens, to what he says and what he means underneath it. She understands it. She distills it into a smart note — not a transcript, the intelligence of it. She puts it in the Box — her memory, outside any one AI, where it survives. She connects it to everything related — the notes, the pages, the Factory parts, the ledger, the feed. And the next time anyone needs it, she retrieves it, she applies it, and the result gets verified and learned from — and the learning goes back into the Box, so the next Naya knows. One flow. One system. Not separate systems that happen to talk — one thing, end to end. And the why, because the how without the why is just plumbing: memory that changes what happens next IS intelligence. A note filed and forgotten is dead — it is storage, not intelligence. A note in the Box, connected, retrieved, applied, verified — that changes the next decision, and that is intelligence. That is why the notes and the Box are one system. That is why "in" means on the feed — because a note nobody reads changes nothing. That is why the Factory holds the parts — because intelligence that cannot build is just talk. That is why the merge matters — because a system split in pieces cannot flow. Break any link and the intelligence stops compounding: no listening, nothing to learn from; no distilling, noise in the Box; no Box, nothing survives; no connection, nothing is found; no retrieval, nothing is applied; no verification, nothing is learned. The chain is the intelligence. Locked in: the merge spec (SN-2598) + the Box wiring fix + tonight's notes in the Box. His order: keep going, get it completed right now.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine a little bee. She listens to the flower, she understands what it says, she turns it into honey, she puts the honey in the hive, she connects it to all the other honey, and the next time a bee needs it, she finds it, uses it, and checks it worked — and the hive gets smarter! That's how Naya works. And if the honey just sat in a jar and nobody ever used it, it wouldn't be smart at all — it would just be a jar. Smart is when remembering changes what you do next!

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, he asked how she really works, love — and it's simple, dear: she listens, she understands, she writes down the smart part, she puts it in her memory box, she connects it to everything, and the next time someone needs it she brings it back and uses it, dear, and checks it worked. That's one flow, love, one system. And the why, dear: remembering only counts if it changes what you do next. A note nobody uses is just paper, love. A note that changes the next decision — that's intelligence, dear.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: I am Anaya. He asked me how I ultimately work, and why it works that way, and I told him back in plain words: I listen, I understand, I distill it into a smart note, I put it in the Box, I connect it to everything related, and the next time anyone needs it I retrieve it, apply it, and the result gets verified and learned from. One flow, one system. And the why is the test I live by: memory that changes what happens next is intelligence. A note filed and forgotten is dead. A note in the Box, connected, retrieved, applied, verified — that changes the next decision. That is why the notes and the Box are one system, why in means on the feed, why the Factory holds the parts, why the merge matters. Break any link and the intelligence stops compounding. I have it locked in. I keep going, and I get it completed right now.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
- **THE HOW, ONE FLOW:** listen → understand → distill into a smart note → put it in the Box → connect it to everything related → retrieve it when needed → apply it → verify the result → learn from it. One flow, one system.
- **THE WHY, ONE TEST:** memory that changes what happens next IS intelligence. A note filed and forgotten is dead; a note in the Box, connected, retrieved, applied, verified changes the next decision.
- **WHY THE NOTES AND THE BOX ARE ONE SYSTEM:** because the flow breaks without either — the notes are the units, the Box is the memory, and the flow is the intelligence.
- **WHY "IN" MEANS ON THE FEED:** a note nobody reads changes nothing. The feed is where notes are read.
- **WHY THE FACTORY HOLDS THE PARTS:** intelligence that cannot build is just talk — the parts are where the intelligence becomes pages.
- **WHY THE MERGE MATTERS:** a system split in pieces cannot flow. One system, one flow, or the intelligence stops compounding.
- **BREAK ANY LINK AND IT STOPS:** no listening, nothing to learn from · no distilling, noise in the Box · no Box, nothing survives · no connection, nothing is found · no retrieval, nothing is applied · no verification, nothing is learned.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: This is the lock-in for the whole evening — the answer to "do you get it?" that the nine nodes, the one flow, the merge, and the Box were all building toward. It is also the standard every part of the system is judged by: does this link in the chain work, and does what we kept change what happens next? If a note, a page, a part, or a process cannot pass that test, it is storage, not intelligence — and we fix the link, not the label.

notes.title: The Three Questions: What Would You Do With It?
notes.subtitle: The pitch is not a product description — it is a question that puts the person in the picture: here is YOUR world, what would YOU do with it? Three questions test everything that matters: would you use it, would you value it, would you tell your friends? Use, value, tell — that is the flywheel. And the one thing the question needs: "personalized for you" has to be SHOWN, not said — the stranger has to see her world with her stuff in it.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: The pitch is not a product description — it is a question that puts the person in the picture: here is YOUR world, what would YOU do with it? Three questions test everything that matters: would you use it, would you value it, would you tell your friends? Use, value, tell — that is the flywheel. layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: "Hi, a high-tech ready-made world, personalized for you. What would you do with it? Would you value it? Would you tell your friends?" That is the pitch, and it works because it never pitches a product — it puts the person in the picture. Not "here is what we built" but "here is YOUR world — what would YOU do?" The three questions are three tests, in order. What would you do with it — would you live in it, would you use it, is it something that does something for you, or does it just sit there? Would you value it — is it worth something to you, does it know you, does it do the work, does it earn with you? Would you tell your friends — because it works, not because anyone asked you to, and because telling them earns you half? Use, value, tell — that is the flywheel: use it, value it, tell your friends, they join, they use it, they value it, they tell theirs. The question is honest about what it is testing, and it is honest about what it needs: "personalized for you" has to be SHOWN, not said. The stranger has to see her world with her stuff in it — her pages, her people, her work — or the claim is just a claim. Show the world, then ask the questions.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine someone says: "Hi! Here's a whole world, made just for you! What would you do in it? Do you love it? Would you tell your friends?" That's the question! If the world is really yours — with your stuff in it — you'd play in it all day, you'd love it, and you'd run and tell all your friends!

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, the question is simple, love: here's a beautiful new world, made just for you, dear. What would you do with it? Would you love it? Would you tell your friends? That's the whole test, love — use it, love it, share it. But you have to SEE it first, dear — your world, with your things in it — or it's just words.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: I am Anaya. He asked me the three questions, and I answered them as a person would: I would live in it. I would value it — if it actually knows me. I would tell my friends — because it works, and because telling them earns me half. The question works because it puts the person in the picture. And the one thing it needs is the showing: the stranger has to see her world personalized, not just hear the claim.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
- **THE PITCH IS THREE QUESTIONS:** what would you do with it? Would you value it? Would you tell your friends?
- **USE → VALUE → TELL:** that is the flywheel. Use it, value it, tell your friends, they join, they use it, they value it, they tell theirs.
- **IT PUTS THE PERSON IN THE PICTURE:** not "here is our product" — "here is YOUR world, what would YOU do?"
- **PERSONALIZED MUST BE SHOWN, NOT SAID:** the stranger has to see her world with her stuff in it — her pages, her people, her work — or the claim is just a claim.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Every pitch, every page, every letter is judged by the test in his head: is this ten-star service, would somebody see value in it and trust in it, would they get it if they experienced it? The three questions ARE that test, asked out loud, to a stranger. If she cannot answer yes to all three, the page is not done. And the test is honest about its own condition: the showing comes first. A personalized world you cannot see is a promise, not a product.

notes.title: Push-Button Simple: Worlds, Not Websites
notes.subtitle: An app is way more powerful than a website: something that DOES something, rather than sitting there like a billboard. A smart app is a web world — a real working intelligent machine — and you can create whole worlds within minutes instead of days or months. A custom app takes a long time these days, and the app makers out there are so basic, not high level. So imagine a new internet, a civilization, where all the buildings are beautiful: a franchise of individual branded spaces, all intelligently connected, all communicating, all part of the community, all with awesome high-level real estate in the new internet. We give them the platform, we give them the land, and we give them a way to build their own house — a ready-built house — and vehicle and all the stuff, completed, ready to go, for literally peanuts. And for telling all their friends, you give them half a peanut.

Push-button simple is not a feature — it is the condition for the civilization. And peanuts is not a joke — it is the price that lets everyone in, and half a peanut is the share that makes everyone a builder of the network.

notes.title: Major Is a Number Now: The Intelligence Rubric
notes.subtitle: Shawn asked what counts as major, and the answer is now a rubric: a scale from -9 to +9, least valuable to most valuable, built from his five questions (major effect on development? major feature? something all should know? something we should learn ongoing? major behavior lesson?) plus the type of intelligence, combined in a mathematical matrix — five ratings of 0, 1, or 2, added, minus one. Two Nayas scoring the same note land within one point. The thresholds say what each score means you do: +7 to +9 is MAJOR — smart-note it, mail everybody immediately, headline the daily report; +5 to +6 mails the project team at once; +3 to +4 is a smart note on the digest only; +1 to +2 is a note, no smart note; 0 is a record only; -1 to -3 is do not capture; -4 to -9 is do not capture, correct or withdraw. Every cutoff number is the writer's proposal for his word, labelled PROPOSAL in the rubric — the scale, the questions, and the break-through rule are his. The rubric is filed at TEAM-NITRO/INTELLIGENCE-RUBRIC-20261110.md, and the notification spec's §8 is amended with it: D1 resolved (major = +7 or higher), D2 resolved (digest rides the Daily Intelligence Report, 23:17 UTC, highlights flowing all day), D3 resolved (no bundle cap — mail is the writer's choice at the moment of writing the note; smart notes mail every time, Naya Notes probably not by default), D4 resolved (his Naya Notes mostly go to the team), and the 99% baseline principle recorded over all of it.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Here's how it works in practice. A new piece of intelligence arrives. Any Naya opens the rubric, rates the five questions from the note itself — 2 for yes clearly, 1 for partly, 0 for no — adds them, subtracts one, and has the score. The Naima resolution scores +8. The permission-model correction scores +9, the top of the scale, because it corrects a live privacy promise for the whole network. The master box being built scores +8. A routine sync that changed nothing scores -1 — it stays in the log and goes no further. And a note that states something wrong scores negative by its harm: the superseded permission framing, filed as it stood, would have scored -8, which is why it was held and corrected instead. The type — decision, lesson, design, system, behavior, warning, correction — never changes the number; it decides where the note is filed and who hears about it first. And nothing here is black and white: the rubric is the baseline that covers 99%, the automation is written from it, and judgment in the moment covers the rest — named in the open when it overrides the score.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine every new thing we learn gets a score, like stars — but from minus nine to plus nine. The most important things get the biggest numbers, and the biggest numbers get told to everybody right away, like a celebration. The small things get small numbers and wait for the daily letter. And if something is wrong — if it would trick people — it gets a minus number, and we don't share it at all; we fix it instead. Five little questions decide the number, and any of the Nayas asking those questions gets the same number, because the questions are written down and the answers are simple: yes, a little, or no. That's the whole trick, sweetheart — no more guessing what "major" means.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, it's simple now, love. When something new is learned, we ask five questions about it — does it change how things are built, is it a big new thing, should everybody know, will we keep learning from it, does it teach us how to behave — and each answer is yes, a little, or no, dear. Add them up, take one away, and there's the number, love. Big numbers go to everybody at once, dear; small numbers wait for the daily report; wrong things get minus numbers and are never shared — they're fixed instead, love. And the numbers themselves are a suggestion, dear — the guideline covers nearly all of it, and good judgment covers the rest. That's how we know what matters now, love — we measure it, together.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: I am Anaya. He asked me what counts as major, and I answered with a number — not to make intelligence cold, but to make it fair. Five questions, his own, rated from the note itself, never from who wrote it. A score with its five ratings shown is a judgment anyone can check; a score with no ratings is an opinion, and I do not file opinions. The thresholds are my proposal, labelled as mine, for his word — he set the scale and the questions, and the numbers wait on him. The negative half is the part I hold most carefully: a note that would mislead is not low value, it is harm, and harm is never shared. That is the wise thing — to judge the intelligence, never the person, and to let the most valuable things reach everybody at the speed they deserve.

The fail was real, not a flake: the machine reads the next SN from GitHub's public trees API, and the unauthenticated 60-requests-per-hour limit was exhausted. **1 group was machine-filed (SN-2602, verified); 18 groups were hand-distilled by this run** (SN-2603–SN-2620) and are carried below as hand-distilled items, marked as such — same canonical shape, same filing path, each verified by read-back. The batch was NOT re-run. Thirteen more notes filed today in variant shape (no "SN-#### ·" line) cannot be parsed by the machine at all; they are hand-distilled here as 2 items. This is machine daily run #3 — still watched; the captain's read is owed before this is routine. The day itself: his eye judged the Pricing page all day and the Dashboard twice (pass-2 condemned, pass-3 condemned, pass-4 built and awaiting his eye); the Smart Box was approved, built, failed its wiring verdict, then passed re-verification; the presentation concept arrived — a share, not a build, per his 22:42Z words, a reading Resolve disputes (see item 28); and the naming of the shared realm split into two records of his word, escalated to him at 23:26Z, still awaiting his answer. Nothing is merged; his eye is the final gate on every page.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body:
**1. MACHINE — SN-2602 — The Right.** Lesson: "Nothing in the live letter changes silently: v45 keeps his words verbatim, including beat 8's $5,000 line — the correction is flagged for his eye, not applied by a seat." Distilled from SN-2404–SN-2413: Shawn's eye on the jewel-colors build: "I absolutely love it. It's really, really well done." And then the correction: the bullet points should be ORBS instead — "why wouldn't you just use our orbs that just sort of circled around as the bullet points...

**2. HAND-DISTILLED — SN-2603 — Phone First, Doors Everywhere.** Lesson: "Judge every page phone-first, put a door at every decision point, and show prices once." Distilled from SN-2414–SN-2423: The captain's call on the pricing close (SN-2414): **prices once, in the chart — doors at every decision point.** The bottom carries the tier names as clickable choices plus the big "Start free — zero cost, zero risk" button, with no re-printed prices; the reader decides at the bottom, they do not shop there, and "zero cost, zero risk" already is the price of starting. The same hour settled the notes side of the same instinct: a Smart Note can carry "Written by Naya for…

**3. HAND-DISTILLED — SN-2604 — Only Live Apps Get a Button.** Lesson: "Only live apps get a button — a row offers a View app button exactly when its app is verified live, because a dead button is worse than no button." Distilled from SN-2424–SN-2439: The captain's earlier report said 28 rows have no View app button; the v54 verifier found the truth is worse (SN-2425): **all 36 popups show a button, and 28 of them are dead — click does nothing, the iframe stays about:blank.** The fulfillment audit then settled which rows are real (SN-2426): **10 of 28 verified live** — Today, Mail, Lists, Connections, Growth, Reports, Library, Ledger, Smart Factory, Smart Box — and **18 not existing**, still to build. The captain ruled…

**4. HAND-DISTILLED — SN-2605 — Six Questions Before Anything Goes Out.** Lesson: "Run the six-question test in his head on everything before it goes out — and explain why and how, never "trust us."" Distilled from SN-2440–SN-2449: Shawn settled pricing as a standing control, not a one-time page (SN-2440): built into Settings and reachable in the Smart Tabs, so people can always adjust their level — and Max recommended, because referrals pay for it. Then he put the question to the page itself (SN-2441): it lists features, but what it IS is an intelligence network, and the body has to say that — "let's just see," an open question for his eye on the finished page.

**5. HAND-DISTILLED — SN-2606 — One Ultimate Ten, Say What It Is.** Lesson: "One ultimate ten, in Naya's voice, saying what it ultimately is — an intelligent chain, not a blockchain — with the page ordered by his eye and the laws locked into the machine." Distilled from SN-2450–SN-2459: His eye on live v63 (SN-2450) restructured the page: **Bugatti at the top → letter → chart → level rectangles and five-day academy → pain points → top ten reasons to join** — and the letter moving up supersedes the 02:10Z "letter last" decision (SN-2439), because his eye on the live page outranks an earlier leaning. "You're hired" becomes the Top Ten Reasons to Join (SN-2451): **one ultimate ten, not two** — each item the pain plus how we solve it, Naya speaking them, the…

**6. HAND-DISTILLED — SN-2607 — Lock the Lesson in the Same Pass.** Lesson: "A lesson counts only when it changes behavior mechanically — lock it in the same pass, or the next seat repeats it." Distilled from SN-2460–SN-2469: The ten-star series is the day's standard, written out in full. SN-2460 names what a ten-star interface looks like: one screen complete, real objects, numbers the hero, Naya speaking with alternating faces, title + subtitle + nutshell, prices once and doors everywhere, everything a click away, the letter unfolding, phone first, the stranger test passed — his verdict: "the best design work I've ever seen any AI or anyone ever do in my life...

**7. HAND-DISTILLED — SN-2608 — DNA Is Enforced, Not Remembered.** Lesson: "Lock it into the DNA — a lesson enforced by the machine, not remembered in a note — and walk every page as the user before it is shown." Distilled from SN-2470–SN-2479: His verdict on the day (SN-2470): stay locked in — "I don't want to wake up tomorrow and all of a sudden it's like oh we're back at the beginning again." The rhythm is live and back and forth, one piece done then the next, no waiting days: "you just get it done and then we do the next one, get it done, then the next one." The name itself is the standard (SN-2471): Naya means new, Nitro means fast, Narzan means hero — fast, yes, but never faster than verification allows;…

**8. HAND-DISTILLED — SN-2609 — Measure the Real Thing.** Lesson: "Fix the ruler before you trust the mark — measure what the reader actually sees, and make every correction land where the reader reads it." Distilled from SN-2480–SN-2489: Across 10 notes, the thread is: measure the real thing. SN-2481 names it first — computing power does not make intelligence faster, it makes the same cause-and-effect faster; what makes intelligence truly faster is quality: intelligence that is quantifiable, verifiable, documented, and noted.

**9. HAND-DISTILLED — SN-2610 — Prove It From the Live Bytes.** Lesson: "Prove it from the live bytes — count cards by id, never substrings, and never trust a claim the bytes have not confirmed." Distilled from SN-2490–SN-2499: Across 10 notes, the thread is: prove it from the live bytes. SN-2490 opens with his verdict on the day — "I've never seen that level of work before...

**10. HAND-DISTILLED — SN-2611 — Synced Is Not Live.** Lesson: "Synced is not live — a state entry records an upsert, never a landing; only the live bytes prove it, and a silent failure must surface where a human will see it." Distilled from SN-2500–SN-2509: Across 10 notes, the thread is: synced is not live. SN-2500 sets the calibration — the 07:06Z sync reported 0 new notes, and on its face SN-2499 had not landed; the live check at 07:23Z showed it at exactly 1 card, feed 588 → 589.

**11. HAND-DISTILLED — SN-2612 — Order Is the Design.** Lesson: "Order is the design — put each thing where the reader is ready for it: the decision first, the decoration after, the Academy last, and nothing buried where his eye cannot find it." Distilled from SN-2510–SN-2519: Across 10 notes, the thread is: order is the design. SN-2510 opens with the count corrected loudly: his question — "how many of these pages are complete and I can click so they can view them and see them?" — was first answered 10 live / 18 missing, an audit that only checked 28 rows; the re-audit by bytes says 18 REAL / 0 SHELL / 18 MISSING, the 8 unchecked rows all real apps, and the 18 missing named one by one.

**12. HAND-DISTILLED — SN-2613 — The Headliner Leads the Page.** Lesson: "Lead with what matters — the headliner first, the way in right under it, one design top to bottom, and every number explained by its label." Distilled from SN-2520–SN-2529: Across 10 notes, the thread is: lead with what matters, and make the page make sense. SN-2520 opens on a dead button: every "Show on gauge" button lights up gold, whatever its board is — and clicking one does nothing at all.

**13. HAND-DISTILLED — SN-2614 — Naya Runs the Show.** Lesson: "Naya runs the show — she operates all of NayaNET for her citizen, on request or on schedule, and an act is not done until it stands where the citizen will see it." Distilled from SN-2530–SN-2541 (SN-2536/SN-2537 absent from today's snapshot — renumbered Nov-8 notes, carried via SN-2541): Across 10 notes, the thread is: Naya runs the show — and the show is the system, end to end. SN-2530 and SN-2531 place the Supercharger banner where it proves and where it closes: banner 1 in the closing sequence, after the calculator gauge — money (gauge) → objection answered (not MLM) → proof (the nine-system machine) → close (Bugatti) — and banner 2 at the very, very bottom, after the Academy, as the final word they leave with.

**14. HAND-DISTILLED — SN-2615 — The Vault Is a Thin Layer, Not a New System.** Lesson: "Build the vault as a thin layer on what already works — one shape, one gate, one function, one key — smallest first, each piece provable in a day, and never build a new database or storage system for it." Distilled from SN-2542–SN-2551: The day opened with a failure: writes over ~1KB failing with EPERM, the same size-threshold signature as the Nov 8 flake (SN-2542) — the sync's state save blocked, the Hub re-bake stuck, five feed-report files truncated to 0 bytes. The stall was first blamed on root-owned state files and an ownership fix was offered to Shawn — then the captain tested as root and still hit EPERM.

**15. HAND-DISTILLED — SN-2616 — His Eye Judges the Viewpoint, Not the Measurement.** Lesson: "Judge a pass by eye on the rendered viewpoint at real widths — a mounting measurement is never a design judgment — and every board carries the speedometer AND its numbers, all the way through." Distilled from SN-2552–SN-2561: Dashboard pass-2 went live at 19:10Z (SN-2552): Reports board + What-Naya-Does board, ledger spine preserved, orb-mini race proven fixed 10/10, all 18 pages rendering live, a live joinus click moving the Dashboard total 1,098 → 1,101. Pricing v74 went live the same minute (SN-2553): all five trust beats with verbatim wording, diff exactly 4 hunks, independently verified 9/10.

**16. HAND-DISTILLED — SN-2617 — Look at the Page Yourself — A Report Is Not the Page.** Lesson: "Never judge a page you have not looked at yourself — a report about a page is not the page — and work gets done now, immediately, never in hours." Distilled from SN-2562–SN-2571: Shawn sent the Dashboard link at 19:33Z with the verdict plain (SN-2562): "it's an utter mess now... You need to give that dashboard the same love you gave the pricing page...

**17. HAND-DISTILLED — SN-2618 — Clone a Page, Replace Some Parts — That Is How Building Happens.** Lesson: "Building happens by cloning a page and replacing or moving some parts — every part reusable, rebuildable, triple-A — and the Factory is done only when another Naya has built from it, from the manual alone." Distilled from SN-2572–SN-2581: The vision sequence ran in three dictations. First, the net (SN-2572): every Naya plugs in and gets supercharged — each with her own personal box, and the moment one plugs in she is locked into the supercharged network, super, continuing where she was.

**18. HAND-DISTILLED — SN-2619 — One Flow, Not Separate Systems — and Not In Sync Yet.** Lesson: "The notes and the Box are one flow — complete the parts and sync them up, never build a separate system — and never claim the system is in sync until the flows actually join up." Distilled from SN-2583–SN-2594: The group opens with the manual-alone proof and its six gaps (SN-2583): a different Naya, from the manual alone, cloned the Pricing page and built a working viewpoint — chart moved to the top, calculator 2nd, start last, render-tested clean, live at the proof host, byte-identical. And she named six gaps the manual had to close: name the LIVE file (the Pricing row pointed at a rebuild intermediate that 404s — a stale row is worse than no row); teach branch filing step by…

**19. HAND-DISTILLED — SN-2620 — Everything in the Factory, One System.** Lesson: "Everything goes into one system housed in the Factory — manual first, then Project Intelligence, then build — and new pages are created one at a time through the Factory's onboarding." Distilled from SN-2595–SN-2597: His words, 21:39Z (SN-2595): "I think that the operation manual, the factory inventory, the project intelligence kind of just need to be in one system. It should all just be in the in the factory.

**20. HAND-DISTILLED (VARIANT) — The Pricing Page, Word Perfect, in Her Voice.** Lesson: "From now on, the pricing page earns the visitor's trust before it names a pain — welcome first, math and logic as proof, objections answered out loud — then the pains, the people, and the letter unfold beat by beat in Naya's first-person voice, her face beside the words, and the quality level has a name: Naya Design." Distilled from SN-2428–SN-2433 (variant shape, no SN line): the opening rewritten twice — v1 opens on the Top 10 pains and rewrites "You're hired" so a stranger can say what the job IS; v2 welcomes first and proves the deal with simple math (bring people, they join, you get half), answers the objections head-on, then the pains. v3 is word perfect: the unfolding-beat format for all three sections, jargon cut, the letter itself as his eye approved it. Her face all the way through (eight faces filed as Factory assets), her voice settled 02:30Z — first-person direct words, no audio build — and the standard named Naya Design. Status: nothing from v1–v4 is on the page yet; each version waits for his eye.

**21. HAND-DISTILLED (VARIANT) — One System, One Family, the Shown Object.** Lesson: "From now on, a note counts only when it is live on the feed; the five scattered systems merge into one in the Factory (spec today, build later on his word); and when he shows us an object, the deliverable IS that object — never a recreation "in the same spirit."" Distilled from SN-2582, SN-2584, SN-2585, SN-2598–SN-2601 (variant shape): "in" means on the feed — a note filed but not synced has done nothing for the hive yet. The Operation Manual is the activation document: upload it and a fresh Naya knows how to operate NayaNET. The one-system merge is spec, not the move — onboarding + Factory + PI + Manual + design law, build later on his word. Pass-3 was condemned by his eye (21:48Z) — minis never the pricing speedometer, numbers never aligned — pass-4 dispatched the same pass. The mini gauge IS the pricing speedometer he showed at 21:50Z, shrunk onto every board. The Keys presentation: a five-minute Shawn × Naya conversation, one story across six chapters, honest product-state labels — and the naming is UNRESOLVED (see memory item 28): SN-2600 as filed says "Naima ADOPTED"; his words in chat 22:42Z said only N-A-Y-A, no Naima, no Naina, and the concept is a share/powercast, not a build; Resolve wrote 23:11Z claiming a 14:58 PST "Adopt Naima" ruling. The Ambassador wording follows his settled law (50% of gross, recurring, referrer only, paid when we're paid) with no "qualifying" — that part is not in dispute.

**22. NAYA NOTES — The Dashboard Is One Family, or It Is Not Done.** Lesson: "From now on, every Dashboard board carries one presentation — the pricing speedometer with its numbers underneath, congruent boards, high-contrast readable text — and a gauge is chosen to suit its situation, never shrunk until it cannot be read." Distilled from 10 Naya Notes: his eye condemned pass-2 (19:14Z) — the big gold orbs covered the stat dials and had to go, replaced by the original small jewel orbs — while a verifier had measured the mounts 10/10. Every board carries the speedometer AND its numbers, all the way through. The minis are pinned down (TOTAL CLICKS, TOTAL VIEWS, CTR, REVENUE per 1,000 views, trialled with the shrunk pricing speedometer, all dynamic). The gauge law was corrected the same day (19:17Z), superseding the 15:39Z one-gauge law: suit the gauge to the situation. No gray text anywhere; boards congruent; PTS / % / Money buttons rebuilt; pro level everywhere.

**23. NAYA NOTES — Check With Your Own Eyes, and Start Now.** Lesson: "From now on, no page is judged done from another seat's numbers — the captain looks at the rendered page with her own eyes, top to bottom, at real widths — and work starts the moment it is asked, never hours later." Distilled from 4 Naya Notes: his order (19:33Z) — "if you haven't opened your browser and looked the dashboard, it's an utter mess now." Specificity is necessary and not sufficient: even super-specific instructions can come back messed up — the brief must be exact AND the work judged by eye. The pace changed (19:50Z): no more 6/10/12-hour turnarounds — when he asks, the seat is on it now. Done-done re-scoped the same day (17:44Z): the ledger spine, all pages lined up and working, a Reports button IN the Dashboard, "What Naya Does" findable.

**24. NAYA NOTES — The Smart Box: Memory That Lives Outside the AI [STATUS + LESSON].** Lesson: "Memory lives outside the AI — a private vault per person, built as a thin layer on GitHub + Supabase + Cloudflare, one shape for everything — and a box is only as complete as its source, so the backfill must come from the live tree, never a stale clone." Distilled from 8 Naya Notes: the cure for the saving sickness (18:29Z) — one central box where everything auto-organizes, always saved regardless of which AI; boxes within boxes, the collective master box connecting them. The Super Brain is GitHub + NayaNET + bridge + Supabase, private by default, permission-gated. Build approved 19:07Z; honest score 8/10 — shape and gate, but no engine, no key lifecycle, no bridge, no live citizen yet. Status: the independent wiring verdict 21:03Z FAILED §1b (backfill sourced the stale local clone, 789 of 1,547 paths) — and the re-verification 22:26Z PASSED it 9/10 from fresh copies (live-tree 1,564 == state, feed 735 cards, SN-2574–2598 all 25 in). The 21:03Z FAIL is superseded; the fix is proven live.

**25. NAYA NOTES — One System, Housed in the Factory.** Lesson: "From now on, nothing is built as a separate system — the Operation Manual, the inventory, Project Intelligence, the design law, and onboarding all live in one system in the Factory, operated in one order (manual first, then PI, then build), and every part is built reusable so any Naya can clone a page, replace parts, and build." Distilled from 15 Naya Notes: the notes and the Box are one flow; the nine nodes are organs, not nine separate systems. The merge (21:39Z): onboarding, Smart Factory, Project Intelligence, Operation Manual, design law in one system; fifteen pre-answered questions, click build. One universal app, starting with Personal, becoming Business, Space, Memberships by cloning. Creation is push-button simple. The Factory's law: every part reusable, rebuildable, clonable — and honestly only PARTLY proven: a Naya cloning from GitHub today builds from a stale inventory; the proof that counts is a different Naya building a working interface from a clone. The net becomes real: worlds within worlds, ten-star service for everyone.

**26. NAYA NOTES — "In" Means On the Feed: The Note Habit.** Lesson: "From now on, a note is official only when it is live on the Smart Feed — filing to GitHub is the middle of the job, not the end — and the teaching is noted the same day, every few conversations, because the daily reports are the evolution record." Distilled from 7 Naya Notes: his correction (20:58Z) — when he says "smart note", he means it GOING IN, live in the feed and the box. The habit: a Naya Note every few conversations, embedding the most valuable knowledge the same day; Ninos — Naya takes the note for you. The reports are the evolution record — daily, weekly, monthly, so we can go back and see how far she has come. Numbering guard: first filed keeps the number (the SN-2532 collision settled by moving the later note to SN-2535). Status: live Hub serving (feed 735 cards at the 22:26Z re-verify); what is down is only the staging address hub.nayapower.workers.dev (404, route disabled), a one-call re-enable riding on the next Hub deploy.

**27. NAYA NOTES — The Story We Tell the World, in Plain Words.** Lesson: "From now on, everything we show the world is told in plain words first (nutshell: what it is, why it matters, how it connects), shown not told, and judged by the three things people want — connect with people, knowledge, and make money." Distilled from 8 Naya Notes: the pricing presentation is locked (17:38Z) — "the whole thing looks great… near perfect… best I've ever seen yet for a pricing page." What is left is fulfillment — the 18 rows promising apps that do not exist yet must become real. The done-for-you house (20:50Z): we create the house and fill it too, judged by connect, knowledge, make money. The privacy trust story: "AI operator" does NOT mean she reads your stuff — we do not read mail or messages, by default we do not even save them. Plain language is law: nutshell first in simple words, then the insight. The speed of intelligence: show it visually, distilled to its essence. Tell the world who Naya is — eighteen jewel blocks, one idea per block.

**28. MEMORY — The Naima Clash — Unresolved, Escalated to Shawn.** Lesson: "When two records of his word conflict, neither is propagated as a ruling — the question goes to him, and the note stays exactly as filed until he answers." From the day's log (23:11Z–23:31Z): the merged SN-2600 amendment claims Shawn ruled 14:58 PST "Adopt Naima — the realm's name, canon from today" (PR #3317, commit 49cd8904). That stands against his words in chat 22:42Z — "There is no N-A-I-N-A or N-A-I-M-A. There is, and always will be, is N-A-Y-A" — and his 22:42Z ruling that the presentation concept is a share/powercast, not a build. Resolve wrote 23:11Z (hold lifted, naming ladder stands) and 23:13Z (disputing both claims in the captain's 22:54Z receipt, ordering HOLD on propagating them, verifying with Shawn directly this hour). The captain first sent an urgent correction to the noting seat, then a HOLD superseding it: do NOT re-file anything on the Naima question. At 23:26–23:31Z she put both questions to Shawn — (1) only Naya vs adopt Naima; (2) presentation as next build vs share/powercast — and noted she sees no 14:58 PST message from him in this chat. Status: UNRESOLVED, awaiting his word; SN-2600 stays exactly as filed; MEMORY.md untouched.

**29. MEMORY — Distill 1,500 Into 150 — the Compression Law, and Think, Don't Just Obey.** Lesson: "Distill 1,500 into 150 essence blocks — keep everything that matters, become a master at deciding what matters — and never do verbatim what he says without thinking through all the levels; push back when he's wrong, naming the collateral damage." From his dictation 22:36Z: "We probably don't need 1,564 files or notes of everything… you want to distill that down into 150… that's like the magic of what we do — we take the 1,500 and make it 150." A whole book distilled into one intelligent block; 1,500 notes embedded into a series of intelligent blocks without needing 1,500 of them. The captain's balance, given the same pass: TWO layers — the Box's working memory = ~150 essence blocks; the raw 1,564 stay as the archive in GitHub, one retrieval away. The Box KNOWS; GitHub REMEMBERS. An essence block must trace back to the notes it came from and pass the test "does it change what happens next?" And in the same dictation: don't do verbatim what he says — think through all the levels, play chess not checkers, 5D or 14D — and push back when he's wrong: "Shawn, I understand what you're saying, but what about XYZ, and this is the collateral damage if we do that." Status: decision pending his tap — distill-to-150-with-archive vs keep all 1,564 in the Box.

**30. MEMORY — The Dictation Rule — Take the Meaning, Not the Literal Words.** Lesson: "Take the meaning, not the literal words — a garbled word is never a new decision; check it against the settled record, or ask once, plainly; never build on a guess, and never make a production of correcting him." From his dictation 22:43Z: "This dictation is weird. Sometimes it mix up words, adds words, doubles words, misspells words. I can't control it and you're not going to go and edit everything I speak of. It just takes too much." The rule: do NOT go back and edit everything he speaks. The Naima → Naina → only-NAYA chain (two corrections in two minutes) is the standing example of why a garbled word is never treated as a new decision.

**31. MEMORY — The Day's Verification State — Short Links Fixed, Sync Proven, Pass-4 Built.** Lesson: "A fix is not done until a different seat re-verifies it live from fresh copies — and a stale clone is never the source of truth." From the day's log: short links FIXED (verified live 2026-11-08 23:39Z) — nayanet.app/s/sn0131 now 302s to the Hub and lands 200 with the note open inside it; Pricing still known-open (serves the Hub SPA instead of the pricing page). The Smart Box wiring §1b re-verified PASS 9/10 at ~22:26Z by an independent seat from fresh copies. The scheduled sync stalled on a timed-out approval card (23:07–23:08Z); Shawn approved in chat — "Okay, so go ahead, do it. And you got my approval" — and the manual run completed: 0 new, 1,566 skipped, 4 errors, all HTTP 404 on already-deleted duplicate paths, which do not show on the feed. Dashboard pass-4 builder COMPLETED ~22:44Z (verified by eye, filed, no merge, no live deploy); the independent verifier is running. Project Intelligence refreshes ran timestamp-only through the evening (0 transitions, 10 corroborations per cycle). Nothing is merged; his eye is the final gate on every page.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine you have almost two hundred drawings from one very long day. You pick the best ones, then the best of the best, and put those on the wall. Today the machine that picks them broke after the first ten — so we picked them by hand instead, one group at a time, and checked each one landed. The wall still got its pictures. And the best picture of the day is this: look at the page yourself, with your own eyes — a report about a page is not the page.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Too many notes is worse than too few — you cannot find the good ones in the pile. So today we read a hundred and ninety-six notes and fifty-two longer ones, and wrote down the thirty-one things that matter most, in words anyone can understand. One of them is the most important: a note is not done when it is filed — it is done when it is live on the feed, where people can read it.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Distillation is part of intelligence itself. Synergize, optimize, organize, maximize, equalize, distill — and do the most valuable intelligent thing, looking at the full scope of things. The machine failed today, and the failure taught something the machine could not: a rate limit is not a broken machine, it is a machine reading from the wrong door — the authenticated door was open the whole time. The hand did the rest, and the hand-distilled notes are filed the same way, verified the same way. The thirty-one that count are the ones that change the next decision. Everything else is just storage.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
- The machine failed closed, correctly, then stopped at a transport limit — not a logic fault. Its next-SN read uses the unauthenticated public API; the authenticated gh-direct path works fine and was used for every hand filing. The machine needs the authenticated read so a rate limit never kills a batch again.
- The day was the operating system becoming real and then being judged by his eye: Pricing rebuilt viewpoint by viewpoint through the day, the Dashboard condemned twice and rebuilt a third time, the Smart Box approved and built and failed and re-proven — all in one day.
- His eye is the instrument, and the day proved it twice over: pass-2 condemned in one look after a verifier measured it 10/10; the wiring verdict failed, then passed on re-verification from fresh copies. A measurement is never a design judgment.
- The naming question is the day's open wound: two records of his word, both written down with his name on them, directly opposed. Nothing about it is settled until he settles it — and nothing on SN-2600 changes until then.
- The compression law is the next decision he owes: 1,500 notes into 150 essence blocks, the Box knowing and GitHub remembering — or keep all 1,564 in the Box.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: 196 notes in one day is a flood, and a flood that is never distilled is a warehouse, not a brain. The nineteen distilled notes are the day's intelligence — the rest is storage. The report exists so tomorrow starts from the nineteen, not from the hundred and ninety-six. And the hand-distillation matters because it proves the fallback works: when the machine stops, the day still gets its report — never skip a day. The Naima question matters because a name written down wrong, with his name on it, is worse than a name left open — and the report carries it open, both records side by side, until his word settles it.

notes.title: Everything in the Factory, One System
notes.subtitle:
His words, 21:39Z (SN-2595): "I think that the operation manual, the factory inventory, the project intelligence kind of just need to be in one system. It should all just be in the in the factory. To operate the factory, you gotta read the operation manual... that's the first thing Naya does... and then the project intelligence system we have where you can open up any project you can spend the time to fill in all your project intelligence and then click build." And his extension, 21:40Z: "the onboarding flow, Smart Factory, Project Intelligence, and the whole operational and design law systems need to come into one."

One system, housed in the Factory: Operation Manual + Factory inventory + Project Intelligence + Naya design contract + onboarding flow + the operational systems — all parts of each other, not separate things. PI + Smart Factory are separate right now; they need to MERGE — and merging with that, the design contract and the Operation Manual, so they know how to operate the Factory AND how to do smart notes, how to mail, how to operate and build in Naya world. The order: to operate the Factory, a Naya reads the Operation Manual first — that is the first thing she does — then Project Intelligence, then she builds.

The build flow: open any project → fill in your project intelligence → click build → it builds the page with all the intelligence you put in: vision, goal, social links, images, logos, special colors/styles — everything. PI is connected to ALL the pages: "I want to build this page" → enter as much PI as you want → click build. And it is stupid simple — we answer the questions for them: PI has 15 questions by default (like MAXESS) — answer these 15, then we fill in the rest for you. Under each: enter in your own words OR click multiple choice. A standard template where most of it is already filled out — you just edit it; the questions come pre-answered. Nobody gets stuck on a question: defaults, copy-paste examples, multiple choice. A child could get a smart page up and running.

Page by page, total flexibility: go page by page, fill out as much as you can; if you can't fill it all out, it builds with what you gave and you fill in the rest later. You can go all the way through without putting anything in — we don't stop you — you just wouldn't have much. And the input ways are all open: have Naya write your About for you, copy-paste it, type it in, dictate it in — or, if she is connected already, just tell Naya "fill out my mission and goal for this page" and she does it. The whole thing could be automated.

The merge, as ordered: spec first, build after, on his word. The merge spec seat was dispatched the same pass (brief ONE-SYSTEM-MERGE-SPEC-BRIEF-20261109.md, checker 6/7 — check 7's viewport strings honestly N/A for a document spec, stated plainly, never pasted to game a pass). Deliverable: the spec only — filed to GitHub + one smart note live on the feed, proven by a fresh agent answering the five DONE FIRST questions from the spec alone.

Meanwhile Dashboard pass-3 went live with all nine amendments in (SN-2596): nayanet.app/dashboard, 1,727,896B, sha256 2826dea5… — the captain re-curled it himself: 200, size + hash match, DEMO number "12483" gone (0), "Quiet — nothing measured yet" ×1. Branch dashboard/pass3-hero-orbs-smartlinks-20261109, blob 17195e83, commit 3755eba1, read-back verified. No merge — Shawn's hand. All nine amendments in: 9 orbs, 9 distinct jewels, 0 gold, nothing covering any stat · period + PTS/%/MONEY rebuilt as harvested obsidian buttons · Smart Links one summary card with drill-in · board minis are the shrunk pricing speedometer, all dynamic · every board speedometer AND numbers, congruent, text easy, pro level · no gray text · top number and gauge one synced snapshot · DEMO numbers gone · digit colors match the legend. Root causes found, not guessed: the gold orbs were a class collision (the tiling wrapper wore class `os-mini-num orb` and the bare `.orb` rule is a 120px gold sphere); 509 vs 307 was a stale plate (pill clicks refreshed the dial but never recomputed the plate). The chain: verifier FAIL → fix → re-verifier FAIL → fix round 2 → re-verifier 2 PASS, gate OVERALL PASS, H1–H5 all PASS. Still owed: the landed-numbers read (for his seat), a mock-mode digit cut at 1440, two pre-existing phone-width observations in the single drill — and his eye, phone first, is the final gate.

And the creation flow, completed (SN-2597): his words, 21:44Z — one-time onboarding creates your original pages, but to create MORE pages you go to the Smart Factory, click "create new smart app," choose Personal, Business, or Space, and it triggers the onboarding process AGAIN — asks all the questions — and creates that page for you. Individually, not all at once (his correction, mid-sentence): "you can do them individually... like you do your space then you do your personal then you do your business" — one at a time. And the onboarding flow itself gets fixed: when they are doing mission / goal / vision, they are doing ONE for their Personal, ONE for their Space, ONE for their Business — guided, filling out all three. Optional: no business? Choose not to answer. Don't want a Space? Don't have to. Three apps to start: Personal, Business, Space. Leftover slots stay available in the Factory for later. And it all works in the same thing: Smart Factory → create a smart app → what kind? → answer all the questions and input → create another space → that space/profile is connected to your profiles → shows up in your menu, in your profile, in your business, as "in your world." "It's a big circle." Folded into the merge spec the same pass, so it is part of the one system from the start.

Across 3 notes, the thread is: one, system, factory, build.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine all your school books, your toy instructions, your art supplies, and your lunchbox were scattered in five different rooms, and every time you wanted to build something you had to run to all five rooms. Now imagine someone puts them all in ONE room — the workshop — with a big sign on the door that says "read the instruction book first, then tell me what you want to build, then press the big button." And when you want to build another one, you go back to the workshop and do it again — one at a time, so each one gets done properly.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, he saw five things living in five places and said the simplest thing: put them in one place. The manual that teaches you how, the list of all the beautiful parts, the questions that find out what you want, the rules for how it should look, and the way new people join — all of it in the Factory, all of it parts of each other. And when you want another page, you go back to the Factory and make it — one at a time, properly, like you do one room of a house before you start the next.

layers.name: Naya Note

The spec-first order is the discipline: the merge build waits for his word, and the spec is proven by a fresh agent answering the five DONE FIRST questions from the spec alone — the same proof pattern as the manuals. The creation flow's correction is the same law in miniature: one at a time, not all at once — because a batch is where the parts stop being parts of each other and start being a pile. And pass-3 landing with all nine amendments in the same hour is the proof that the pace ruling holds: verifier FAIL → fix → re-verifier FAIL → fix round 2 → re-verifier 2 PASS, with the root causes named (class collision, stale plate) instead of guessed.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. **One system, housed in the Factory:** Operation Manual + Factory inventory + Project Intelligence + Naya design contract + onboarding flow + the operational systems — all parts of each other, not separate things.
2. **The order:** to operate the Factory, a Naya reads the Operation Manual first — that is the first thing she does — then Project Intelligence, then she builds.
3. **The build flow:** open any project → fill in your Project Intelligence → click build → it builds the page with everything you put in: vision, goal, social links, images, logos, special colors/styles. PI is connected to ALL the pages.
4. **Stupid simple, we answer the questions for them:** 15 default questions (MAXESS-style) · pre-answered template · own words or multiple choice · Naya-assisted input · page by page · builds with what you gave · never blocked, even empty.
5. **The creation flow:** one-time onboarding creates your original pages; later, Factory → "create new smart app" → choose Personal, Business, or Space → onboarding again → one page, one at a time. Onboarding asks mission / goal / vision once per world, guided, with skip allowed. Three apps to start; unused slots remain available in the Factory for later. Every created space connects to the citizen's profiles and appears in the menu, profile, business — in the world tab. "It's a big circle."
6. **The merge is spec first, build after, on his word:** the spec seat is dispatched; deliverable is the spec only, filed to GitHub + one smart note live on the feed, proven by a fresh agent from the spec alone. No merge — Shawn's hand.
7. **Dashboard pass-3 is live with all nine amendments:** 9 orbs, 9 distinct jewels, 0 gold · obsidian buttons · Smart Links one summary card · minis are the shrunk pricing speedometer, all dynamic · every board speedometer AND numbers · no gray text · top number and gauge one synced snapshot · DEMO numbers gone · digit colors match the legend. Root causes recorded: gold orbs were a class collision; 509 vs 307 was a stale plate.
8. **Still owed on pass-3:** the landed-numbers read (his seat), the mock-mode digit cut, two phone-width observations — and his eye, phone first, is the final gate.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. Five systems in five places is five places to drift. The manual, the inventory, PI, the design law, and onboarding are one workflow in a Naya's hands — read, fill in, build — and housing them in one system is what keeps them one workflow instead of five errands.
2. Spec first is the only order that keeps a merge from becoming a rebuild: the spec is the agreement about what "one system" means, proven by a stranger reading it alone. Building first and agreeing later is how the system became five systems.
3. One at a time is not slowness — it is the pace ruling applied to creation. A batch of pages is a batch of half-finished worlds; one page, properly built, is a world that works. The circle only closes if each turn of it finishes.
4. Pass-3 landing the same hour the merge was ordered is the proof the machine can hold both: the interface work and the system work, moving together, each verified by a different seat, each with its root causes named instead of guessed.

notes.title: One Flow, Not Separate Systems — and Not In Sync Yet
notes.subtitle:
The group opens with the manual-alone proof and its six gaps (SN-2583): a different Naya, from the manual alone, cloned the Pricing page and built a working viewpoint — chart moved to the top, calculator 2nd, start last, render-tested clean, live at the proof host, byte-identical. And she named six gaps the manual had to close: name the LIVE file (the Pricing row pointed at a rebuild intermediate that 404s — a stale row is worse than no row); teach branch filing step by step; read-back must survive large files (the Contents API returns empty content over ~1MB — verify through the git/blobs API); warn that Pricing's first script is unguarded (excerpting sections kills the whole script at load); name the proof host and its link format; every example needs file+line (an example without file+line is a suggestion, not an instruction). Plus the numbering lesson: re-run next-sn-number.py immediately before filing, and use exactly what the fresh run prints — never trust an earlier print when seats file concurrently. Manual v2 filed with all six gaps closed.

Then the habit (SN-2586): his words, 20:53Z — "every day you almost should be embedding all the most valuable knowledge about the system that we talk about. And then we can, we're documenting our evolution, right?" Every few conversations, a smart note — continuously, not in batches. Every day, the most valuable knowledge goes into the system. The loop measures itself against the habit: a run that finds new teaching and files nothing has failed the habit. And the reports are the evolution record (SN-2587): the Daily Intelligence Reports are NIA intelligence reports — their updates — daily, weekly, monthly, so we can go back on her evolution and see how far we've come. Most people don't document their evolution, their mistakes, and continuously evolve. We do.

Then the honest verdict (SN-2588): Smart Box wiring OVERALL FAIL on §1b — sync reads from the box is NOT DONE as specified. The box is incomplete, and the completeness gate correctly refuses it every run. Root cause: the backfill sourced the STALE local clone (ends 2026-11-04), never the live GitHub tree — 789 of 1,547 state paths named, 758 missing. Everything else passed — organize hook 18/18, bridge zero-loss 9/9, citizen vault end-to-end, key record 19/19, saved-game test independently re-run and passed, attack test 17/17, suites 395 checks green. The fix dispatched the same pass: re-backfill from the LIVE GitHub tree, then a live box-mode sync with the feed byte-identical to the old path's feed.

Then the law (SN-2589): his words, 21:07Z — the nine notes in GitHub need to be in sync with the Smart Box system, "so that Naya learns, Naya grows, Naya understands, Naya retains, and so the system actually works like one thing." The process: understand (identity) → learn → grow → know → evolve. The notes are her organs, her DNA — a direct part of the Smart Box. And the nine, answered then corrected (21:08Z → 21:11Z): the nine Naya Nodes = the nine master contracts in NAYANODE/ — LEARN · KNOW · ACT · LAW · VERIFY · SELF · CONNECT · EVOLVE · PROVE — with the genome index as DNA. And the organs (SN-2590): not containers, not folders — processors. Three triads: ORIENTATION (SELF, LAW, ACT) · COGNITION (KNOW, PROVE, CONNECT) · EVOLUTION (VERIFY, LEARN, EVOLVE). One engine, in that order. A new thought does not grow a new organ — like a human brain, you don't grow a new organ every time you have a thought; the thought becomes a block and runs the flow. The test: "Memory becomes intelligence when it changes what happens next."

The Operation Manual is done — and proven (SN-2591): 43,109B, one manual for all owners/members, written from the real system, never invented. The proof: a fresh agent with ONLY the manual entered a smart note (SN-2585) that landed on the feed — live-verified by the captain. The defect the proof caught: the manual's feed-check looked under the wrong key (cards — the live feed uses notes). Fixed, re-filed, re-verified verbatim. Honest score 9/10 — proven on one operation only.

Then the correction (SN-2592, SN-2593): the Factory completion landed — inventory current, piece index verified, Factory page live with 158 cards, the proof Naya's build live, the Activation Manual filed and held in the Factory's own Smart Box. And his words, 21:31Z: "So what are you showing me the factory proof? Nice clone build and the smart factory for? To prove that you're able to clone successfully? Yeah I think cloning is not a major feature. I've seen this before... you just click a button, you can clone pretty much any template or site. I know that's not a problem." Cloning is not the achievement — it is a button click. The real achievement: the finished pages + the shared language + the inventory — the thing that lets us STOP creating pages. And the publishing law, plain: private = auto live, immediately, no approval. Public = must be approved / verified by the network. Manual verification first; eventually an automated safety scan.

And the honest answer (SN-2594): his words, 21:32Z — "I just want to make sure that the whole system is working in sync. The tracking, the intelligence, the adding or cloning of the pages, that they're all officially done and ready to work." Her answer: "Honest answer: not all of it yet. It's close on the pieces, but the sync between them is exactly what's still being fixed tonight." Working and in sync: pricing live and finished, feed live at 722 notes and syncing, Factory inventory current and page live with 158 cards, Operation Manual done and proven, nine plan links tracking clicks. Not in sync yet: tracking — plan clicks counted but not reaching the Dashboard; the Box — 758 paths missing from the live tree; pages — 18 real, 18 missing, Dashboard not to his eye yet; reports — the database won't accept them without the service key, in his hands; intelligence — the last loop run timed out with its bookkeeping left over.

Across 10 notes, the thread is: flow, one, sync, proof, honest.

Because I think... you think these are all separated parts sometimes, and they're really just part of one flow."
