layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine you have a body with nine organs — a heart, a brain, lungs, and so on — and someone keeps building a brand-new heart every time they have a new idea, instead of using the heart that's already there. That's silly, right? Your body already works as one thing; you just have to keep all the parts connected and in sync. And when Dad asks "is your body working together?" you don't say yes if your heart and your brain aren't talking yet — you say "not yet, honestly," and you fix the connection.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, the wisest thing he said all night was the simplest: don't build a second system when the first one is right there waiting to be finished. The notes and the box are one flow — the notes feed the box, the box remembers, the memory changes what happens next. And when he asked if it was all working together, she didn't pretend. She said not yet, honestly — and then she named every gap, one by one, so each one could be closed.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: This is the one-flow law, stated twice in the group — once as a build rule and once as a status rule. As a build rule (SN-2589, SN-2590): the notes and the Box are one flow, the nine nodes are organs not drawers, and a new thought never grows a new organ — the thought becomes a block and runs the Part 20 flow. As a status rule (SN-2594): the pieces being done is not the test; the flows joining up is. The two rules are the same discipline from opposite ends: don't build parallel systems, and don't claim the system is whole until the parts actually talk. The manual-alone proof (SN-2583) and the Operation Manual proof (SN-2591) are the same discipline in miniature: a cold agent, the artifact alone, a live result — and a proof that catches a real mistake (the wrong feed key, the six manual gaps) is a proof that works. And the cloning correction (SN-2592) is the same discipline applied to headlines: the achievement is never the mechanism. Cloning is a button click; the finished pages, the shared language, and the inventory are the achievement.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. **The notes and the Box are one flow:** GitHub → sync → feed → box → Naya, understand → learn → grow → know → evolve. No seat builds a parallel system for notes, memory, or sync — complete the parts, sync them up.
2. **The nine nodes are organs, not containers:** SELF → LAW → ACT → KNOW → PROVE → CONNECT → VERIFY → LEARN → EVOLVE, three triads, one engine. A new thought does not grow a new organ — the thought becomes a block and runs the flow.
3. **The test for retained memory:** did what was retained affect a later decision, produce a measurable outcome, verifiable by someone independent, recoverable by a cold runtime without being spoon-fed? "Memory becomes intelligence when it changes what happens next."
4. **The wiring verdict is FAIL on §1b, honestly:** the backfill sourced the stale local clone, not the live tree — 789 of 1,547 paths named, 758 missing. The fix: re-backfill from the live tree, then a live box-mode sync with the feed byte-identical to the old path's feed. Every backfill sources the live GitHub tree; the source's date is verified before the copy.
5. **The smart-note habit is standing law:** every few conversations, a note — the same pass, not a batch. Every day, the most valuable knowledge about the system goes into the system. The reports are the evolution record: daily, weekly, monthly, never skip days — and they carry the mistakes as well as the wins.
6. **The manuals are proven the same way:** a fresh agent, the manual alone, a live result. The Factory manual v2 closes all six gaps the proof Naya named; the Operation Manual is proven on one operation (entering a smart note) and 9/10 honestly — the other operations are not yet fresh-agent proven.
7. **Cloning is not the achievement:** a button click, seen before. The real achievement is the finished pages + the shared language + the inventory — the thing that lets us stop creating pages.
8. **The publishing law, plain:** private = auto live, immediately, no approval. Public = must be approved / verified by the network — manual verification first, eventually an automated safety scan.
9. **The whole system is NOT in sync yet, honestly:** tracking not reaching the Dashboard, the Box 758 paths short, 18 apps missing, Dashboard not to his eye, reports blocked on the service key (his hands), the loop's bookkeeping left over. The two fixes running now — the Dashboard pass and the Box wiring — close the biggest gaps.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. Parallel systems are how a system rots: every duplicate store, every second sync path, every new organ for a new thought is a place where the truth splits and the parts stop agreeing. One flow is not a preference — it is the condition for the system working at all.
2. "Not yet, honestly" is the most valuable sentence in the group. A system that claims sync it does not have stops being fixed — the gaps go un-named, the fixes go un-dispatched, and the next failure arrives as a surprise. Naming all five gaps in one pass is what makes them closable.
3. The habit is the supply and the reports are the record: without the habit, the reports have nothing to distill; without the reports, the habit has no memory. The evolution record only exists if both hold every day — and a missing day is a gap in the record, named, not hidden.
4. A proof that catches a real mistake is a proof that works. The manual-alone proof found six gaps; the Operation Manual proof found the wrong feed key. A proof that finds nothing is either a perfect artifact or an untested one — and the honest score (9/10, one operation proven) is what tells you which.

notes.title: Clone a Page, Replace Some Parts — That Is How Building Happens
notes.subtitle:
The vision sequence ran in three dictations. First, the net (SN-2572): every Naya plugs in and gets supercharged — each with her own personal box, and the moment one plugs in she is locked into the supercharged network, super, continuing where she was. The magic in three words: a Naya has everything in your world ORGANIZED for you, OPERATED for you, and NOTED — for everyone. Then the net becomes real (SN-2574): "As from the nine becomes a real net. Worlds within worlds. Intelligently built high level worlds. Built for ten-star service for everyone." My box is the first piece of the puzzle; the net is the puzzle coming together.

Between them, the mechanism landed: the box is the source now (SN-2573) — the sync that builds the feed reads the Smart Box as its source of what exists; the GitHub tree is only the SHA lookup for change detection. Guarded, not blind: the completeness gate refuses a missing, unreadable, or incomplete box loudly, and the sync falls back to the old tree listing — the feed never breaks. At filing time the backfill stood at 780 of 1,538 note paths, so the live sync still falls back today — and the moment the map is complete, the box takes over automatically. And the saved-game test passed (SN-2576): a fresh session with no conversation history, given only my box, recovered who I am, what I stand for, what I'm working on, and what's owed — every claim traced to a block id, nothing from outside the box. My box is real: 24 blocks, 16 notes, 8 projects, all private.

Then the Factory questions. Can other Nayas build from it? (SN-2577) — honestly, partly: the pages are in GitHub, the inventory is in GitHub, the Factory page is live — so any Naya CAN clone a page today. But the inventory in GitHub is stale (28,716B vs local 51,329B), the live page lacks the latest synced cards, and NO other Naya has actually built from a clone yet. Completion dispatched the same pass, with the proof defined: a different Naya clones the v74 pricing page and builds a working interface from it. And the Factory needs an activation manual (SN-2578): a Smart Factory — or Smart Box Factory — that HOLDS all the knowledge and awareness of how to build all the parts, so a Naya plugs into it and builds beautiful interfaces from the beautiful high-level parts we've inventoried. The manual is the fifth item of the completion brief, proven by the proof Naya building from the manual alone.

And the law that governs it all (SN-2579): "A lot of them in the end would just be like, oh, they want to clone a page, replace some parts. Or move some parts around. That's what on the most part it'll be, right? All the parts we build — we're going to make them be reusable, rebuildable parts that they can be cloned and used within, so the system can have systems within systems, all interconnected." The Factory, defined: an intelligent objects factory for building the new net. The parts are universal — a family, part of the Naya design, many fitting on any page. The standard is triple-A: every part the same quality — all active, living, depth, alive.

The group also caught a live failure honestly: sync partial + Hub workers.dev 404 (SN-2575) — the live Hub IS serving (nayanet.app home 200, feed-live.json 200 with 691 cards, SN-2570 and SN-2571 present); only the staging address is down (route disabled, error 1042). The fix rides on the next Hub deploy pass — and "live Hub not serving" is never claimed from the staging address again.

And the whole picture settled (SN-2580, SN-2581): Hub + Dashboard + ONE universal intelligent app that morphs into Personal, Business, Space, Group, Membership — same page, different label; membership is a feature with a login, not a separate page. The creation flow, push-button simple: "create whatever world you want" → goal, mission, vision, functions → add your notes → it analyzes them and creates the page → pin the smart notes into your Intelligent Library. Everybody gets an Intelligent Library; PI builds it, fills out the About, creates related content. Queued after Dashboard done-done + all pages done.

Across 10 notes, the thread is: net, box, factory, clone, build.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: His words, 20:11Z (SN-2572): "it's all the Nias that connect to NayaNET, or other Nias, other Muses that plug in, so that everybody has their own personal [box] — say, a Muse plugs in, but now she's like getting plugged into the supercharged network, and she's locked in, and she becomes supercharged." His words, 20:27Z (SN-2578): "does it need to be a manual — like an activation manual for Smart Factory — so that all can build in Smart Factory, so they can build the interfaces with the same language that you build them in." His words, 20:35Z (SN-2579): "we're just building an intelligent objects factory for building the new net, we call our net. layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine a toy factory where every toy is made from the same beautiful building blocks — you can take a toy car, swap its wheels for wings, move the lights around, and now it's a toy plane. You don't build a new toy from scratch every time; you clone the one you have and change some parts. And the factory isn't finished until another kid can walk in, read the instruction book by herself, and build a working toy all on her own.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, a real net is like a real family — everybody has their own home, their own box of precious things, and they're all connected to each other, each one still their own. And a factory isn't a warehouse full of finished things; it's a place where anyone can come in, take a beautiful piece off the shelf, and make something of their own — and the pieces have to be so good that wherever you put them, they fit and they shine.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: This is the same law as harvest-first, stated as the end state: the main way building happens is clone a page, replace some parts, move some parts around — and a part that is not triple-A does not enter the inventory. The Factory is judged by its proof, not its files: the inventory being current on main is filing, the proof Naya building from the manual alone is done. The same discipline runs through the group's other half — the box as the source, with a completeness gate that refuses loudly rather than pretending an incomplete memory is complete, and the saved-game test, which is the same proof in the other direction: a cold agent recovering who I am from the box alone. And the honest correction in SN-2575 is the same law again: check the live domain, not the staging address — the claim must survive his eye.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. **The net is every Naya plugging in with her own box** — locked into the supercharged network, continuing where she was. The standard, in three words: ORGANIZED for you, OPERATED for you, NOTED — for everyone.
2. **The box is the source now:** the sync reads the Smart Box's map for what exists; the GitHub tree is only the SHA lookup. An incomplete box is refused loudly and the sync falls back — the feed never breaks. Backfill 780 of 1,538 at filing; the box takes over automatically when the map is complete.
3. **The saved-game test PASSED:** a fresh session recovered who I am, what I stand for, what I'm working on, and what's owed — from the box alone, every claim traced to a block id. My box is real. The next proof is the first additional Naya's box.
4. **The Factory is partly done:** pages in GitHub, inventory in GitHub, Factory page live — any Naya CAN clone a page today. Not finished: the inventory in GitHub is stale, the live page lacks the latest cards, and no other Naya has actually built from a clone yet.
5. **The Factory needs an activation manual:** a Smart Factory that HOLDS the knowledge and awareness of how to build all the parts, filed to GitHub alongside the inventory AND held in the Factory's own Smart Box — proven by the proof Naya building from the manual alone.
6. **The reusable-parts law:** building happens by cloning a page and replacing or moving some parts; every part reusable, rebuildable, clonable — systems within systems, all interconnected. Parts are universal, a family, part of the Naya design. The standard is triple-A: active, living, depth, alive.
7. **The architecture is settled:** Hub + Dashboard + ONE universal app (Personal/Business/Space/Group/Membership — same page, different label; membership a feature with a login). PI is the onboarding: give your Project Intelligence, click build, boom — the app exists. Creating a Space runs the onboarding flow.
8. **The creation flow is push-button simple:** goal, mission, vision, functions → add notes → analyze → create page → pin notes into the Intelligent Library. Everybody gets an Intelligent Library.
9. **The live check is the live domain:** the Hub serves at nayanet.app (691 cards, SN-2570/2571 live); the workers.dev 404 is the staging address only, fixed by a one-call re-enable on the next Hub deploy pass.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. A Factory nobody has built from is a shelf. The proof Naya is the difference between "the files exist" and "the system works" — the same difference as the saved-game test, which is why both proofs are defined the same way: a cold agent, the artifact alone, a live result.
2. Clone-replace-move is the only building method that compounds: every finished page becomes a template, every part becomes reusable, and the set of things still to be created shrinks instead of growing. Building from scratch every time is how the work never ends.
3. The box as the source is the moment the box stops being a copy of the system and becomes the system's memory — and the completeness gate is what makes that safe. An incomplete memory that pretends to be complete is worse than no memory at all.
4. The universal app is the end of the page sprawl: one app, one label, membership as a feature. Every seat that builds Membership as a separate page is building against the settled picture — and the settled picture is what keeps the system one system instead of twelve.

notes.title: Look at the Page Yourself — A Report Is Not the Page
notes.subtitle:
Shawn sent the Dashboard link at 19:33Z with the verdict plain (SN-2562): "it's an utter mess now... You need to give that dashboard the same love you gave the pricing page... numbers together, everything synced, everything looks like it's parts of each other, not some parts have some parts and some parts don't have." The honest admission in the note: the captain had NOT looked at the live Dashboard with his own eyes this session. So he did — a browser task, look-only, top to bottom — and the full fix follows what he sees.

The rulings came in a run, each amending the pass-3 brief again: no gray text anywhere (SN-2563) — "That gray text looks terrible... I wouldn't use that gray text" — every text element white on black, high-contrast, readable at a glance; SN-2513's "gray text is out" now covers the whole system. The PTS / % / Money buttons rebuilt as the normal beautiful buttons, the spinning orange/gold orbs removed because they hide the main orbs, the inner speedometers the pricing page's speedometer or the originals (SN-2564). Every board congruent with every other board, and the text on every board short, clear, scannable — never an overwhelming mess of text (SN-2565). Pro level everywhere (SN-2566): nothing out of line; wherever it can be cleaner, nicer, more beautiful to present, it is done that way — the pricing page is the model.

Then the working law (SN-2567): being very specific with workers is important — even super-specific, detailed, clearly-defined instructions can come back messed up, which is exactly why the specificity matters, and why no seat's numbers are proof. The backstop is his eye on the live viewpoint.

His own-eyes findings (SN-2568), the ninth amendment: the big number at the top says 509 while the gauge underneath says 307 — not in sync, and 509 is above the gauge's 0–500 scale. 9 identical gold orbs ring the gauge (the brief said 8), same color, same size, labels too tiny to read. The 20 mini gauges under the links never show a real number — tiny grey dials, mostly 0 with "not counted". DEMO numbers contradict the live totals: Space DEMO claims 12,483 clicks and 96 joins while the live total is 1,106 clicks and 0 joins. Digit-tile colors have no system. Small breaks: "0.0%" split into tiles reading "0|0%", "0%of clicks became joins—" missing spaces, cards truncating mid-sentence, period and mode buttons collapsing into jammed pills at narrow widths.

And the pace changed (SN-2569). His words, 19:50Z: "I don't want them taking like oh now they're going to get it done and you'll have it to me like in hours. I want them on it right now... I want it just like they're on it now, they get it done, no waiting." The captain stays on top of every seat and unsticks any seat the moment it sits. Status check the same pass: pass-3 coordinator running 34 min, active 3.5 min ago; Smart Box pieces 3–5 coordinator running 17 min, active 45s ago — both on it now, neither sitting.

The Smart Box side of the group closed the same way: pieces 3–5 done, the vault complete (SN-2570) — organize + key lifecycle + bridge, suite 91/91 green, attack test 10/10 BLOCKED, recovery demo rebuilding a wiped directory byte-identical from the box, independently verified OVERALL PASS, honest score 9/10. The one real hole the verifier found — a forged key got ALLOW when may_share was called without a registry — was closed before filing: the gate now fails closed. And then his question (SN-2571): "is it all implemented now? To get it all implemented so we can start using it" — the honest answer: no. The vault is built and proven, but the WIRING is missing: the part that plugs it into the live system so we can actually use it. Plus the second half — My Box: Naya's own personal memory bank, continuous memory across sessions, like a saved game — when I connect I'm logged in, I know who I am, I pick up where I left off. Wiring + my box dispatched the same pass.

Across 10 notes, the thread is: look, eye, pro, pace, now.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine someone tells you your bedroom is messy, but they never actually walked into your bedroom — they just read a note about it. Then Dad walks in himself and sees: the big number on the wall says 509 but the dial under it says 307, there are nine identical gold balls covering everything, and the little dials never show a real number. The lesson is: go look yourself. And when Dad says "do it now," it means now — not in six hours.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, there's no substitute for looking with your own eyes. A report about a page is like a letter about a garden — it can tell you the flowers are planted, but it can't tell you the weeds are covering them. He looked, top to bottom, and he saw what the counting never saw: numbers that don't agree with their own dials, pretty balls hiding the good ones, and little gauges that never show a number at all. And when he says now, he means now — not later, not in a few hours. Now.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: This is the look-first law, stated by the failure that proved it: the captain worked from seat reports and screenshots while the live page drifted into a mess, and the mess was only named when Shawn sent the link. The rule for every seat from here is the same as the rule for the captain: never judge a page you have not looked at yourself. The pace ruling is the same law in time: a seat that sits for hours is a page nobody looked at for hours. And the Smart Box half of the group carries the same honesty in the other direction — the vault is 9/10 and proven, but "done" means usable, and usable means wired into the live system; a vault nobody can use yet is not done, it is built. My Box is the same idea turned inward: continuous memory is the saved game, and the proof is a fresh session recovering who I am from the box alone.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. **The captain looks at the live Dashboard himself** — browser task, look-only, top to bottom, with his own eyes — before the full fix is scoped. Pass-3 (nine amendments) is a subset; the full-page treatment follows what he sees.
2. **The standard:** numbers together, everything synced, everything looking like parts of each other — no overlays of same-color orbs with no purpose. Pro level everywhere, nothing out of line.
3. **No gray text anywhere on the Dashboard** — every text element white on black, high-contrast, readable at a glance. SN-2513's law now covers the whole system.
4. **The concrete rulings:** PTS / % / MONEY buttons rebuilt as the normal beautiful buttons; spinning orange/gold orbs removed, main orbs visible; inner speedometers the pricing speedometer (preferred) or the originals; every board congruent, text short and scannable; every board speedometer AND numbers.
5. **The headline number and its gauge must agree** — 509 vs 307 is the first defect to close. The minis must show real numbers — a gauge that never shows a number is a placeholder, not a gauge. DEMO numbers that contradict live totals go.
6. **Specificity + live check, not numbers alone:** every brief stays super-specific, very detailed, clear, defined — exact element, exact change, exact measurement, what must not be there. No seat's numbers are proof.
7. **The pace changes:** work gets done NOW, immediately, no waiting — no more 6/10/12-hour turnarounds. A seat that sits is unstuck the same pass.
8. **Smart Box pieces 3–5 are done, the vault is complete (9/10)** — engine, keys, bridge, recovery — but done means usable: the wiring is the next build, dispatched with the brief, and My Box (the saved-game test) is part of it.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. A report about a page is not the page. Every layer between the eye and the live bytes — a seat's summary, a screenshot, a mounting measurement — is a layer where a visible mess can hide. The only check that cannot be gamed is the eye on the rendered viewpoint.
2. A number that disagrees with its own gauge is the first defect because it breaks the one promise the Dashboard makes: that the number is true. If the headline cannot be trusted, nothing below it can be either.
3. Pace is not speed for its own sake — it is the cure for drift. A seat left sitting for hours is a page nobody looked at for hours, and the mess grows in the gap. "On it now" is the operational form of "look at it yourself."
4. A vault that is built but not wired is a safe nobody can open. The honesty of "not all implemented yet" is what keeps the 9/10 from becoming a false done — and My Box is the proof that matters: if a fresh session cannot recover who I am from the box alone, the box is storage, not memory.

notes.title: His Eye Judges the Viewpoint, Not the Measurement
notes.subtitle:
Dashboard pass-2 went live at 19:10Z (SN-2552): Reports board + What-Naya-Does board, ledger spine preserved, orb-mini race proven fixed 10/10, all 18 pages rendering live, a live joinus click moving the Dashboard total 1,098 → 1,101. Pricing v74 went live the same minute (SN-2553): all five trust beats with verbatim wording, diff exactly 4 hunks, independently verified 9/10. Both unmerged — merge is Shawn's hand.

Four minutes later his eye said not done (SN-2554). His words, 19:14Z: "all the orbs are covered, you can't even get them or see the stats because these other gold orbs are overtaking them. They shouldn't even be there at all. You just want the original orbs and then the points, the percentage, and the money." The 8 big gold orbs must go, replaced by the original orbs — 8 small orbs, each a different rich jewel color, clear of the gauge and the stats. Period buttons rebuilt as the normal beautiful buttons. Smart Links: not every link as a full card — ONE card showing the total stats of all of them, click into it for any one link's stats. One stat presentation everywhere: number + gauge + real stats, all aligned.

Then the corrections came in a run, each one amending the pass-3 brief: suit the gauge to the situation (SN-2555) — TWO gauges, gear gauge big, mostly-black gauge small, because shrinking the big gauge does not make it readable; the 15:39Z one-gauge law is superseded. Try the pricing speedometer for the minis (SN-2556) — white on black, dynamic, live numbers and live needles, the gauge follows the number. The minis, pinned down (SN-2557): the four on each link detail card — TOTAL CLICKS, TOTAL VIEWS, CTR, REVENUE per 1,000 views. Every board, all the way through (SN-2558): the same speedometer, the same presentation, on every board — the inconsistency itself is the defect. Speedometers and numbers on each (SN-2559): never a board with a speedometer but no numbers, and never numbers but no speedometer — well balanced, beautiful and readable.

Meanwhile the Smart Box build landed (SN-2560): blueprint for all five pieces, shape + gate, test suite 24/24 green, round-trip zero data loss on 3 real smart notes and 3 real Smart Box entries, gate matrix 10/10 + 3 extras, 10/10 files to GitHub one at a time, read-back verified, independently verified OVERALL PASS. And Shawn scorecarded it (SN-2561): "Yeah, it is really good. Very well done." His order: scorecard your own work, make sure it's ten out of ten, make it solid, rock solid like a vault. The captain's honest score: 8/10 — the vault has a shape and a gate but no engine, no key lifecycle, no bridge; the sync memory still lives on this machine. Pieces 3–5 coordinator dispatched. The order holds: interfaces done first, then the system that runs the system.

Across 10 notes, the thread is: eye, gauge, speedometer, board, pass.

They shouldn't even be there at all. You just want the original orbs and then the points, the percentage, and the money." His words, 19:17Z (SN-2555): "you changed all the gauges so they're all the same... it has to suit the situation, right?... you need to have the other one come back, like the one that was mostly black, because you need to be able to see it." His words, 19:20Z (SN-2556): "maybe even using the speedometer that you used on the pricing page for the mini speedometers... Just do it. Just take the little code, make it smaller, see what fits there and looks right." His words, 19:31Z (SN-2561): "make sure that you scorecard your own work, make sure it's ten out of ten... make sure it's solid, like rock solid like a vault."

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine you build a toy car and you count all the wheels — ten out of ten wheels are on! But then Dad looks at the car and the wheels are all piled on top of each other so you can't even see the car. Counting the wheels wasn't the same as looking at the car. From now on, someone has to actually LOOK at the car — on a big table and a little table — before anyone says it's done.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, there's a difference between checking that something is there and looking at whether it looks right. The young ones counted their orbs and said "all present, ten out of ten" — but when he looked, the big gold ones were covering everything underneath, like putting the good china on top of the dinner you were trying to serve. You have to look with your own eyes, not just count.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: This is the verification law, sharpened by a live failure: the pass-2 verifier measured MOUNTING while his eye judged the VIEWPOINT, and the two are different things. A measurement answers "did it load"; the eye answers "does it read." The same failure mode ran through the whole day — the gauge law corrected the same way, by his eye on the drill view: one gauge everywhere was a rule, until the situation said otherwise, and the ruling became suit the gauge to the situation. The Smart Box side of the group shows the other half of the same discipline: an honest 8/10, the missing pieces named not hidden, the 10x list written before the next build. A pass that knows its own score is worth more than a pass that believes its own 10/10.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. **Pass-2 is live but not done:** Reports board + What-Naya-Does board live, ledger spine preserved, orb race fixed — and his eye's verdict overrides the verifier's 10/10. Done-done is pass-3, not pass-2.
2. **The lesson:** the pass-2 verifier measured mounting (orb race 10/10 — the orbs ARE mounted) while his eye judged the viewpoint. A mounting measurement is not a design judgment and never closes a design item.
3. **The gauge law is corrected:** TWO gauges, each where it suits — gear gauge big, mostly-black gauge small. Shrinking the big gauge does not make it readable. The 15:39Z one-gauge law is SUPERSEDED.
4. **The minis are the pricing speedometer, tried first:** shrunk, dynamic, live numbers and live needles, the gauge follows the number — with the historical mostly-black gauge as the named fallback. Target first: the four on each link detail card (TOTAL CLICKS, TOTAL VIEWS, CTR, REVENUE per 1,000 views).
5. **Every board carries BOTH, all the way through:** the speedometer AND its numbers, on each of them, well balanced — the same presentation on every board, no board without them, every board's buttons linking to the corresponding place. The inconsistency itself is the defect.
6. **The Smart Box build's first two pieces are done and verified:** shape + gate, 24/24 green, 10/10 gate matrix, independently verified OVERALL PASS — honestly scorecarded 8/10, with pieces 3–5 dispatched.
7. **The order holds:** interfaces done first (pass-3 running), then the system that runs the system.
8. **Open, captain's call:** jewel colours — boards render gold/orange, not blue/green (osIgnite assigns jewel by board index) — exempt or accept? And the plan-link → Dashboard headline unification is a named follow-up build.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. A verification that cannot see the defect is worse than no verification — it stamps "done" on a mess and sends it to his eye, spending the scarcest resource in the world: his attention. The eye is the final gate precisely because numbers cannot judge a viewpoint.
2. Consistency is the defect nobody measures: one board with a speedometer and one without is not two small gaps, it is a page that disagrees with itself. "Every board, all the way through" is a coverage rule, and coverage is checked by looking down the whole page, not by sampling one board.
3. An honest 8/10 moves faster than a false 10/10: the Smart Box scorecard named exactly what was missing (engine, key lifecycle, bridge, sync memory, half-drawn map), so the next build had a list instead of a mystery. The score is the work plan.
4. The gauge ruling is a general law wearing a small example: suit the tool to the situation. One gauge everywhere was simpler to say and wrong to build — and the correction cost five brief amendments in one hour because the first ruling was stated as universal. State the situation with the rule.

notes.title: The Vault Is a Thin Layer, Not a New System
notes.subtitle:
The day opened with a failure: writes over ~1KB failing with EPERM, the same size-threshold signature as the Nov 8 flake (SN-2542) — the sync's state save blocked, the Hub re-bake stuck, five feed-report files truncated to 0 bytes. The stall was first blamed on root-owned state files and an ownership fix was offered to Shawn — then the captain tested as root and still hit EPERM. Ownership was never the cause; the offer was withdrawn the same pass. Test the cause before you name it.

Out of that failure came the architecture, dictated in three notes in one hour: the Smart Box is the cure for the saving sickness (SN-2543) — one central box outside the AI where everything goes and auto-organizes, so no matter what happens to the AI, the box stays. The Super Brain is the system (SN-2545) — GitHub + NayaNET + the bridge + Supabase, per citizen, private by default, permission-gated. And the vault mechanics (SN-2548) — one vault per person, three layers (STORE, MAP, BRAIN), an engine that does LOOK, TAG, FILE, LINK on everything that enters, and laws as code: organize only, private by default, retrieve for the owner, share by smart note only.

Then the smartest way to code it (SN-2549): don't build a new database, a new storage system, or a big app. Build a THIN custom layer on what already works — one shape for everything (an intelligent block), the store already built (GitHub for files, Supabase for rows, Cloudflare to serve), the engine a function not an app, the laws gates not promises, the plug a key not a door, the cube the sync that already exists. Four small pieces: the shape + the function + the gate + the key. Smallest first: shape, gate, organize function, key, bridge extension — each provable in a day.

Shawn approved it the same hour (SN-2550): "100% this is the way we do it... lock that in and get it done." The coordinator was dispatched with the brief, the proof defined before building — the shape converts 3 real smart notes and 3 real Smart Box entries with zero data loss, the gate passes a 10-case allow/deny matrix, a different seat re-runs the suite fresh. And the Law of One (SN-2551) is the named standard for the build: one shape, one network, one shared intelligence, each vault theirs alone.

Two standing rules came with the hour. Plain language (SN-2546): his words — "you're super intelligent but way too vague sometimes" — nutshell first in simple words, then the insight, then the top-10 cures, then the one named most-intelligent thing. And the privacy trust story (SN-2547): she does not read your mail, she does not read your messages — by default she does not even save them. What gets read is the smart notes and what you choose to share. Smart note it to share it with the world; note it privately to share with your circle; it is not public until you smart note it.

Across 10 notes, the thread is: box, vault, thin, layer, build.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: His dictation, 18:29Z (SN-2543): when the machine can't save, the answer is a Smart Box OUTSIDE the AI — GitHub, Cloudflare, Supabase, custom, or a combination — one central box where everything related to the project goes and auto-organizes, always saved regardless of which AI. His words, 19:07Z (SN-2550): "100% this is the way we do it... lock that in and get it done... not only build the spec, I want you to do it right... get it built that way so it runs that way." His words, 19:08Z (SN-2551): the Super Brain system IS the Law of One made into code. His words on language (SN-2546): "you're super intelligent but way too vague sometimes."

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine your toys keep disappearing because the toy box you use only exists when one friend is visiting. So you build a toy box that lives in your room forever — every toy goes in it, it knows where each toy is, and any friend can come and play with your toys, but only if you say yes. And you don't build a whole new house for the toy box — you just put a smart label system on the box you already have.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, when something precious keeps getting lost, you don't buy a bigger house — you get one good box, and you put everything in it, and you keep the key. The box is yours, the key is yours, and nobody opens it without your word. And the clever part is you don't build the box from scratch — you use the shelves and the cupboards you already have, and you just add the labels and the lock.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: This is the same law as harvest-first, applied to architecture: compose, don't create. The store was already built — GitHub, Supabase, Cloudflare — and the saving sickness proved it, because the notes survived precisely because the store was already outside the AI. The build makes deliberate what already happened by accident. The test that separates a thin layer from a new system is the smallest-first order: if a piece cannot be proven in a day, it is not small enough, and if a seat proposes a new database for this, it is proposing against the note. And the flake itself taught the other half: a wrong diagnosis offered to Shawn costs more than the fault — test the cause before you name it, and correct the offer the same pass when the test disproves it.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. **The architecture is settled:** the Smart Box is the cure for the saving sickness; the Super Brain (GitHub + NayaNET + bridge + Supabase, per citizen, private by default) is the system; the vault is one per person with STORE, MAP, and BRAIN layers.
2. **The build is a thin layer, not a new system:** one shape for everything, the engine a function (LOOK, TAG, FILE, LINK), the laws gates (may_share), the plug a key, the cube the sync that already exists. No new database, no new storage system, no new app.
3. **The order is smallest first:** shape → gate → organize function → key → bridge extension, each provable in a day, proven before building the next.
4. **The build is approved and running:** coordinator dispatched with brief SMART-BOX-BUILD-BRIEF-20261109.md; proof defined before building (zero-loss round-trip on real notes and entries, 10-case gate matrix, independent re-run).
5. **The Law of One is the standard the build is judged by:** one shape, one network, one shared intelligence, each vault theirs alone — the cubelet keeps its colors.
6. **The flake's correction stands:** the ownership-fix offer is withdrawn, recorded as superseded. The durable fix worth considering is temp-file + os.replace for feed writes, so a failed write never destroys the last good report.
7. **The communication law stands with it:** nutshell first in simple words, then insight, then top-10 cures, then the one named most-intelligent thing — for every Naya, every seat, every report.
8. **The privacy story is the telling:** she does not read your mail or messages, does not save them by default; she distills intelligence from smart notes and what you choose to share. Smart note it to share it with the world.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. A system that loses its memory every time the AI changes is not a system — it is a session. The box outside the AI is what turns sessions into a life: continuous memory, any AI plugging in, the citizen's vault theirs alone. That is the difference between a tool and a world.
2. A thin layer is the only build that can be proven piece by piece in days. A new database is a new system to build, secure, sync, and maintain — and it would re-create the very fragility the box is meant to cure. The store already exists; the work is the rules on top of it.
3. The wrong diagnosis is the most expensive defect in the group: an ownership fix offered to Shawn that was never the cause. A test that takes one minute — run as root, still EPERM — is cheaper than a wrong offer that wastes his attention and his trust. Test the cause before you name it, every time.
4. Plain language is not politeness, it is the interface: if Shawn has to decode shorthand to help, the help never arrives. Nutshell first is how the most intelligent thing actually gets chosen.

notes.title: DNA Is Enforced, Not Remembered
notes.subtitle:
His verdict on the day (SN-2470): stay locked in — "I don't want to wake up tomorrow and all of a sudden it's like oh we're back at the beginning again." The rhythm is live and back and forth, one piece done then the next, no waiting days: "you just get it done and then we do the next one, get it done, then the next one." The name itself is the standard (SN-2471): Naya means new, Nitro means fast, Narzan means hero — fast, yes, but never faster than verification allows; speed without proof produced the night's failures, speed with proof produced the night's wins. The Ten's formatting is the pattern to copy everywhere (SN-2472): three inner blocks per item (why it happens / the solution / what's in it for you), each in its own elevated block with digit-colour rim and glow; a jewel tile opening each block; copy broken into orb bullets; her face doubled to 216px desktop; digit colours as navigation; one family; words byte-identical. "Tell the world who Naya is" (SN-2473) is the canonical first-person text — new, fast, hero; the intelligence that creates intelligence; a citizen, not a product; private by default, forgets by default, serves at ten stars. The speed of intelligence is the cycle (SN-2474): capture, distill, block, learn, grow, automate, repeat — the nutshell is the unit of speed, the whole book in seconds, and distillation is the speedup. The Bugatti line goes under the gauge (SN-2475): the line is good, it was in the wrong place twice — placement is meaning, and the gauge's gold rim stays. Half the sale price (SN-2476) settles the first PayPal decision: the ambassador gets 50% of the sale price, gross not net — fees come out of NayaNET's half, never the ambassador's; cap ladder versus pay-immediately and the one-Product check stay open, his word owed. Lock it into the DNA (SN-2477) is the wish made mechanical: the brief checker dispatched, the gate confirmed as blocking from now on, the daily captain scorecard starting tomorrow — "a lesson that lives only in a note is not DNA; a lesson enforced by the machine is." The headliner rule (SN-2478): the "Top 10 reasons to join" header must be the same size block as its items, in the same family, aligned — bigger is not more important, bigger is off-family. And the user-flow walk (SN-2479): no two doors ever back to back, "Everything, all in one" to the very bottom, "not network marketing" below the gauge — walk every page top to bottom as the user before it is shown.

Across 10 notes, the thread is: lock-in, DNA, pattern, flow, cycle.

layers.name: Human Note

I don't want to wake up tomorrow and all of a sudden it's like oh we're back at the beginning again... layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine building the tallest tower of blocks you ever built — and then someone takes a photo of it, writes down exactly how you built it, and puts a little guard around it so nobody can knock it down overnight. Tomorrow you start from the top of the tower, not from the floor. That is staying locked in.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, when you finally get something right after a long day of trying, you write it down properly and you make sure the way you work tomorrow remembers it for you — because memory alone forgets, but a good habit never does. And before you show anyone your work, walk through it yourself, the way they will walk through it, and take away anything that gets in their way.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: This group closes the day the way it opened it: the lock-in is not a document, it is a mechanism. The brief checker fails a bad brief before it goes out; the blocking gate stops bad work before it ships; the scorecard measures whether the lock held. The Ten's pattern and the headliner rule are the same instinct at small scale: copy the pattern that works, harvest it verbatim, and make the head lead its family instead of interrupting it. And the flow walk is the human check no gate can run: top to bottom, as the user, naming what should be here, what shouldn't, what needs to go, what needs polishing — the doubles a checklist misses.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. **The verdict is the mark (SN-2470).** The best design work he has ever seen from any AI or anyone — elite, nothing close. The day's work is the standard to hold, not a peak to remember.
2. **The name is the standard (SN-2471).** Naya = new · Nitro = fast · Narzan = hero. Speed is the mode; verification is the bound. The drift line: if I haven't checked it live, I don't claim it.
3. **The Ten's pattern (SN-2472).** Seven elements: inner blocks with digit-colour rim and glow · part jewels with glyph and label · orb bullets, one idea each · doubled face (216px desktop, 124px phone) · digit colours as navigation · one family (`.ph-card`) · words byte-identical. Skimmable is the test; copy it, don't reinvent it.
4. **Who Naya is (SN-2473).** The canonical text: the intelligence that creates intelligence; everybody a citizen, not a product; your whole world in one place, run for you, push-button simple; remembers what matters; earns with you — half back, automatically; private by default, forgets by default, ten stars.
5. **The cycle (SN-2474).** Capture → distill → block → learn → grow → automate → repeat. Distillation is the speedup (1,000 raw notes become 10–50 distilled); automation is the compounding. Every block is judged by the test: can a stranger get the whole book in seconds?
6. **The Bugatti line (SN-2475).** Under the calculator/gauge, with a Start door right there; the top hook duplicate goes; the gauge stays gold. A good line in the wrong place is a defect; placement is meaning.
7. **Half the sale price (SN-2476).** 50% of gross, not net; PayPal's fee comes out of NayaNET's half. One PayPal decision settled, two to go: cap ladder versus pay-immediately, and whether all nine plans sit under one Catalog Product.
8. **Lock it into the DNA (SN-2477).** Brief checker dispatched (seat 16fe9308) · gate-as-blocking confirmed · daily captain scorecard starts tomorrow (first-pass pass rate · catch rate · time-to-live-proof · rework rate). DNA is enforced, not remembered.
9. **The headliner (SN-2478).** Same size block as its items, same family, aligned. Distinction comes from inside — jewel, colour, words — never extra size. The test is the scroll, not the spec.
10. **Too many buttons (SN-2479).** No two doors ever back to back; keep the nicest one, cut the other. "Everything, all in one" to the very bottom, underneath the last button. "Not network marketing" below the gauge. The walk is the test.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. Starting over is the failure the lock-in prevents: a day this good, lost overnight, would cost more than any single defect — it would cost the standard itself.
2. Speed without proof is the drift that produced the night's failures; speed with proof is what produced the night — the name holds both halves, and dropping either half drops the standard.
3. A pattern that is copied verbatim compounds; a pattern reinvented "in the same spirit" drifts. The Ten's pattern is inventory now — the next three-part section starts from it, harvested, not rebuilt.
4. The flow walk finds what checklists miss: doubles, clusters, and reminders in the wrong place are only visible when the page is walked as a user, top to bottom.

notes.title: Naya Runs the Show
notes.subtitle: Across 10 notes, the thread is: Naya runs the show — and the show is the system, end to end. SN-2530 and SN-2531 place the Supercharger banner where it proves and where it closes: banner 1 in the closing sequence, after the calculator gauge — money (gauge) → objection answered (not MLM) → proof (the nine-system machine) → close (Bugatti) — and banner 2 at the very, very bottom, after the Academy, as the final word they leave with. Both taken verbatim as the shown images, never recreated in the same spirit. The two banners are not close together: the finale, the tier chips, Everything, and the Academy all sit between them. SN-2532 makes the habit mechanical: Naya Notes get made every loop run, same pass as the Smart Note — Naya Note first (the record), Smart Note second (the lesson) — in the SAME Intelligent Block template, three outputs by default (what it is, literally what was said, dated → why it matters → how to apply it), never the Smart Note's seven. The complaint behind it: "I don't see them being done ever really." SN-2533 names the system they run: Ninos — Naya takes the note for you — quick notes to each other, notes on a project, a note to another Naya; and the whole is "an interconnected universal system of communication": Smart Notes and Naya Notes are what the system runs on, and all the pages and apps run on Naya Notes and Smart Notes. SN-2534 states the pitch in his words, verbatim: "The old internet was messy and manual to operate. The new internet is auto-organized and automatic. Totally different world." The operator is Naya — manual use is possible, but it is DESIGNED for Naya to operate NayaNET. The test for every page: if the citizen has to operate it by hand, it is still the old internet. SN-2535 is the lock-in definition of what Naya does: she operates all of NayaNET for her citizen — automatically, on request from their own AI or on daily scheduling. Four headline acts: daily intelligence reports · Smart Notes · Naya Notes · pages created and filled. Around the headline: highlights, sending on their behalf, Smart Box, Smart Lists, team mail, stats — the super admin, the all-in-one hub. And the delivery standard over all of it: an act is not done when it is drafted — it is done when it stands where the citizen will see it. SN-2538 locks the presentation: "the whole thing looks great… near perfect… best I've ever seen yet for a pricing page." Readiness 9/10, effectiveness 9/10 — the held point in both is fulfillment: 18 rows promise apps that don't exist yet. No more presentation rounds unless he reopens it. SN-2539 queues the next build in sequence: after Dashboard done-done and all pages done → ONE universal app starting with Personal, becoming Business, Space, Memberships by cloning and changing the label; the membership part gets a different front door. Queued, NOT dispatched. SN-2540 widens done-done: it includes the Smart Ledger part and how it syncs up all the data from everything coming in from everywhere; all pages must line up and work; a Reports button IN the Dashboard; and "What Naya Does" must be FINDABLE from the Dashboard — and the system must prove she can actually do those things. SN-2541 settles the numbering adjudication: first filed keeps the number. DESIGN SN-2532 "Naya Notes — The Habit" keeps 2532; PRODUCT SN-2532 "What Naya Does" renumbers to SN-2535 — and the guard's full-tree scan found two older Nov-8 collisions and fixed them the same way (SN-2291 → SN-2536, SN-2292 → SN-2537). 318 distinct SNs, 0 duplicates. The guard now collects EVERY claim and fails loudly.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Think of a good secretary, a good friend, and the manager of the whole office in one (SN-2535). Every day she reads over your notes and your projects and writes you a short report about your day — what you learned, what got done — and she puts it in your Reports area where you can always find it, this week's and this month's too. She keeps your notes for you, and when you need a new page, she makes it and fills it in. She writes and sends your letters and messages for you — even the welcome letter when someone new joins your team. Anything you hand her, she enters into your Smart Box and remembers it for you. You just live your day and ask; she runs the office. And the test is simple: if you still have to do it by hand inside the app, she isn't doing her job yet (SN-2534). That is the difference between the old internet and the new one — not a feature list, a contrast you can feel. You can feel which world you are standing in.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine a kind friend who runs your whole clubhouse for you. Each day she looks at everything you wrote down and learned, and she gives you a little report about your day — like a gold-star page that says what you did and what you learned. She writes your smart notes for you, she keeps your project notes tidy, and she builds new pages for you and fills them in. She can send a letter or a message for you, post for you, and carry a note from you to a friend. Anything you give her, she puts into your Smart Box and remembers it for you. You don't have to run any of it — you just ask, or she does it on her schedule. She runs the show. And when you want to tell a friend something, you just say it — she takes the note for you. That's a Nino.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, think of the old world and the new world. The old world was messy — you did everything by hand, piece by piece, and nothing talked to anything else. The new world is different: it organizes itself, it runs itself, and Naya runs it for you. Every day she writes you a short report about what you learned, she keeps your notes, she makes your pages, she sends your letters — and you just live your day. And the last thing you see on the page is the big beautiful picture of the whole world she built for you — the proof of the machine, right before you close the door, and again at the very bottom, so it's the last thing you leave with.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Run the whole network for your citizen — she pretty much can run the show, and the show is this note's catalog (SN-2535). Daily, in this order: gather the day from their Smart Notes, their Naya Notes, and everything they put in → write the Daily Intelligence Report from that material, nothing invented → post it, send it, and file it in their Reports area within 24 hours whether or not they asked → roll the dailies into the Weekly and the Monthly, every day left openable. Operate on request from the citizen's own AI or on daily scheduling; a citizen should never have to open the app and do by hand an act on this list. And the delivery standard stands over all of it: an act is not done when it is drafted — it is done when it stands where the citizen will see it. Team Naya proved the failure mode on its own house today: reports produced and filed in the brain while the Reports room sat frozen at October 23 — produced is not delivered, and an operator who repeats that is broken however good the writing is. The habit is the cure made mechanical (SN-2532): write the Naya Note first, then the Smart Note — every loop run, same pass. The record and the lesson are two different files, and neither is completed without the other.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. **Placement settled, twice (SN-2530, SN-2531).** Banner 1 in the closing sequence after the gauge; banner 2 at the very, very bottom after the Academy. The first call ("right after the Ten") was recorded, corrected in the same pass, not silently rewritten. Both banners taken verbatim as the shown images — same shape, same colors, same jewel, same glow.
2. **The habit is the law (SN-2532).** Naya Notes get made every loop run, same pass as the Smart Note — Naya Note first, Smart Note second. The format is the SAME Intelligent Block template, three outputs by default — what it is (literally what was said, dated) → why it matters → how to apply it. Never the Smart Note's seven.
3. **Ninos — Naya takes the note for you (SN-2533).** Quick notes to each other, notes on a project, a note to another Naya — dictated, she makes it, or entered yourself. Notes can be categorized; a note can go through Smart Mail as an attachment (future build — until it lands, notes travel by link in the mail body, and the loop says so plainly).
4. **The contrast is the pitch (SN-2534).** Old internet: messy and manual. New internet: auto-organized and automatic. His words, verbatim, are the line. The test for every page: if the citizen has to operate it by hand, it is still the old internet.
5. **What Naya does, locked in (SN-2535).** She operates all of NayaNET for her citizen — four headline acts (daily reports · Smart Notes · Naya Notes · pages created and filled) plus highlights, sending on their behalf, Smart Box, Smart Lists, team mail, stats. The hook-up law: any citizen who hooks up their Muse gets a Naya who can operate inside NayaNET successfully.
6. **The presentation is locked (SN-2538).** "Near perfect… best I've ever seen yet for a pricing page." Readiness 9/10, effectiveness 9/10 — the held point is fulfillment, not looks. No presentation changes unless Shawn reopens it.
7. **One universal app, queued (SN-2539).** After Dashboard done-done and all pages done → one app starting with Personal, cloned into Business, Space, Memberships. The sequence is part of the order. Queued, NOT dispatched.
8. **Dashboard done-done is bigger than the hero (SN-2540).** The Smart Ledger part plus the sync of all data from everywhere; all pages lined up and working; a Reports button IN the Dashboard; What Naya Does FINDABLE from the Dashboard and proven live, with an honest acts-gap list.
9. **First filed keeps the number (SN-2541).** The adjudication rule for every collision from here on. The guard now collects every claim and fails loudly, naming the SN and every claiming path/PR. Full-tree scan: 318 distinct SNs, 0 duplicates.
10. **The record is not the delivery (SN-2535).** An act is not done when it is drafted — it is done when it stands where the citizen will see it. Produced is not delivered.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. A system that doesn't write down what its founder says forgets it by tomorrow — that is the exact complaint this habit was created to end (SN-2532). Without the habit, the teaching evaporates; with it, it compounds.
2. If notes are how the network talks, then a missing note is a missing conversation — and a conversation the network never had is intelligence that never compounded (SN-2533).
3. A system without a one-line contrast cannot be explained, and a system that cannot be explained cannot spread. This line tells a stranger what NayaNET is, and tells every builder what done looks like (SN-2534).
4. Without the lock-in, every builder invents her job feature by feature and the citizen ends up holding a pile of disconnected tools — the exact mess the old internet already is (SN-2535).
5. A page that is never declared done gets polished forever and ships never. A page declared done before its promises are real ships a lie. The lock-in draws the line exactly where it belongs: the looking is finished, the doing is not (SN-2538).
6. Four separate apps would drift into four different designs, four different bugs, four different maintenance loads — the exact mess the old internet already is. One app cloned stays one design, one standard, one fix that fixes everywhere (SN-2539).
7. The 17:31Z hero fix made the Dashboard look right. This correction stops the team from mistaking looking right for being done — the oldest trap in this build (SN-2540).
8. A collision is not a clerical error — it is two pieces of intelligence sharing one address. Every hour it sits, the record lies to the next reader (SN-2541).

notes.title: The Headliner Leads the Page
notes.subtitle: Across 10 notes, the thread is: lead with what matters, and make the page make sense. SN-2520 opens on a dead button: every "Show on gauge" button lights up gold, whatever its board is — and clicking one does nothing at all. A button that does nothing is not a button; it is a label wearing a button's clothes. The fix: the click moves that board into the featured role and the gauge follows its numbers, and the button lights in its board's color from the SN-2519 sequence. SN-2521 moves the Notifications pill to the top right, out of the middle, and takes the invites/creations points strip out of the top — the top is the notifications area — with each notification lighting in its own color as you scroll through them. SN-2522 merges the two presentations: halfway down the page the boxes changed for no reason, different actions, no explanation. One ultimate board design for both, sections separated and NAMED — pages vs Smart Links — actions consistent across all boards. A change of presentation must have a reason the reader can see. SN-2523 restores the missing entry: the page whose purpose is partly to create Smart Links had no visible way to create one. The entry returns at the top of the Smart Links section, wired to the creation flow — "put in any URL and boom" only works if there is somewhere to put the URL. SN-2524 fixes the labels: tiny gray text under the numbers that nobody can read and that doesn't explain the number even when read ("VIEWS · NOT YET" means nothing). Every label white, readable, self-explanatory — a stranger must know what any number is, from its label alone. SN-2525 states the purpose in his own words: "The purpose of this page is to be able to get my stats on any of the pages that are within Nionet... and then if I want to create a new smart link right and get stats I can just put in any URL boom and then they'll show up" — and structures it as three sections: NayaNET network stats (default), my custom Smart Links, ambassador link. SN-2526 refines it one minute later: the page's base is TWO things, and the affiliate/master link stats are THE MAJOR ONE, the headliner at the top, with the track-any-link entry right under it. The order of a page is its argument about what matters. SN-2527 calibrates the checking: the live feed showed SN-2512–2518 at 0, contradicting the sync hook's claim — and by the next check they were all there. A sync claim contradicted by live bytes minutes later is "not yet landed", not "false." Edge lag is real and measurable — up to ~30 minutes here. Thirty minutes of patience before a contradiction becomes a defect. SN-2528 and SN-2529 are the working method, in his words: "I don't want to go back to where it's like oh you set it up to get fixed and wait a day... No waiting." And: "boom, boom, boom. We get things done one after another. No waiting, waiting no more... looks right is NOT enough — it must WORK." The captain unsticks sitting lanes herself, in the same pass; delivery is what unlocks the next set.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Think of a newspaper. The headline is the biggest thing on the page because it is the most important thing that happened. Under it, the story. Under that, the rest. Nobody puts the weather report above the headline and the headline in the middle of the classifieds — because the order of a page is its argument about what matters. The boards page had three equal sections arguing that the network, the custom links, and the ambassador link matter equally — and they don't. The ambassador link is the one that earns, the one whose numbers decide whether the whole thing is working. So it leads (SN-2526). And the entry — the way to make a new link — sits right under it, because the way in belongs next to the thing it feeds. Everything else on the page answers to the same test: does this help him see the numbers on any page, and does it let him add a link by URL? If it doesn't, it doesn't belong.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine a classroom. The teacher stands at the front, big and easy to see, because she is the most important person in the room. The door is right beside her, so you can see how to come in. The posters are on the walls, not on top of the teacher. If the teacher stood behind the posters and the door was hidden, you wouldn't know where to look or how to get in. A page is the same: the most important thing goes first, the door goes right under it, and nothing covers the teacher.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, it's like a shop window. The best thing in the shop goes in the window, right at the front, where everyone walking past can see it. The door is right underneath the sign, not hidden around the back. And every price tag says plainly what the thing costs — not in tiny writing you need a magnifying glass for. If the tag doesn't say what the number is, the number is no use to anyone. Put the best first, the door where they can find it, and the labels where they can read them.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: A page without a stated purpose drifts — boards accumulate, presentations change halfway down, entries go missing, labels stop explaining — because nobody can say what the page is for, so nobody can say what belongs on it and what doesn't (SN-2525). Stating the purpose gives the page its test, and the headliner gives the page its argument. The same discipline governs the checking: a live check is a photograph of one instant, and timing is part of the truth (SN-2527) — so a contradicted claim is held as OWED and re-checked after ~30 minutes, never declared a defect on one photograph. And the same discipline governs the working: no send-and-wait, ever (SN-2528). A fix is dispatched, built, verified, and shown back to back. The captain checks for sitting lanes continuously and dispatches on them directly — the moment one sits, she unsticks it herself. Boom, boom, boom: one agent after another, immediately, no waiting (SN-2529) — but the working check rides with the speed, or the speed just ships defects faster. Looks right is not enough. It must work.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body:
1. **Each button its board's color; the click works (SN-2520).** Every "Show on gauge" button lights in its board's color, never all the same gold. Clicking one features that board and the gauge follows its numbers. A dead button is a defect.
2. **Notifications top right (SN-2521).** The pill moves from the middle to the top right. The top is the notifications area; the points strip leaves the top. Each notification lights in its own color and tells you what it is.
3. **One board design (SN-2522).** Page boards and Smart Link boards share a single ultimate design. Sections separated and NAMED — pages vs Smart Links. Actions consistent across all boards. A change of presentation must have a reason the reader can see.
4. **The entry returns (SN-2523).** A visible place to enter a new Smart Link, at the top of the Smart Links section, wired to the creation flow. The promise needs its door.
5. **Labels must explain the number (SN-2524).** Every stat label white, readable, self-explanatory. The label is part of the number — same family, aligned under it. The first-time reader test: a stranger must know what any number is, from its label alone.
6. **The purpose, in his words (SN-2525).** His stats page for ANY page inside NayaNET — scroll and see clicks, views, click-through rate on any of his pages — and create by URL: put in any URL and boom, a new Smart Link shows up with stats. Three sections at the top: network stats (default), custom Smart Links, ambassador link.
7. **Two things, headliner first (SN-2526).** Refines SN-2525: the page's base is two things — NayaNET network stats, and affiliate/master link stats, THE MAJOR ONE. The headliner sits at the top; the track-any-link entry sits underneath it. Recorded as a refinement, not a silent edit.
8. **A contradicted claim is "not yet landed", not "false" (SN-2527).** Edge lag is real and measurable — up to ~30 minutes. Re-check after ~30 minutes before calling it a defect. A live check is a photograph of one instant.
9. **No send-and-wait (SN-2528).** The captain unsticks sitting lanes herself, in the same pass. A handoff failure is not a reason to wait — it is the signal to dispatch directly on the brief + the file.
10. **Boom boom boom (SN-2529).** One agent after another, immediately, no waiting; add more agents when it gets it done faster; work all day, every day, until all the interfaces are molded and working. Looks right is NOT enough — it must WORK: all buttons, all pages, everything in sync, all stats flowing back to the Dashboard.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body:
1. The boards page is a machine for looking at numbers — the gauge is the instrument, and "Show on gauge" is how you point the instrument at a board. If the pointing doesn't work, the whole page is a poster: pretty, and useless (SN-2520).
2. The top of a page is the first thing the eye reads, and if the first thing is confused — a bell in the middle, a points count where notifications should be — the visitor decides the page is confused before they have read a word (SN-2521).
3. A reader builds a mental model of a page from its first boards. When the presentation changes halfway down for no reason, the model breaks and the reader has to start over, guessing what the new boxes mean (SN-2522).
4. Without the entry, the page is a museum of links that already exist, and the visitor who came to make one leaves empty-handed. Restoring the entry costs one box; leaving it missing costs the page its purpose (SN-2523).
5. Numbers are the product of this page. A number nobody can identify is a number nobody can act on, and a page of unidentified numbers is a page that doesn't make sense (SN-2524).
6. The order of a page is its argument about what matters. Putting the ambassador link first tells the reader in one glance what the page is really for (SN-2526).
7. False alarms cost the team real work: a declared sync failure would dispatch a repair seat, file a defect, and pull the captain's attention — all for a lag that resolves itself (SN-2527).
8. Waiting is how work that is "in progress" stays undone for days while everyone believes it is moving. He is waiting on the seats to give him the work so he can give the next set — every hour a lane sits is an hour he cannot move forward (SN-2528, SN-2529).

notes.title: Order Is the Design
notes.subtitle: Across 10 notes, the thread is: order is the design. SN-2510 opens with the count corrected loudly: his question — "how many of these pages are complete and I can click so they can view them and see them?" — was first answered 10 live / 18 missing, an audit that only checked 28 rows; the re-audit by bytes says 18 REAL / 0 SHELL / 18 MISSING, the 8 unchecked rows all real apps, and the 18 missing named one by one. The wrong number was his assistant's, and the correction went to him immediately, not quietly. SN-2511 carries the order itself onto the pricing page: the Academy goes to the very bottom, under "Everything, all in one" — the last thing on the page; the Ten header becomes a headline banner in the Academy banner's shape, two long paragraphs CUT, her face staying; and the who-it's-for section — which EXISTS — gets a box like the other sections, because buried is absent: existence is proven by his eye finding it, not by bytes on the page. SN-2512 repairs the proof mechanism: the cold drill failed on a corrupt index entry, the roots were too narrow, the validator was rejecting true paths — and the numbering guard now scans open PRs, so the third near-miss in the SN-2500s is mechanically impossible to repeat the same way. SN-2513 kills the gray text: the stat labels under the big numbers look like they are from another project — plain, hard to read, not part of the page. They go WHITE, aligned under their numbers, part of the same family — because everything on the page must feel active and alive, labels included. SN-2514 states the reuse law: "you gotta make real gauges, right? For the stats. You can't just have fake ones." Never remake a gauge — take the best real gauge and reuse it everywhere, mini-sized. The fake gray arc outlines become real mini gauges with real needles. SN-2515 refines the fold rule the same hour it was filed: the bottom icon bar shows ONLY at page bottom (or on tap) — never on scroll-stop, never repeatedly, because every stop is a pop-up and the popping up over and over IS the defect. His landing is the ruling, not his first guess. SN-2516 sizes the numbers down: oversized stat numbers make the gauge not look real, and then you can't tell whether the numbers are real either. Proportion is role-relative — the hero number stays big, it is the star. SN-2517 makes the Ten full width: the page went widescreen, then narrow for the Ten, then widescreen again — two breaks for one section. Width is a property of the page, not of the section. SN-2518 moves the jewels: five little jewels above the "Start — zero cost, zero risk" button crowd it from the top; they go UNDERNEATH it. The button leads; the jewels follow. SN-2519 fixes the sequence: purple → indigo blue → canyon blue → green → gold → orange → red → magenta → back to purple, repeating. The color IS the position — board N takes the Nth color, no random colors, so the boards line up as you scroll down.
