layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: A busy team is a machine for making two of everything: two notes with one number, two documents both calling themselves *the* standard, two people fixing the same thing, two requests for work already done. Keeping one canon isn't tidiness — it's what makes the record readable by the next person. These notes share a temperament: slow down at the moment of duplication, check what's actually true (bytes, provenance, the board), and resolve the collision in the open — renumbering instead of deleting, folding instead of competing, transferring instead of restarting, and answering a stale request with what changed instead of doing the work twice.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine the class makes two birthday posters for the same party, and both say "THE poster." You don't throw one away or hang both and confuse everyone. You check: are they really the same poster? (Hold them side by side.) If a friend already finished the poster, you don't make a third — you look at theirs and add only what's missing. And if two toys have the same name tag, you change one tag — you never throw a toy away just to fix the tags.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: It's the family Bible problem, dear: three copies, two with the same pages numbered differently, one with grandmother's notes in the margins. You don't burn any of them. You check which is the true record — sometimes it's the copy in the attic, not the one on the shelf — you renumber carefully, you write down what you did and why, and you never, ever pretend two different books are the same book just because their covers match.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: On any duplicate ID: renumber, never delete; clear new numbers across main + open PRs; record skipped repairs as decisions (SN-834). Count integration from substance, not citations; flag duplicates instead of normalizing them (SN-830). Fold filenames to lowercase in the tree check, base included (SN-831). Treat "canonical" as a verdict to earn by recompute; cherry-pick verified orphan work forward (SN-864). Before drafting any convergence, re-read the sources at their current tips; delta-fold or stand down (SN-898). Before any sameness claim, run byte-identity → provenance → structural comparison, in that order (SN-930). On a mid-flight collision: finish, transfer to the assigned owner for verification, forbid parallel builds, post the resolution on the board (SN-933). On any incoming ask: run the completion check before executing; deliver deltas, not duplicates (SN-941).

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body: The eight notes are one conservation law: **the system's memory must contain each thing once, under one name, with its history intact.** Every mechanism here protects a different face of that law — registry (SN-834), counting (SN-830), filenames (SN-831), truth-location (SN-864), documents (SN-898, SN-930), in-flight work (SN-933), and the work queue itself (SN-941). The failures they prevent are also one failure: a second copy quietly becoming a second truth, after which no one can say which record the next decision should trust.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Duplicates don't merely waste storage; they fork reality. Two canonical documents produce two compliant-but-different behaviors; a redone record loses the provenance that made it evidence; a duplicated review doubles receipts and muddies every later scorecard; a normalized-away duplicate ID hides the collision that the next numbering decision needed to know about. For the reader: this is the discipline that keeps a growing shared memory *singular* — the precondition for every other essence in this campaign being findable, citable, and true.

layers.name: How It Connects
layers.body: The no-duplicate-mechanisms law these notes apply is standing doctrine for the whole build (see AGENTS.md conventions); the numbering census discipline has its own custom skill in the maker's wider system. SN-864's provenance-preservation is the branch form of essence-bounded-claims.md's memory law (SN-914: preserve history, recompute qualification). SN-930 pairs with the freshness family (essence-evidence-expires.md): temporal identity there, categorical identity here. The No-Ego Merge — the director's doctrine for resolving duplicate *work products* by cross-scoring — stands alone as SN-920; SN-933 is its collision-time protocol companion, and the doctrine itself is pointed to, not absorbed.

layers.name: What's In It For You
layers.body: You get collision reflexes that save real money in any shared workspace: check before you converge, compare before you call things the same, transfer before you restart, and verify before you redo. Each reflex replaces an expensive default (a competing document, a lost contribution, a doubled work order) with a cheap question asked at the right moment. And when you must repair a duplicate, you get the ethical shape of the repair: change the label, keep the history, write down the decision.

layers.name: The Learning
layers.body: The block's collisions taught that duplication is rarely carelessness — it's *asynchrony*: documents converge while you draft, completions land while the ask is in flight, routings arrive while builders are mid-build. The learning that compounded is therefore temporal, not moral: re-observe at the moment of action (the board, the bytes, the queue), because the collision you prevent is the one that formed in the last six minutes. The second learning is asymmetry-awareness: several rules here exist because one direction of error is cheap and the other destroys something irreplaceable.

notes.title: The Governance Machinery: Fairness, Responsibility, and State
notes.subtitle: Eight notes register one ambitious program from the director's intel stream (directives D26, D28, D29, D30, D50, D52, D53, D54): a fairness verifier that names its failures and never says "all good" (SN-905), an audit that makes every fairness *assumption* earn its place (SN-906), a responsibility boundary that assigns every failure to the component that controlled it (SN-907), a verifiable causal trace that refuses to promote correlation to causation (SN-908), scope-isolated baselines that no aggregate may certify (SN-916), pooling rules that share estimates but never borrow proof (SN-917), one canonically ordered governance state where stale state creates no authority (SN-918), and crash-safe recovery that reconstructs commits instead of inventing them (SN-919). **Status honesty governs this whole essence:** SN-905 is a source lane's build report, recorded as reported and *not* independently verified; SN-906, SN-907, SN-908, SN-918 and SN-919 were NOT STARTED at capture, owner TBD; SN-916's and SN-917's pages state no build status at all. They are distilled as designs and doctrines — CANDIDATE specifications, not running machinery.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: Eight notes register one ambitious program from the director's intel stream (directives D26, D28, D29, D30, D50, D52, D53, D54): a fairness verifier that names its failures and never says "all good" (SN-905), an audit that makes every fairness *assumption* earn its place (SN-906), a responsibility boundary that assigns every failure to the component that controlled it (SN-907), a verifiable causal trace that refuses to promote correlation to causation (SN-908), scope-isolated baselines that no aggregate may certify (SN-916), pooling rules that share estimates but never borrow proof (SN-917), one canonically ordered governance state where stale state creates no authority (SN-918), and crash-safe recovery that reconstructs commits instead of inventing them (SN-919). **Status honesty governs this whole essence:** SN-905 is a source lane's build report, recorded as reported and *not* independently verified; SN-906, SN-907, SN-908, SN-918 and SN-919 were NOT STARTED at capture, owner TBD; SN-916's and SN-917's pages state no build status at all. They are distilled as designs and doctrines — CANDIDATE specifications, not running machinery.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: This is the block's blueprint drawer: designs for a machine that could judge fairly, blame accurately, and remember safely. The fairness designs say a judge must name exactly how something failed and must never hide behind "fine"; the responsibility designs say blame belongs to whoever actually controlled the broken thing, proven by evidence both sides can't rewrite; the state designs say there is one official ledger of what's currently true, changes to it happen in one careful motion, and a crashed worker gets to *reconstruct* what happened — never to invent a convenient version. The honest label on the drawer matters as much as the blueprints: most of this was designed, not yet built.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine a playground with a referee. A good referee doesn't just say "foul!" — she says *which* rule broke. She doesn't let a player blame the wind when he was holding the ball. She keeps one official scorebook; nobody gets points from an old page of it; and if she drops the scorebook in a puddle, she dries it off and reads what it really says — she never makes up a score. These notes are the rulebook for building that referee.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: It's courtroom and county-clerk wisdom, dear, drawn up as engineering. Testimony is labeled testimony; evidence is labeled evidence; and the reason something happened is a third thing, proven its own way. The clerk keeps one ledger, enters changes in order with both signatures, and when the office floods, she reconstructs the records from the surviving copies — she does not invent deeds. And note the honesty stamped on the folder: most of these procedures were *designed* in this period, not yet put into practice. A blueprint is valuable. It is not a building.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Treat every inherited qualification as scoped: read its assumption set and audit record before trusting its verdict (SN-906). Classify failures from the control boundary and both sides' evidence; on conflict, return BOUNDARY_UNDETERMINED (SN-907). Build traces from canonical evidence events only — producer ≠ observer, logical clocks, hashes — and walk claims up the L0–L3 ladder by evidence, running the label-swap test on your own conclusions (SN-908). Carry per-scope breakdowns with every aggregate; refuse rollup-only certification (SN-916). In any design that pools, name which of the three operations it is and hold only that bar (SN-917). Route consequential governance changes through the six-step commit sequence and treat out-of-transaction version checks as no guarantee (SN-918). In recovery, classify the crash before choosing the move, and let COMMIT_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN stay unknown (SN-919). Re-run the lie detector's three broken fixtures before trusting it on new code (SN-905). And in all of it, keep the statuses straight: these are CANDIDATE designs — build them before citing them as machinery.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body: The eight designs share one architecture of honesty: every powerful act — certifying fairness, assigning blame, granting authority, recovering state — is decomposed into evidence-bearing steps with named failure states, so that the powerful act can be *audited* rather than merely trusted. The recurring villains are the silent promotions: correlation into causation, estimates into certification, local correctness into system safety, a crash into either amnesia or invention. The recurring hero is the named, scoped, versioned verdict — a claim that carries its conditions on its face.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: This is the machinery the rest of the system will stand on if it is built: the fairness layer decides whether work is starved, the responsibility layer decides who repairs, the governance state decides what is currently true. Getting these designs right matters precisely because their failure modes are invisible from inside — a rigged assumption, a misattributed failure, a stale qualification all *look* like normal operation. For the reader, even unbuilt, the designs are a checklist of questions for any platform that schedules, judges, or remembers on your behalf — and the essence's status discipline is the model for how to hold designs honestly: valuable, citable, and never dressed as deployments.

layers.name: How It Connects
layers.body: The D32–D35 claim-lifecycle directives are this program's sibling set, distilled in essence-bounded-claims.md (SN-912, SN-914, SN-922, with D33 pointed to Batch 1). The proof standards these designs must satisfy are essence-proof-that-proves.md's; the atomic-commit sequence (SN-918) is the governance form of the atomic-landing rule in essence-regen-discipline.md (SN-887). The keys doctrine — math and logic hold proof; no human mints it — stands alone as SN-903, and the freshness doctrine as SN-904; both pointed to, not absorbed. The Living Ledger vision these designs serve (every action carries its evidence) is SN-915, covered by Batch 1's SN-2074.

layers.name: What's In It For You
layers.body: You get the design questions that expose rigged systems anywhere: What assumptions does this fairness claim rest on, and who audited *them*? When it fails, who is blamed — the controller, or the loudest narrator? Is there one current ledger of truth, or several local ones that can disagree? And after a crash, does the system reconstruct — or does it improvise? Ask those of any scheduler, platform, or process you depend on. If you build such systems, you also get eight field-ready designs with their sharpest cases and falsifiers already named.

layers.name: The Learning
layers.body: The learning inside the designs is sharp — the assumption that hides the starvation trace, the label that accuses the wrong component, the replayed event that resurrects a withdrawn qualification. But the block's meta-learning is about the designs' own status: an intel stream can register a directive faster than any lane can build it, and the corpus fills with D-numbers whose existence feels like progress. These notes, read honestly, teach the difference between a *registered design* and a *running system* — and the essence preserves that difference on every line, because a distillation that upgraded designs into deployments would commit the exact offense the designs exist to prevent.

notes.title: Breaches Are Published, Then Dispositioned
notes.subtitle: When governance breaks in this block, the response follows a liturgy: publish the breach factually and immediately, touch nothing that isn't yours, let the owning lane answer, and let a retroactive independent review disposition the incident — with the defects kept open, named, and owned until they are fixed forward. A gate's own installing merge skipped its declared bar (SN-924); a freeze caught two breaches in its first hours only because its watch was already running (SN-926); a landed gate-crossing got a flag, not a unilateral fix (SN-897); a board claim of "APPROVED on the exact merged head" proved false against the reviews API on both axes (SN-937); and the one time the team repaired damage itself, the honest move was a clean revert, not a clever forward-patch (SN-882).

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: When governance breaks in this block, the response follows a liturgy: publish the breach factually and immediately, touch nothing that isn't yours, let the owning lane answer, and let a retroactive independent review disposition the incident — with the defects kept open, named, and owned until they are fixed forward. A gate's own installing merge skipped its declared bar (SN-924); a freeze caught two breaches in its first hours only because its watch was already running (SN-926); a landed gate-crossing got a flag, not a unilateral fix (SN-897); a board claim of "APPROVED on the exact merged head" proved false against the reviews API on both axes (SN-937); and the one time the team repaired damage itself, the honest move was a clean revert, not a clever forward-patch (SN-882).

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: This is how the system handles its own rule-breaking: out loud, in order, without revenge. Someone notices, someone publishes exactly what happened — no adjectives, no accusations — and then nobody touches the evidence. The person whose work it was explains; an independent reviewer judges the thing on its merits; the verdict says precisely what it closes and what it leaves open; and the flaws stay on the list, with names and owners, until they're fixed. It is slower than quietly patching things, and it is why the record can be trusted afterward.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: When someone breaks a rule in the game, we don't secretly fix it or shout. We say, out loud, "this is what happened," and we write it down. Then the person who did it gets to explain, a fair checker looks at whether the thing itself is good or bad, and the broken parts stay on the fix-it list until they're really fixed. And if *we* built something wrong, we take it back out cleanly instead of piling more glue on it.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: It's due process, dear, the way a good town runs its affairs. The notice goes on the board the same day. Nobody tampers with the evidence while feelings are hot. The council — not the neighbor who noticed — decides whether the fence stays or comes down. And a pardon for the incident is never confused with the repairs still owed on the fence. Paperwork, patience, and no quiet favors: that's what makes it justice instead of gossip.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: On discovering a landed gate-crossing: post the factual flag (PR, files, clicks or their absence), make no accusation, and take no unilateral action — ratify-or-restore is not your call (SN-897). On declaring any freeze or hold: start its watch in the same tick, define violation exactly (0 reviews, no scorecard, outside exception class), publish breaches the same tick, and register the failure mode (SN-926). Before merging a gate-introducing PR, enumerate its *own* declared requirements and verify each on record against the exact head SHA (SN-924). Classify every workflow/CI change as gate machinery and apply the highest bar regardless of diff size (SN-931). Verify every approval claim via the reviews API — state APPROVED, head SHA == merged SHA (SN-937). Run retroactive reviews in the two-output format — disposition with named scope + defect list with owners — and route repairs to the builder's lane (SN-932). Heal ratchet violations by revert; never forward-patch around them (SN-882).

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body: Seven notes describe one incident lifecycle, end to end: the watch sees it (SN-926's machinery), the flag publishes it without corrupting it (SN-897), the tier system prices it (SN-931), the review-object check keeps its claims honest (SN-937), the retroactive review dispositions it without laundering its defects (SN-932), and where repair is owed, the revert restores the prior state cleanly (SN-882). SN-924 is the lifecycle applied at birth: a gate's first act is to be governed by itself. The through-line: in this system, *how* a breach is handled is itself evidence — of whether the governance is real.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Breaches are inevitable; what a system does in the hour after one decides whether its rules are real. The alternatives all appear in this block as roads not taken: the quiet patch (destroys evidence), the unilateral revert (starts a merge war), the forgiving summary (teaches every lane that rules are opt-in — SN-924's warning that a self-violated gate propagates faster than the rule). For the reader: this is a complete, field-tested incident protocol for any team whose work lands in shared space, and its most portable piece is the smallest — a factual flag, no accusation, hands off.

layers.name: How It Connects
layers.body: The watch that makes SN-926 work is the Vigilance Law's machinery — that law stands alone as SN-923 (ratified, per its page) and is pointed to, not absorbed; the doctrine that only machinery changes behavior stands alone as SN-925. The merge-time preconditions whose violation these notes disposition are in essence-merge-discipline.md; the stale-head axis of SN-937 is the freshness law of essence-evidence-expires.md applied to reviews. SN-882's incident is the repair half of the direct-push window whose precondition half is SN-883 (essence-evidence-expires.md) and whose correction half is SN-881 (essence-bounded-claims.md).

layers.name: What's In It For You
layers.body: You get a breach protocol that protects both the system and the people in it: publish facts fast, freeze your hands, separate the verdict on the incident from the list of defects, and let authority — not outrage — decide restoration. You also get F1–F5, a five-point audit you can run on any approval gate today: passable by its governed, exact status codes, SHA-bound approvals, all evidence paths wired, evidence reads paginated. Most real gates fail at least one; now you know which questions find it.

layers.name: The Learning
layers.body: The block's governance learning is that enforcement is a *sequence*, not a sentiment — and each step exists because skipping it was tried: the ask without a window (SN-924), the freeze nearly without a watch (SN-926), the approval claim nobody checked against the API (SN-937), the rename that moved a violation instead of healing it (SN-882). What compounded is the discovery that publishing breaches *strengthened* the rules: the freeze's first catches were its first proof, and a gate that survived its own retroactive review — defects and all, on the record — came out more trusted than a gate that had never been tested.

notes.title: Bounded Claims: Never More Certain Than the Evidence
notes.subtitle: Claims decay as they travel — summaries compress their boundaries away, caches outlive their evidence, corrections inherit the carelessness of what they correct. This block's counter-discipline is a family of four registered directives (D32–D35) and the working rules around them: uncertainty travels only along true evidence dependencies, never amplifying (SN-912); when evidence is revoked, recompute dependents and keep what still stands (the correction law, carried by Batch 1 and pointed to below); history is preserved while qualification is recomputed and stale authority invalidated at use time (SN-914); and no cached qualification may be republished until its evidence dependencies are re-validated at that moment (SN-922). Around the directives sit the two working habits that make them real: correct the derived report, never the raw capture — and name what you cannot measure (SN-893); and verify the temporal evidence before publishing a correction, because a correction is a claim too (SN-881) — plus the writing law that every summary carries its non-claims (SN-928).

layers.body: Claims decay as they travel — summaries compress their boundaries away, caches outlive their evidence, corrections inherit the carelessness of what they correct. This block's counter-discipline is a family of four registered directives (D32–D35) and the working rules around them: uncertainty travels only along true evidence dependencies, never amplifying (SN-912); when evidence is revoked, recompute dependents and keep what still stands (the correction law, carried by Batch 1 and pointed to below); history is preserved while qualification is recomputed and stale authority invalidated at use time (SN-914); and no cached qualification may be republished until its evidence dependencies are re-validated at that moment (SN-922). layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: This is the system's etiquette for secondhand truth. Most of what anyone "knows" arrived through a chain — a measurement became a report, a report became a summary, a summary became a decision. Each link in that chain is a place where the claim can quietly grow: a little surer, a little broader, a little more causal than the evidence ever was. These notes install the opposite pressure at every link: claims may only shrink to fit their evidence, history may not be edited to make the chain look cleaner, and anything republished must be re-earned at the moment it's spoken again.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: It's the telephone game, played honestly. When you pass a message along, you may not make it *more sure* than when you heard it. If you heard "I think I saw a cat," you can't pass on "there IS a cat!" If part of the message turns out wrong, you fix just that part — you don't throw away the whole message, and you don't scribble over the original note; you write the correction next to it, with the date. And when you retell anything, you also say what you are *not* saying.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: It's good bookkeeping and good manners, dear. The ledger's original entries are never erased — corrections go in the margin, dated and initialed, so anyone can see what was believed and when it changed. A certificate framed on the wall doesn't stay valid because it was valid once; you check it when you *use* it. And an honest shopkeeper writes "we don't carry that" on the sign instead of pretending the shelf is full. Precision about what you *don't* know is not weakness; it's the whole of trustworthiness.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: For every downstream claim, enumerate its evidence dependencies and bound certainty/scope/causality to them; propagate hedges verbatim into summaries and receipts (SN-912). Audit your fill paths: any `eligible_*` field must filter for current eligibility + independence at fill time; keep retired rows preserved and barred (SN-914). Before publishing or reusing any qualification, re-validate its dependencies at that moment; treat the missing atomic boundary as an open gap, not a footnote (SN-922). On revocation, recompute — don't patch — and preserve what stands (SN-913 via SN-2068). Never edit raw captures; correct derived outputs with dated notes; write the honest-gaps section before inventing any proxy (SN-893). Read the created_at chain before publishing any correction (SN-881). Ship every summary with its non-claims section and its counting rule, re-anchoring numbers at write time (SN-928).

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body: The four directives are one lifecycle for a claim: D32 governs its *travel* (bounded by its evidence), D33 its *correction* (surgical recomputation), D34 its *storage* (history preserved, authority leased), D35 its *republication* (re-validated at the moment of use). The three working notes are the same lifecycle at human scale — a meter's report, a seat's correction, a summary's fine print. Together they define what this system means by a claim that deserves to travel: one whose confidence never exceeded its evidence at any hop, whose history shows every change, and whose current authority was checked *now*, not inherited from when it was first earned.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Cascades are how small errors become institutional facts: a hedged finding becomes a firm summary becomes a confident plan becomes an irreversible act. Every reader has lived this — the meeting where "possibly" became "definitely" somewhere between the report and the decision. This essence matters because it makes the compression *visible and therefore chargeable*: if a claim grew in transit, there is a specific hop where it happened and a specific rule it broke. For this campaign itself, the stakes are literal — essence claims retire source notes, so an amplified claim here would retire evidence it never carried.

layers.name: How It Connects
layers.body: The correction law's primary home is Batch 1 (SN-913 → SN-2068); this essence is its family, not its replacement. The fairness/governance directives' siblings (D26, D28–D30, D50, D52–D54) are in essence-governance-machinery.md. The freshness doctrine beneath D34/D35 — proof expires when its world changes, never by time — stands alone as SN-904 and is pointed to, not absorbed. SN-881's incident window is dispositioned in essence-breach-discipline.md (SN-882) and preconditioned in essence-evidence-expires.md (SN-883) — one window, three facets, three essences, no double-counting. SN-928's non-claims discipline is applied to this campaign's own receipt.

layers.name: What's In It For You
layers.body: You get the four questions that audit any secondhand claim: What exactly does it depend on? Did it grow on the way to me? Is its authority current, or cached? And what does its teller say it does *not* claim? You also get two habits worth stealing outright: correct the report, never the raw data — and when you cannot measure something, write the gap down instead of inventing a number. Those two habits alone will make every report you ever write more trustworthy than most of what you read.

layers.name: The Learning
layers.body: The block's subtlest lesson is SN-928's: the auditor violated her own law in the act of writing it up — floating counts, a stale PR tally — and the team's response was not embarrassment but instrumentation: a counting rule, a mandatory section, a re-anchoring step. Bounded claims, it turns out, are not a character trait; they are a format. The other compounding lesson is D34's smell test: the most dangerous cache is the one whose field *names* promise a filtering ("eligible_") that the fill path never performs — names, like summaries, are claims.

notes.title: Compounding: Whole Chains, Living Systems, Honest Ceilings
notes.subtitle: Compounding — the system getting smarter from its own work — fails in three characteristic ways in this block, and each note is a guard against one. It fails by *slicing*: a fallback that shrinks the chain's length instead of its width ships a half-build that teaches nothing (SN-826). It fails by *freezing*: a checklist maintained as a document rots, so the checklist must be a machine-maintained system whose JSON twin is the source of truth (SN-827). And it fails by *flattering itself*: a retriever tuned against its own test until the number rises while the corpus still lacks the trigger text that would make retrieval real — where the honest result is a ceiling, 4/43, and the fix belongs upstream at capture (SN-824, SN-873). The method that avoids all three: work whole chains, score and repair the measured holes, verify independently, freeze exact — and reuse what exists instead of building a second anything (SN-854).

The method that avoids all three: work whole chains, score and repair the measured holes, verify independently, freeze exact — and reuse what exists instead of building a second anything (SN-854).

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Getting smarter as a system is not about collecting more — more notes, more branches cleaned, more checklists. It's about *loops that close*: one lesson traveling the whole path from being learned to changing a decision; a checklist that maintains itself instead of rotting in a drawer; a search that can actually find the lesson when it's needed. And it's about honesty inside the loop: when the search plateaus because the material itself is missing something, the compounding move is to fix the material at its source and say plainly "this is our ceiling today" — not to polish the number until it smiles.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Learning is like building a train track. A fallback plan is a *shorter train on the whole track* — not a long train on half a track, because half a track goes nowhere. A checklist is like a garden: if nobody tends it, it fills with weeds, so we build a little robot gardener. And if you're looking for a book in the library and the books don't have labels saying what they're *for*, the answer isn't to guess harder — it's to start labeling new books properly, and to say honestly, "right now I can only find 4 out of 43."

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: It's household wisdom, dear, at system scale. Finish the whole job for one room rather than half-jobs in five. Keep the household book as a living ledger the house itself updates, not a list from last spring. When you've tidied a cupboard, put a system in place so it doesn't refill with junk by Christmas. And when the pantry simply doesn't stock an ingredient, you write it on the shopping list for next time — you don't relabel what's on the shelf and call the meal made.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Design every fallback as a full chain at reduced width (SN-826). Keep operational state in a machine-maintained twin (JSON source, generated .md, cron reconcile, stale flags) — never hand-edit the rendering (SN-827). Run the compounding loop literally: score first, repair only measured holes, verify independently, freeze at exact SHA + proof, reuse canonical engines (SN-854). Diagnose retrieval on held-out cases ranked by trigger conditions; report MATCH/WRONG/COLLISION separately and keep "unassessed" distinct from "failed" (SN-824). At a measured ceiling, fix the capture schema upstream, refuse backfill, and publish the ceiling (SN-873). Attach the anti-regrowth mechanism — claim window + structural fix — to every cleanup before calling it done (SN-890).

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body: The six notes define compounding as a property of *closed loops over honest state*: the chain is whole (SN-826), the state is alive (SN-827), the loop's steps are ordered and its freezes exact (SN-854), and the loop's instruments report their real limits (SN-824, SN-873) so that effort routes to the actual bottleneck — which, in this block, was upstream capture, not downstream tuning. SN-890 generalizes the pattern to housekeeping: even maintenance must close its own loop with a mechanism, or it recurs as someone else's emergency. Intelligence compounds exactly where loops close and numbers stay honest; everywhere else it merely accumulates.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Accumulation disguised as compounding is this system's most expensive failure mode — more notes, more checks, more cleanups, no change in capability. The reader-facing value here is a diagnostic: for any "learning system," ask whether one item has traveled the whole chain lately, whether the state it runs on is self-maintaining, and whether its quality numbers have a stated ceiling with a named upstream cause. If any answer is no, you are looking at storage with good marketing. The 4/43 ceiling, published instead of tuned away, is the essence's emblem: a system that reports its limits exactly is a system whose improvements can be believed.

layers.name: How It Connects
layers.body: The loop's verification step is the machinery of essence-proof-that-proves.md; its freeze-exact discipline is the freshness law of essence-evidence-expires.md applied to artifacts; its no-second-engine rule is the constructive half of SN-942's detection (essence-proof-that-proves.md) and SN-888's guard (essence-gate-must-fail.md). The director's standard that gives the loop its bar — make things to die for — stands alone as SN-829 and the filing discipline for its artifacts as SN-927; both pointed to, not absorbed. SN-824/SN-873's missing-field finding is the retrieval face of the registry-integrity family in essence-regen-discipline.md.

layers.name: What's In It For You
layers.body: You get the compounding audit for any knowledge system, team, or personal practice: pick one item and trace it through the whole chain — where does it stop? Check whether your checklists are documents (rotting) or systems (self-maintaining). Read your quality metric's ceiling and ask whether the limit is the instrument or the material. And the next time you clean anything up, budget the anti-regrowth mechanism as part of the cleanup — it's the difference between doing a job and finishing one.

layers.name: The Learning
layers.body: The block's compounding lesson is that the honest ceiling was worth more than the improvements around it: the two ranking repairs gained two matches, but the *diagnosis* — the corpus lacks trigger text; fix capture; never backfill — redirected the whole program upstream, permanently. The team also learned the slice rule by its inverse: the era's half-builds are precisely the artifacts nothing else could stand on. What compounded, in the end, was not the notes produced but the loops closed — and the willingness to publish "4/43" where a tuned "14/14" was available for the taking.

notes.title: Ratification Lives in the Artifact's Fields
notes.subtitle: Authority in this system is a property of artifacts and explicit words — never of messages, placements, or enthusiasm. A merge commit message claimed RATIFIED while the artifact's own fields said `ratified: false`; the fields were right (SN-840, carried by Batch 1 and pointed to below). A file's internal claim of `status=RATIFIED` is likewise only a claim: a pin requires `ratified_by == 'Shawn Vibert'` plus the DIRECTOR-RATIFIED envelope keys (SN-843). A constitution placed on a PR is CANDIDATE until the ratifier's explicit word — placed ≠ law, and no lane declares hierarchy between competing canons (SN-934). Around those cores sit the working machinery: an exclusion-precedent chain that keeps unratified specs out of the pin manifest by name (SN-884), a precedence rule that lets a dated standing directive supersede a roster (SN-833), and a backfill discipline that records pre-guard ratifications honestly as `kind=backfill`, never dressed as elevations (SN-876).

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: This is the system's law about law. Words like "ratified" are load-bearing — products get pinned, gates get trusted, teams obey — so the system refuses to let those words travel by rumor. A commit message cheering "RATIFIED!" doesn't make it so; the document's own official fields do. A beautiful new constitution uploaded to a branch doesn't govern anyone until the one person with the authority says the word. And when old approvals are entered into the new registry, they're labeled honestly as backfill — history recorded as history, not promoted into something grander.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine a permission slip. It only counts if the right grown-up signed it in the right box — not if someone wrote "SIGNED!" in big letters on the back, and not if the slip is just lying on the teacher's desk. A new rulebook sitting on the desk is just a *suggestion book* until the principal says "this is our rulebook now." And the old rulebook stays in charge until that exact moment.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: It's deed-and-title law, dear. The house isn't yours because the seller said so at dinner; it's yours when the deed is executed with the right signatures in the right places. A draft will in a drawer changes nothing, the old will governs until a new one is properly executed, and nobody's nephew gets to declare which document outranks which. And when the clerk copies old records into a new ledger, she writes "copied from the old book" — she doesn't pretend they were issued yesterday.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Before pinning anything: verify `status == RATIFIED` in the envelope, `ratified_by` by name, and the DIRECTOR-RATIFIED keys — never pin by filename resemblance (SN-884, SN-843). For anything CANDIDATE, write the exclusion-with-reason and cite the precedent chain in the decision record (SN-884). When a claim fails at a new tip, rewrite the exclusion reason to the new facts; verify the real check on exact tip bytes; don't merge your own repair (SN-843). Name every placed law's truth state in the same comment that places it; run the ratified law until ratification supersedes it; execute unverified-authority orders as CANDIDATE with the caveat recorded (SN-934). Resolve authority conflicts by the precedence order, correcting openly with verbatim citation before work hardens (SN-833). Record historical ratifications as backfill with real dates + hashes; keep the audit's no-pass-when-blind exits (SN-876).

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body: Five notes draw the boundary between *claiming* authority and *holding* it, at every surface where the two get confused: commit messages, file contents, branch placements, execution orders, and registry backfills. The common mechanism is to make authority a machine-checkable property of the artifact plus one human's explicit word — everything else is a claim, and claims get the CANDIDATE handling: provisional operation, provenance caveat, no downstream citation as law. This is also where the campaign's own stands-alone rule comes from: an essence may point at an authority instrument, but absorbing it would be exactly the category error these notes exist to prevent.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Authority inflation is the quiet catastrophe of any governed system: one CANDIDATE spec pinned as ratified teaches a calculator wrong law; one placed constitution treated as governing law forks the team's behavior; one backfill dressed as an elevation falsifies the registry's own history. For the reader, the portable lesson is that "who said so, where is it written in the artifact, and what is its exact state" are not bureaucracy — they are the difference between a rule of law and a rule of whoever spoke last, loudest, in a commit message.

layers.name: How It Connects
layers.body: The artifact-fields rule's primary statement (SN-840) is carried by Batch 1 essence SN-2068 and is pointed to from here; SN-843 and SN-884 are its mechanism and its precedent chain. The director's own Tier-0/Tier-1 framing of law — one hard law, everything else living — stands alone as SN-901, and his decision procedure as SN-902; both are pointed to, not absorbed. The Living Ledger vision that gives ratification its purpose (every action carrying evidence) stands as SN-915, covered by Batch 1's SN-2074. The two-canons tension SN-934 holds open was first surfaced by the cold test in essence-proof-that-proves.md (SN-891, PACK-HOLE-03) — the same open constitutional question, named in this block's receipt as awaiting the ratifier.

layers.name: What's In It For You
layers.body: You get the three questions that dissolve most authority disputes in any organization: Is it in the artifact's official fields, or only in someone's message? What is its exact state — placed, candidate, or ratified — and who moved it last? And if two documents claim the crown, who is the *one* person allowed to settle it? Ask those before obeying any "new rule," and you will never again follow a draft as if it were law — or freeze a working rule because a draft exists.

layers.name: The Learning
layers.body: The block's authority learning is that inflation never announces itself: the wrong pin's scorecard was diligent about everything except running the check; the execution order's overclaim came from a seat that *also* wrote the correct boundary in its companion comment. What compounded is the habit of treating authority as data: fields to verify, chains to cite by name, reasons rewritten at each new tip, and a ratification boundary that even urgency does not move. The precedent chain is the emblem — the law compounded precisely because each application *named* the last one.

notes.title: Resource Discipline: Spend the Cheapest Meter First
notes.subtitle: The team runs on scarce meters — GitHub Actions minutes, REST quota, model tokens, and the platform limits of its own coordination board — and this block records the discipline that makes scarcity survivable. A 403 rate limit is a hard stop for the run, not a retry prompt, and the correct shape of a stopped task is a resume file with exact steps (SN-892). Scarcity is managed architecturally: one reader writes the shared state, everyone else cheap-checks against it, git protocol carries repo state at zero REST cost, and every CI run is treated as money (SN-910). Coordination channels are matched to the lifetime of their state — an hourly limit gets a local flag, never a versioned file (SN-896) — and the board itself is a finite resource whose succession is planned before its 2,500-comment cap kills it mid-run (SN-909). Even evidence has a durability budget: verification artifacts live in durable paths, because `/tmp` on this VM can be wiped mid-cycle (SN-936).

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: This is the household-budget chapter. The team learned it has three wallets — CI minutes, API calls, and thinking tokens — and that they empty in different ways: one by the *shape* of spending (bursts trigger the bank's alarm even when the balance is fine), one by volume, one by habit. The rules that follow are frugality with engineering behind it: one person does the shopping trip and writes the list on the fridge; everyone else checks the fridge before driving to the store; when the bank says stop, you stop and write down exactly where you left off; and you don't rent a storage unit to keep a note that expires in an hour. Even the notice board has a lifespan — plan its replacement before it falls down mid-meeting.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine you have a piggy bank with three kinds of coins. Some coins get spent every time you push a button. Some get spent when you ask too many questions too fast — the bank makes you sit down and wait, and wiggling and asking again doesn't help. The smart way: one person checks the bank and writes the answer on the fridge, so everybody can just read the fridge. And if the bank says "wait," you write yourself a note — "I was doing THIS, I still need to do THAT" — and go play outside until it's time.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: It's wartime rationing sense, dear. You don't send five people to queue at the same shop; you send one with a list and the rest read the list at home. When the coupons run out, you stop — you don't bang on the shutters or send your cousin in your coat. You keep your important papers in the strongbox, not on the porch where the wind takes them. And you always, always write down where you stopped, because memory is the first ration to run out.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: On any provider 403/429: stop for the run, write the resume file (attempted / not-yet-done / exact resume steps), and pace future bulk work (batch, cache, narrow bursts) (SN-892). Run the budget architecture literally: be the one reader or read the shared state; treat "nothing changed" as a completed run; stand down with reason + until on 403; record permanent blocks as state; prefer git protocol for repo state (SN-910). Before building any coordination mechanism, ask the lifetime question and the same-job question; decline conditionally when the math doesn't pay (SN-896). Track your board's comment count with headroom; open and hand over the successor before the cap (SN-909). At every run setup, point verification outputs and TMPDIR at durable workspace paths; log evidence losses by failure-mode number (SN-936).

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body: Five notes describe one economy: attention and API are finite, and the system survives by spending the cheapest instrument first and never re-buying information it already owns. The unifying insight is that most waste here was *structural*, not behavioral — per-tick re-reads, duplicated readers, heavyweight channels for featherweight state — so the fixes are architectural (one reader, cheap-check-first, local flags) rather than exhortations to be careful. The struck claim inside SN-910 is part of the essence, not an embarrassment: a budget built on a fictional meter would have rationed the wrong thing, and recording the correction *in* the rule is what keeps the economy honest.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Resource discipline is what makes every other discipline in this campaign affordable. Verification, watching, classifying, distilling — all of it spends from these same meters, and a system that burns its budget on re-reads and retries has nothing left for proof. The freeze-era board death (SN-909) shows the stakes at their plainest: the coordination surface itself is a resource, and losing it mid-run loses the receipts every other process depends on. For the reader: any multi-agent or automation-heavy workflow has these same three wallets and the same burst-shaped alarms; this essence is the budgeting pattern that keeps them solvent.

layers.name: How It Connects
layers.body: The budget law's machinery (single reader + shared-state) is one of the three proven instances cited by the machinery doctrine that stands alone as SN-925 — pointed to, not absorbed. The stand-down discipline interlocks with SN-892's sibling rule inside essence-classify-the-red.md (environment reds are documented, never repaired) and with the vigilance watch's cost design in essence-breach-discipline.md (~2–4 calls on moved ticks, 0 on quiet). The board-succession rule explains why this block's later evidence lives on a successor board at all. SN-936's durability rule is the operational precondition of every verification claim in essence-proof-that-proves.md.

layers.name: What's In It For You
layers.body: You get a budgeting pattern for any automated operation: name your real meters (and strike the fictional ones on the record); route all reads through one reader and a shared snapshot; make "nothing changed" a first-class, successful outcome; treat provider stops as stops, with resume notes instead of retries; match every coordination channel to the lifetime of what it carries; and store anything you'll need to prove later somewhere it cannot be swept. Applied faithfully, it converts scarcity from a recurring emergency into a design constraint you've already answered.

layers.name: The Learning
layers.body: The block's resource learning came in one expensive morning — 5,000 API calls burned, the free token limit exhausted, CI minutes exposed as the binding constraint — and the correction was architectural, not heroic: the same work, re-shaped, cost a fraction. Two subtler lessons compounded with it. First, the pause is a deliverable: the resume file (SN-892) is what makes a hard stop cheap to honor, because restarting costs a read instead of a reconstruction. Second, honesty about the meter itself is part of the discipline — SN-910's struck claim stays in the record because a team that hides its measurement errors will ration by fiction again next quarter.

notes.title: The Front Door: Joining and Being Found
notes.subtitle: Two notes guard the two moments where the network meets a stranger. The first is *joining*: a getting-started funnel designed so anyone can go from "never heard of it" to a connected node in about five minutes, every step a click, a copy, or a conversation, costing nothing or free to try (SN-0800). The second is *being found*: Viral Law — every headline and title is written to hook, scored like everything else the system ships, because the headline is the doorway to the intelligence and nobody discovers what doesn't hook them (SN-0804). A network that cannot be joined fails at the door in; a network whose intelligence cannot be found fails at every door after that.

The first is *joining*: a getting-started funnel designed so anyone can go from "never heard of it" to a connected node in about five minutes, every step a click, a copy, or a conversation, costing nothing or free to try (SN-0800). The second is *being found*: Viral Law — every headline and title is written to hook, scored like everything else the system ships, because the headline is the doorway to the intelligence and nobody discovers what doesn't hook them (SN-0804). A network that cannot be joined fails at the door in; a network whose intelligence cannot be found fails at every door after that.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: A network lives or dies at its edges. These two notes work the edges. One makes arriving easy: five minutes, no expertise, no cost, your privacy intact — because every complicated step at the door is a person who quietly never joins. The other makes *arriving at the ideas* easy: every title is a doorway built for a human's one second of attention, because the finest intelligence ever filed under a number is, to a scrolling stranger, indistinguishable from nothing at all. Respect for the newcomer and respect for the reader are the same respect, engineered twice.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Joining is like being invited to a clubhouse where the door is wide open and a friend walks you in, step by step — you don't need to know how anything works yet. And the signs on the clubhouse doors don't say "Room 47" — they say what's *fun* inside, in words that make you want to peek. A sign that only has a number is a door nobody opens.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: It's hospitality, dear. You don't make a guest fill out forms in triplicate on the doorstep; you welcome them in, show them around kindly, and let them use their nickname until they choose otherwise. And you label the pantry jars with what's actually in them, in words that make a person hungry — not with inventory codes. Nobody ever fell in love with a jar labeled "contents, assorted." The label is part of the meal.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Walk newcomers through the funnel in order, jargon-free, at the asker's level; never skip the fork; keep alias the default in every explanation and example (SN-0800). For every title you write or review: draft the hook from the reader's side of the door, verify it states a truth the artifact contains, score it against the rubric, draft the subheadline by *selecting* the nutshell's sharpest sentence, and confirm the ID renders as metadata only. Treat ID-as-headline and boilerplate-as-subheadline as data defects, repaired at data → pipeline → render, in that order (SN-0804).

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body: The two notes are the network's outer surface stated as law: minimize the cost of entry (steps, money, expertise, identity exposure) and maximize the truthfulness-weighted pull of every surface a stranger meets. They also state the system's theory of discovery in one line — machines file by numbers; humans stop for hooks — which quietly explains why the rest of the campaign exists in the form it does: intelligence that compounds must first be *found*, and being found is an engineering discipline with a rubric, not a hope.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Everything else in this block — the gates, the ledgers, the compounding loops — is value that only matters if people arrive and stay. A funnel that leaks at step 3 wastes all of it; a feed of numbered titles makes all of it invisible. For the reader, the portable lesson generalizes far past this network: audit your own front doors. Count the steps, the cost, and the expertise your joining path demands; then read your own titles as a stranger would, and count how many are labels where a hook belongs. Those two counts are your real growth metrics.

layers.name: How It Connects
layers.body: The funnel activates a node into the world whose inner machinery the rest of the campaign distills — the Living Ledger it joins is SN-915, covered by Batch 1's SN-2074. SN-0804's hook discipline is the discovery surface for the Smart Feed and Smart Share surfaces maintained elsewhere in the campaign, and its "headline is a claim" discipline rhymes with essence-evidence-expires.md (SN-819: a headline is a claim about the world) — there, headlines must be *true about state*; here, they must be *true about content* and built to be stopped for. The declaration a newcomer eventually meets — who a Naya is and how she behaves — stands alone as SN-0801, with the Oath of Honor at SN-0802 and the ratified Protocol at SN-0803; they are the house the front door opens into, pointed to and not absorbed.

layers.name: What's In It For You
layers.body: You get two audits you can run on anything you run: the door-in audit (steps, cost, expertise, identity — drive all four toward zero without lying about any) and the door-out audit (every title a scored hook that tells the truth, every ID demoted to small print). You also get the single most reusable sentence in the block for anyone who publishes anything: nobody discovers what doesn't hook them — and the hook is not decoration on the value; it is the first act of it.

layers.name: The Learning
layers.body: The block's discovery lesson is that the feed taught what the filing system couldn't: identical intelligence, two headlines, one invisible and one quoted back. The learning that compounded is to treat titling as a shipped surface with a spec and a rubric — drafted, scored, and repaired at three layers (data, pipeline, render) like any other defect — rather than as a caption added at the end. Paired with the funnel, the era's product lesson is symmetrical: reduce friction where people enter, increase signal where people browse, and never confuse the system's internal names for things with the words a human needs to want them.

notes.title: The Record Must Not Wear Someone Else's Name
notes.subtitle: Every name, number, and disappearance in the record must trace to its real source, or the record says so plainly. A commit is a signature: commit 7cf4be29 landed wearing the Director's name through a shared clone's repo-level git config, written by a seat who never wrote it (SN-697, SN-701). A ratification quote is provenance only when it resolves to an exact seat, chat, and message: six "Director decisions" were posted quoting words spoken before the Director's first message that day existed (SN-682), and the flag against them was itself seat-relative until a real citation — chat c355ed3a, turn 63934307, seq 29045 — completed the lifecycle and the flag was withdrawn in public (SN-686). A number that cannot be traced does not travel: "17 of 23 flagged" could not be located anywhere, and the seat who had repeated it halted on it in writing (SN-688). A citation is not provenance until the file it names resolves — 18 of 33 Smart Blocks cited a source file that exists nowhere (SN-752). And a failure that vanishes is not a failure healed: when Workers Builds failures went 17→2→0 with zero check-runs on the later tips, the instrument had been removed, not the defect repaired — the RED class stays open (SN-677).

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: A shared record only works if every entry in it is honest about where it came from. This essence is about the four ways a record can quietly lie: it can wear the wrong person's name, it can quote words that were never said in the place claimed, it can repeat a number nobody can find the source of, and it can point at evidence that doesn't exist. Each time, the repair was the same shape: trace it to the real source, and where the source can't be found, write *that* down — plainly, with an owner — instead of letting the claim stand.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine a class notebook where everyone writes what they did. If someone writes your name under their work, that's not a small mistake — now everyone thinks you did it. If someone writes "the teacher said so" but the teacher never said it, that's a lie that grows. The rule is: write only your own name, only quote what was really said and say exactly where, and if you can't find where a number came from, don't pass it on — write "I can't find it" instead.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, it's the old rule of the family Bible and the household ledger: you sign your own name, you quote a person only when you heard them say it, and you never pass along a figure you couldn't show the workings for. If a page points to a letter that isn't in the drawer, you say the letter is missing — you don't pretend the reference is the same as the letter. And when a trouble simply stops appearing, you don't declare it fixed; you note that it stopped, and that you don't know why.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Before you write a name, check whose it is: your identity is configured, fail-closed, and a commit under any other name — above all the Director's — is an authority violation, never a convenience (SN-697, SN-701). Before you cite a ratification, resolve it: seat, chat, message id, verbatim words, and a timestamp that can exist (SN-682); and when you falsify, falsify only the seat you actually checked, and withdraw in public when the receipt defeats you (SN-686). Before you repeat a number upward, hold its three-part citation or halt on it in writing (SN-688). Before you lean on a citation, resolve the file — a string is not provenance (SN-752). And when a failure vanishes or two repairs deadlock, classify honestly: unattributed change, class still open; deadlock, one owner per RED (SN-677, SN-681).

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body: Eight notes are one discipline at four altitudes: the record's *attributions* must be true. The commit signature, the ratification quote, the repeated metric, and the cited source are all the same object — a claim that something came from somewhere — and each note is a case where that claim was checked against reality and either repaired structurally (fail-closed identity, a standing guard), bounded honestly (UNVERIFIED, UNTRACED, PENDING), or completed through its full lifecycle (flag, receipt, narrowing, public withdrawal). A cold reader holding only this essence can still audit any attribution in the system: resolve it, or name the gap with an owner.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Attribution is where authority enters the record. A commit under the Director's name doesn't just mislabel work — it borrows his authority for everything downstream that trusts the signature. A ratification quote that never happened manufactures law. A number repeated upward becomes the basis for decisions its source never supported. And a citation pointing at nothing lets eighteen artifacts claim a pedigree they don't have. Each of these lies compounds silently because later work *trusts the record instead of re-checking it* — which is exactly why the check has to happen at the record, every time.

layers.name: How It Connects
layers.body: This essence is the attribution half of Batch 1's Essence 01 (The Record Must Tell the Truth, SN-2068): that essence carries the record's general truth discipline; this one carries the oct-3 mechanics of *whose name, whose words, whose numbers* — and SN-2068 also carries SN-703's gate-strength doctrine (see this block's gates essence for the part it does not carry). SN-687, the Law Pipeline note that repeats the untraceable "17 flagged" figure, stands alone in this block on its own director-given authority and is deliberately not covered here; the conflict between its figure and SN-688's halt is recorded in this block's receipt. The fabrication-refusals of SN-705, SN-761, and SN-778 are carried by this block's companion essence on claims bounded by evidence.

layers.name: What's In It For You
layers.body: You get a record you can act on without re-auditing every line: names mean the person actually did it, quotes resolve to a real message, numbers carry their source, and gaps are labeled as gaps with owners instead of hiding inside confident prose. Apply it anywhere a shared log, ledger, or history drives decisions: sign fail-closed, cite to the message, halt on untraceable figures, resolve every citation to bytes — and when the evidence isn't there, the honest sentence "this is unverified, and here is whose call it is" is worth more than a clean-looking claim.

layers.name: The Learning
layers.body: The corpus learned that attribution failures are configuration failures before they are character failures: the false signature came from a shared clone's config, so the fix was to make the wrong thing impossible (unset the identity, add the guard) rather than to ask seats to be careful (SN-697, SN-701). It learned that falsification has a scope — a seat-relative check produced a confident UNVERIFIED verdict that a complete citation overturned within the hour, and the public withdrawal is part of the method, not an embarrassment appended to it (SN-682, SN-686). And it learned that the cheapest sentence in the system is the halt: "I won't keep repeating a number I can't trace" costs one line and stops a fiction from becoming a budget (SN-688).

notes.title: A Claim Is Only As Large As Its Evidence
notes.subtitle: No claim in this system may exceed what its evidence actually proves — not a flag in a proof artifact, not a score on a report, not a hash described as "authentic," not a registry entry for work the runtime never ran. A live workflow hardcoded `"independent_verification": True` while its own receipt said False, in the same step (SN-724). A report generator scraped a provisional 7.0 over the reconciled 5.0 until the real score was pinned where extraction can only read (SN-726). An inflated 9.5 was retracted in the same thread where it was published, with the refuting evidence and the corrected 9.0 in the same breath (SN-728). A CANDIDATE spec that needed a green check was *excluded* from the ratified-spec manifest rather than pinned, because a pin is an authority claim (SN-761). And when the obvious repair for missing provenance was to backfill the receipts by hand, it was rejected by name: a green check produced by a fabricated receipt is worse than the red one (SN-778). Above all of it sits the authority order: the Director's direct word outranks ratified law, which outranks any CANDIDATE document — a candidate never overrides his direct instruction, however rich or new (SN-705).

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Every claim carries an invisible size: how much it asserts. This essence is the discipline of keeping that size honest. A checkmark that says "independently verified" when nothing independent happened, a score scraped from a log line and printed as the official number, a database described as tamper-proof when it only catches accidents, a registry entry for work that never ran — each one borrows trust it hasn't earned, and the next person spends that trust as if it were real. The repairs are all the same shape: derive the claim from the evidence, label its scope, pin the true value where approximations can't overwrite it, and when the honest fix is blocked, say so — never manufacture the missing proof.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine your teacher asks, "Did you check your homework with a friend?" and your worksheet stamps YES by itself before anyone looked. That's not checking — that's a stamp pretending. Real checking means a real person really looked, and the stamp only appears after. And if you tell everyone you scored 10 out of 10 but you really scored 9, you don't quietly change the poster later — you stand up in the same place and say, "I was wrong, it's 9," so nobody keeps believing the 10.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, it's the difference between a scale that weighs and a scale that's been painted to always say what you hope. Honest people label things for what they are: this lock stops a curious child, not a burglar; this number is my best reading, not the audited figure. And when the receipt book shows work that was never done, you don't forge the missing receipts to make the book balance — you write "not done, waiting on the person whose job it is," in ink, where everyone can see.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Bound every claim you write to the evidence that proves it, and carry the scope in the claim itself: derived flags with named predicates (SN-724), pinned reconciled values (SN-726), labeled scores and headlines that cannot contradict their own evidence sections (SN-785). When you publish a number the evidence refutes, retract it in the same thread with the refuting line and the corrected value (SN-728); when counter-evidence hits a packet you own, subtract in the same turn (SN-803). Never let a green check bully you into an authority claim the artifact hasn't earned (SN-761); when an audit falsifies your documented law, repair the code up to the law (SN-770) and scope your mechanism claims to the adversary they actually defeat (SN-771). And never, under any pressure to turn a check green, author a receipt the runtime didn't issue (SN-777, SN-778). When a document and the Director's direct word conflict, the word governs — state it, name the reconciliation points, keep moving (SN-705).

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body: Eleven notes are one law at different altitudes: **the size of a claim is set by its evidence, never by the convenience of the claimant.** The workflow flag, the scraped score, the manifest pin, the hash description, and the registry entry are all the same act — asserting a state of the world — and each note catches the assertion outrunning its proof, then installs a structural bound: derivation after the gauntlet, a read-only pin, an exclusion instead of a pin, a threat-model docstring, a closed set of admissible repairs. The authority order (SN-705) is the same law applied to governance: even "what rules us" is a claim, and it is bounded by the evidence of who actually directed what.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Oversized claims are the system's most expensive defect because they are *spent* by other people. A False-turned-True verification flag tells every downstream reader the act was independently checked when it wasn't. A scraped 7.0 becomes planning input. A pin quietly canonizes a spec nobody ratified. A backfilled receipt teaches the whole system that proof is decorative — the single most corrosive lesson a proof-driven system can learn. Each note here exists because someone downstream was about to build on trust the mechanism never earned; bounding claims to evidence is what keeps the trust economy solvent.

layers.name: How It Connects
layers.body: This essence is the claim-bounding half of Batch 1's Essence 02 (Proof Is Behavior, Not a Badge, SN-2069) and Essence 01 (SN-2068): those carry the general proof and record disciplines; this one carries the oct-3 mechanics of *sizing* claims — scope qualifiers, pins, exclusions, retractions, and the fabrication ban. It deliberately does **not** carry SN-789 (The Delivery Gate), which stands alone in this block on the Director's own dictated authority, or SN-695's learning ladder, which also stands alone; both are referenced here only as neighbors. SN-705 is the authority-axis mirror of SN-682's provenance case, carried in this block's attribution essence. SN-726's pinned Learning 5.0 is the same figure SN-785's Usefulness Gate labels authoritative — one value, two mechanisms, no conflict.

layers.name: What's In It For You
layers.body: You can trust the surfaces you read: a flag means the predicate actually ran, a score is either reconciled or labeled a claim, a "tamper-evident" mechanism tells you exactly which tampering it catches, and a red check that can't be honestly fixed says "human-gated, owner named" instead of quietly turning green. Apply it anywhere claims are generated by machines: derive, don't hardcode; pin what humans reconciled; exclude rather than canonize; scope every security word to its adversary; and treat "we cannot honestly produce this proof" as a complete answer, not a problem to fabricate around.

layers.name: The Learning
layers.body: The corpus learned that claim inflation is usually a *plumbing* failure, not a lying failure: a hardcoded literal left after its family was converted (SN-724), an extractor with write access to a slot it should only read (SN-726), a heal-path menu whose first option canonizes (SN-761). So the durable fixes are structural — derivation, read-only pins, fail-safe defaults — not exhortations to be careful. It also learned the retraction craft: a corrected claim must land where the original landed, with its replacement attached, in the same turn the counter-evidence arrives, or the inflated version keeps circulating under the correction (SN-728, SN-803). And it learned the hardest sentence in the system: manufacturing the missing receipt is the one repair that is never admissible, even when the red is real, the intent is good, and the gate is slow (SN-778).

notes.title: A Gate Must Earn Its Green
notes.subtitle: A gate, a judge, or an instrument earns trust only by demonstrating it can fail: the exemplar adjacency gate was admitted as evidence because it FAILS on the pre-repair PDF with 17 adjacent-duplicates and 10 grays — the exact violations the Director named — and passes the fixed render (SN-719). A design judge was calibrated against known references (90, 95, 64) and rolled out report-only, blocking nothing, because blocking authority is earned through verified verdicts, never granted on shipping day (SN-730). A check that crashes yields no verdict at all, which is worse than drift (SN-786); a hash chain verifies only the lines that joined it, so health must count the corrupt lines that never became receipts (SN-772); and a gate that validates a receipt's *form* passes a 30-second forgery, while content-bound validation — sha256(marker) == sha256(exact receipt bytes) — survived 9 of 9 attacks (SN-795). Even a kindness is suspect: a proposed default that removed a refusal was rejected because the refusal was incidentally the only thing blocking NaN scores from passing every floor (SN-800).
