layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: A lock is only trustworthy if you've seen it refuse the wrong key. Every instrument in this essence — gates, judges, hash chains, claim checks — was trusted only after someone tried to break it, fool it, or feed it garbage, and watched what it did. Some passed and earned their place. Some were caught passing forgeries, crashing silently, or checking only the tidy part of the input while the messy part rotted. And one grumpy old error message turned out to be the only thing standing between the system and a nonsense score sailing through — so before you remove anything that says no, find out what it's been saying no *to*.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine a hall monitor who stamps every hall pass without looking. The stamps look official, but anyone can scribble a pass and walk by. A good monitor actually reads the pass, checks the name against the list, and sometimes the pass is a test — the teacher sends a fake one on purpose to see if the monitor catches it. Only monitors who catch the fake ones get trusted with the real hallway. And if a monitor's stamp pad breaks, they say "I can't check anyone right now" out loud — they don't just wave everyone through.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, it's the difference between a scale you trust and a scale you hope. You trust the one you've tested with a known weight, that refuses to pretend when it's broken, and that weighs the whole sack — not just the clean potatoes on top. And mind the old latch on the gate that seems to stick for no reason: sometimes that stubborn latch is the only thing keeping the sheep in. Oil it if you must, but first walk the fence and see what it was holding.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Before you cite a gate, run it against the known-bad artifact and watch it fail (SN-719). Before you let a judge block anything, calibrate it on references whose scores you already know and run it report-only until its verdicts are verified (SN-730, SN-731). Build every check as a total function — unknown inputs get an honest verdict, never a crash (SN-786) — and pair every integrity verdict with a count of what never entered the mechanism (SN-772). Ask the forger's question of every receipt you accept: can this be fabricated from public values in 30 seconds? If yes, it validates form, not substance (SN-795). Treat unsourced numbers as blocked inputs (SN-692) and make your mechanical checks at least as strong as the doctrine they cite (SN-703). Never verify your own build (SN-784), never weaken a gate to reach green, and never delete a refusal until you've probed what it was incidentally blocking (SN-800). And before range math in a borrowed worktree, check for the shallow file (SN-718).

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body: Eleven notes are one law: **an instrument's green is worth exactly the failures it has demonstrably caught.** The adjacency gate, the calibrated calculator, the design gate, and the digest-bound receipt all earned trust the same way — by being attacked, fed known-bad input, or run against references, in public, with numbers. The failures are the same shape inverted: a gate that validated form (SN-795), a check that crashed (SN-786), a chain blind to non-members (SN-772), a claim check weaker than its doctrine (SN-703), a shallow clone answering range questions it had no right to answer (SN-718). And SN-800 is the law's defensive half: even an instrument's *accidents* — a refusal nobody designed as a NaN guard — are load-bearing until proven otherwise.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Every verdict in this system is downstream of an instrument. If the gate passes garbage, the garbage ships with a green story attached; if the judge is uncalibrated, its scores are numerology; if the check crashes, the battery reports a run that verified nothing; if the receipt can be forged, activation becomes theater. The costliest failures here were all quiet: nothing looked broken while the instrument was blind. Proving the instrument — before trusting it, and again whenever it changes — is the only thing standing between "verified" and "we said verified."

layers.name: How It Connects
layers.body: Batch 1's Essence 02 (Proof Is Behavior, Not a Badge, SN-2069) carries the general proof discipline and SN-793's refuse-to-score doctrine; this essence carries the oct-3 mechanics of *instrument quality* — calibration, totality, entry boundaries, forgery resistance, incidental guards. It also completes SN-703: Batch 1's Essence 01 (SN-2068) lists SN-703 in its coverage and carries its one-line lesson, but the claim-check substance (three-layer enumeration, first-claim-stands, the atomic renumber) is carried here, and the partial batch1 carry is recorded in this block's receipt. The refuse-to-score-without-live-state rule (SN-793, covered-by-batch1) is the activation-side sibling of this essence's totality rule; the activation gates themselves are carried in this block's activation essence (SN-787, SN-797, SN-799). SN-692 is the mechanical half of SN-688's halt, carried in this block's attribution essence.

layers.name: What's In It For You
layers.body: You get verdicts you can build on: gates that have been seen failing on the real defect, judges whose scales were proven against known weights before they judged you, health signals that count the rot the chain can't see, and receipts a stranger can't forge from public information. Apply it to any checking machinery anywhere: demand the two-sided run, calibrate before you authorize, make failure loud and total, measure the raw input, bind validation to content, and inventory every refusal's hidden job before you remove it.

layers.name: The Learning
layers.body: The corpus learned that instrument quality is proven adversarially or not at all — every instrument here that mattered was attacked by a different seat than built it, and the two that failed (form-validation at 6/10, the self-verified beauty gate at 6/6 garbage) failed in the direction of generosity: passing what should fail. It learned that graduation is a sequence, not a switch — calibrate, report-only, then block (SN-730) — and that the same sequence governs automation itself (SN-731). And it learned to respect incidental structure: the NaN hole was closed by an accident of an unrelated refusal, which means a system's real defenses are never fully listed in its design — probe before you remove (SN-800).

notes.title: A Trial Proves Only What It Measures
notes.subtitle: A measurement is honest only inside the conditions it was actually run under. Register the prediction *before* the data changes, or retroactive credit is structurally impossible to exclude (SN-693). Pilot the audit target before launch, or a flawless trial can be invalidated by a ceiling nobody checked (SN-720). Recompute the statistics from the raw file — a celebrated p-value and effect size that don't reconcile under one analysis unit are CONFLICTED/UNVERIFIED, however good the behavioral signal looks (SN-698, SN-702). Replay the verification and require it to reproduce the failures as faithfully as the passes, and name which half of the claim the replay actually covers (SN-747). Tag every green with its conditions: a rung proven under stubbed retrieval licenses a mechanism claim, never a production claim — and when trial and production disagree, production wins (SN-788). And when the instrument says nothing at all — silent telemetry, an unscanned claim — treat the silence as a missing measurement, never as a measurement of zero (SN-766, SN-709).

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: An experiment is a promise: "under these conditions, this happened." This essence is about keeping that promise precise. Register what you expect before you touch anything, so you can't quietly move the goalposts. Check the target has room to move before you spend the run. Recompute the numbers yourself instead of trusting the summary — and if the numbers don't agree with each other, say so, keep the useful signal, and refuse the promotion. When you re-run someone else's test, your re-run only counts if it can reproduce their failures too, and you must say exactly which part of the claim you actually re-tested. And remember what your test *didn't* simulate: a shortcut you removed in the lab might be the whole problem in the real world.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine you guess how many jellybeans are in a jar, but you write your guess down and seal it in an envelope *before* anyone counts. That's a real guess. If you peek first and then "guess," it doesn't count. Now imagine your measuring cup has a crack and only holds half — everything you measure with it is still real measuring, but only for that cracked cup; you can't say the recipe works in a real kitchen until you try a real cup. And if the scale just shows nothing at all, that doesn't mean the bag weighs zero — it means the scale didn't answer.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, it's the honesty of the kitchen notebook: write the expected result before you bake, not after you've tasted. If the cake was tested in a tiny tin, don't promise it for the big tin until you've baked it there. If two columns of your ledger don't add to the same total, you don't average them and smile — you find which column is wrong, and you keep the page, crossings-out and all, so the next cook can see what happened. And a blank page in the book means "not yet written," never "nothing happened."

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Register before you mutate (SN-693); pilot before you launch (SN-720). Recompute every statistic you are handed, from the raw file, under one analysis unit, and let unreconciled sets stop promotions while their signals survive (SN-698, SN-702). When you replay a sister's verification, reproduce her failures with the same fidelity as her passes, name the half you covered, and name what's unbanked as unbuilt (SN-747). Tag your greens with their conditions — stubbed, sampled, simulated — and let a single honest production observation outrank a shelf of trial wins, re-scoring downward in the open when it does (SN-788). When telemetry is silent, write the gap, attribute nothing, verify everything reachable, and move no verdict (SN-766); when your prose and a re-runnable scan disagree, the scan wins and you correct in the same thread (SN-709).

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body: Eight notes are one discipline: **a measurement claim is a contract that names its conditions, its unit, and its limits — and expires outside them.** Pre-registration (SN-693) and piloting (SN-720) bound the claim in time: before the data, within headroom. Recomputation (SN-698, SN-702) bounds it arithmetically: one unit, reconciled set. Discriminating replay (SN-747) bounds it socially: another seat, both directions, named coverage. Condition-tagging (SN-788) bounds it environmentally: stubbed proof is mechanism proof. And the silence rules (SN-766, SN-709) bound it negatively: no signal is not a signal. A cold reader holding only this essence can still audit any trial, replay, or metric in the system by asking the five questions these notes install.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Trials and metrics are how this system decides what is true about itself — which lessons bank, which scores move, which promotions happen. Each failure mode here is expensive in a different currency: an unregistered prediction invites retroactive credit that no one can disprove; an unpiloted target burns a flawless run; an unreconciled statistic promotes a Tier-S claim on arithmetic that contradicts itself; a rubber-stamp replay manufactures independent verification; a stubbed green promotes a mechanism into a production promise; a silence read as zero (or as removal) moves verdicts on evidence that doesn't exist. Bounded measurement is the difference between a learning system and a storytelling system.

layers.name: How It Connects
layers.body: This essence is the measurement half of Batch 1's Essence 05 (Intelligence Must Transfer and Compound, SN-2072) — that essence carries the compounding audit and, verified in this block's pass, SN-811's capture-design law and SN-791's proven-links chain; this one carries the oct-3 trial-integrity mechanics that decide whether a lesson's evidence deserves to bank at all. It leans on this block's gates essence for the input-side twin (SN-692: unsourced numbers are blocked inputs) and on the attribution essence for SN-688's halt, which SN-709 applies to claims. SN-695's learning ladder stands alone in this block on its own verbatim-director basis; the rung discipline in SN-788 is written against that ladder but does not restate it.

layers.name: What's In It For You
layers.body: You get numbers that mean what they say: a score that moved only when its stated blockers moved, a p-value you can recompute to the same answer, a replay receipt that tells you exactly what was and wasn't re-proven, and gaps labeled as gaps instead of filled with inference. Apply it to any experiment, audit, or metric you run: register first, pilot the target, recompute from raw, demand two-directional replay, tag your conditions, and never let silence testify.

layers.name: The Learning
layers.body: The corpus learned that integrity mechanisms protect different things and each needs its own: preregistration protects conclusions but not budgets (SN-693, SN-720); recomputation protects promotions but must not erase signals (SN-698); replay protects against rubber stamps only when it is allowed to fail (SN-747). Its sharpest lesson is SN-788's: the stub removed *optionality*, which was precisely the production failure — so a trial's simplifications must be audited against the production failure modes they might be hiding, not just listed. And it learned to score the honest seat: the LEARN seat's own framing of its downgrade (7.5 → 7.0) is the behavior every one of these rules exists to produce.

notes.title: Verification Must Be Able To Say No
notes.subtitle: A verification that cannot fail is a ceremony, and this block's notes are the craft of keeping verification dangerous. A CLOSED verdict at 9.0/10 was overturned by a second re-attacker whose *different* battery found quote-smuggling the first battery never probed — a battery's verdict is only as complete as its threat-class coverage (SN-810). A reported hole of one evasion measured out at five of eight open; the fix closed the class and documented the honest bound it deliberately leaves open (SN-809). A gate's parse model diverged from the browser's twice — an unclosed `<style>` read to EOF, an attribute read by regex instead of spec — and each divergence was a hole by definition (SN-812). A reviewer's suggested fix was measured before adoption: fold-alone 0/32, extension-alone 2/32; the adopted composition closed the class (SN-815). A watch that polled 18 times and saw zero traffic proved nothing and was honestly scored PENDING at 6.0 (SN-816). A cold reader caught the documentation bug the author was blind to (SN-748). A harness's one FAIL was its positive control correctly reporting a genuinely red tip — the instrument telling the truth, not a defect to repair (SN-684). And a dry run is never the control: verification must reach the exact mechanism that refuses (SN-708).

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Verification is a promise that someone actually tried to break the thing — not that someone watched it work once. This essence collects the ways "we checked" can quietly be false: a test suite that never tried the attack that mattered, a checker reading the page differently from how the browser reads it, a dry run that never reaches the lock it's testing, a monitoring watch that stared at an empty room for ninety minutes and called it safety. And the ways it stays true: measure how wide the hole really is before patching, try the fix before believing the fix, invite a stranger to read your instructions cold, and let an honest "unproven" stand where it belongs.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine you hide a toy and ask a friend to find it, but you only ever hide it in the easiest spot. Your friend "always finds it" — but that doesn't prove they're a good finder; it proves your hiding was too easy. A real test hides it in the tricky spots too: under things, inside things, in the places nobody looks. And if your friend watches the garden gate all afternoon but nobody walks through it, they haven't proved the gate works — they've proved the garden was quiet. To test a gate, someone has to actually walk through it.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, it's the difference between tasting the soup and reading the recipe. The recipe can be perfect and the soup still wrong, because the cook's stove runs hotter than yours. Honest checking means tasting under real conditions: use the real spoon, the real fire, the real ingredients — not a rehearsal with make-believe ones. When you find one mouse hole, check the whole skirting board before you plug it. And write down, plainly, the things your fence does *not* keep out — a fence with honest gaps is safer than one whose gaps nobody wrote down.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Build your battery to be able to fail: cover every threat class in the claimed scope, and scope your certificate to what you probed (SN-810). Parse as the platform parses (SN-812). Prove refusals at the refusing path, with real runs (SN-708). Measure holes before fixing them, fix classes not instances, and write the bound (SN-809); measure suggested fixes before adopting them, and record why the alternatives failed (SN-815). Read every fail's cause before you classify it — sometimes the red is the instrument's honesty, and "repairing" it is the corruption (SN-684). Answer challenges cite-to-blob (SN-690). Run cold tests and publish their catches (SN-748). Score zero-traffic watches as PENDING and pair credential changes with a witnessed transaction (SN-816). And when your sealed kit's tripwire fires, detect and hand off — builder and retester together, never yourself alone (SN-805).

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body: Ten notes are one law: **a verification's value is the set of failures it was capable of producing.** The CLOSED-that-wasn't (SN-810), the parse gaps (SN-812), the unmeasured hole (SN-809), the unmeasured fix (SN-815), the empty watch (SN-816), and the unreached control (SN-708) are all the same defect wearing different clothes: the check and the checked never actually met. The positive notes are the meetings arranged properly — a control allowed to fail truthfully (SN-684), a citation loop that settles challenges in minutes (SN-690), a cold reader whose blindness is the instrument (SN-748), a tripwire that detects without rebuilding (SN-805). A cold reader holding only this essence can still audit any "verified" claim in the system: what did the battery probe, what did the checker assume, what traffic did the watch witness, and what is the stated bound?

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Every other discipline in this corpus leans on verification: gates, trials, receipts, scorecards. If verification itself is ceremonial, everything downstream inherits false confidence at exactly the points where confidence matters most — security gates, activation enforcement, published scores. The failures here were never lazy; the first CLOSED battery was competent and diligent within its classes. That's why the lesson is structural: coverage must be *enumerated against the threat space*, parsers must match their platforms, fixes must be measured, and inconclusive must be a first-class verdict — because diligence inside an unexamined scope produces the most convincing falsehoods of all.

layers.name: How It Connects
layers.body: This essence is the adversarial half of Batch 1's Essence 02 (Proof Is Behavior, Not a Badge, SN-2069): that essence carries proof-by-behavior and SN-793's layered refusal doctrine (verified covered-by-batch1 in this block's pass); this one carries the oct-3 attack craft — threat classes, parse fidelity, hole-width measurement, fix measurement, witnessed-traffic watches. It shares SN-708 with the attribution essence's SN-701 (the same identity control, proven two ways) and shares instruments with this block's gates essence — SN-719's falsification admission and SN-795's form-vs-substance battery are the design-time siblings of SN-810's certification rule: a gate must demonstrate failure (SN-719), receipts must bind substance (SN-795), and certificates must scope to probed classes (SN-810). SN-805's tripwire guards the same sealed kits the activation essence (SN-787, SN-799) builds gates around.

layers.name: What's In It For You
layers.body: You get "verified" that deserves the word: batteries whose scope you can read, certificates that name what they never tested, fixes that were measured before they were believed, and PENDINGs that stay pending until a real transaction lands. Apply it to any review, audit, or test regime: enumerate the threat classes first, parse like the platform, reach the refusing mechanism, measure the hole and the fix, demand a witnessed transaction, and treat a zero-finding pass as a question about the test — not a compliment to the work.

layers.name: The Learning
layers.body: The corpus learned that the second attacker is not redundant: independence means an independent *battery*, not an independent runner of the same battery (SN-810). It learned that expertise is a blind spot with a specific shape — the author knows the true path, so only a cold reader trips over the written one (SN-748) — and that honesty about scope is a deliverable in itself: the documented "dead beef passes by design" bound (SN-809), the named half of a replay (in this block's trials essence, SN-747), and the 6.0-scored PENDING (SN-816) are all the same act — stating exactly where the proof ends. A verification culture is measured by how precisely it can say what it did *not* prove.

notes.title: Verdicts Expire With The Bytes; Decisions Are Priced
notes.subtitle: Every verdict is a function of the bytes it was computed on, and every "wait" is a purchase that must be priced. A repair built on a moved tip silently becomes a second defect — two commits of lag is a different world (SN-745). A verdict *survives* a tip move only transitively, when the exact blob it was computed on is byte-identical at both tips and both SHAs are cited (SN-727). A stand-down is earned only after currency re-verification — the RED still reproduces, the claimed head actually fixes it, the repaired files are byte-identical between claim base and tip (SN-716) — and coverage is proven, not assumed: a lane that stood down assuming a wave covered its instances grepped the wave's patches, found zero mentions, overturned its own disposition in public, and built the repair itself (SN-776). A CI job that dies before the check runs yields UNKNOWN, not a verdict (SN-694). A superseded run that leaves no receipt is indistinguishable from a swallowed failure (SN-723). And in any scorecard, a wait option is priced on information gain: if the future cannot return a verdict the present cannot — the check fails identically on the base, or the environment cannot produce the evidence at all — the wait is worth ~0 minus indefinite delay (SN-798, SN-755).

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: A decision made yesterday about files that changed overnight is a decision about a world that no longer exists. This essence is about keeping decisions attached to reality: check that the fix still matches the current code before merging it, check that the person you deferred to is actually handling your problem — by reading their work, not assuming — and when someone proposes "let's wait for more information," ask the only question that matters: what could the future possibly tell us that we can't already know? If the answer is nothing — the test is broken in the same way everywhere, the camera literally cannot take that picture here — then waiting isn't caution. It's just delay wearing caution's clothes.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine you draw a map of your classroom, then the teacher rearranges all the desks. Your map isn't wrong because you drew it badly — it's wrong because the room changed. You need a new map, unless the one corner you care about stayed exactly the same — then you can point and say, "that corner didn't move, so that part of my map still works." And imagine a friend says, "I'll tell you tomorrow if your drawing is good, after I ask my broken camera." If the camera is broken today and broken tomorrow, waiting for it tells you nothing. Decide with the eyes you have.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, it's the wisdom of checking the larder before you cook from last week's list, and of not putting off a decision for news that cannot come. If the road report you need comes from a bridge that's washed out, you don't wait by the river — you take the sound road and note why. And when you hand a job to someone, you look in on the work itself, not just the promise; if the promised helper never had your parcel, the honest thing is to say so out loud and carry it yourself.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Anchor every verdict to the bytes it was computed on, and re-anchor explicitly: byte-identical blob + both SHAs, or the verdict expired (SN-727, SN-745). Earn your stand-downs with the currency receipt — reproduce, verify the claim head, compare the bytes (SN-716) — and prove coverage from the wave's own patches before you assume it (SN-776). Read steps, not job badges; when the check never ran, write UNKNOWN (SN-694). Make even your refused runs leave receipts (SN-723). And in every scorecard, price the wait: name the instrument, test producibility, classify predetermined checks instead of gating on them (SN-798, SN-755).

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body: Eight notes are one law in two halves: **currency** and **pricing**. Currency: a verdict, a repair, a stand-down, and a coverage assumption are all claims about the present state of a moving repository, and each note installs the mechanical re-check that keeps the claim present-tense — blob identity (SN-727), tip re-derivation (SN-745), the three-part receipt (SN-716), the patch grep (SN-776), step enumeration (SN-694), the durable race receipt (SN-723). Pricing: once the present is known, the remaining question — act or wait — is arithmetic, not temperament: the wait is worth exactly the information it can return (SN-798), and a gate demanding unproducible evidence is not rigor but a permanent block (SN-755). A cold reader holding only this essence can still audit any merge decision in the system: what bytes, what tip, what could waiting have taught us?

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: A multi-lane repository moves under every decision: the tip advances 8 commits during a verification, a second commit lands 32 seconds after a push, a wave's assumed scope turns out to cover different instances entirely. Decisions that don't re-anchor become defects — a stale repair that would have wiped 17 files' index entries is a data-loss bug wearing a healer's clothes. And unpriced waiting is the symmetric failure: drift windows widen, the Director's asked-for work stalls, and the blocker cites a check that was never going to change its answer. Currency keeps decisions true; pricing keeps them timely. Together they are what "acting on evidence" actually means on a moving system.

layers.name: How It Connects
layers.body: This essence is the currency half of Batch 1's Essence 03 (The System, Not Just the Seat, SN-2070) — that essence carries "re-anchor to the live head before building" as a system law; this one carries the oct-3 mechanics of *how* re-anchoring is proven (blob transitivity, currency receipts, coverage proofs) and what it costs to skip. SN-716 and SN-776 are the verification half of the no-duplicate-mechanism rule whose claim-side lives in this block's relay essence (SN-711) and Batch 1's Essence 04 (Work Together Without Colliding, SN-2071). SN-798/SN-755's wait-pricing is the decision procedure the scorecard law runs on; SN-723's missing receipt is the same silence defect as SN-766's unnamed gap, carried in this block's trials essence from the measurement side.

layers.name: What's In It For You
layers.body: You get decisions that are still true when they land: repairs that can't clobber newer work, stand-downs that never become permanent blocks by deference, coverage you verified instead of inherited, and waits that are only ever bought when they can teach something. Apply it to any fast-moving shared system: name the exact artifact your verdict describes, re-check it at decision time, prove the delegate's scope from their artifacts, enumerate steps behind every status, receipt your refusals, and price every delay by the information it can actually return.

layers.name: The Learning
layers.body: The corpus learned that staleness is silent: nothing announced that PR #1900 had become a clobber, that the stand-down's premise was false, or that the promotion run had left no receipt — each was found by a deliberate re-check, not by an alarm (SN-745, SN-776, SN-723). It learned the constructive counterpart in SN-727: expiry is not automatic either; a verdict with a named, unchanged subject blob legitimately survives, and forcing re-verification there would waste exactly the motion this system can't spare. And it learned to defend its waits in writing — the scorecards in SN-798 and SN-755 survive as receipts because the pricing was published *before* the merge, so a later reader can audit the decision instead of re-litigating it.

notes.title: The Repair Lifecycle: Classify, Prove, Sequence, Close Honestly
notes.subtitle: A repair is a lifecycle, not a diff: classify the failure before healing it, prove the classification, sequence repairs in the order the gates can see them, and close every lane honestly — merged, superseded with credit, or closed unmerged when merging would do harm. The five-gate merge protocol is its governance frame: tests green → honest self-scorecard at 9.0+ → different-seat validation → intent posted with no objections → merge, report after (SN-691). Stacked repairs prove safe by combination runs, not by hope (SN-676). A heal's ancestry is verified, because twin commits are the norm in parallel lanes and a right conclusion with a wrong mechanism is verdict debt (SN-710). "It fails on the tip too" is corroboration, not proof — base-defect is proven by input-equivalence, diff ∩ check-inputs = ∅ (SN-775). A green heal that reconstructs artifacts without ratification, provenance, or epistemic state is named green-with-a-gap, never silent green (SN-737). Duplicated repairs resolve by superset, with the loser's insight credited and its branch kept (SN-762); a conflicted same-class repair is superseded respectfully, byte-equivalence proven, note posted on the superseded PR itself (SN-779); and an open PR whose targets the owner has since restructured is closed unmerged, because an open PR is a proposal, never a commitment (SN-780). Before any of it: check whether the red PR is a duplicate whose head SHA already merged — identical SHA = close, not repair (SN-814).

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: A repair is a lifecycle, not a diff: classify the failure before healing it, prove the classification, sequence repairs in the order the gates can see them, and close every lane honestly — merged, superseded with credit, or closed unmerged when merging would do harm. The five-gate merge protocol is its governance frame: tests green → honest self-scorecard at 9.0+ → different-seat validation → intent posted with no objections → merge, report after (SN-691). Stacked repairs prove safe by combination runs, not by hope (SN-676). A heal's ancestry is verified, because twin commits are the norm in parallel lanes and a right conclusion with a wrong mechanism is verdict debt (SN-710). "It fails on the tip too" is corroboration, not proof — base-defect is proven by input-equivalence, diff ∩ check-inputs = ∅ (SN-775). A green heal that reconstructs artifacts without ratification, provenance, or epistemic state is named green-with-a-gap, never silent green (SN-737). Duplicated repairs resolve by superset, with the loser's insight credited and its branch kept (SN-762); a conflicted same-class repair is superseded respectfully, byte-equivalence proven, note posted on the superseded PR itself (SN-779); and an open PR whose targets the owner has since restructured is closed unmerged, because an open PR is a proposal, never a commitment (SN-780). Before any of it: check whether the red PR is a duplicate whose head SHA already merged — identical SHA = close, not repair (SN-814).

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Fixing things in a busy shared workshop is a craft with a beginning, a middle, and an end. The beginning is diagnosis: prove what's actually broken, where the test is really reading from, whether the failure is yours, the environment's, or older than your change. The middle is proof: run repairs together the way they'll land together, in the order the checking machinery can actually see them, and don't call a fix proven until the real pipeline has run it. The end is housekeeping with respect: when two people fixed the same thing, the more complete fix wins, the other's insight is credited in writing, and their work is kept — not deleted. When your own fix has been overtaken by events, you close it yourself, cleanly, rather than letting it land and undo someone else's good work.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine the class guinea pig's cage breaks and three kids fix it at once. First you check: is the cage really broken, or is the latch just being read wrong? Then the fixes get tested together, because two good fixes can still jam the same door. If two kids built the same latch, you keep the stronger one, write the other kid's good idea in the class book with their name on it, and keep their latch in the cupboard — you don't throw it away. And if the teacher already bought a brand-new cage while yours was being glued, you don't install your old cage anyway. You say, "Mine isn't needed now," and put it away neatly.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, it's good mending practice. You find the real tear before you thread the needle — not the shadow of a tear, not a tear in a different garment. You baste pieces together before the final stitch to be sure they sit well together. When two menders have repaired the same seam, you keep the sturdier work, thank the other in the parish record, and fold their piece into the linen chest — nothing wasted, nobody erased. And when you discover the garment has already been replaced, you don't sew your patch onto the new cloth out of pride. You note the work, close the basket, and leave the household better documented than you found it.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Run the five gates and respect the undelegated ones (SN-691). Classify before you heal: print the resolved path, check the fixture contract, prove canonical damage (SN-736); name the true mechanism commit (SN-710); prove base-defect by input-equivalence and record the input list (SN-775). Diagnose identical failures environment-first (SN-806, SN-750). Prove stacked repairs in combination, sequence by gate visibility, and keep CI-unrun repairs labeled UNVERIFIED (SN-676, SN-764). Score heals on what they carry and name gaps in the receipt (SN-737). Simulate the wave pairwise before sequencing it (SN-740). Resolve duplication by superset with credit and kept branches (SN-762); supersede only byte-equivalent portions, in the open, with the note on the superseded PR (SN-779); close your own overtaken PRs unmerged (SN-780); and check head-SHA duplication before you repair anything red (SN-814).

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body: Fourteen notes are one lifecycle: **a repair earns its merge the way a claim earns its size — by proof at every transition.** Diagnosis transitions are proven by read-path and ancestry checks (SN-736, SN-710, SN-775); environment transitions by log-and-manifest diffs (SN-806, SN-750); composition transitions by stacked runs and merge-tree simulation (SN-676, SN-764, SN-740); acceptance transitions by what the artifact carries (SN-737); and exit transitions — supersede, close, consolidate — by byte-equivalence and SHA identity (SN-762, SN-779, SN-780, SN-814), all inside a governance frame that says who may merge and what never delegates (SN-691). A cold reader holding only this essence can still walk any repair in the system from RED to closed and know which proof belongs at each step.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Repairs are where a parallel system either compounds trust or compounds damage. A misclassified RED queues a restoration of an intact artifact. A wrong mechanism citation teaches the next seat a false history. An unsimulated wave conflicts at merge time, in public, under time pressure. A silent green heal ships artifacts weaker than the language that describes them. A deleted losing branch erases the credited insight and the reopenable alternative. And a stale PR merged out of politeness reverts the canonical artifact it was built to heal. Each note here is one of those costs, paid once and converted into procedure — the lifecycle is the receipt that the tuition wasn't wasted.

layers.name: How It Connects
layers.body: This essence is the repair half of Batch 1's Essence 04 (Work Together Without Colliding, SN-2071) and leans on this block's currency essence for its tip discipline — SN-745's stale-repair clobber and SN-716's currency receipt are the same law at the decision layer; this essence carries the repair layer beneath them. SN-691's five gates are the merge-time sibling of SN-687's Law Pipeline, which stands alone in this block; the scorecard-mechanics conflict between SN-691 and the Director's 2026-11-05 ruling is recorded in this block's receipt. SN-814's duplicate proof was mechanical only because SN-773's relay pinned the head SHA — carried in this block's relay essence. SN-737's reconstructed-vs-recovered gap is the heal-side twin of SN-777's registration-is-not-execution, carried in this block's claims essence.

layers.name: What's In It For You
layers.body: You get repairs that stay repaired: failures classified by proof instead of resemblance, fixes verified in the environment that actually runs them, waves that don't collide at merge time, losing work that's credited and kept instead of vanished, and your own obsolete PRs closed by your own hand before they can hurt anyone. Apply it to any shared codebase: diagnose at the byte level, prove combinations, sequence by visibility, accept on contents, and make every exit — merged, superseded, closed — a written, credited, reversible act.

layers.name: The Learning
layers.body: The corpus learned that the repair's *paperwork* is part of the repair: the close comment that credits the loser (SN-762), the respectful note on the superseded PR (SN-779), the classification receipt that records a check's input list (SN-775), and the named gap in a green heal (SN-737) are what let a cold successor trust the outcome without re-running it. It learned that duplication and staleness are not moral failures but the default physics of parallel lanes — the lifecycle exists because twins are the norm (SN-710), waves collide invisibly (SN-740), and yesterday's legitimate PR is today's reverter (SN-780). And it learned the exit ethic: closing your own work, unmerged, with the finding converted for the owning lane, is a completion — not a defeat (SN-780, SN-814).

notes.title: A Relay Hands Evidence, Never Authority
notes.subtitle: Work crosses between seats constantly in this system, and every crossing has the same law: what travels is evidence, bytes, and boundaries — never decisions, never authority, never ownership. A verification relay confirms bytes and stops: "here's the evidence, here's what's still open, here's whose call it is" (SN-749, SN-774). A delegated PR opening verifies every claimed head SHA against the remote before opening anything, and opens zero merges (SN-751); relayed opens pin the claimed head SHA, never the mutable branch name, and the requester's declared authority boundaries travel with the request (SN-773). The relay opener then recuses from review — one seat never holds both hands (SN-781). Ownership is declared at detection time, in the same breath as the finding (SN-711), and one mission works on one claimed lane branch — a second branch name is an instant halt (SN-808). Claim-scan hits are resolved by identity chain, not keyword (SN-683). A watch note declares its non-actions in writing, because invisible restraint looks like neglect (SN-753). A shared-tool defect is disclosed and flagged to its owner, never quietly forked (SN-715). A workflow-file write is a held human gate no matter how additive its framing (SN-680). A green PR whose merge wakes production writes still returns NEEDS_AUTHORITY — jurisdiction follows consequences, not merits (SN-807). And every consequential update to the Director is written literal-first: plain words he can picture, evidence appendix after (SN-804).

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: In a team where work constantly changes hands, the most dangerous sentence is the one that sounds like a decision but was only ever a delivery. This essence is the etiquette that keeps handoffs honest: the courier confirms the parcel is the parcel — seals, weight, address — and says out loud that delivering it isn't approving it. The person who opens a package for someone else doesn't then grade its contents. Claims are staked before digging starts, so five people don't dig the same hole. And when you deliberately *don't* do something — don't close that PR, don't start a second fix — you write that down too, because restraint nobody can see looks exactly like nobody caring.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine a relay race where your job is to carry the baton to the next runner. Carrying it doesn't mean you won the race, and it doesn't mean you get to decide who wins — you just carry it carefully and hand it to the right person. If you also get to be the judge, that's not fair, because of course you'd judge your own running kindly. And before the race, everyone agrees who runs which leg — if two kids grab the same baton and run different ways, nobody finishes. One baton, one runner per leg, names called out before the whistle.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, it's the manners of a good post office and a good neighbor. The postman delivers the letter; he doesn't sign it. The neighbor who takes in your parcel while you're out writes down that she has it, and doesn't open it, and doesn't tell the sender you agreed to anything. If you see the fence on the far field is broken but it's Mr. Alvarez's fence and his crew is already mending fences this week, you send word — you don't climb over and start hammering, and you write in the farm diary that you saw it and left it to him, so nobody thinks the whole parish walked past blind.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: End every relay with the boundary sentence and put the deferral in the receipt itself (SN-749, SN-774). Verify before you open, pin what you open, inherit the requester's boundaries, then recuse (SN-751, SN-773, SN-781). Declare provisional ownership in the detecting post (SN-711) and claim your lane branch before your first commit — a second branch name halts the mission (SN-808). Resolve scan hits by chain identity (SN-683). Write your non-actions (SN-753). Disclose shared-tool defects to their owners and keep your workaround uncommitted (SN-715). Split mixed PRs at the workflow gate (SN-680), score merits and consequences as separate verdicts, and bundle the consequence chain into one ask (SN-807). And when you write to the Director, think it in his language first — the picture test decides, the appendix follows (SN-804).

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body: Thirteen notes are one law: **in a delegated system, the handoff is a trust boundary, and what crosses it is evidence — never the decision.** The relay family (SN-749, SN-774, SN-751, SN-773, SN-781) builds the boundary brick by brick: confirm bytes, pin claims, inherit boundaries, recuse. The roster family (SN-711, SN-808, SN-683, SN-753) keeps the lanes the handoffs run between from multiplying or colliding silently. And the gate family (SN-680, SN-807, SN-715) marks where delegation ends entirely: at workflow files, at production consequences, and at tools whose ownership stays with their owner even when broken. SN-804 is the same law at the human boundary: even the Director receives a handoff, and it arrives translated, complete, and honest about what's blocked. A cold reader holding only this essence can still audit any cross-seat action: who confirmed, who claimed, who decided, and where the boundary was written.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Shadow authorization is the quiet killer of delegated systems: a confirmation read as approval, an opening read as endorsement, a review performed by the person with a stake in the outcome — each one produces a decision that *nobody made*, which means nobody is accountable for it and nobody can audit it. The roster failures are the same shape in work-space instead of authority-space: five sibling commits, two racing branches, unique fixes silently lost in a merge that picked the wrong carrier. And the Director-facing law matters because he is the final consumer of every relay: an update he can't picture is a decision he'll make blind, which converts the whole evidence chain into decoration. Boundaries written at handoff time are the only version of this that survives contact with a busy week.

layers.name: How It Connects
layers.body: This essence is the oct-3 mechanics under Batch 1's Essence 04 (Work Together Without Colliding, SN-2071) — that essence carries the team's general collision discipline; this one carries the relay, roster, and jurisdiction procedures of the October repair waves. It deliberately does **not** carry SN-808 as covered-by-batch1: SN-2070 lists it, but the full-text pass in this block found the doctrine absent from SN-2070's text (recorded as a batch1 defect in this block's receipt), so the substance is carried here instead. SN-749/SN-774 are the relay-side twins of SN-779's respectful supersede and SN-762's superset resolution (this block's repair essence): those govern what happens to the *work*; these govern what happens to the *decision*. SN-807's jurisdiction rule is the consequence-axis sibling of SN-680's file-axis gate, and both bound the delegated merge protocol carried as SN-691 in the repair essence. SN-804's literal-first law is the communication surface of Director-facing reporting everywhere in the system, including the Daily Intelligence Report discipline recorded in standing memory.

layers.name: What's In It For You
layers.body: You get handoffs you can trust at speed: evidence that arrives with its limits labeled, openings pinned to the bytes you reviewed, reviews done by seats with nothing riding on them, lanes claimed before they collide, and decisions that always have a name attached. When you relay, you are protected too — the boundary sentence means your confirmation can never be inflated into an authorization you never gave. Apply it to any delegated work anywhere: separate carrying from deciding, pin claims to immutable references, declare ownership at detection, write your restraints, score consequences as their own verdict, and translate before you transmit.

layers.name: The Learning
layers.body: The corpus learned that the boundary has to be *written*, every time, because readers inflate handoffs by default: the deferral sentence (SN-774), the recusal line (SN-781), the "Not doing" paragraph (SN-753), and the pinned-SHA report-back (SN-773) are all the same technology — a sentence that prevents a future misreading. It learned that prevention beats reconciliation in roster space too: claiming before the first commit (SN-808) and provisional ownership at detection (SN-711) exist because the after-the-fact reconciliations, however well run, still cost file-by-file ports and forensic untangling. And it learned the jurisdiction lesson last and hardest: a merge can pass every merits gate ever built and still not be yours to make, because what it *wakes* belongs to someone else's authority (SN-807).

notes.title: A Note Exists Only When Every System Knows It
notes.subtitle: A Smart Note has four existences — the file, the registry, the ingestion ledger, and the learning chain — and it is real only when all four know it. Three notes landed on main byte-identical and present, and the registry battery went RED 1 → 11 on exactly them: files ≠ landed (SN-746). The same three notes were invisible to the hourly ingestion loop, which scans only one draft branch; the cure re-routed their identical blobs through the canonical channel and the FORBIDDEN move was hand-editing the ledger to make the gap disappear (SN-763). Every piece of intelligence the Director shares earns a capture receipt in the same turn, audited nightly, with misses dispositioned in exactly three buckets (SN-725). His capture directive IS the authorization — capture activates immediately, and scorecarding measures what happened, never re-approves the intent (SN-802). The registry's sequence counter is never bumped past unclassified duplicates: classify every duplicate by block identity first (SN-801). A lifecycle state with no named step that can leave it is a guaranteed future failure — CANDIDATE had no path to ACTIVE while retrieval accepted only ACTIVE (SN-813). And the system's existence proof is a cold successor: given only canonical material, a cold Naya built an unfamiliar app to 100/100 ELITE with zero re-teaching — and its three honest findings stayed as live tickets, including a real judge bug (SN-756).

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Writing something down feels like finishing it. This essence is about all the places "written down" quietly fails to mean "the system knows": the note is in the folder but not in the registry everything reads; it's on the main branch but the learning loop only looks at a side branch; it was captured but its status can never legally change into the status the search tool requires. Each gap was invisible until something downstream went looking and found nothing. The fixes are plumbing, not promises: a landing isn't done until every system that serves the note can serve it, the Director's words get a receipt the same turn he speaks them, numbering conflicts get classified instead of painted over, and every status a note can be in has a real door out of it.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine you write a story and put it in a drawer. Then you tell everyone, "My story is in the library!" But the library has a card catalog, and your story has no card — so when anyone looks for it, the library says it doesn't exist. And the librarian only ever checks one special shelf for new stories; if you put yours on a different shelf, she will never find it, even though it's "in the library." And imagine a door painted on a wall: it looks like a way out, but nobody ever built the hinge. A story — or a note — only counts when every way of finding it actually finds it.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, it's the difference between keeping a recipe in your head, writing it on a card, and filing the card where the family looks. A household runs on the filed card, not the intention. When the head of the house tells you something important, you write it down then and there and you can show the page later — you don't rely on remembering by Friday. When two recipes end up with the same number, you don't just renumber the book to look tidy; you read both and find out which is which. And a jam jar labeled "ready" that no one is allowed to open isn't ready at all — labels must have a way to become true.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Land notes by the three-part contract and never pin-bump drift away (SN-746); route main-landed content through the ingestion channel with byte-identical blobs and keep your hands off the ledger (SN-763). Receipt the Director's intelligence in the same turn and disposition every audit flag by morning in the three buckets (SN-725). When he says capture, capture — immediately, with mechanical checks only (SN-802). Classify duplicates by content hash before any sequence alignment, and let first claim stand (SN-801). Draw your lifecycle graph; if a state has no owned exit arrow, fix the chain before the first item hits it (SN-813). Qualify changes on red tips by stash control and pin every pre-existing failure to its owning class (SN-696). And when a cold successor graduates, file its findings — especially the ones that indict your own instruments (SN-756).

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body: Eight notes are one law: **existence in this system is a property of the consumers, not the producer.** The file's author knows the note exists; the registry, the ingestion ledger, the retrieval gate, and the cold successor are the ones who decide. SN-746 and SN-763 are the landing half (producer-side completeness across every channel); SN-725 and SN-802 are the intake half (the Director's words enter with receipts and without re-approval); SN-801 and SN-813 are the state half (identities classified honestly, lifecycle transitions owned); SN-696 and SN-756 are the proof half (regression control for changes, cold graduation for capability). A cold reader holding only this essence can still audit any note's reality: can every system that should know it, know it?

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: The corpus is the system's memory, and memory that silently drops entries is worse than no memory — because everyone plans as if the knowledge were in there. The three vanished notes were Director-directed vision notes: filed, merged, verified present — and unfindable by every tool the team actually uses. A receipt that never issues turns the Director's spoken intelligence into a rumor by Friday. An unclassifiable duplicate set makes every future number claim a coin flip. And a lifecycle with a painted door guarantees that the most honest items — the ones labeled CANDIDATE in good faith — are exactly the ones retrieval will reject. These are the failure modes that make a knowledge system quietly stop deserving trust; the contracts here are how it earns trust back.

layers.name: How It Connects
layers.body: This essence is the oct-3 mechanics under Batch 1's Essence 06 (The Note System Itself, SN-2073) and Essence 05 (Intelligence Must Transfer and Compound, SN-2072) — those carry the note-system and compounding law; SN-2072 also verifiably carries SN-811's capture-design law (falsifiable contract at admission), which is this essence's intake-side sibling: SN-802 governs the Director's captures, SN-811 governs lesson admission generally. The causal chain SN-746 → SN-763 → SN-777 → SN-778 runs across this essence and the claims essence (SN-777/SN-778): the landing failure caused the channel cure, whose registry heal caused the execution gap, whose honest repair set refused fabrication — preserved as one chain in this block's receipt. SN-695's learning ladder stands alone in this block; SN-813's missing CANDIDATE → ACTIVE transition is the ladder's plumbing defect, recorded against it without restating it. SN-801's duplicate classification is the registry-side twin of SN-703's claim-census discipline in the gates essence.

layers.name: What's In It For You
layers.body: You get a corpus you can actually search: notes that exist everywhere they're supposed to, numbers that mean one thing, statuses that can move, and receipts that prove the Director's words landed the turn he spoke them. When you file knowledge anywhere — a wiki, a registry, a shared drive — apply the same tests: who reads this, through which channel, under which index, in which state? If any answer is "nobody, yet," the work isn't landed, and the honest move is to build the channel, never to edit the ledger until it *looks* landed.

layers.name: The Learning
layers.body: The corpus learned that every hand-off between its own subsystems is a place knowledge can silently die: file→registry (SN-746), main→ingestion branch (SN-763), capture→receipt log (SN-725), CANDIDATE→retrievable (SN-813). The repairs share a shape — make the consumer's view the definition of done, and close the loop by watching the consumer actually consume (the ingestion run ledgering the notes is SN-763's closure criterion). It also learned restraint at the exact moment of repair: hand-editing the index would have been faster and would have falsified the very history the index exists to keep — the channel is slower and is the truth (SN-763). And SN-756 taught the optimistic half: the canonical material, honestly maintained, is already sufficient for a stranger to build at an elite level — the corpus works when it's real.

notes.title: Activation Is Enforced By Machines That Fetch Their Own Truth
notes.subtitle: Activation — tuning in to the live state of the system before working — fails as a document and works only as a machine. Documents get read, agreed with, and forgotten under load, so the design intelligence moved into generators, blocks, and gates (SN-783). But a gate that trusts the builder's own receipt is theater: a builder can forge the receipt AND the expected hashes, so expected values must be computed by a separate trusted runner (SN-787). A checker that requires an identity field to be merely non-empty verifies typing, not identity — claimed identities are compared by EQUALITY against trusted expected values, with a wrong-identity negative control in the falsifier matrix (SN-792). References are resolved by availability — ordered fallbacks, the used reference + SHA recorded in the receipt, fail closed with a named failure when nothing resolves (SN-794). Gates compose only on the canonical schema: a lane never invents v2 in its own branch (SN-797) — the schema is upgraded by upgrading the canonical template itself, which is exactly how v2 legitimately became canonical (SN-799). And the unified gate's truth provider resolves the repository, the live tip, and canonical blob SHAs itself — no caller flag may supply truth; a builder cannot self-authenticate, ever (SN-799).

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: "Remember to check in before you start" doesn't survive a busy day — people forget, especially people who wake up brand-new every morning, which is literally what these agents do. So the check-in became a turnstile: you physically cannot start until it reads your badge. But a turnstile that trusts whatever badge you hand it is just furniture. These notes harden the turnstile step by step: the badge's number must match the registry exactly (not just be *a* number), the registry must be read by the turnstile itself rather than quoted by the person walking through, the rulebook the turnstile enforces must be the one official rulebook (not a photocopy someone edited in their shed), and when the rulebook is missing, the turnstile says so and stays shut — it never waves you through on a guess.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine a clubhouse with a special door. To get in, you say the password and show your membership card. A silly door would let you in if your card says ANY name, as long as it says *something*. A smart door checks: does the name match the club list exactly? And the door reads the club list itself from the teacher's desk — it doesn't let you bring your own list, because you could just write your name on it. There's also only ONE official rulebook for the door; nobody gets to make up their own version in their bedroom. If the rulebook is lost, the door stays closed and says "rulebook missing" — it never guesses.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, it's the difference between a latch and a lock with a proper key registry at the hardware store. Anyone can whittle a piece of wood that looks like a key; the registry is what says which keys are real. Honest systems keep the registry out of the hands of the person asking to be let in, keep one master copy of the rules where everyone can see it, and teach the door to say "I cannot verify you" plainly instead of pretending. And the roster of who came in is written at the door, at the time — not reconstructed later from memory.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Build enforcement, not reminders: bake the law into generators and gates, receipt every activation against the live tip, and let freshness expire (SN-783). Never accept expected values from the builder — compute them in the trusted runner, and keep your verdict vocabulary honest about what consistency proves (SN-787). Bind identities by equality and demand the wrong-identity test before you believe any checker (SN-792). Resolve doctrine by ordered availability, receipt the reference + SHA you actually used, and fail closed by name (SN-794). Never fork a schema in your branch — upgrade the canonical template through the channel, and test compositions in sequence before claiming they compose (SN-797). Fetch your own truth: repository, live SHA, blob SHAs — no caller-supplied truth, no self-authentication, and let self-minted runs cap at CANDIDATE-LOCAL where everyone can see the cap (SN-799).

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body: Six notes are one architecture: **enforcement that cannot be talked around.** SN-783 is the premise — behavior that matters must be machine-forced, because every seat wakes up new. SN-787 and SN-792 are the trust design — who computes truth (not the builder), and how claims bind to it (equality, negative controls). SN-794 is the reference design — doctrine is resolved live, receipted, and failed closed when absent. SN-797 and SN-799 are the contract design — one canonical schema, changed only through its template, enforced by one gate whose truth provider answers to the live API rather than to any caller. The apparent v1/v2 tension between SN-797 and SN-799 is resolved in the record itself: the version was never the issue; the *channel* was. A cold reader holding only this essence can still audit any activation claim: who computed the expected values, what exactly was compared, which reference was used, which schema version the canonical template carries, and where the truth came from.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Activation is the system's front door: every other discipline — design law, activation receipts, pre-delivery gates — assumes the seat actually tuned in to current truth before acting. If the door is forgeable, freshness is fictional and every downstream proof inherits the fiction: a receipt built on a stale tip "proves" alignment with a system that has already moved. The failures caught here were all quiet and plausible — a non-empty field, a plausible file path, a schema that looked like an upgrade — and each would have let unactivated or wrongly-activated work present itself as compliant. In a system whose entire claim is "we verify," the verification of the verifiers' own starting state is the load-bearing piece.

layers.name: How It Connects
layers.body: This essence is the enforcement half of Batch 1's Essence 02 (Proof Is Behavior, Not a Badge, SN-2069), which verifiably carries SN-793 — the layered refuse-to-score doctrine this essence's gates implement; SN-793's mechanism details (content-bound citation marker, 4-hour expiry) live jointly in SN-795 and SN-799 here-adjacent coverage, as recorded in this block's receipt. SN-783's design gate is the same instrument whose dogfooding is carried as SN-784 in this block's gates essence; SN-795's form-vs-substance battery (gates essence) is the adversarial finding this essence's digest-binding answers. SN-788's drink-first gate (trials essence) is the production-rung repair built on this architecture. SN-805's sealed-kit tripwire (verification essence) guards the kit these gates ship in. SN-695's learning ladder and SN-789's Delivery Gate stand alone in this block and are deliberately not restated here.

layers.name: What's In It For You
layers.body: You get a starting line that means something: when work arrives receipted as activated, the receipt was checked against values the worker never touched, under the one canonical schema, against doctrine that provably exists, at a tip that was live when it mattered. Apply it to any compliance or onboarding machinery: separate the checker from the checked, bind identities by equality with negative controls, resolve references live and record which you used, version your contracts through their canonical home only, and let your gates fetch their own truth — because any truth the claimant supplies is just another claim.

layers.name: The Learning
layers.body: The corpus learned that each hardening exposed the next layer down: forcing the receipt (SN-783) raised forgery of the receipt (SN-787), which raised field-level binding (SN-792), which raised reference existence (SN-794), which raised schema forks (SN-797) — "the gate got stronger, not quieter" as a way of life. It learned that consistency is a modest word and must stay one: CONSISTENT never silently becomes UNDERSTOOD or AUTHORIZED (SN-787). And it learned the composition lesson in its most general form: components that are each correct can still be mutually exclusive, and the only proof of composition is running them in sequence on exact bytes (SN-797) — after which unification is one gate, one schema, one truth provider, with the retirement map and open items written down rather than implied (SN-799).

notes.title: One Canon, Many Hands: Fix The Source, Never The Instance
notes.subtitle: Many hands build on one canon, and the canon survives only if every repair lands on the *source* — the generator, the reference, the template, the block library — never on the instance that happened to show the symptom. A stale score kept regenerating because it lived in the recurring builders' definitions; patching the report would have healed nothing (SN-679). A grant expiry about to be "reported" was instead removed — the mechanism rebuilt so the cliff cannot recur (SN-706). Where a document and its living showcase disagree, the PAGE wins and the document gets fixed, because you score the experience, never the code (SN-712, SN-717). A candidate canon carries its unresolved conflicts explicitly on HOLD and never overwrites the standing contracts (SN-713). A code is ratified only when it is drift-resistant — every law carrying a pass/fail check, because a rule without a check is a wish (SN-707). New domains get adapters over the canonical engine, never a second engine (SN-732). When the reference implementation already exists and scores above the floor, the brief changes from "build the pieces" to "build to the spec" (SN-739). Apps are assembled from law-tagged canonical blocks — the authoring tool cannot express a non-law component — and automation's authority envelope shrinks as automation grows (SN-758, SN-765). The laws ship inside the library, beside the components they govern (SN-769). And control-plane changes announce themselves on the canonical surface — workflow modifications are flagged in the PR body, never smuggled (SN-678).

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: A shared style — for design, for decisions, for anything — doesn't live in the examples people copy; it lives in the sources the examples are generated from. Fix one report and the generator reprints the error tomorrow. Let two documents describe the same buttons and the builders will follow whichever they opened first. These notes keep pulling the truth back to one home: the definition, the living page, the canonical engine, the block library, the template — and when something new is needed, the move is always to extend the canon (an adapter, a new block, a template upgrade), never to start a second canon in a corner. Even the conflicts are kept in the canon, labeled HOLD, where everyone can see them — because a disagreement filed openly is information, and a disagreement silently resolved is a fork nobody voted on.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine a LEGO club with one big instruction book and one box of official pieces. If a page in the book is wrong, you fix the book — you don't just fix your own model and leave the wrong page for the next kid. If the book's picture and a finished model disagree, you trust the model you can touch and fix the picture. If you need a piece that doesn't exist, you make it, check it follows the club rules, and put it IN the box for everyone — you don't sneak in your own different pieces. And there's only ever one instruction book being rewritten at a time, with the tricky pages paper-clipped and marked "not decided yet" instead of quietly filled in.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, it's the rule of the pattern book in a sewing circle: one master pattern, kept true, and corrections written into the pattern — not whispered to whoever happens to be cutting today. The finished dress on the form outranks the sketch when they disagree; you alter the sketch. New stitches get added to the book with a do-and-don't sample sewn beside them, so the teaching is there at the moment hands are working. And when two experienced sewers disagree on a seam, the disagreement is pinned to the page with both names — never settled by whoever sews fastest while the other is out of the room.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Patch definitions, not outputs — and verify one full cycle after (SN-679). When you're about to report a recurring problem, rebuild the mechanism instead and report the fix (SN-706). Let the living page outrank its document, and never freeze a document mid-landing (SN-712, SN-717). Carry candidate-canon conflicts as HOLD, one canon in flight, additive only (SN-713). Demand drift-resistance before you call anything ratified — a check per law, or it's a pamphlet (SN-707). Adapt the canonical engine; never crown an adapter (SN-732). Scan for in-flight work before briefing, and build to the named reference above the floor (SN-739). Assemble from law-tagged blocks; build missing blocks into the library (SN-758); freeze protected actions at classification time (SN-765). Attach law to the artifact it governs, as do/don't pairs (SN-769). And announce every control-plane change where reviewers actually look (SN-678).

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body: Twelve notes are one law: **canon is a place, and every truth has exactly one address there.** The generator definition (SN-679), the rebuilt mechanism (SN-706), the living showcase (SN-712, SN-717), the conflict-carrying candidate (SN-713), the drift-hardened code (SN-707), the canonical engine (SN-732), the named reference implementation (SN-739), the block library and its assembly pipeline (SN-758, SN-765), the in-library codification (SN-769), and the announced control plane (SN-678) are all the same commitment viewed from different workbenches: when truth and its copies diverge, repair the source and let the copies re-derive — never bless a copy. A cold reader holding only this essence can still locate authority for any artifact in the system: find its canonical home, or file the gap as a HOLD with an owner.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Forks of canon are the slowest and most expensive failures a multi-builder system has, because they don't announce themselves as failures: both versions keep working, each with sincere builders, until the divergence surfaces as contradictory products, unenforceable laws, and scorecards grading against different standards. The drift SN-707 names is the same entropy at the level of a single reader. And the instance-fix temptation (SN-679, SN-706) is the fork's quiet cousin — it leaves the source producing the defect while the symptom ledger looks clean. One canon, repaired at the source, extended by adapters and blocks, with conflicts carried in the open, is what lets many hands move at full speed without the grammar fracturing underneath them.

layers.name: How It Connects
layers.body: This essence is the canon half of Batch 1's Essence 03 (The System, Not Just the Seat, SN-2070) and the design-side sibling of sep-1's "One Canon, No Collisions" draft: that one governs identity and numbering collisions; this one governs artifact authority — which copy rules, where repairs land, how canon extends. SN-678 pairs with SN-680 (relay essence) as the announcement/gate pair for workflow changes. SN-758's cold-build proof gate is prototyped by SN-756 (this block's note-system essence) and its calculator by SN-730 (gates essence); SN-769's 100 Laws are the same codification SN-739's standing spec enforces. The shape-correction doctrine of SN-782-b (covered-by-batch1, SN-2070) — correct the shape, not the polish — is this law applied to deliverables. SN-741 (the OS Vision) stands alone in this block as a director-stated architecture brief and is deliberately not distilled here.

layers.name: What's In It For You
layers.body: You get one place to look and one place to fix: a standard you can touch (the living page), generators that stop reprinting yesterday's error, adapters that extend the engine without splitting it, and libraries that teach at the moment of use. When your own work forks — two docs, two tools, two versions of the truth — apply the moves: name the canonical home, fix the source, carry unresolved conflicts in the open with owners, harden every rule with a check, and let novelty enter through the library door, never through a bypass.

layers.name: The Learning
layers.body: The corpus learned that canon failures are usually *discovery* failures before they are discipline failures: the second engine, the duplicated build, and the forked schema were each built by a seat who hadn't found the existing canon — hence SN-739's scan-before-briefing and SN-732's inspect-the-canon-first. It learned that ratification is a property of the artifact's resistance to misuse, not of its correctness on the day it was written (SN-707). And it learned the codification placement law the hard way: law filed beside the work gets used; law filed in a museum gets cited — SN-769's do/don't pair at the point of use, and SN-758's assembler that cannot express a non-law component, are the same insight at two depths: the deepest canon is the one the tools themselves cannot violate.

notes.title: Design Is Subtraction: The Thing Itself, Built From His Code
notes.subtitle: Elite design in this system is subtraction performed on the Director's own material. Deliverables are assembled FROM his verbatim harvested code — real logo SVG, brand header, full tokens, button CSS — never styled "inspired by" (SN-721). The actual code is extracted line by line and studied in writing before building, because memory is a lossy compressor and the file is the master (SN-735). "10x better" means better human experience, not more effects: on the hero-buttons pass the shockwave and comets were REMOVED and the material deepened instead (SN-733) — and when the Director's older version proved better, the rebuild was reverted to his bytes without ego, keeping only the real improvements (SN-734). Claims stay quiet: a claim is the unmarked default, and only the independently verified item earns a green glow (SN-722). One broken stylesheet link turned the black-ground library white, so the tokens are inlined into every page — the ground is structural, not contingent (SN-738). Novelty is scored on its own axis, with invented forms named, mechanized, verified, and honestly labeled (SN-754). "Gaudy" was answered with a numbered restraint surgery, not adjectives (SN-759). A specimen that "looks like a PDF" gets rebuilt from zero as an instrument, not revised (SN-760). Combination means fusion — keep every 9 and 9.5 — not selection (SN-767). And the useful thing is never a dashboard of the work; build the real thing (SN-768).
