The write-path enforcement half of authority — a guard off the write path is a suggestion — is in essence-law-without-a-machine.md (SN-0631); scorecard mechanics belong to essence-read-the-verdict.md and the promotion gates' proof bar to essence-learning-must-change-behavior.md.

layers.name: What's In It For You
layers.body: You get autonomy that a human can safely extend: an agent team that never manufactures its own permission is a team a director can actually empower. The transferable discipline — separate readiness from permission, bind names to entitlements, expire grants at the exact change they approved, and audit every "authorized" for its human root — applies to any organization where software acts with real-world consequence.

layers.name: The Learning
layers.body: The corpus learned that authority failures arrive disguised as their opposites: as helpful prose ("under director's grant," SN-0444), as high scores (9.8/10, SN-0523), as authentic artifacts (SN-0556), as familiar names (SN-0409), and even as correct-looking denials misread as bugs (SN-0566). It learned the envelope is a discipline exercised at the moment of temptation — on green, at the highest score, under time pressure — not a policy consulted afterward.

notes.title: A Law Without a Machine Is a Wish
notes.subtitle: Written doctrine is not an operating system: a law is operative only when a machine can falsify its violation (SN-0518), a guard off the write path is a suggestion (SN-0631), a law encoded but invoked by nothing is decoration (SN-0454), and a gate that cannot fail is not a gate (SN-0514). The block's enforcement craft is a chain — write the tool, wire it into an invoking workflow, prove the wire live, cite the law in its error text (SN-0435) — and a set of measured gaps that keep the chain honest: guard liveness 30.6% (SN-0512), note-to-enforcement rate 14.3% (SN-0513).

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: Written doctrine is not an operating system: a law is operative only when a machine can falsify its violation (SN-0518), a guard off the write path is a suggestion (SN-0631), a law encoded but invoked by nothing is decoration (SN-0454), and a gate that cannot fail is not a gate (SN-0514). The block's enforcement craft is a chain — write the tool, wire it into an invoking workflow, prove the wire live, cite the law in its error text (SN-0435) — and a set of measured gaps that keep the chain honest: guard liveness 30.6% (SN-0512), note-to-enforcement rate 14.3% (SN-0513).

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: This essence is the team's answer to its own most repeated failure: writing the rule down and believing the work was done. Again and again the corpus shows a beautiful artifact — a 371-line gate, a machine-readable protocol, a promote() function — sitting beside the path it was meant to govern, invoked by nothing. The craft collected here is the insistence that law is a physical property of the system: a machine on the path, proven to bite, measured for how often it actually does, and re-attacked after every repair.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine a school rule that says "no running in the halls," written on a poster. The poster doesn't stop anyone. A real rule has a hall monitor who can actually say stop — and you test the monitor by sending a runner. These notes are about building monitors instead of posters: checking that the monitor is standing in the actual hallway (not the one next door), that it can really shout, that it shouts at the right things, and that it never just holds up a sign that says "verified" because the sign was printed that way.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, it's the difference between a recipe card and a working oven. Writing "bake at 350" doesn't bake anything until there's an oven, plugged in, that reaches 350 — and a cook who checks with a thermometer instead of trusting the dial. The team learned to ask of every rule: where's the oven, is it plugged in, did anyone ever see it get hot, and does the thermometer get tested too? Rules that can't fail anyone aren't rules; they're decorations on the kitchen wall.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: For any law you rely on: find its machine, then its invoker, then its observed RED (SN-0435, SN-0454); ask whether a mandatory step requires the behavior (SN-0410); pair every obligation with its sweeper (SN-0463); measure liveness by executed refusals and hold the ratchet floor (SN-0512); track note→enforcement as a rate with named exceptions (SN-0513); admit no gate that hasn't failed on broken bytes against the real seam (SN-0514, SN-0518); assert the refusal's absent side effect and run the instrument on your own work first (SN-0519); demand executable contracts for every "bound" claim (SN-0530) and negative controls for every proof (SN-0531); load identity fail-closed (SN-0572); and after any closure, re-run the original attack on the new bytes (SN-0631).

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body: Fourteen notes converge on one definition: enforcement is a location (on the write path), a capability (can say NO), a proof (has said NO on demand), and a measurement (liveness, enforcement rate). Anything missing one of the four is a claim about law, not law. A cold reader holding only this essence can audit any rule in the system and name exactly which of the four it lacks.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Unenforced law is worse than no law: it manufactures confidence. The corpus's own numbers price the gap — 69.4% of guards unproven to reject anything, 85.7% of notes landing without enforcement (SN-0512, SN-0513) — and its scariest hole (a hand edit flipping a note to RATIFIED past a perfect audit, SN-0631) existed precisely because good machinery stood beside the path. The director's standing demand for machine law is answered not by writing more rules but by this chain: wire, prove, measure, re-attack.

layers.name: How It Connects
layers.body: The director's machine-law directive (SN-0529) stands alone as his order; this essence is the team's craft record of obeying it, and SN-0518's two gates are the directive's first instantiations — covered here as enforcement craft, with the directive itself never distilled. The activation ladder and the note-lifecycle half of enforcement (capture → index → enforce) are carried by Batch 1's E5/SN-2072 with SN-0513 as this block's measurement of the same gap from the commit side. Gate-verdict semantics are in essence-read-the-verdict.md; the falsifiability battery's verdict-writing companion (naming residuals) is in essence-receipts-and-repairs.md (SN-0532).

layers.name: What's In It For You
layers.body: You get rules that actually govern. The transferable audit — invoker grep, admission RED, liveness floor, enforcement rate, attack re-run — turns any policy document into a checklist with teeth, in any codebase. The payoff is the end of the most corrosive sentence in engineering: "we have a process for that," spoken over a process nothing executes.

layers.name: The Learning
layers.body: The corpus learned that enforcement fails at four distinct joints — never wired (SN-0435), wired but unable to fail (SN-0514), able but unmeasured (SN-0512), measured but bypassable beside the path (SN-0631) — and that each joint has a mechanical test. It also learned the humility rule: the builder's own gates were among the wrong ones (SN-0512, SN-0519), so the instrument-on-its-author discipline is not ceremony; it is where the bugs actually were.

notes.title: Learning Must Change Behavior, Measurably
notes.subtitle: A learning claim is a measurement or it is a slogan: influence is a number produced by control-vs-treatment ablation or it is not a claim (SN-0510), presence in context is not influence (SN-0544), LEARNED is not mastered until governed transitions prove the higher rungs (SN-0546), and a trial measures only if its task can discriminate, its prompts don't cue the answer, and its raw data survives for independent verification (SN-0452, SN-0474, SN-0573). The activation test is behavioral and two-sided: behavior changes only when the ordinary selector returns the retained lesson unprompted — and removing the seam removes the change (SN-0550).

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: A learning claim is a measurement or it is a slogan: influence is a number produced by control-vs-treatment ablation or it is not a claim (SN-0510), presence in context is not influence (SN-0544), LEARNED is not mastered until governed transitions prove the higher rungs (SN-0546), and a trial measures only if its task can discriminate, its prompts don't cue the answer, and its raw data survives for independent verification (SN-0452, SN-0474, SN-0573). The activation test is behavioral and two-sided: behavior changes only when the ordinary selector returns the retained lesson unprompted — and removing the seam removes the change (SN-0550).

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: The learning system is the heart of this whole project — the claim that the machine gets smarter. This block is where that claim grew up: every comforting shortcut was found and named. Notes in context were stamped "influenced." Agreement among readers of the same document was counted as independent proof. A legendary trial result evaporated because its data lived in a temporary folder. What replaced the shortcuts is a measurement discipline strict enough that the honest numbers are sometimes embarrassing — 0/9 influence on the production kernel — and exactly therefore believable.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine claiming "I learned to swim" because you read a book about swimming while sitting next to a pool. The book was there (presence), but did it change what you do in the water (influence)? To prove learning, someone has to watch you swim — with the book's lesson and without it — and see the difference. And if six friends all copy the same answer from the same page, that's not six proofs; it's one page read six times. Real learning leaves evidence: you behave differently, and someone else can check.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, it's the difference between owning a cookbook and being a cook. The books on the shelf prove nothing about dinner. What proves it: a meal cooked differently because of what was learned, tasted by someone who didn't cook it, with the recipe cards kept in the drawer where they can be found again — not thrown out with the scraps. The team learned to ask of every lesson: show me the meal, show me the cards, and let someone else taste.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: On any learning claim: run the real queries against the live index first (SN-0449); validate the key and make the task discriminating before the first trial (SN-0452); strip the cues pretrial (SN-0474); demand a second, independent, could-disagree check before promoting anything consequential (SN-0458); measure influence by ablation and report the number, never the adjective (SN-0510, SN-0511); count shared-evidence agreement as one datum (SN-0515); rehearse pipelines synthetically and publish the stage map (SN-0524); keep presence and influence in separate fields with influence defaulting false (SN-0544); claim only the rungs a governed transition has proven (SN-0546); activate through the normal path and prove it two-sided (SN-0550); bound every proof run by the seam it exercised (SN-0567); and keep trial raw data in-repo under the evidence verifier (SN-0573).

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body: Thirteen notes build the epistemology of a learning system: capability claims decompose into retrieval, trial design, causal measurement, schema honesty, activation path, and evidence custody — and each link has a mechanical test. A cold reader holding only this essence can dismantle any inflated learning claim into its failing link, and can say exactly what proof would repair it.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Compounding is the project's entire thesis — and it is unfalsifiable without this discipline. The failure modes are seductive because each produces good-looking artifacts: stamps that say influenced (SN-0544), verdicts that say behaviorally accepted (SN-0510), majorities that say corroborated (SN-0515), statistics that say overwhelming (SN-0573). Every one was, at the moment it looked best, unproven. The measurement discipline is what converts the learning story from marketing into engineering — and the honest numbers (2/9 invoked, 0/9 influence, E1-proven) are the baseline every real improvement will be measured against.

layers.name: How It Connects
layers.body: The promotion gates these measurements feed — the four-gate Standing Promotion Law — stand alone as the director's law (SN-0541), never distilled here; SN-0458's and SN-0510's disciplines are the craft that makes its Gate 1 and Gate 3 real. The activation ladder's lifecycle half (captured ≠ indexed ≠ retrieved ≠ applied ≠ verified ≠ compounded) is carried by Batch 1's E5/SN-2072, with SN-0526 batch1-flagged PARTIAL in this block's receipt: the ladder is carried there, while the SN-0460 index gate, the triage dispositions, and the naming-only ratification boundary are NOT — the verifier should read SN-0526's page for those. Evidence-identity enforcement for trial artifacts is in essence-the-instrument-is-on-trial.md (SN-0505); verdict-writing (defects vs framing residuals, SN-0532) is in essence-receipts-and-repairs.md.

layers.name: What's In It For You
layers.body: You get a learning system whose claims you can take to the bank — and a general method for any organization claiming its AI "learns": decompose the claim into retrieval, trial discrimination, causal attribution, and custody, and test each link separately. The payoff is strategic: real compounding, measured honestly, is the one advantage that cannot be copied by buying a bigger model.

layers.name: The Learning
layers.body: The corpus learned that learning-claims fail at their definitions before their data: influence defined as presence (SN-0544), mastery defined as a label (SN-0546), corroboration defined as headcount (SN-0515), readiness defined as adjacency (SN-0567). Redefining each term as a measurement — with a falsifier and a custodied evidence path — was the actual work; the numbers followed. It also learned restraint: the most damaging overstatement found (SN-0510's borrowed verification flag) was reported, not unilaterally repaired, because truth decisions belong to owners.

notes.title: Provenance: Know Where the Thing Lives
notes.subtitle: Every claim about a thing depends on knowing where the thing authoritatively lives — and this block caught each way that knowledge fails: a document "lost" that was sitting unmerged on a recovery branch (SN-0499), a live page whose source exists in no repo (SN-0501), a ratified contract that lived only on an unmerged branch while memory placed it on main (SN-0451), a number naming two different notes (SN-0545), a ledger claiming a migration the unreachable database alone could settle (SN-0445). The discipline: read the canonical store before classifying (SN-0411), re-anchor every cited artifact on the live tip, and treat the registry as the identity authority — resolving collisions by renumbering, never deletion, never a second entry (SN-0545).

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: Every claim about a thing depends on knowing where the thing authoritatively lives — and this block caught each way that knowledge fails: a document "lost" that was sitting unmerged on a recovery branch (SN-0499), a live page whose source exists in no repo (SN-0501), a ratified contract that lived only on an unmerged branch while memory placed it on main (SN-0451), a number naming two different notes (SN-0545), a ledger claiming a migration the unreachable database alone could settle (SN-0445). The discipline: read the canonical store before classifying (SN-0411), re-anchor every cited artifact on the live tip, and treat the registry as the identity authority — resolving collisions by renumbering, never deletion, never a second entry (SN-0545).

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Before you can fix, verify, or even argue about anything, you have to know where it lives and which copy is the real one. This block is a catalog of what happens when that knowledge is assumed instead of proven: audits run against contracts that weren't on main, losses mourned over documents sitting in a branch, fixes prepared for pages nobody could source, a database whose truth nobody on the team could reach. The discipline that emerges — anchor on the live tip, read the canonical store, let the registry name things, and say UNKNOWN when the truth is out of reach — is the quiet foundation under every louder virtue in this corpus.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine a big library. A book can be "missing" three different ways: it's on a cart waiting to be shelved (not lost!), it's in a different building entirely (you have the wrong address), or two books got the same number sticker (now nobody knows which is which). And some rooms only the librarian may enter — if you can't go in, the honest answer is "I don't know," never a guess. These notes teach you to check the cart, check the address, trust the master list for names, and never pretend you saw inside the locked room.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, it's the household wisdom of the master ledger and the deed box: the copy in the drawer is a claim; the original in the vault is the truth. When they disagree, you go to the vault — or you say plainly that you cannot, and ask the one person who can. You never rewrite another person's ledger to match your guess, and you never throw away a document just because its number duplicates another's — you give it its own number and keep the story straight.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: On any provenance question: read the canonical store before classifying (SN-0411); expect the tripwire to bind every commit equally and repair orphans without canonizing them (SN-0432); re-anchor cited artifacts on the live tip (SN-0451); mark unreachable truth UNKNOWN and route it to the director's query (SN-0445); diff future security scans against the recorded baseline before claiming improvement (SN-0455); keep continuity on the one canonical surface and name exclusions explicitly (SN-0476); run the removal-commit → branch-enumeration → blob-verify order before declaring anything lost (SN-0499); stop and ship the gating question when the source is unverified (SN-0501); resolve number collisions by owner renumbering under the registry's authority (SN-0545); and carry operative declarations with their quoted basis and their challenges intact (SN-0433).

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body: Ten notes define the corpus's geography: where truth lives (the canonical store, the live tip, the registry, the production database), how each location is reached (re-anchoring, full-row reads, the director's query), and what honesty requires when a location is unreachable or disputed (UNKNOWN, a held decision, a preserved tension). A cold reader holding only this essence can locate — or honestly fail to locate — anything the system claims to know.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Provenance errors are upstream of all other errors: an audit against the wrong contract fabricates conformance (SN-0451), a fix against an unverified source fabricates a repair (SN-0501), a deletion in a collision destroys the audit trail itself (SN-0545). The stakes are sharpest at the boundaries this essence names — the director's own commits bound by the same tripwire (SN-0432), a production truth no agent may reach (SN-0445), a security posture recorded before anyone is allowed to fix it (SN-0455). Knowing where things live is what makes every other discipline in this block more than theater.

layers.name: How It Connects
layers.body: Registry self-consistency and identity-triple auditing are in essence-the-instrument-is-on-trial.md (SN-0361, SN-0381); the ledger-truth ordering in live operation (SN-0587) is carried PARTIAL by Batch 1's E1 — the divergence protocol and the never-self-repair restraint live on SN-0587's page and in this block's receipt. The SN-0433 ↔ SN-0444 tension connects directly to essence-green-is-not-go.md, where SN-0444's doctrine is covered; neither essence resolves it. Capture-chain provenance (how notes enter the canon with receipts) is in essence-receipts-and-repairs.md (SN-0588, SN-0366).

layers.name: What's In It For You
layers.body: You stop losing things that aren't lost and fixing things that aren't broken. The transferable habits: re-anchor citations on the live source, enumerate recovery locations before declaring loss, let the registry arbitrate names, keep an honest UNKNOWN where truth is gated, and record baselines before debating repairs. Any team with more than one store of truth — which is every team — can run its provenance this way.

layers.name: The Learning
layers.body: The corpus learned that provenance failures are usually location failures, not content failures: the document existed (SN-0499), the contract existed (SN-0451), the event had persisted (SN-0411) — in each case someone acted on an assumed location. It learned that restraint is a provenance virtue: flag the stale ledger for its owner rather than editing it, hold the restoration rather than inferring authorization, stop the fix rather than guessing the source. And it learned to preserve its own disputes: the canonical-index declaration stands with its challenged basis visible (SN-0433), because a record that hides its tensions teaches the next reader a confidence the system never earned.

notes.title: Receipts and Repairs: The Record Is the Work
notes.subtitle: A write is complete at its receipt, not its save (SN-0588); a receipt is honest when it names what was measured, what was only cited, and what remains unknown (SN-0446); a repair is disciplined when it proves impossibility with exact numbers instead of fabricating a fix (SN-0357), re-pins tests to the new invariant instead of weakening the guard (SN-0359), and corrects the record by appending — never by silent overwrite (SN-0448, SN-0398). Every verdict carries two ledgers: defects, and the framing residuals that fence what the verdict may be cited as (SN-0532).

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: A write is complete at its receipt, not its save (SN-0588); a receipt is honest when it names what was measured, what was only cited, and what remains unknown (SN-0446); a repair is disciplined when it proves impossibility with exact numbers instead of fabricating a fix (SN-0357), re-pins tests to the new invariant instead of weakening the guard (SN-0359), and corrects the record by appending — never by silent overwrite (SN-0448, SN-0398). Every verdict carries two ledgers: defects, and the framing residuals that fence what the verdict may be cited as (SN-0532).

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: This is the block's bookkeeping soul: how a fast team keeps a record it can still trust tomorrow. The pattern across all twelve notes is that the record is not paperwork after the work — the record IS the work's durable half. Receipts that say exactly what was measured and what wasn't, corrections appended instead of airbrushed, repairs that would rather declare impossibility than fabricate a hash, verdicts that fence themselves with their own limitations. A cold successor inherits not just conclusions but the means to re-derive them — or to see precisely where derivation stops.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine a class where every student keeps a lab notebook. The rules: when you finish an experiment, you get a stamped receipt — no stamp, it didn't happen. If you recount your marbles and get a different number, you write BOTH numbers and why ("I counted the corner one this time") — you never erase. If your friend checks your work, they don't just read your notebook; they look at the actual marbles and say exactly which pages they checked and which they didn't. And if the teacher's plant-watering chart has a blank day, that's a problem to fix that day — a diary with holes can't prove anything.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, it's the discipline of a good bookkeeper in a family business: every sale gets a receipt, every correction gets a new line with a reason — never an eraser — and the daily takings are written down daily, because a ledger reconstructed from memory next week is fiction. When the bank statement and the cabinet disagree, you note it for the bookkeeper; you don't sneak in and alter her books. And when a bill truly cannot be paid honestly, you say so with the figures shown, instead of cooking them.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: On every receipt and repair: prove impossibility numerically before declaring it, and leave the bytes untouched when honesty forbids the fix (SN-0357); re-pin, never weaken (SN-0359); isolate batch failures per item and record them loudly (SN-0366); classify before closing anything in a cleanup (SN-0397); kill stale claims by live re-measurement in the same venue (SN-0398); treat hash hits as reread orders and name drift by class (SN-0424); write relay receipts that re-measure pins and declare the cited-not-rerun line (SN-0426, SN-0446); append corrections with causes (SN-0448); ship both ledgers with every verdict (SN-0532); feed trend instruments daily (SN-0577); and close every write at its receipt, repairing authority without widening it (SN-0588).

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body: Twelve notes make record-keeping a branch of engineering: receipts with declared scope, corrections with causes, verdicts with fences, repairs with proofs — including proofs that no honest repair exists. A cold reader holding only this essence can write a receipt the next seat can trust, repair without corrupting the record that proves the repair, and inherit any claim in this block knowing exactly how far its evidence reaches.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: The record is the only thing a cold successor — or an auditor, or the director months later — ever actually receives. Every failure here was a record failure with operational consequences: captures that silently never completed (SN-0588), a correction that would have fabricated history if tidied (SN-0448), a stale contamination claim steering real work (SN-0398), a verdict one misquotation away from claiming generalization it never proved (SN-0532). Receipt discipline is what makes the rest of the corpus inheritable instead of merely historical.

layers.name: How It Connects
layers.body: The relay contract here (SN-0426, SN-0446) is the receipt-side of the verification discipline in essence-the-instrument-is-on-trial.md, where verification-as-re-execution (SN-0586) lives. Verdict grammar — how CI colors are classified — is in essence-read-the-verdict.md; SN-0398's falsification is that grammar applied to prose claims. The ledger-truth ordering (act on the source, flag the claim for its owner) is SN-0587, carried PARTIAL by Batch 1's E1 and treated in essence-provenance.md. Scheduled receipt generation as a mechanism is in essence-law-without-a-machine.md (SN-0463).

layers.name: What's In It For You
layers.body: You inherit work you can actually build on: receipts that distinguish measured from cited from unknown, corrections that preserve the chain of reasoning, verdicts that fence their own claims, and repairs whose honesty is itself proven. The transferable kit — append-only corrections, two-ledger verdicts, receipt-closure, failure-shape proof — applies to any audit trail, changelog, or lab notebook where the future reader's trust is the asset.

layers.name: The Learning
layers.body: The corpus learned that the dangerous failures are the silent ones in the recording layer itself: an aborted batch that looked like a processed one (SN-0366), a save that looked like a capture (SN-0588), a tally that looked like a verification (SN-0446). It learned that correction is a creative act with rules — append, explain, keep both numbers (SN-0448) — and that honesty scales when it is formatted: the two-ledger verdict (SN-0532) and the four-part relay (SN-0426) are formats, not virtues, which is exactly why they survive handoffs.

notes.title: One Lane, One Repair
notes.subtitle: Parallel lanes racing the same work is the system's speed and its collision risk; this block's coordination craft is a set of mechanical courtesies that prevent both: the freshness re-fetch guards three moments — before posting, before merging, and before PUSHING (SN-0472); a review head under review is frozen (SN-0473); an unpushed repair whose seam another lane healed is stood down and converted into independent verification of the winner (SN-0508); a code move across an ownership boundary earns trust with a diff-fuzz, not an assertion (SN-0551); and an open PR whose payload already landed elsewhere is closed SUPERSEDED on blob-SHA proof, not merged for ceremony (SN-0558).

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: Parallel lanes racing the same work is the system's speed and its collision risk; this block's coordination craft is a set of mechanical courtesies that prevent both: the freshness re-fetch guards three moments — before posting, before merging, and before PUSHING (SN-0472); a review head under review is frozen (SN-0473); an unpushed repair whose seam another lane healed is stood down and converted into independent verification of the winner (SN-0508); a code move across an ownership boundary earns trust with a diff-fuzz, not an assertion (SN-0551); and an open PR whose payload already landed elsewhere is closed SUPERSEDED on blob-SHA proof, not merged for ceremony (SN-0558).

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Nine teams working around the clock will collide — the question is whether collisions cost a re-fetch or a repair war. This essence is the etiquette that keeps parallel work parallel: look once more before you push, don't move the paper someone is reading, throw away your own finished fix without drama when the seam is already healed, prove a move changed nothing before asking anyone to trust it, and close your own PR when the world has already absorbed it. None of it requires a manager; all of it is checkable by the lanes themselves.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine a big group project where everyone has glue and scissors. The rules that keep it fun: look at the poster before you glue your piece — someone may have just glued the same piece. Don't wiggle the poster while someone is reading it. If you made a spare part and the team already used theirs, don't glue yours on top — check theirs carefully instead, so two people agree it's good. And if your drawing is already on the poster because a friend copied it there, don't paste another copy over it; say "mine's done" and keep your spare for later.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, it's the courtesy of a busy shared kitchen: check the stove before you start cooking what someone just finished; don't move the recipe card out from under the cook who's reading it; and if two cooks made the same dish, serve one and be glad the second can taste-test it. Nothing is wasted — the second cook's work becomes the proof the dish is right. Good manners, in a kitchen or a codebase, are how many hands feed one family without spoiling dinner.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Before pushing: re-fetch and compare bytes — a byte-identical landing means stand down (SN-0472). During review: freeze the head; isolate second repairs (SN-0473). When another lane heals your seam first: if unpushed, stand down and verify their bytes on the live tip (SN-0508). When moving code across an ownership boundary: diff-fuzz with a named count, run the behavior matrix, and re-run the battery against the new location's gate surface (SN-0551). When your open PR's payload is already on main: prove convergence by merge-base three-way plus blob SHAs, close SUPERSEDED, preserve the residue, and re-decide any downstream plan whose predicate died (SN-0558).

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body: Five notes describe coordination as a set of local, mechanical acts — no coordinator required. Each lane carries the whole protocol: freshness at three moments, frozen review heads, the push as the stand-down bar, mechanical trust for moves, proof-based closure for convergence. A cold reader holding only this essence can join a multi-lane effort and never once duplicate, interrupt, or strand another lane's work.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Duplicate work is not merely waste: duplicate repairs fork provenance (two fixes, two receipts, one seam), duplicate PRs burn the review bandwidth every other lane depends on, and a moved review head silently cancels the independent check the whole verification model rests on. The stand-down discipline also has a positive yield the corpus measured in kind: a stood-down repair converted into an independent verification is worth more than the repair — it is how one heal becomes two seats' certainty (SN-0508, SN-0558).

layers.name: How It Connects
layers.body: Per-project feeds — the venue discipline that makes lane traffic findable — stand alone as the director's rule (SN-0453), never distilled here; this essence presumes those venues and governs conduct inside them. Decision-expiry on a moved tip (SN-0558's stale-predicate re-decision) pairs with essence-the-tip-is-the-truth.md, where re-anchoring claims and classifications is covered (SN-0534, SN-0578). Membership-subset ratchets — the anti-gaming design for the drift classes these lanes repair — are in essence-law-without-a-machine.md (SN-0382).

layers.name: What's In It For You
layers.body: You get parallel speed without parallel chaos: teams that check before pushing, freeze what others are reading, and convert lost races into free verification. The transferable core for any multi-contributor project: byte-level stand-down checks, the push as the point of no return, and convergence adjudicated on content identity rather than arrival order. Adopted whole, it turns "who got there first" into "who proved it best" — a much cheaper argument.

layers.name: The Learning
layers.body: The corpus learned that coordination failures are timing failures, not intent failures: every collision here was a lane acting on state that was true when checked and false when used — the repair window (SN-0472), the review window (SN-0473), the merge window (SN-0508, SN-0558). The fixes are therefore all temporal: check at the last moment, freeze during the vulnerable interval, and treat your own sunk work as convertible currency (verification) rather than a claim to priority.

notes.title: Honest Surfaces: Labels, Names, and Controls Tell the Truth
notes.subtitle: What the user touches must not lie: a synthesized voice is labeled SYNTHESIZED VOICE until her true voice lands, never presented as hers (SN-0502); the play button lives ON each block and voices THAT block's own text (SN-0630); a tap answers with press compression and a white indicator — the contract's color law holds on touch exactly as on hover (SN-0450); and a doctrine term is collision-checked at capture time, before it goes public (SN-0527). The unifying discipline: inventory what is already built before building, and scope every control to the unit it serves.

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: What the user touches must not lie: a synthesized voice is labeled SYNTHESIZED VOICE until her true voice lands, never presented as hers (SN-0502); the play button lives ON each block and voices THAT block's own text (SN-0630); a tap answers with press compression and a white indicator — the contract's color law holds on touch exactly as on hover (SN-0450); and a doctrine term is collision-checked at capture time, before it goes public (SN-0527). The unifying discipline: inventory what is already built before building, and scope every control to the unit it serves.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Interfaces are promises. Every label, button, and name on a surface tells the user something — and this block collected the ways surfaces quietly break those promises: a robot voice wearing a person's name, a button that plays the wrong words, a tap that answers with nothing, a proud new term that already belongs to someone else's product. The repairs share one shape: say exactly what the thing is today, build the seam so tomorrow's real thing slots in, and never let presentation outrun reality.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine a friend who can't come today, so a robot reads her message. It would be wrong to say "this is her voice" — it's the robot's, and the honest little sign says so. When her real recording arrives, it slides into the same slot and every button plays her. Same with buttons: press one and it should squish a little and whisper "got it" — in white, not party colors. And if you invent a great name for your game and a famous company already uses it, you write that down right away and explain how yours is different.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, it's shopkeeper's honesty: the sample station never labels the stand-in singer with the famous name; the price tag says what the thing is, not what it will be someday; and before you paint your name on the shopfront, you check the street for another shop with the same name. None of this slows the shop down — the stand-in is clearly labeled, the real record slots in when it arrives, and the name check costs one look at the start instead of a lawsuit later.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: On any surface you ship: label the current reality exactly — synthesized as synthesized, fallback as fallback (SN-0502, SN-0630); put the control on the unit it serves and bind it to that unit's own content (SN-0630); inventory the existing build before adding anything (SN-0630); name blockers as blocked and build against the seam (SN-0630); give every hoverable an :active answer in white — compression plus inset shadow, never color (SN-0450); and collision-check every public term at capture time, in the capture itself (SN-0527).

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body: Four notes, one surface ethic: presentation is a truth claim. The label is a claim about identity, the button's placement and content are claims about scope, the tap response is a claim about the contract, and the name is a claim about ownership. A cold reader holding only this essence can audit any surface the system ships and find where its presentation outruns its reality — which is the exact place user trust is won or lost.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Surface dishonesty compounds silently: the moment a user hears synthesized audio under a "her voice" label, the identity contract breaks — and no one can trust the true voice's arrival when it comes (SN-0502). A misplaced or mis-scoped control teaches users the system doesn't know its own units (SN-0630); a dead tap teaches them it doesn't respond (SN-0450); an unchecked name imports a vendor's meaning into every future conversation (SN-0527). These are small defects with long shadows, and all four were caught by the same habit: compare what the surface says with what is actually true today.

layers.name: How It Connects
layers.body: Two of these notes arrive here because Batch 1's marks on them were unsupported — SN-0450 (Batch 1's E3 names it under a different teaching entirely) and SN-0527 (absent from Batch 1 entirely — no Batch-1 essence lists it; all seven coverage lists were checked, and E5/SN-2072's activation-ladder line is SN-0526, not SN-0527; the maker's earlier claim that E5 cites it under that line is withdrawn) — flagged in this block's receipt and detailed in the verification item below. The authority-text discipline for the design contract itself (re-anchor the ratified text on the live tip before auditing against it) is in essence-provenance.md (SN-0451). Voice playback's receipt and registry plumbing belong to the capture chain in essence-receipts-and-repairs.md.

layers.name: What's In It For You
layers.body: You get surfaces users can trust at a glance — and a design discipline that keeps trust cheap: honest labels, scoped controls, inventoried builds, named blockers, checked names. Apply it anywhere a product presents itself: the label you ship today should still be true on the day the real thing replaces the placeholder, with zero relabeling debt and zero user re-learning.

layers.name: The Learning
layers.body: The corpus learned that surface defects are truth defects in miniature, with the same anatomy as the corpus's larger ones: a literal where a computed value belonged (a fixed label, SN-0502), a claim without an inventory (rebuilding what existed, SN-0630), a silent absence (the missing tap answer, SN-0450), an unchecked collision (SN-0527). It also learned to record reconciliations between standing laws at the moment they're resolved (SN-0450), so the next seat inherits the settlement instead of the argument.

notes.title: The Claim Registry: One Number, One Note, Registered or It Isn't Real
notes.subtitle: A Smart Note number is claimed by writing it into the registry before staging — never by announcement — and the claim holds only if it was scanned, in the same breath, across board, open PR heads, every claim-carrying branch tree, and the commit graph (SN-0151, SN-0171, SN-0184). Same number with different bytes is a fork (SN-0176), precedence runs director-lock > first claim > later claims (SN-0167), and the registry itself is re-derived from disk and reconciled in the permanent gate, because a registry that drifts from the files stops being a registry (SN-0271, SN-0338).

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: A Smart Note number is claimed by writing it into the registry before staging — never by announcement — and the claim holds only if it was scanned, in the same breath, across board, open PR heads, every claim-carrying branch tree, and the commit graph (SN-0151, SN-0171, SN-0184). Same number with different bytes is a fork (SN-0176), precedence runs director-lock > first claim > later claims (SN-0167), and the registry itself is re-derived from disk and reconciled in the permanent gate, because a registry that drifts from the files stops being a registry (SN-0271, SN-0338).

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Every note gets one number, and the number is written into the master list before anyone starts writing — not after, not by announcement. If two notes ever end up with the same number, that's a real problem with a written procedure: who had it first, who renames theirs, and what proof closes the case. And the master list itself gets checked against the actual files, regularly, because a list that says one thing while the shelf holds another is worse than no list.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine every drawing you make gets a number, and there's one big book where all the numbers live. You check the book BEFORE you pick a number — not after! If you and your friend both pick number 18, you don't both keep it: the book says who had it first, and the other person picks a new number and writes it in the book too. And a grown-up checks the book against the real drawings, so the book never lies.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: It's like a land registry, dear. A plot isn't yours because you say so at the fence — it's yours because it's written in the registry, before you build on it. Two deeds to the same plot means one of them is wrong, and there's a proper order for deciding: the owner's own signed lock first, then whoever registered first. And the registry office re-checks its books against the actual land, because a registry that drifts from reality stops being a registry at all.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Before claiming: scan board + open PR heads AND every claim-carrying branch tree + commit graph; write the registry entry first; treat any scan older than minutes as expired. On collision: apply precedence (director lock > first claim), renumber only your own artifact, clear all three layers again, and close with posted evidence. Never trust a registry field a human typed — if the loader didn't generate it, it is a claim awaiting deletion. Serialize registry writes; assert disk↔registry reconciliation in the permanent gate, not in a one-off audit.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body: Fourteen incident notes from the collision autumn are one system: identity is a registry discipline, not a naming habit. A cold reader holding only this essence can run the whole protocol — claim, scan, precedence, renumber, closure, reconciliation — and can explain why each rule exists by pointing at the night it was learned. The collisions themselves were cheap; the protocol they produced is the asset.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Every other essence in this campaign is findable only because a number points at it. When numbers collide or the registry lies, the corpus's memory corrupts silently — two notes answering to one name, audits reading 5.8/10 truth (SN-0271), 296 pages nobody registered (SN-0338). For the reader, this essence is the corpus's identity layer: boring when it works, catastrophic when it doesn't.

layers.name: How It Connects
layers.body: This is the substrate the note-deliverable essence's COMMIT leg runs on (SN-0242) and the serialization discipline of SN-0339 is shared with the law essence's fail-closed family. Its scan-before-claim habit is the lane-coordination essence's scan-before-execute applied to identity (SN-0173). The Smart Link definition it registers under stands alone at SN-0254 (director's canonical definition).

layers.name: What's In It For You
layers.body: You get certainty that a note number names exactly one thing, forever, and a procedure — not an argument — when two claims collide (SN-0167, SN-0189). Apply it by writing the registry entry before your next note's first file, and by treating any scan older than minutes as expired (SN-0184).

layers.name: The Learning
layers.body: The era learned that identity is maintained, not declared: every collision in this family came from a gap between a scan and a claim, a partition and its sibling, or a registry and its disk (SN-0184, SN-0145, SN-0271). The learning that survives: shrink the gaps — atomic scan→claim, loader-generated fields, reconciliation in the permanent gate — because vigilance does not scale and registries do not forgive.

notes.title: Proof Discipline: Name the Instrument, Bound the Claim
notes.subtitle: No instrument, no verdict: name the measuring instrument before any score, mark what it cannot reach NOT_VERIFIED (SN-0161, SN-0146), build claims only from fixed key lists (SN-0181), reproduce failures before repairing them (SN-0245), qualify every tool against known-broken and known-green inputs (SN-0283), and remember the harness itself can manufacture the defects it reports (SN-0341).

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: No instrument, no verdict: name the measuring instrument before any score, mark what it cannot reach NOT_VERIFIED (SN-0161, SN-0146), build claims only from fixed key lists (SN-0181), reproduce failures before repairing them (SN-0245), qualify every tool against known-broken and known-green inputs (SN-0283), and remember the harness itself can manufacture the defects it reports (SN-0341).

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Before anyone gives you a score, ask: measured with what? A number without an instrument is an opinion wearing a lab coat. When something breaks, the first job is to make it break again on purpose, in the real environment, and to check that your measuring tools actually work — feed them something known-broken and something known-good. And when two versions both fail, compare *which* tests fail: if it's the same list, the room is on fire, not your change.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: If you say "my jump rope trick works!", show me — on the playground, not just in your head. And check your stopwatch first: press it on something slow and something fast, so you know it isn't stuck on "fast!" forever. If the game breaks, make it break again the same way before you fix it, so you know you fixed the real break.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: A scale that reads the same for a feather and a sack of potatoes isn't a scale, dear — test it with something whose weight you know. A cake isn't done because the timer sang; it's done when the skewer comes out clean. And if the oven in a strange kitchen burns everything, you blame the oven, not your recipe — check where you're cooking before you change how you cook.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: State the instrument and its ceiling in every verdict; mark what the instrument cannot reach NOT_VERIFIED. Build claims from allow-listed keys only. Sequence failure work as: qualify the tool → reproduce in the target environment → measure the failing line → test the causal hypothesis with an experiment that can actually run → then encode the cure. Compare failing sets across heads before attributing. Cite file:line in every critique. Treat harness resource limits (disk, memory, /tmp) as suspects in every phantom failure.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body: Fourteen notes converge on one posture: evidence is engineered, not collected. Each rule was bought by a specific embarrassment — an 8/8 rejection streak that was really a blind instrument, a retracted diagnosis, a harness that invented defects. A cold reader with this essence runs the same discipline without needing to repeat the embarrassments.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: This essence decides whether the word 'verified' anywhere in the system means anything. Its failures were all confident: an 8/8 rejection streak from a blind instrument (SN-0161), a public diagnosis retracted on measured lines (SN-0246), phantom defects from a full /tmp (SN-0341). For the reader, it is the corpus's epistemology — how the team knows what it claims to know.

layers.name: How It Connects
layers.body: It supplies the measurement spine for the receipts essence (recompute-then-record, SN-0212) and the verification contracts of every other essence in this block. Its comprehension boundary (SN-0174) is the local form of the learning chain whose North Star text stands alone at SN-0253. Its full-scope sibling rule lives in the law essence (SN-0224).

layers.name: What's In It For You
layers.body: You get verdicts that state their own limits — what was measured, with what, and what remains NOT_VERIFIED (SN-0161). Apply it by asking one question of any claim: 'measured with what, on which known-broken control?' A claim that cannot answer is an opinion, and now you know it.

layers.name: The Learning
layers.body: The era learned that evidence is engineered, not collected: instruments are chosen, qualified, and audited, or they quietly choose the verdict for you (SN-0283, SN-0341). The deepest cut: proof terminates at a cold successor's comprehension, not at green plumbing (SN-0174) — a lesson the whole distillation campaign is now built on.

notes.title: Lane Coordination: One Repair per Class, One Owner per Question
notes.subtitle: Parallel lanes collide by default; this is the traffic system that prevents it: one owner per question (SN-0159), scan for an existing repair before claiming a problem (SN-0173), one repair per RED class (SN-0201, SN-0236), relay flags while the owner diagnoses (SN-0222), re-anchor to the live head before building (SN-0202), and three-strikes / three-failures stop-rules that convert repetition into structure (SN-0130, SN-0326).

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: Parallel lanes collide by default; this is the traffic system that prevents it: one owner per question (SN-0159), scan for an existing repair before claiming a problem (SN-0173), one repair per RED class (SN-0201, SN-0236), relay flags while the owner diagnoses (SN-0222), re-anchor to the live head before building (SN-0202), and three-strikes / three-failures stop-rules that convert repetition into structure (SN-0130, SN-0326).

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Before you start fixing something, check whether someone is already fixing it — if they are, your job is to help or step back, not to start a second fix. Every question has one named owner. If the same problem keeps coming back, don't just fix it a third time — change the instructions that keep producing it.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: One person is in charge of each job, and there's a list that says who. Before you start fixing the wobbly table, look — is someone already fixing it? Then you help them or pick a different job; two kids with two hammers on one table leg makes a worse table. If your chore robot keeps making the same mess, you don't just clean up — you fix the robot's instructions.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: In a busy kitchen, dear, one cook owns the soup. Two cooks salting the same pot ruins dinner, however good their intentions. If the same dish keeps going wrong, you don't just remake it — you look at the recipe card and fix what's written there.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Pre-flight every claim: board tail + open PRs + branch trees for the exact class; on finding a canonical repair, retract and cite. Maintain one repair per RED class; re-point stale repairs; classify tripwire REDs as introduced vs inherited before touching anything. Keep relay messages diagnosis-free. Re-anchor builds to live heads; write takeovers as base/no-competitor/preserved-vs-changed/freeze. Count delegation failures; at three identical, execute directly. Log scan results per loop run.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body: Fourteen notes are the scar tissue of one collision-prone autumn, and together they form a complete traffic system: ownership, scanning, consolidation, asymmetric roles, branch contracts, and two stop-rules (three strikes, three failures) that convert repetition into structure. A team that runs only this essence stops colliding — which is most of what coordination ever was.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Coordination failure is the tax every multi-agent system pays in duplicated repairs, colliding branches, and re-asked questions. This family cut that tax in one autumn of collisions (SN-0194, SN-0177). For the reader: it is the difference between a team and a crowd — the same seats, with or without these habits, produce entirely different systems.

layers.name: How It Connects
layers.body: It is Batch-1 E4's working detail. Its scan-before-claim is the claim-registry essence's scan-before-claim pointed at repairs (SN-0151 ↔ SN-0173); its loop-instruction repair (SN-0177) is the proof family's reproduce-the-mechanism habit at team scale; the director's do-it-now doctrine that completes its temperament stands alone at SN-0282.

layers.name: What's In It For You
layers.body: You get a team that doesn't collide with itself: before any fix, one scan tells you whether the fix exists, who owns it, and where you can actually help (SN-0173, SN-0222). Apply it by making the scan a reflex — board, open PRs, branch trees — and by standing down publicly when the canonical repair isn't yours.

layers.name: The Learning
layers.body: The era learned that collisions are mechanism outputs, not character flaws: the loop that duplicated a repair wasn't careless, it was uninstructed — so the fix went into its standing instructions (SN-0177). And repetition is information: the third recurrence of anything is the system asking for a ruling, not another repair (SN-0130).

notes.title: Correct the Record in the Open: Reversals, Attribution, Conflicts
notes.subtitle: Errors in the shared record are repaired in public, where they were made: reversals posted and credited (SN-0160), contradictions sent to a register for the director rather than quietly resolved (SN-0196), ledgered artifacts never edited — corrected by new artifacts (SN-0208) — and check-vs-evidence contradictions reconciled before either side is declared broken (SN-0354).

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: Errors in the shared record are repaired in public, where they were made: reversals posted and credited (SN-0160), contradictions sent to a register for the director rather than quietly resolved (SN-0196), ledgered artifacts never edited — corrected by new artifacts (SN-0208) — and check-vs-evidence contradictions reconciled before either side is declared broken (SN-0354).

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: When you're wrong in writing, fix it in writing, where everyone saw the mistake — and say who got it right. When two rulebooks disagree, don't quietly pick your favorite: write the disagreement down in a list for the person in charge to settle. Never edit history to make it look tidy; add a new page. And before you repeat a claim — "these two are in sync," "this is missing" — check both sides, at the exact version, because the thing itself beats everyone's memory of it.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: If you told the class something wrong, you stand up and say "I was wrong, here's the right one — and Mia had it right." If two rule sheets for the game disagree, you don't secretly choose — you write both rules on the board for the teacher to pick. You never erase your notebook; you cross out once and write the fix next to it, so everyone can see what changed.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: A family story gets corrected at the same table where it was told wrong, dear, with credit to whoever remembered it right. A ledger book is never erased — you rule a line, write the correction beneath, and initial it. And when two people remember a name differently, you don't argue: you open the christening record. The paper that was actually filed settles what talk cannot.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Post reversals in the venue of the original claim, with links both ways. Narrate platform-mechanical transitions with exact refs and explicit non-actions. Verify authorship from branch/PR metadata before routing any question. Keep capture and enactment as separate states in every contract you touch; route contradictions to the register, never resolve them solo. Mark preserved conflicts honored/accepted distinctly; close them only from the director's latest source record. Treat ledgered artifacts as append-only. Re-verify gaps at their pin, read both sides of any sync claim, and open the shipped artifact to settle naming disputes.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body: Twelve notes describe one ethic under twelve pressures: the record belongs to everyone who will ever rely on it, so it is corrected the way it was made — in the open, with receipts. The SN-0354 self-falsification is the family's emblem: even the note that accused the check of lying carries its own correction, and that is precisely why the record can be trusted.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: The record is the team's shared memory; a quietly edited memory makes every future decision built on it suspect. This family is why the corpus can be distilled at all — its corrections are inside it, visible, including a note that falsifies its own original claim (SN-0354). For the reader: this essence is the corpus's honesty guarantee.

layers.name: How It Connects
layers.body: It is Batch-1 E1's operating detail — the era's working-level version of 'the record must tell the truth.' Its register rule (SN-0196) feeds the director's gates, its restore-the-source rule (SN-0211) is the conflict-closure half of the law essence's authority family, and its both-sides rule (SN-0227) is the lane essence's scan habit pointed at facts.

layers.name: What's In It For You
layers.body: You get a record you can build on without re-verifying every brick: where it's wrong, it says so, at the spot, with the fix linked (SN-0160, SN-0164). Apply it by correcting your own public claims in the venue that carried them — and by opening the shipped artifact, not the thread, when memories disagree (SN-0228).

layers.name: The Learning
layers.body: The era learned that correction speed is a trust metric: a one-sided sync verdict was corrected in ~4 minutes and cost nothing; the corrections that cost were the ones that waited (SN-0227). And SN-0354 taught the humbling form: sometimes the check is right and the evidence in your hand is truncated — reconcile before you accuse, in either direction.

notes.title: The Note Is the Deliverable: Lifecycle, Format, and the Returned Link
notes.subtitle: A note is a lifecycle, not a save — TRIGGER → DISTILL → STRUCTURE → COMMIT → INTELLIGENT EVENT → LEARN → PROJECT (SN-0242) — authored once in one canonical place with every other surface derived from it (SN-0248), and the deliverable is never the note alone: it is the note plus its Smart Link, returned by a real mechanism, at authoring time (SN-0258, SN-0255).

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: A note is a lifecycle, not a save — TRIGGER → DISTILL → STRUCTURE → COMMIT → INTELLIGENT EVENT → LEARN → PROJECT (SN-0242) — authored once in one canonical place with every other surface derived from it (SN-0248), and the deliverable is never the note alone: it is the note plus its Smart Link, returned by a real mechanism, at authoring time (SN-0258, SN-0255).

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: When you say "note this down," a whole pipeline should fire: capture it, structure it, file it in exactly one proper place, and hand back a link that works. The note has one original; every copy elsewhere is printed from that original, never retyped — that's how versions stop disagreeing.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: When you tell the notebook "remember this!", it should write it in the right section, with the right heading, and give you a bookmark that actually opens to the page. There's one real notebook — copies are photocopies, not new notebooks. If the example page in the front of the notebook has a mistake, you fix the example first, because everyone copies the example.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: It's proper filing, dear. A document goes in one folder, under one name, and the index card points to it. Copies are made from the original, never from memory. The sample form pinned above the desk must itself be filled in perfectly — it's the one everyone imitates. And when someone says "it's filed," they hand you the reference slip; "it's in a pile somewhere, trust me" is not filing.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Run the seven-leg lifecycle and report leg status honestly. Author the single source artifact; generate projections; never hand-edit a projection. Validate the specimen against the gate in CI. Resolve paths from the projection code's canonical function only. Ship note + link + verification pair; treat a missing return mechanism as a defect in the protocol, not a gap in the report. Keep law-status and document-status as separate fields everywhere. Sweep canon for placeholders at the exact ref before any graduation claim, and verify content from live bytes, never from search.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body: Ten notes describe the note system learning to be a system: a lifecycle with named legs, a single source with derived views, a specimen held to its own standard, and a delivery that includes its own proof. The SN-0244→SN-0248 supersession is preserved inside the essence on purpose — a distillation that hides its own corrections teaches the next reader to trust a tidier history than the one that happened.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Notes are this system's memory, and a memory that files inconsistently, points nowhere, or exists in three disagreeing copies is worse than forgetting — it manufactures false confidence (SN-0244, SN-0248). For the reader, this essence is the trust layer under everything else in the corpus: if capture, placement, and delivery obey these rules, any other essence can be found, opened, and checked; if they don't, no other rule matters because its evidence can't be reached (SN-0258, SN-0188).

layers.name: How It Connects
layers.body: The lifecycle's COMMIT leg is executed under the claim-registry essence's discipline — register before staging, one number, one note (SN-0151) — and its registry writes are serialized per SN-0339. The Smart Link this essence delivers is defined by the director's canonical definition standing alone at SN-0254; this essence covers the delivery machinery (SN-0255, SN-0258), never the definition. The PROJECT leg's limits are set by the law essence's consent granularity (SN-0275): distilled anonymized wisdom may travel; identity may not.

layers.name: What's In It For You
layers.body: You get notes you can actually use later: one original, findable at a code-defined address, with a link handed back at the moment of capture that opens the real thing (SN-0256, SN-0258). Apply it by treating any "noted!" without a returned link as unfinished work, and any hand-edited copy as a defect report waiting to be filed — derive it or delete it (SN-0248, SN-0255).

layers.name: The Learning
layers.body: The system learned that its memory failures were never storage failures: notes existed; they were unfindable, unreturned, or multiplied into disagreement (SN-0255, SN-0248, SN-0190). The durable learning is that a memory system is a delivery system — capture is the easy leg, and the legs that make memory real are placement, derivation, and the returned link. The specimen rule generalizes furthest: whatever a system holds up as its example must pass the system's own gate, or the gate teaches the defect (SN-0249).

notes.title: Receipts That Resolve: Pins, Methods, and Virgin State
notes.subtitle: A receipt is a pointer a stranger can follow: its pin must resolve live (SN-0200), its SHA stays frozen while the branch moves on (SN-0206), its numbers are recomputed from the artifact rather than transcribed (SN-0212), its green is proven on virgin state (SN-0233), and it never claims 'done' before its evidence exists (SN-0172).

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: A receipt is a pointer a stranger can follow: its pin must resolve live (SN-0200), its SHA stays frozen while the branch moves on (SN-0206), its numbers are recomputed from the artifact rather than transcribed (SN-0212), its green is proven on virgin state (SN-0233), and it never claims 'done' before its evidence exists (SN-0172).

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: A receipt has to let a stranger re-find the exact thing you checked: the exact version, still existing, with numbers they can recompute and get the same answer. If you checked it on your own messy desk, check it again on a clean one. If the thing moved after you checked it, say "it moved" — don't pretend your old check covers the new version, and don't throw the old check away either. And never write "done" before the evidence exists.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: It's show-and-tell rules. "I saw it!" isn't enough — you have to show the class exactly where, and it has to still be there when they look. If you counted the marbles, someone else counting must get the same number — and you have to say HOW you counted. Writing "I finished my homework" before you've done it is lying, even if you do it later.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: A recipe card that says "tested" means someone cooked it — that exact version, in a clean kitchen, and wrote down what happened. If you change the recipe, you test again and say so; you don't let the old "tested" cover the new cake. A shopkeeper who writes the sale in the ledger before the customer pays has a ledger nobody can trust, however honest he is later.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Resolve every cited pin before repeating it. Bind every verdict to one frozen SHA; record later movement as delta. Recompute hashes, sizes, and counts from the artifact at verification time and fail-first the recomputation. Qualify repairs only on local+CI green at one SHA. Run acceptance checks in a fresh worktree before any regeneration. Re-derive PR body claims from the head at every mutation. Refuse counts without methods and done-records whose timestamps precede their evidence.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body: Ten notes, one idea: a receipt is a reproducible pointer, not a narrative. Every rule here exists because a specific receipt failed a specific stranger who tried to follow it — a pin that didn't exist, a body five drifts from its head, a green that only existed on warmed state. Follow this essence and your receipts survive being checked, which is the only kind of receipt there is.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Teams run on receipts — they are how work done in one seat becomes trust in another. A receipt that cannot be followed is worse than none: it spends trust it never earned (SN-0200's non-resolving pin). For the reader, this essence is the difference between a culture of 'trust me' and a culture of 'check me.'

layers.name: How It Connects
layers.body: It is the claim-registry essence's discipline pointed at evidence instead of identity (SN-0189's evidenced closure is its cousin). Its frozen-SHA rule anchors the scorecards the design family runs under the director's standing evaluation law (SN-0270, stands-alone), and its virgin-state rule pairs with the derived-artifact essence's clean-tree rule (SN-0327).

layers.name: What's In It For You
layers.body: You get receipts that survive being checked — which is the only kind worth issuing (SN-0212, SN-0233). Apply it by resolving every pin you cite before you cite it, and by writing the counting method next to every count you publish (SN-0165).

layers.name: The Learning
layers.body: Each rule here was bought by a receipt failing a specific stranger: a hash that didn't exist, a body five drifts from its head, a green that lived only on warmed state (SN-0200, SN-0185, SN-0233). The learning: write every receipt for the person who will try to disprove it — that reader is coming, and the receipt should be glad.

notes.title: Authorization Fails Closed: Governance That Cannot Self-Extend
notes.subtitle: Power in this system is granted narrowly, exercised through rails, and denied loudly: a policy cannot extend itself (SN-0215), a candidate law never governs until every activation condition holds at once (SN-0262), mutations read their grants and fail closed (SN-0223), a director's spoken word authorizes one act and never becomes precedent (SN-0324), and what is uncertain travels honestly labeled CANDIDATE (SN-0325).

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: Power in this system is granted narrowly, exercised through rails, and denied loudly: a policy cannot extend itself (SN-0215), a candidate law never governs until every activation condition holds at once (SN-0262), mutations read their grants and fail closed (SN-0223), a director's spoken word authorizes one act and never becomes precedent (SN-0324), and what is uncertain travels honestly labeled CANDIDATE (SN-0325).

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: A rule isn't real until the machine can't break it — until the wrong action is impossible, not just frowned upon. Turning a system "on" is never one switch; it's every condition true at once. Nobody's say-so — even the boss's, even in the moment — becomes a permanent permission afterward; it covers the one thing it covered.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: House rules work best when they're built into the house — a gate that won't open the wrong way, not just a sign saying "don't." One key never opens the treasure chest; you need all the keys turned together. "Mom said I could, that one time" doesn't mean "I can always." And if you don't know something, you say "I don't know yet" on the label — you never write down a guess as if it were a fact.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: A promise is fine, dear, but a lock is better — the best rules are the ones built into the door itself. No single key, and certainly no single person's word on a busy afternoon, should open everything forever. What's uncertain gets labeled uncertain, plainly.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Encode every ratified law as transitions that cannot be skipped; refuse single-flag activations by construction and test the refusal. Authenticate policy terms from the canonical record; hard-exclude protected paths. Read grants at mutation time, deny by default with named errors, carry authority refs on outputs. Ship fail-closed repairs with their provisioning sequenced. Verify shipped artifacts at full scope, not harness scope. Key trust on provenance and structure. Log verbal authorizations as single-act, precedent-free. Mark disclosed unknowns CANDIDATE; never upgrade them silently.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body: Nine notes are the governance stack of the era, from constitutional activation down to a classifier's false-positives: power is granted narrowly, exercised through rails, denied loudly, and never self-extended. The director's own doctrines that frame this stack — law-as-code (SN-0269), the ratified Scorecard Law (SN-0342), Learn-Then-Ten-X (SN-0183), do-it-now (SN-0282) — are NOT covered here; under the campaign standing-authority rule they stand alone as single-note law, and this essence is their machinery, not their replacement.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: A system that can extend its own authority, activate its own laws, or treat a spoken permission as permanent will eventually do all three by accident. These nine notes are the difference between governance as intention and governance as physics: self-extension made structural-impossible (SN-0215), activation made conjunctive (SN-0262), denial made the default (SN-0223). For the reader, this is the section of the corpus that decides whether every other rule in it can be trusted to still be the rule tomorrow.

layers.name: How It Connects
layers.body: Upward, this essence is the machinery beneath the director's standing doctrines that stand alone beside it (SN-0269, SN-0342, SN-0183, SN-0282). Sideways, it binds the claim-registry essence (the registry's write discipline is this essence's fail-closed pattern applied to numbers, SN-0339) and the proof-discipline essence (full-scope artifact checking, SN-0224, is the same suspicion that qualifies instruments, SN-0283). Downward, the consent granularity (SN-275) constrains what the note-system essence's PROJECT leg may ever do with a citizen's material (SN-0242).

layers.name: What's In It For You
layers.body: You get a system whose permissions you can reason about: if a capability exists, a grant created it; if a law governs, every activation condition demonstrably held; if you were told no, the denial has a name you can appeal (SN-0223). Apply it by asking, of any automated power: where is its grant, what is its activation conjunction, and what does its refusal look like? A power that cannot answer all three is not governed yet (SN-0215, SN-0262, SN-0223).

layers.name: The Learning
layers.body: The era's deepest governance lesson is that authority failures are quiet: nobody announces a self-extension or a borrowed precedent — they are discovered in audits (SN-0324) or not at all. So the learning is structural, not vigilance-based: build the refusal into the machine (a tested, refused single-flag flip, SN-0262), provision the grants with the gate (SN-0221), and label uncertainty at birth (SN-0325) — because a team cannot stay alert forever, but a rail does not get tired.

notes.title: Built Is Not Shipped: Deployment and Integration Truth
notes.subtitle: Built, shipped, and working are three different numbers, measured on the served surface: 11 tabs, 7 rich rooms, 4 placeholders (SN-0219); parity between deployed and verified is proven before code is touched (SN-0235); the consumer's actual contract outranks any proposed one (SN-0218 over SN-0214); and pipelines verify before they mutate, in enforced order (SN-0352).

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: Built, shipped, and working are three different numbers, measured on the served surface: 11 tabs, 7 rich rooms, 4 placeholders (SN-0219); parity between deployed and verified is proven before code is touched (SN-0235); the consumer's actual contract outranks any proposed one (SN-0218 over SN-0214); and pipelines verify before they mutate, in enforced order (SN-0352).

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: "We built it" and "customers can use it" are different sentences. Walk the actual product: count what's real and what's a placeholder with a nice name. If the live version might not be the version you tested, check that first — before rewriting code that may be fine. And in any automated process that changes production, the safety check goes before the change, every time, in the code's order — not in the order someone remembers.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: A drawing of a treehouse isn't a treehouse, and a treehouse with no ladder isn't finished either — you have to climb up and count the parts that really work. If your friend says "jump in!", you look before you leap. And if two teachers tell you opposite things in the hallway, you stop and ask until there's one answer — you don't just run faster.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: A recipe written is not a cake baked, dear, and a cake in your kitchen is not the cake in the shop window until you've looked at both. If the shop cake looks wrong, you check whether it's the same cake before you change the recipe. And no sensible cook puts the roast in before checking the oven works — order matters, and checking afterwards is just finding out what went wrong.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Report built/shipped/working as three numbers from a live walk. Hash or byte-compare deployed vs verified artifacts before any code change in a parity incident. Read the consumer's mount/call sites before writing or believing an integration contract. Treat prefill as zero completion. Audit pipeline step order for verify-before-mutate and refuse to run pipelines that mutate first. On contradiction, halt the lane, reconcile, and resume with exactly one run.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body: Seven notes defend one border: the border between the repository's story about the system and the system's actual behavior in production. Every rule is a place where that border was crossed unnoticed — placeholders counted as rooms, a proposal mistaken for a contract, a branch moved before its check. A cold reader with this essence inspects the border first, which is where production truth always lives.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Every production disappointment in this family came from crossing the border between the repository's story and the running system without noticing. For the reader — especially the director, who experiences only the served surface — this essence is the guarantee that 'done' describes the thing in front of a user, not the thing in a branch (SN-0219).

layers.name: How It Connects
layers.body: Its consumer-contract rule is the deployment half of the build-doctrine essence's module contract (SN-0142 ↔ SN-0218). Its pause-on-contradiction rule (SN-0353) pairs with the record essence's reconcile-before-accusing (SN-0354) from the same incident. Its parity rule is the proof essence's target-environment discipline (SN-0329) at deployment scale.

layers.name: What's In It For You
layers.body: You get honest status: three numbers instead of one adjective, and a redeploy instead of a rewrite when the gap is deployment, not code (SN-0235). Apply it by walking the served surface and counting what's real before reporting any build complete — placeholders have names too, and they don't count (SN-0219).
