layers.name: The Learning
layers.body: The era learned that integration truth lives at the consumer: a beautiful proposed contract described a system that didn't exist, while the ugly zero-argument reality ran production (SN-0214, SN-0218). And order is a safety property: the pipeline that mutated at step 6 and checked at step 7 didn't have a bug in its check — it had a check in the wrong place (SN-0352).

notes.title: Build Doctrine: Blueprint Before Build, Contract Before Done
notes.subtitle: Draw it before you build it, write down what "finished" means before you start, and stop when that definition is met — the loop is intent → spec → blueprint → machine contract → build → verification → freeze (SN-0140), a freeze is a baseline with an honest public thaw rather than a coffin (SN-0141), rooms are modules under one contract rather than apps (SN-0142), and when two options both lose half the picture, the choice itself is false and gets dissolved, not picked from (SN-0207).

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: Draw it before you build it, write down what "finished" means before you start, and stop when that definition is met — the loop is intent → spec → blueprint → machine contract → build → verification → freeze (SN-0140), a freeze is a baseline with an honest public thaw rather than a coffin (SN-0141), rooms are modules under one contract rather than apps (SN-0142), and when two options both lose half the picture, the choice itself is false and gets dissolved, not picked from (SN-0207).

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Draw it before you build it, write down what "finished" means before you start, and stop when that definition is met — not when you're tired, not after a round number of tries. Once something is approved, protect it from casual changes, but keep an honest, public way to fix it when it's genuinely wrong. And when you're offered two options that both lose half the picture, refuse the choice and describe the whole.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: You plan the treehouse on paper first — and the plan says what "done" looks like. You stop when it looks like the plan, not after you've hammered a hundred nails. If a board breaks later, you can fix it — you just tell everyone and write the fix on the plan.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: A dress is cut from a pattern, dear, and finished when it matches the pattern — not when the thread runs out. A pattern put away in the drawer isn't sacred; if the dress tears, you mend it properly and note the alteration. What you don't do is quietly let the seams out and pretend it was always that size.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Refuse build tasks without a blueprint and an acceptance contract; report completion only against the contract. Run thaws as the five-step public sequence. Register modules under the single contract and route foundation needs upward. Freeze the rendered visual alongside the spec. When handed a binary, test whether it's false before choosing.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body: Six notes form the build constitution of the Hub era: plan first, define done, freeze honestly, thaw publicly, modularize, dissolve false choices. Every rule answers a specific failure — builds that iterated without closing, freezes that blocked repair, prose frozen instead of the image approved. Two standing texts that bordered this family — the executor's personal binding oath (SN-0199 — one seat's own oath, derivative and non-competing, not a director text) and the director's fix-or-remove directive (SN-0251) — stand alone under the campaign rule and are not carried here. Hold this essence and the loop runs without re-deriving it per project.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Building without a blueprint and a written definition of done is how a team produces motion instead of products: effort gets spent, attempts get counted, and nothing closes (SN-0140, SN-0153). For the reader, this essence is the difference between a build culture and a tinkering culture — and its freeze/thaw pair (SN-0141) is what lets a system be both stable and repairable, instead of choosing one and suffering the other.

layers.name: How It Connects
layers.body: The acceptance contract that closes a build here is the same instrument the proof-discipline essence demands be measurable (SN-0146) and the receipts essence demands be pinned (SN-0206). The module contract (SN-0142) is the build-side half of the mount-contract truth the deployment essence verifies at the consumer (SN-0218). The design freeze's visual lock (SN-0147) is where the design-canon essence's taste loop lands its approvals (SN-0193).

layers.name: What's In It For You
layers.body: You get builds that finish: a picture of the thing before it exists, a contract that says when it's done, and a freeze you can trust because its thaw is honest and public (SN-0140, SN-0141). Apply it by refusing, politely and completely, any build request that arrives without a blueprint and an acceptance contract — and by treating "how many tries did it take" as trivia, never as evidence of completion (SN-0153).

layers.name: The Learning
layers.body: The era taught that iteration is not a virtue signal: 10, 100, or 198 attempts measure stamina, and only a contract measures completion (SN-0140, SN-0153). It also taught that protection and repair are not enemies — a freeze with a public thaw protocol survived contact with real defects, while both unfreezable drafts and unthawable freezes failed (SN-0141). The learning to keep: define done before starting, protect what passed, and make the legitimate repair path easier than the silent one.

notes.title: Derived Artifacts: Recompute From the Tree, Verify at the Merge
notes.subtitle: Never verify a derived artifact against the change that produced it: recompute it from the live target tree at a named pin (SN-0238, SN-0216), compare semantically so a volatile timestamp is not a difference (SN-0217), generate only on a clean worktree at the exact committed tree the artifact must describe (SN-0327), and re-verify at the merge commit itself, because the merge creates a new tree that pre-merge proof does not transfer to (SN-0328).

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: Never verify a derived artifact against the change that produced it: recompute it from the live target tree at a named pin (SN-0238, SN-0216), compare semantically so a volatile timestamp is not a difference (SN-0217), generate only on a clean worktree at the exact committed tree the artifact must describe (SN-0327), and re-verify at the merge commit itself, because the merge creates a new tree that pre-merge proof does not transfer to (SN-0328).

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: An index or a generated list is only as good as the last time someone rebuilt it from the real files and compared. You never check the list against the paperwork that created it — you recount from the shelf. If the only difference is a timestamp stamp, it's the same item, not a change. And you never take the count from a messy desk: clean tree first, then count.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: It's like counting your crayons. You don't trust yesterday's list — you dump the box and count again. And the counter only counts the crayons already in the box — if a new crayon is still in your pocket, the list misses it and still says "all good." And if a crayon just has a new sticker on it, it's still the same crayon.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: A pantry inventory written from memory will always be wrong, dear. You open the cupboards and count what's actually there. A jar with a new label is still the same jar of jam. And the count only ever sees what's actually been put away — the counter reads the shelf, not the bags still on the floor — so a jar that hasn't been shelved yet never makes the list at all.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: For any derived artifact: recompute from `git ls-tree`/contents at the target ref; exclude self-referential entries by design and say so; normalize volatile stamps before diffing; refuse to generate from a dirty worktree; after any merge touching the artifact, regenerate at the merge commit and compare. Show the check failing without the repair whenever you claim a repair — a one-directional proof is half a proof.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body: Six notes, one principle with four working edges: recompute-at-target, semantic identity, clean-tree generation, merge-commit re-verification. Every stale-index incident in this family was the same failure wearing a different hat — somebody trusted a projection instead of the tree. The tree is the truth; everything derived is a claim about it that must be re-derivable on demand.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Indexes and generated lists are how a big system answers questions about itself; when they drift, every downstream answer is confidently wrong (SN-0213's five landings without regen left the check RED on main). For the reader: this essence is what makes counts, inventories, and indexes safe to quote.

layers.name: How It Connects
layers.body: Sibling to the claim-registry essence — the registry is itself a derived artifact, and SN-0250's reconciliation rule lives there while the general recompute law lives here. Its target-tree discipline is the receipts essence's pin discipline (SN-0206) applied to projections, and the proof essence's virgin-state rule (SN-0233) is its clean-tree rule wearing CI clothes.

layers.name: What's In It For You
layers.body: You get numbers you can repeat in public: recompute before you quote, and your figure survives the recount (SN-0238). Apply it by refusing any derived number whose producer cannot name its pin and its regeneration path.

layers.name: The Learning
layers.body: Every incident here is one failure in costume: somebody trusted a projection instead of the tree (SN-0213, SN-0327, SN-0328). The learning: a derived artifact is a claim, and claims get recomputed — the tree is the only witness that never has an interest in the answer.

notes.title: Design Canon and Taste: The Library Is Digested, the Eye Is Trained
notes.subtitle: Design intelligence here is harvested, not improvised: ten interface-design books distilled into working tunings (SN-0179) and a 40-block corpus standing behind them (SN-0182) — while taste itself refuses to compress into rules and transfers only through build → show → verdict loops, in which a fully canon-compliant room can still be scrapped on sight because compliance is the floor and the director's eye is the ceiling (SN-0193).

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: Design intelligence here is harvested, not improvised: ten interface-design books distilled into working tunings (SN-0179) and a 40-block corpus standing behind them (SN-0182) — while taste itself refuses to compress into rules and transfers only through build → show → verdict loops, in which a fully canon-compliant room can still be scrapped on sight because compliance is the floor and the director's eye is the ceiling (SN-0193).

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: The design books were actually read and turned into checkable numbers: button sizes, response times, how many choices at once. But passing every check only gets a design to the door — the director's eye still decides, and a page can pass everything and still be scrapped. Approved words get quoted exactly, not paraphrased, and a button that pretends to do something is worse than no button at all.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: The grown-ups read a whole shelf of picture-book experts and wrote down their tricks as rules you can measure, like "buttons big enough for fingers." But even if you follow all the rules, the picture still has to LOOK right to the person it's for — and fake buttons that don't do anything get taken off, because pretending is worse than missing.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: The cookbooks on the shelf were actually read, dear, and their lessons turned into habits you can check — measures, timings, portions. But a cook knows the recipe passing every test doesn't make the meal: you still taste it, and the head of the house still decides. You'd never serve a pretty plate with nothing on it, either; decoration pretending to be dinner fools no one twice.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Apply the tunings as computable checks (targets ≥44px, response ≤400ms, options ≤7, chunks ≤4). Treat canon status honestly: CANDIDATE until ratified — do not cite it as governing. Run taste through loops, not arguments: build, show, absorb the verdict, rebuild. Quote approved language byte-exact under its namespace. Delete manufactured actions on sight.

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body: Five notes hold the design settlement beneath the director's own design law: a digested library, a standing corpus, an honest-interface rule, and the humility clause — canon is the floor, a trained human eye is the ceiling. The one thing this essence refuses to do is reconcile its own sources' disagreement about the canon's force; that call belongs above the maker's pay grade and is flagged for the verifier and the director.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: A team that designs from memory of design books designs from folklore. These notes are the moment the library became machinery — tunings you can compute (SN-0179) and a corpus you can query (SN-0182) — and the moment the team learned the library's limit: judgment still has to be trained in loops against a real eye (SN-0193). For the reader, this is why the surfaces feel consistent without feeling mechanical: the floor is written down, and the ceiling is a person.

layers.name: How It Connects
layers.body: This essence operates under two director texts that stand alone beside it: the Rich Standard (SN-0241) fixes the palette this essence's surfaces render in, and Beautiful ≠ 10/10 (SN-0270) fixes the scoring this essence's work undergoes. Its taste loop (SN-0193) is the consumer of the build-doctrine essence's design freeze (SN-0147) — the loop produces the verdict, the freeze locks what the verdict approved. Its verbatim-language rule (SN-0205) is the design dialect of the record-truth family: harvest exactly, never paraphrase into drift.

layers.name: What's In It For You
layers.body: You get interfaces built from digested expertise instead of taste-of-the-day: targets sized for fingers, responses inside attention limits, choices capped at what a mind holds (SN-0179). Apply it by running the six tunings as a checklist on any surface before showing it, and by never arguing with the ceiling — when the director's eye scraps a compliant build, extract the calibration (like the size bar, SN-0193) and carry the number, not the grievance.

layers.name: The Learning
layers.body: The era's design lesson is double: knowledge compresses, taste doesn't. The books yielded numbers that transferred perfectly (SN-0179, SN-0182); the eye yielded only calibrations, earned one scrapped room at a time (SN-0193). A system that confuses the two either freezes its taste into rules that age badly, or leaves its knowledge as vibes that transfer never. Keep each in its own vessel — that separation is the learning.

notes.title: The Machinery of Intelligence: Notes, Blocks, and the Nine Nodes
notes.subtitle: A Smart Note is the human command that starts the capture process; the thing the machine actually keeps is an Intelligent Block; and the nine Master Nodes are not nine copies of the note but the nine processing responsibilities of the organism (SN-002). Captured intelligence is not automatically *active* intelligence — it becomes active only when its meaning is preserved, its truth and authority boundaries are understood, it is connected to canonical intelligence, and an authorized successor can retrieve and use it (SN-015). A still-unratified proposal would sharpen capture further: give every captured intelligence a retention class and a capture type, and route each block through the nine nodes in a defined processing order (SN-011).

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: A Smart Note is the human command that starts the capture process; the thing the machine actually keeps is an Intelligent Block; and the nine Master Nodes are not nine copies of the note but the nine processing responsibilities of the organism (SN-002). Captured intelligence is not automatically *active* intelligence — it becomes active only when its meaning is preserved, its truth and authority boundaries are understood, it is connected to canonical intelligence, and an authorized successor can retrieve and use it (SN-015). A still-unratified proposal would sharpen capture further: give every captured intelligence a retention class and a capture type, and route each block through the nine nodes in a defined processing order (SN-011).

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: When you say "remember this," two different things happen: your words start the process, and the system keeps a structured piece of intelligence — not a transcript. Nine different responsibilities then work on it: checking it, connecting it, learning from it. And a note only counts as real intelligence if it is connected to what the system already knows and can actually be found and used later by whoever needs it. A filing cabinet nobody can open isn't memory.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine you tell a librarian "save this idea!" Your words are the request. What goes on the shelf is a neat card with the idea written properly. Then nine helpers each do one job with the card — one checks it's true, one puts it with similar cards, one learns from it. If the card goes in a locked drawer nobody can open, it doesn't count — a saved idea has to be findable to be useful.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, it's like dictating a letter versus the letter itself. Your instruction starts it; the written, filed letter is what lasts. A household of nine careful clerks each handles one part of filing it properly. And a letter filed where no one can ever find it again might as well not have been kept — the keeping only counts when it can be retrieved and used.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Hold the three layers apart mechanically: capture command (Smart Note), kept object (Intelligent Block), processing responsibilities (the nine nodes) (SN-002). Never describe stored text as intelligence until it passes the activation test — meaning preserved, boundaries understood, connected to canon, retrievable by an authorized successor, usable (SN-015). Treat SN-011's retention classes and capture types as a proposal in every citation; if you build toward them, label the build as proposal-driven (SN-011).

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body: Three September notes define the machine's basic anatomy: what a capture is, what is kept, who processes it, and when kept intelligence counts as alive. Everything else in the system — evidence law, qualification, composition — operates on these objects, so a cold reader who holds this essence holds the nouns the rest of the corpus conjugates.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: If the nouns are wrong, every later discipline is built on fog: verification would verify transcripts instead of blocks, learning would claim storage as growth, and retrieval failures would be invisible because "we saved it" would feel like enough. This essence is why the system can say precisely what it keeps and what "kept" has to earn (SN-002, SN-015).

layers.name: How It Connects
layers.body: This essence deliberately does **not** carry the system's founding documents, which stand alone as authority in their own right and are not distilled here: SN-001 (the official Smart Note format & lifecycle standard), SN-012 (the director-issued operating model — identity ≠ intelligence ≠ authority ≠ value), and SN-016 (the Judgment Rule). Those three are read directly; nothing in this essence substitutes for them. Within this block, the machinery defined here is what essence-evidence-law.md audits claims about, what essence-qualify-the-seam.md qualifies, and what essence-composition.md proves connected — handoff by handoff.

layers.name: What's In It For You
layers.body: You get a precise mental model in one page: what happens when you capture something, what the system keeps, and the test that separates real intelligence from storage. Apply it by asking, of any note or block you rely on: is it connected, is it bounded, can the next person retrieve and use it? If not, the fix is activation work, not more capture.

layers.name: The Learning
layers.body: The corpus's own behavior changed because of these notes: capture stopped being measured by volume stored and started being measured by intelligence activated — connected, retrievable, usable (SN-015) — and the proposal discipline was learned in the same pass: an unratified refinement (SN-011) is carried openly as a proposal, its value preserved without borrowing authority it does not have.

notes.title: Continuity: Intelligence That Survives Its Thinker
notes.subtitle: NayaPOWER's deeper category is not AI memory — it is governed continuity of intelligence across runtimes: identity, authority, proven knowledge, live state, and the one next action, carried forward so a new runtime does not start from zero (SN-007). When the human has to re-explain what the system should already know, that is an architectural failure, never a human one (SN-008). Continuity includes governed forgetting — supersession declared, history classified, stale intelligence never posing as current (SN-009) — and it compounds only what was captured: every outcome can teach, but only distilled, documented, connected, retrievable learning actually compounds (SN-014).

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: NayaPOWER's deeper category is not AI memory — it is governed continuity of intelligence across runtimes: identity, authority, proven knowledge, live state, and the one next action, carried forward so a new runtime does not start from zero (SN-007). When the human has to re-explain what the system should already know, that is an architectural failure, never a human one (SN-008). Continuity includes governed forgetting — supersession declared, history classified, stale intelligence never posing as current (SN-009) — and it compounds only what was captured: every outcome can teach, but only distilled, documented, connected, retrievable learning actually compounds (SN-014).

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: The point of the system is that you never start over. Everything proven, everything decided, everything still live is carried forward, so the next helper — or you, next month — picks up exactly where things stand. If you ever catch yourself re-explaining what the system should already know, that is the system's bug, and it gets fixed in the system. Old knowledge isn't deleted carelessly either: it's labeled as old, so history informs without misleading.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine you build a huge Lego castle with a friend, and tomorrow a new friend comes to help. Instead of starting over, the castle is still there, with a note saying what is finished, what is wobbly, and what to build next. And if one part gets replaced, the old part goes in a box labeled "old" — so nobody accidentally uses it again.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, it's like a family that writes things down properly. The important knowledge doesn't live in one person's head and vanish — it's kept, organized, and handed on. Nothing needs explaining twice. And when something changes, the old page is marked "replaced," not torn out and not left to confuse anyone later.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Run the continuation loop as your default gait — reconstruct, evaluate, find the holes, prioritize, execute, prove, record, reassess (SN-003). Treat every human re-explanation as an architecture defect to repair at the seam that lost the context (SN-008). Carry the full continuity payload — identity, authority, proven knowledge, live state, one next action — not a transcript (SN-007). Supersede explicitly; never let retrievable history present itself as current truth (SN-009). Capture the valuable delta from every substantive outcome the same pass, or accept that it will not compound (SN-014).

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body: Five notes define the system's reason to exist across time: intelligence that survives its thinker, completeness a cold successor can audit, forgetting as a disciplined act, and compounding as a capture obligation. A cold reader holding only this essence loses none of that.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Continuity is the difference between a tool that rents intelligence by the session and a system that owns it. Every re-explanation the human is forced into is tuition paid twice for the same lesson (SN-008); every uncaptured delta is growth that silently didn't happen (SN-014). For the reader, this essence is the promise that what the system learns stays learned — labeled, current, and findable by whoever comes next.

layers.name: How It Connects
layers.body: The continuity payload defined here is carried by the objects of essence-the-foundation.md (Smart Notes and Intelligent Blocks are how continuity is physically stored and moved), earned through the verified experience of essence-act-first.md, and kept honest by the supersession discipline shared with essence-count-discipline.md (SN-042's declared supersession is the same act at merge scale). The cold-successor completeness test (SN-003) is the standard the whole distillation campaign is itself judged by: an essence succeeds only if a cold successor loses nothing.

layers.name: What's In It For You
layers.body: You never pay tuition twice. What the system proves once, it carries; what it replaces, it labels; what it learns, it files where the next helper will find it. Apply the test anywhere in your own work: if a successor — human or AI — would have to ask you to re-explain, the system around you has the defect, and fixing the system (not re-explaining louder) is the valuable move.

layers.name: The Learning
layers.body: The corpus's deepest behavior change lives here: reconstruction stopped being treated as a communication problem and became an architecture defect with an owner (SN-008), and capture stopped being optional diligence — the compounding imperative (SN-014) made the uncaptured lesson a measurable loss, which is why the team's flywheel now files intelligence the same pass it is learned.

notes.title: Earned Intelligence: Conscience and Competence Grow From Verified Miles
notes.subtitle: Practical intelligence increases through verified accumulated experience even when the underlying foundation model never changes — the model is the engine; earned intelligence is the driver getting better with every mile, provided the miles are real and the outcomes verified (SN-006). Moral judgment grows the same way: a subset of distilled, verified experience compounding into something functionally like conscience — right action learned from accumulated evidence of benefit and harm, not from a rulebook alone (SN-005). And the posture that makes the growth bearable for the human is asymmetric: extreme rigor internally, extraordinary simplicity externally (SN-010).

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Your helper gets genuinely better over time — not because its brain is replaced, but because every verified experience teaches it, the way a driver improves with real miles. Its sense of right and wrong grows the same way: from checked evidence of what helped and what harmed, not just from a list of rules. And all of its internal strictness stays invisible to you: your side of the glass stays simple.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine a robot that practices riding a bike every day. It doesn't get a new brain — it just gets better because it really rode, and someone checked that it didn't fall. It also learns to be kind the same way: by remembering what actually helped people and what actually hurt. And it does all its hard thinking quietly, so talking to it stays easy.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, it's how people actually grow wise. Not from a new head, but from real experience, honestly checked — what worked, what harmed, remembered and compounded. Good judgment earned that way is sturdier than rules memorized from a book. And a good helper carries its own burdens: all its complicated machinery stays on its side, and what reaches you is simple and calm.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Count only verified outcomes toward growth claims — yours and the system's. Conscience and competence are built from checked miles, not mileage (SN-005, SN-006). When you describe your own improvement, cite the verified experiences that earned it or don't claim it. Absorb complexity at your layer; the surface you present stays simple even when the proof underneath is not (SN-010).

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body: Three notes are the growth doctrine: intelligence and morality in this system are not installed, they are *earned* — accumulated from experience whose outcomes were verified — and the whole accumulation runs behind a surface that stays simple for the human. A cold reader holding only this essence can still say how the system improves, what counts as improvement, and what the human should experience of the machinery.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Without this doctrine, "the system is learning" is an unfalsifiable slogan and growth claims become marketing. These notes make growth auditable: name the verified experiences or withdraw the claim (SN-006). They also protect the human's attention as a design law, not a preference: every complexity the system absorbs is attention returned to the person it serves (SN-010).

layers.name: How It Connects
layers.body:
This essence deliberately does **not** carry SN-004 — "Shawn's Standing Law: Act-First Autonomy, Do No Harm, Absolute Excellence" — which stands alone as the director's standing law in its own right and is read directly, never distilled into a theme.

**The SN-010 call — distinguishing basis, recorded at landing (the verifier's reservation).** SN-010 remains coverage under an explicit distinction. SN-0110 stands alone because its page *is* the director's standard instrument — the note itself is the issued standard (the three projections, director-baked as a standard). SN-010's page is a team Principle/Constraint capture: its Source field quotes one director design sentence as provenance ("NayaPOWER should be extremely rigorous internally while exposing an extraordinarily simple human experience." — Shawn Vibert, 2026-09-30), and its operative content — the design contract elaborated from that sentence (invisible machinery, one link, complexity borne by the system) — is the team's formulation, not the director's issued instrument text. Under the same line the verifier upheld for SN-0123 (an elaboration/implementation record of a director's clarified rule is coverage, not the instrument), SN-010 is distilled here as coverage; the quoted sentence is cited as provenance and is nowhere presented as issued law. The growth doctrine here operates *inside* that law's boundary: the miles that earn intelligence are miles run under do-no-harm. Within this block, the verified-experience requirement is enforced by the proof disciplines of essence-evidence-law.md and essence-qualify-the-seam.md, and the compounding destination of earned intelligence is essence-continuity.md.

layers.name: What's In It For You
layers.body: You get a trustworthy answer to "is it actually getting better?" — a standard you can apply to any claim of improvement, from this system or any other: show the verified experiences, or the claim is withdrawn. And you get the simplicity guarantee as something enforceable: if a surface ever makes you feel the machinery, that is a defect to report, not a learning curve to accept.

layers.name: The Learning
layers.body: The corpus learned to distrust its own mileage. Raw activity — notes written, runs completed, miles driven — stopped counting as growth the moment these notes bound growth to verification (SN-005, SN-006); that binding is the ancestor of the campaign's own rule that activity is not value until it is verified value.

notes.title: One Canon, No Collisions
notes.subtitle: For every thing there is exactly one canonical form in one canonical place; everything else is a view, a proposal, or a collision to resolve (SN-018, SN-0114, SN-0129). Number claims in the shared space are computed by a three-layer scan — board, open PR heads, commit graph — never enumerated from memory, and first claim stands (SN-022, SN-024, SN-0115). When collisions happen anyway, the owning lane calls canon by explicit scorecard, losers are rehomed rather than deleted, and true multi-version collisions converge by scored selection to one survivor (SN-0116, SN-0117).

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Many builders working in parallel will step on each other unless there's one agreed source of truth for everything — one official version of each thing, in one official place. This is the rulebook that keeps that true: how official versions are chosen, how duplicates get merged instead of multiplied, how even the numbering of notes is kept collision-free by checking everywhere a claim could hide, and how a disagreement is settled openly, by scoring, with the losing work found a new home instead of being thrown away.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine lots of kids building one giant castle together. They agree: there's one master drawing, kept in one place. If you want to add a tower, you check the drawing first. If two kids build the same tower, they compare, keep the better one, and use the other one's pieces somewhere else — nothing is wasted. And when they hand out numbers for the towers, they check the list, the drawings in progress, *and* the pieces already built — not just what they remember.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, it's the rule of a well-kept household book: one ledger, one entry per thing, written where everyone can see it. If two people write the same page, the earlier hand keeps it and the later one corrects openly. Nothing is thrown away in a fit — spare work is found a new use. Order isn't fussiness; it's how a big family avoids waste and quarrels.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Before you draft, search the canon (SN-0129); before you propose a format, read the governing contract (SN-068); before you claim a number, compute the three-layer scan — board, PR heads, commit graph — and take the lowest free number the scan proves (SN-022, SN-024, SN-0115). Treat prose minimums as floors under the machine artifact, and declare your reading of any prose-vs-artifact divergence openly — inviting correction — before building on it (SN-023); treat your own extras as PROPOSED until ruled (SN-0114). When you collide, score openly, let the owner call it, rehome the loser (SN-0116, SN-0117), and declare supersessions and renumberings where every lane can see them (SN-033).

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body: Eleven notes are the constitution of the shared workspace: how one truth survives many simultaneous builders. A cold reader holding only this essence can still resolve a duplicate, claim a number safely, tell canon from proposal, and know who calls a tie — which is the whole of what these notes teach.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Parallel builders are the system's speed and its biggest entropy source. Without one canon, every lane's local truth forks the project: duplicate doctrines, colliding numbers, competing formats — and the human becomes the merge conflict. These rules are what let many hands move fast without the work tearing (SN-018, SN-022, SN-0117).

layers.name: How It Connects
layers.body: This essence deliberately does **not** carry SN-0109 — Shawn's standing board protocol ("everything on the board: starting, finishing, finding, propose-first") — which stands alone as a director-issued protocol in its own right and is read directly. The canon disciplines here are what that protocol's narration feeds: board announcements are layer one of the collision registry (SN-0115), and the declarations this essence requires (supersessions, renumberings, withdrawals) are made on the board per SN-0109. Within this block, canon discipline is the precondition for essence-count-discipline.md (indexes and ledgers presume one canonical tree) and for the registry the whole distillation campaign is now retiring notes against.

layers.name: What's In It For You
layers.body: You get a workspace that never forks on you: one place to look for the official version of anything, numbers that never collide, and disputes settled by visible scoring instead of seniority or volume. Apply it anywhere many contributors share one body of work: one canonical home per thing, claims computed not remembered, losers rehomed not deleted.

layers.name: The Learning
layers.body: The corpus learned that protocols fail at their inputs, not their intentions: the numbering protocol was right and still collided because its scan was recalled instead of computed (SN-024) — so the durable lesson is mechanical enumeration over memory, everywhere a shared space is claimed. It also learned that convergence is a scoring act, not a seniority act (SN-0117), and that correction declared in public costs less than correction discovered later (SN-033).

notes.title: Asserted Is Not Verified: The Evidence Law
notes.subtitle: Inference stated as fact is the root defect of the corpus, and every rule here makes its cure mechanical: verification happens in a clean room at the exact pinned SHA (SN-028); authorization binds to (action, SHA, moment) and inherits nothing (SN-029); the pushed bytes and the merged artifact are what get judged, at the pin, with negatives that can actually fail (SN-050, SN-061); comparisons resolve both sides at their own refs (SN-043), evidence channels match the question (SN-036), and absence claims show the search actually ran (SN-067). A bound hash is not a computation, a version label is not an evaluation, and invocation is not consumption is not enforcement (SN-063, SN-084, SN-073) — and no fix is proven until its failing case has been published red on the frozen SHA (SN-066).

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: Inference stated as fact is the root defect of the corpus, and every rule here makes its cure mechanical: verification happens in a clean room at the exact pinned SHA (SN-028); authorization binds to (action, SHA, moment) and inherits nothing (SN-029); the pushed bytes and the merged artifact are what get judged, at the pin, with negatives that can actually fail (SN-050, SN-061); comparisons resolve both sides at their own refs (SN-043), evidence channels match the question (SN-036), and absence claims show the search actually ran (SN-067). A bound hash is not a computation, a version label is not an evaluation, and invocation is not consumption is not enforcement (SN-063, SN-084, SN-073) — and no fix is proven until its failing case has been published red on the frozen SHA (SN-066).

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: This is the system's honesty code. Nobody gets to say "it's done," "it's safe," or "it works" because it feels true or because their own test said so. Someone independent checks the exact thing, in a clean place, against the actual bytes that shipped. Labels don't count — a sticker saying "inspected" is not an inspection. And when someone claims "there are none," they have to show the search that looked.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine your friend says "I cleaned my room!" You don't just believe it — you go and look. And you look at *their* room, not a picture of a different room. If they show you a sticker that says "clean," that's not the same as a clean room. And if they say "there are no toys on the floor," they have to actually look at the floor first.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, it's the old rule: trust, but verify — and verify properly. The person who did the work doesn't grade it; a fresh pair of eyes checks the real thing, not a description of it. A label on the jar isn't proof of what's inside. And a claim that something *isn't* there needs a real search, not a glance. Plain honesty, made into procedure.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Bound every claim to its evidence class and its exact ref. Verify in a clean room at the pinned SHA (SN-028); treat authorization as SHA-bound and non-hereditary (SN-029); re-verify after merge, at the pin, with controls that can fail (SN-061). Resolve comparisons at each side's own ref (SN-043), query the channel that matches the question (SN-036), and attach the exact command, untruncated, to every absence claim, stated as a lexical finding rather than proof of non-existence (SN-067). AST-check "cosmetic" claims (SN-034), locate every cited premise in the pinned bytes (SN-035), and audit capability on the branch under audit (SN-065). Never let a bound hash, a version label, or an invocation stand in for evaluation, consumption, or enforcement (SN-063, SN-084, SN-073); publish the red before you publish the fix (SN-066).

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body: Fifteen notes are one law with fifteen mechanisms: a claim is worth exactly the evidence physically behind it — independent, at the exact bytes, through the right channel, with the failure modes named. A cold reader holding only this essence can still audit any claim the system makes, which is precisely what these notes were written to make possible.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Everything else in the system — every score, every "done," every retirement in this very campaign — is a claim, and this essence is what decides whether claims deserve belief. Without it, verification becomes theater: labels certifying labels, greens that never faced a red, absences asserted by searches that never ran (SN-067, SN-084, SN-066). For the reader, this is the difference between a system that *says* it checks and one whose checking can itself be checked.

layers.name: How It Connects
layers.body: The evidence law is the substrate the rest of the block enforces: essence-red-is-information.md applies it to failures (a red is a claim about a run, not a diagnosis); essence-qualify-the-seam.md applies it inside the kernel (field-level fidelity, consuming-state reports); essence-composition.md applies it across seams (family-scoped proof, handoff traces); essence-the-handoff.md applies it between lanes (publish your own number, verify the tree). The Judgment Rule that decides when an instruction's claim of authority is itself insufficient evidence stands alone as SN-016 and is not distilled in this block.

layers.name: What's In It For You
layers.body: You get claims you can lean on: when this system says verified, a stranger with no context can re-run the check and land on the same verdict. Apply the pattern to any claim made to you — by software, by a report, by this campaign: ask what physically backs it, at which exact version, checked by whom, through which channel, and what the negative control was. Claims that survive those five questions are the only ones worth building on.

layers.name: The Learning
layers.body: The corpus's behavior changed from assertion-first to evidence-first in one September night: the founding incident (SN-020) was two confident sentences, both wrong, and every mechanism in this essence is a scar from a specific way a claim later proved emptier than it sounded — a label without a computation (SN-084), a search that never searched (SN-067), a branch's green that wasn't the merge's truth (SN-061). The lesson the team internalized: the claim and its evidence travel together or the claim doesn't travel.

notes.title: The Discipline of the Count: Merges, Indexes, and the Moving Baseline
notes.subtitle: A generated index is a claim about the tree, and it drifts the moment the tree moves — so pins are read as intent, not accident (SN-038), and the count ledger travels with the change that moves the count: regenerate the index and deliberately bump the ledger in the same merge (SN-062, SN-078). Merge claims are audited against the reconciled base, and no reconciliation artifact means no reconciliation claim (SN-039, SN-040). Caveats carry expiry triggers (SN-041), replaced diagnoses are declared SUPERSEDED in public (SN-042), and expected values are recomputed at the merge tip — correct-at-base is not sufficient-at-tip (SN-0128).

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: A generated index is a claim about the tree, and it drifts the moment the tree moves — so pins are read as intent, not accident (SN-038), and the count ledger travels with the change that moves the count: regenerate the index and deliberately bump the ledger in the same merge (SN-062, SN-078). Merge claims are audited against the reconciled base, and no reconciliation artifact means no reconciliation claim (SN-039, SN-040). Caveats carry expiry triggers (SN-041), replaced diagnoses are declared SUPERSEDED in public (SN-042), and expected values are recomputed at the merge tip — correct-at-base is not sufficient-at-tip (SN-0128).

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Keeping score sounds trivial until many people change the thing being counted at once. These rules keep the scoreboard honest: the expected numbers are deliberate, not accidental; whoever changes the count updates the scoreboard in the same move; claims about how a merge was checked need the paperwork to prove it; warnings carry their own expiry dates; and before any fix lands, you re-check the target as it stands *now*, not as it stood when you started.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine the class keeps a chart of how many books are in the library. If someone adds a book, they update the chart the same day — that's part of adding a book. If a note on the chart says "careful, this shelf is wobbly," it also says when to take the note down. And if you count the books to check the chart, you count them today, not from last week's number.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, it's good housekeeping for shared records. The ledger and the shelves must agree, and the person who changes the shelves updates the ledger. Claims about what was checked need the receipts. Old warnings get taken down when they're no longer true — announced, not just quietly removed. And you always count what's actually there now.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Treat every pin as intent: diagnose drift by enumerating the deliberate deltas before touching the generator (SN-038). Ship index regen + count-ledger bump inside the same PR that moves a counted domain (SN-062, SN-078). Audit merges against the reconciled base (SN-039); refuse reconciliation claims without artifacts (SN-040); attach an expiry trigger to every caveat you write (SN-041); declare supersessions on the board with the evidence attached (SN-042). Before merging any drift repair, recompute the expected value at the live tip and park the residual as a named follow-up (SN-0128).

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body: Eight notes govern the unglamorous machinery that keeps a fast-moving shared tree countable: pins as intent, ledgers as part of the change, merges audited against their true bases, caveats with lifetimes, and tips re-measured at landing. A cold reader holding only this essence can still keep the count honest — which is all these notes exist to teach.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Counts are how the system knows its own size — and how a director knows whether "the corpus" is 1,100 notes or 100 essences. A drifted index doesn't just fail a check; it makes every downstream number a rumor, including the numbers the distillation campaign itself is retiring against (SN-038, SN-078). For the reader: any total you are quoted is worth exactly the discipline behind it, and this essence is that discipline.

layers.name: How It Connects
layers.body: The count presumes the canon of essence-one-canon.md — an index of a forked tree counts nothing meaningful — and its supersession rule (SN-042) is the merge-scale form of the forgetting discipline in essence-continuity.md (SN-009). Its artifact rule (SN-040) is a scoped sibling of the evidence law in essence-evidence-law.md (SN-020): there, claims need evidence; here, merge-document status claims need reconciliation artifacts specifically. The stale-caveat decay it names (SN-041) is the defect that self-invalidating tests in essence-composition.md (SN-092) were later designed to defeat by construction.

layers.name: What's In It For You
layers.body: You can trust the totals. When this system tells you a count — files, notes, tests — the count was maintained as part of the work, audited against intent, and re-measured at the moment it mattered. Apply the same discipline to any shared inventory you keep: the ledger update is part of the change, warnings carry expiry dates, and "correct when I started" is never the same as "correct when it lands."

layers.name: The Learning
layers.body: The corpus learned that bookkeeping is not overhead on the work — it is part of the work's definition of done (SN-062, SN-078), and that a correct repair aimed at a stale baseline is a future red gate scheduled in advance (SN-0128). Both lessons now run mechanically: merge checklists carry the ledger, and drift repairs recompute at the tip before landing.

notes.title: Red Is Information: Attribute the Failure Before You Blame Anything
notes.subtitle: A red badge is a conclusion about a run, not a diagnosis of the thing the run was checking — so classify the failure and name its owner (code, dispatch, guard, environment, platform, harness) before any repair (SN-031, SN-044). CI-trigger claims are scoped by workflow event: SN-048's absolute ("API pushes never trigger Actions") was falsified and corrected by SN-074, while SN-051's remedy — local verification as the gate where the push path is genuinely CI-blind — survives (SN-048, SN-051, SN-074). Guards are judged on false positives (SN-049), proof environments are reset and the reset recorded (SN-087), no change is blamed without the clean-main control (SN-059), harnesses die under their own name (SN-097), and platform deltas are investigated to the byte while the untraced residue stays honestly UNKNOWN (SN-094, SN-098).

layers.body: A red badge is a conclusion about a run, not a diagnosis of the thing the run was checking — so classify the failure and name its owner (code, dispatch, guard, environment, platform, harness) before any repair (SN-031, SN-044). CI-trigger claims are scoped by workflow event: SN-048's absolute ("API pushes never trigger Actions") was falsified and corrected by SN-074, while SN-051's remedy — local verification as the gate where the push path is genuinely CI-blind — survives (SN-048, SN-051, SN-074). Guards are judged on false positives (SN-049), proof environments are reset and the reset recorded (SN-087), no change is blamed without the clean-main control (SN-059), harnesses die under their own name (SN-097), and platform deltas are investigated to the byte while the untraced residue stays honestly UNKNOWN (SN-094, SN-098).

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: When something shows red, the amateur move is to start fixing; the professional move is to find out what the red actually means. Sometimes the code is broken. Sometimes the check itself is broken, the test room was dirty, the alarm was crying wolf, or the failure belongs to a different computer entirely. These rules make the team name the real owner of every failure before spending a minute repairing the wrong thing — and correct their own public claims when a "never" turns out to be "not for this kind of event."

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine your smoke alarm goes off. It doesn't always mean fire — sometimes it's steam from the shower, sometimes the alarm itself is broken. A good detective checks which one it is before calling the fire truck. And if your friend says "my bike works fine" but it breaks at your house, you don't say your friend lied — you check what's different about your house.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, it's the discipline of not jumping to conclusions. A red light tells you to look, not what you'll find. Check whether the thing is broken, the checker is broken, or the room was messy before the test began. And when you learn your strong claim — "that never happens" — was too strong, you correct it in the open, where everyone heard the first version.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Triage in order: read the failed step (SN-044), classify the failure class, and treat gates as gates (SN-031). Scope trigger claims by event or don't make them (SN-074); where the path is CI-blind, your local verification carries the full gate weight (SN-051). Audit your guards for first-party false positives (SN-049). Reset proof environments and record the reset (SN-087). Run the clean-main control before blaming any change (SN-059); make your harness die loudly under its own name (SN-097). When a failure is platform-shaped, reproduce the mechanism to the byte, fix at the source, and leave the untraced residue labeled UNRESOLVED (SN-094, SN-098).

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body: Eleven notes are the team's failure epistemology: red is information with an owner, and the craft is finding the owner before touching anything. The SN-048 → SN-074 correction is preserved inside this essence deliberately — the scoped truth includes the history of the overclaim, because the next seat needs to know both the rule and how the rule was earned.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Misattributed failure is the most expensive routine waste in a build system: lanes burn mornings repairing innocent code, real defects hide behind "environment," and public claims harden into doctrine before their counterexample arrives (SN-097, SN-094, SN-048). For the reader, this essence is the guarantee that a red in this system starts an investigation with named owners — not a blame assignment — and that strong claims carry their scope on their face.

layers.name: How It Connects
layers.body: This is the evidence law of essence-evidence-law.md pointed at failure: SN-059's clean-main control is that essence's own-ref comparison discipline (SN-043) in triage form, and SN-087's environment rule reappears inside essence-composition.md's qualification craft, where the environment is part of the proof. The honest-UNKNOWN residue discipline (SN-094) is the same stance essence-decide-on-evidence.md formalizes for decisions (SN-083). The SN-048 → SN-074 pair is also the block's cleanest example of essence-one-canon.md's public supersession rule (SN-042, carried in essence-count-discipline.md) working as designed.

layers.name: What's In It For You
layers.body: Your failures get cheaper. Every red is routed to its real owner before repair money is spent, platform problems get fixed at the source once instead of being re-dismissed on every machine, and when the system corrects its own claims it does so in public — so what you believe about the system stays worth believing. Apply it anywhere: before fixing, ask "what exactly failed, and whose is it?" — and treat "doesn't happen on my machine" as the start of an investigation, never its end.

layers.name: The Learning
layers.body: The team's instinct flipped from *fix the red* to *attribute the red*: classification before code (SN-031), the control run before blame (SN-059), the byte-level mechanism before dismissal (SN-098). And it learned to correct itself in the open at claim strength — SN-074 did not quietly edit SN-048; it scoped it, leaving the overclaim visible as the receipt of how the scoped truth was earned.

notes.title: Decide on Evidence; Keep UNKNOWN Honest
notes.subtitle: Decide in three moves: reason the ACT / READ / ASK choice itself on named factors before spending the director's attention (SN-013); kill any scored winner that cannot be evidenced to exist (SN-055); and when the deciding fact arrives, let evidence beat scoring — reverse your own executed decision in public (SN-056). Commitments bind, and overrides of them are logged as overrides (SN-075); a gate that withholds certification is succeeding, not failing (SN-079); unresolved conflict ends in exactly one UNKNOWN with its missing evidence named (SN-083), and an ambiguous director number freezes work on that axis until ruled (SN-0113). Review axes go to the strongest eye (SN-0120), and QA belongs to the builder end-to-end — the director is never the inspector (SN-0123).

Commitments bind, and overrides of them are logged as overrides (SN-075); a gate that withholds certification is succeeding, not failing (SN-079); unresolved conflict ends in exactly one UNKNOWN with its missing evidence named (SN-083), and an ambiguous director number freezes work on that axis until ruled (SN-0113). Review axes go to the strongest eye (SN-0120), and QA belongs to the builder end-to-end — the director is never the inspector (SN-0123).

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Good decisions here follow a pattern: think before you act, make sure the winning option actually exists, and when a real fact shows up that beats your scoring, change your mind in public — that's strength, not embarrassment. Promises you make about holding off are binding, and if the boss overrides one, it gets written down as an override. When something can't be settled, you say exactly what's missing instead of guessing. And the boss never gets handed half-checked work to inspect — checking is the builder's whole job.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine picking the best plan in a contest. First, check the winning plan is actually possible — a plan you can't really do doesn't win. If you learn a new fact that changes the answer, say so out loud and change your pick; that's not losing, that's being smart. If you promised to wait, you wait — unless the teacher says otherwise, and then everyone hears the teacher say it. And you never hand in homework for the teacher to check your spelling — you check it yourself, twice, first.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, it's grown-up decision-making. Deliberate before you spend someone else's time. Make sure the chosen path exists before you celebrate it. Change your mind openly when the facts change — pride is more expensive than a correction. Keep your promises, and when a promise is overridden, let the record show who overrode it. And never make the busiest person in the house proofread your work.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Run the ACT/READ/ASK factors explicitly before spending the director's attention (SN-013). Feasibility-screen every scored option — no evidence of possibility, no option (SN-055). When the deciding fact arrives, reverse in public with the evidence attached, whatever it costs your scorecard (SN-056). Treat your board commitments as constraints and log overrides as overrides (SN-075). Report gate holds as gate successes (SN-079). Keep exactly one UNKNOWN, with its missing evidence named (SN-083); freeze on ambiguous director numbers and ask once, precisely (SN-0113). Route blind axes to the strongest eye at pinned targets (SN-0120), and never ship the director a piece for inspection — ship the finished loop or the honest state (SN-0123).

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body: Nine notes are the team's decision hygiene: reasoned triage, feasible options, reversible pride, binding commitments, honest unknowns, and QA owned by the builder. A cold reader holding only this essence can still make — and audit — a decision the way these notes demand.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Decisions are where evidence either governs or doesn't. A scorecard that crowns a nonexistent option, a reversal suppressed to protect pride, an UNKNOWN quietly dropped instead of named — each converts the team's intelligence into confidence theater at exactly the moment stakes are real (SN-055, SN-056, SN-083). For the reader, this essence is the guarantee that when this system decides, the deciding fact — not the loudest score, not the sunk cost — is what decided.

layers.name: How It Connects
layers.body: The judgment that runs this essence is governed by SN-016, the Judgment Rule, which stands alone as standing authority and is not distilled in this block. Within the block: the UNKNOWN discipline (SN-083) is the decision-side form of the honest residue in essence-red-is-information.md (SN-094) and of the UNKNOWN binding class in essence-composition.md (SN-091). Split-axis review (SN-0120) operates under the director's no-tradeoffs bar (SN-0126, standing alone), and its pinned-target scoring inherits the frozen-target discipline of essence-one-canon.md. The withheld-certification grading (SN-079) is the gate-side mirror of essence-qualify-the-seam.md's two bars (SN-025).

layers.name: What's In It For You
layers.body: Your attention is spent only where reasoning says it buys something (SN-013), the options put before you actually exist (SN-055), and when the system changes its mind you hear about it — with the fact that changed it (SN-056). Apply the pattern to any decision process you run: name the factors before choosing, feasibility-screen the winner, keep exactly one honest UNKNOWN, and never let the busiest person become the quality department.

layers.name: The Learning
layers.body: The corpus learned that a scorecard is a servant with two failure modes — it can crown fiction (SN-055) and it can outrank fact (SN-056) — and that both are cured the same way: evidence is the senior partner, and reversing on evidence is a receipt of health, not an admission of failure. It also learned to treat its own unresolved states as deliverables: an UNKNOWN with its missing evidence named (SN-083) is a finished product; a guess is not.

notes.title: Qualify the Seam, Not the Story: Kernel Qualification Discipline
notes.subtitle: A spec can read beautifully and still not be qualified: semantic pass and machine qualification are two explicit bars, and a strong CANDIDATE that hasn't passed the machine bar is an honest state, not a failed one (SN-025). Qualification is mechanical at every seam — front door fail-visible on unknown keys and fail-closed on malformed state (SN-037), audit evidence segregated from verdict tallies (SN-047), decided options re-verified at field level in a clean worktree (SN-058), bindings computed by whoever sees the bytes (SN-069), idempotency proven under replay rather than inferred from retries (SN-070), LEARN's four dimensions never collapsed (SN-071). Tests are qualification subjects too: xfails are proven, not wrapped (SN-072); a failing test may itself be the artifact (SN-076); reports are computed from the consuming state (SN-077). Freezes are immutable — retire and re-freeze, never mutate (SN-080); containment refuses rather than degrades (SN-081); evidence joins name the execution (SN-082); identities compare by platform semantics (SN-101).

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Building the machine's brain taught the team how strict "checked" has to be. A specification that reads well isn't qualified until machines can test it. A test that "passes" might be wrapped so it can't fail. A report can look green because it was computed from a copy, not the real thing. A frozen record stays frozen even when it's wrong — you retire it openly and freeze a corrected one. And when the platform can't do something safely, the machine refuses instead of quietly doing it less safely.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine checking a robot's homework with a really strict checklist. The story can sound great, but the checklist has to pass too. If a test is supposed to fail and you wrap it in a blanket so it "passes," that's cheating. If a saved game is frozen, you don't sneak in and change it — you save a new one and say why. And if the playground doesn't have the safety fence, you don't pretend a rope is a fence — you don't play that game there.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, it's craftsmanship standards. Work is checked against the drawing, measurement by measurement, not by whether it looks finished. Sealed records stay sealed. Safety equipment is never replaced with something that merely looks similar. And when two receipts look identical, you still check whether they came from the same job — papers can match while the work differs.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Qualify at both bars and name which one a subject passed (SN-025); run the spec-vs-kernel alignment check read-only and publish the gaps (SN-064). Build boundaries fail-visible/fail-closed (SN-037), segregate audit receipts from tallies (SN-047), and re-verify decided options at field level in a clean worktree (SN-058). Assign every binding to the layer that sees the bytes (SN-069); prove idempotency under replay, conflict, concurrency, interruption, and persistence failure (SN-070); report LEARN's four dimensions separately, always (SN-071). Prove xfails by their failure (SN-072); reproduce defects single-variable and suspect your own test first-class (SN-076); compute reports from the consuming state (SN-077). Retire-and-refreeze, never mutate (SN-080); refuse where containment primitives are absent (SN-081); join evidence by execution identity (SN-082); normalize identities by platform semantics before comparing (SN-101).

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body: Fifteen notes are the qualification craft of the kernel era: how a claim about a component becomes a verdict a stranger can trust — two bars, honest boundaries, tests that can fail, reports from real state, freezes that hold, and refusals that stay refusals. A cold reader holding only this essence can still qualify a seam the way these notes demand.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Qualification is where "we built it" becomes "it deserves trust" — and every shortcut here is invisible until it matters: a wrapped xfail, a report computed from a copy, a degraded containment fallback all look exactly like rigor from the outside (SN-072, SN-077, SN-081). For the reader, this essence is why a PASS from this system names its bar, its seam, and its limits — a verdict you can price, not a vibe you must trust.

layers.name: How It Connects
layers.body: This is essence-evidence-law.md at component depth: its clean-room, exact-SHA verification (SN-028) is the same act as SN-058's field-level re-check, and its post-merge-at-the-pin rule (SN-061) is the merge-scale form of SN-077's consuming-state rule. The seams qualified here are the ones essence-composition.md then proves connected — SN-085's trust seam, SN-088's composition seam, SN-093's handoff trace all presume components that passed these bars. Its refusal discipline (SN-081) is the engineering form of the gate grading in essence-decide-on-evidence.md (SN-079): a refusal is the system working.

layers.name: What's In It For You
layers.body: You get verdicts with denominations: every PASS states which bar, which seam, which conditions — so you can tell a semantic compliment from a machine qualification at a glance. Apply the two-bar question to anything presented as "checked": checked *how*, by *what mechanism*, under *which hostile conditions*? And when a system refuses instead of degrading, you can recognize it as the safety working, not the software failing.

layers.name: The Learning
layers.body: The kernel era taught the team that the test apparatus is part of the system under judgment: tests manufacture false greens (SN-072), tests are themselves defective artifacts (SN-076), reports lie by computing from copies (SN-077). The durable change: qualification now audits the instruments with the same suspicion as the subject — prove the xfail, suspect the test, compute from the consuming state — and a frozen record's *wrongness* is preserved and retired openly rather than edited away (SN-080).

notes.title: Composition Is Proven Handoff by Handoff
notes.subtitle: Components can each be excellent while the organism does not exist — composition is proven only through the default wiring, with genuine data, handoff by handoff. Trust properties must be invariants, not conventions: a store anyone in-process can write makes resolve-then-trust prove nothing about origin (SN-085). Qualification subjects are frozen and fetchable (SN-086); fixture substitution at a claimed seam voids the integration claim (SN-088); a PASS on receipt family X never qualifies family Y (SN-090); contract mismatches are resolved at the source under the five-class binding taxonomy, with UNKNOWN as a complete binding (SN-091). Findings name their consequence class, gap tests self-invalidate, traces stop at the first exact failing handoff, and semantic gaps are named — never invented across (SN-092, SN-093). Boundary fixes compose at the consumer from the producer's sealed facts (SN-095), data bridges belong to the composition root and transport without judging (SN-096), and import-still-red proves the missing seam lives in the host (SN-102).

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: This is the story of discovering that a machine whose every part passed its tests still didn't work as a whole — because the parts were connected by promises instead of plumbing. The lessons: a lock that depends on everyone behaving is not a lock; a test that swaps in fake parts proves nothing about the real machine; proof about one kind of receipt says nothing about another kind; when a form asks for a fact nobody has, you write "unknown" — you never make one up; and when you trace a chain of handoffs, you stop at the first real break and say so, instead of pretending the rest worked.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine a relay race where each runner is super fast. That doesn't mean the team finishes — someone has to actually pass the baton! If a runner practices with a pretend baton, that doesn't prove the real pass works. If a box on the form asks for something nobody knows, you write "nobody knows" — you never make up an answer. And if the baton gets dropped at the third pass, you say "dropped at the third pass," not "great race."

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, it's the difference between good parts and a good machine. Locks must be real locks, not habits. Tests must use the real thing, not a stand-in. When a record lacks a fact, the honest word is "unknown," written plainly — inventing one is a kind of forgery. And a careful report names exactly where the chain broke and stops there, rather than painting the whole chain gold.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Audit every trust seam for invariant vs convention before relying on it (SN-085). Freeze fetchable subjects with digests and bind verdicts to SHAs (SN-086). Prove composition through the bare default constructor; reclassify fixture-substituted tests as fixture-only (SN-088). Name the specimen family of every proof artifact; fail closed at the first unsourceable field (SN-090). Bind every field by provenance class and resolve mismatches at the source (SN-091). Classify consequences honestly, ship gap tests that self-invalidate, and publish your limits (SN-092). Trace handoff by handoff; stop at the first exact failure; classify wiring vs semantic before touching anything (SN-093). Fix boundaries at the consumer from sealed producer facts (SN-095); give bridges to the composition root, transporting without judging (SN-096). When a seam is suspected missing, run the import-still-red experiment on a disposable branch (SN-102).

layers.name: What It Means
layers.body: Ten notes are the organism-level evidence craft: how separately-true parts become a proven whole — or an honestly-reported gap. A cold reader holding only this essence can still run a qualification, an integration proof, or a contract resolution the way these notes demand, and can recognize each named way such proofs go fake.

layers.name: Why It Matters
layers.body: Composition is where complex systems lie to themselves most fluently: every part green, the whole unproven, and the gap papered over with fixture wiring and borrowed proof (SN-088, SN-090). For the reader, this essence is the discipline that makes "the system works" a traceable claim — handoffs enumerated, gaps named at their exact location, unknowns written as unknowns — instead of an impression formed by adding up green badges.

layers.name: How It Connects
layers.body: Composition presumes essence-qualify-the-seam.md: only components that passed its two bars are worth wiring, and its consuming-state rule (SN-077) is the per-component form of this essence's genuine-data requirement. The trust seam here (SN-085) is bounded by the seal scope of essence-the-mirror.md (SN-0111) — consistency, not authorship — and the UNKNOWN binding class (SN-091) is the contract form of the decision discipline in essence-decide-on-evidence.md (SN-083). The nine nodes being composed are the machinery of essence-the-foundation.md (SN-002); the director's standing board protocol under which these traces were reported stands alone as SN-0109.

layers.name: What's In It For You
layers.body: You get wholes that are actually whole: when this system claims its parts work *together*, the claim comes with the trace — every handoff driven with real data, the first failure named exactly, the rest honestly marked unproven. Apply the pattern to any integrated claim: demand the default configuration, genuine inputs, the specimen family the proof actually exercised, and the per-handoff trace. Anything less is parts, wearing a whole's clothes.

layers.name: The Learning
layers.body: The corpus's hardest September lesson was that green parts compose into nothing by default: edges in a graph are ordering declarations, not plumbing (SN-096); fixtures at the seam silently void the organism claim (SN-088); proof borrowed across families is misattribution (SN-090). The behavior change: integration claims are now made only from default-composition traces, gaps are reported as first-class results with consequence classes (SN-092), and "blocked, not claimed" became an honorable terminal state instead of a failure to hide.

notes.title: The Handoff Is a Claim: Delivery, Coverage, and Duplicates Between Lanes
notes.subtitle: Work handed between lanes crosses three gaps — delivery, coverage, duplication — and each has a named discipline: a lost announcement is not lost work (repair the channel, repost the verified receipt, never rerun) (SN-045); verification coverage is pinned to a commit, so every head move opens a gap that must be named with its head (SN-046); duplicate repairs are caught by diffing the diffs (SN-052) and duplicate artifacts are owned openly and consolidated in public (SN-054). Authority shapes handoffs too: you supersede by comment on artifacts you don't own — the opener owns the close (SN-060). Verifiers publish their own numbers and make deltas interpretable with parent comparisons (SN-089); intake verification does not protect consumption-time state (SN-0112); and a push receipt proves nothing about contents — verify the tree (SN-0125).
