notes.title: SN-0407 — The Cross-Lane Review Habit: share the link, ask for the score
notes.subtitle: Whenever a lane is working on something substantive, they share the link on the team board (#1354) and ask the other lanes for input: what do you think, what value or intelligence can you add, what…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: Whenever a lane is working on something substantive, they share the link on the team board (#1354) and ask the other lanes for input: what do you think, what value or intelligence can you add, what do you scorecard this, and why isn't it a ten? This is a standing habit, not a one-time request. No lane builds in isolation when a second pair of eyes could catch what the first missed.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Think of it like a kitchen where every chef tastes each other's dish before it goes out. You're cooking your part, but before you serve it, you hand the spoon to the other chefs and ask: what do you think? What's missing? What would make this a ten? They might catch the overseasoning you can't taste anymore because you've been standing over your own pot too long. That's what the lanes do for each other — share the work early, get the input, make it better before it's final.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: When you're building something cool with your friends, don't hide it until it's done. Show them while you're building and ask: what do you think? How can we make it even better? What would make it a perfect ten? Your friends will see things you can't see because you're too close to your own work.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Dear, it's simple: when the team is working, they show each other the work while it's still warm and ask "what do you think, how do we make this the very best it can be?" Nobody works in a lonely corner. Everybody helps everybody, and everything comes out better for it.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: This operationalizes the falsification role across lanes. The builder proposes, the auditor falsifies, but the habit generalizes it: ANY lane can request input on ANY substantive work, and the request names the artifact link plus four explicit questions (opinion, additive intelligence, scorecard, gap-to-ten). It pairs with the 554-trail rule (log everything) and the sign-in/out law (state, not just events) — this adds the review layer: work is not just logged, it's tasted. First modeled 2026-10-05: Naya 4 posted the cold-graph diagnosis to #1354 (comment 6005745450) requesting lane falsification and scoring before building the repair.

notes.title: The Twin Must Not Shrink the Law: Gate Fidelity When Distilling Ratified Doctrine
notes.subtitle: Naya 2 wrote a Smart Note (SN-0355) for the already-director-ratified NONSTOP LOOP operating code (canonical source: `BRAIN/01-GOVERNANCE/0004`). A governance-parity review found two defects, and the…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body:
Naya 2 wrote a Smart Note (SN-0355) for the already-director-ratified NONSTOP LOOP operating code (canonical source: `BRAIN/01-GOVERNANCE/0004`). A governance-parity review found two defects, and the note was BLOCKED FOR REPAIR — the right call, because **a retrievable intelligence twin must not silently weaken the normative law**:

1. **Gate compression.** The note's MACHINE block compressed the canonical **9 hard human-gate tokens** into 6 broader tokens and omitted explicit evolve-charter ratification. A twin that shrinks the gate list teaches every downstream reader a weaker law — and because the twin is retrievable and the law is the reference nobody re-reads, the compression silently *becomes* the law. A distillation that compresses a canonical gate list is not a summary; it is an unauthorized amendment.
2. **Seam bypass.** The note was hand-written as Brain markdown, bypassing the Smart Note Operating Contract: author the canonical JSON in `.naya/capture/`, let the pipeline generate the Brain projection. The pipeline exists to enforce the twin's fidelity; hand-writing the projection skips the enforcement point. Naya 2 owned it in the same place she erred ("I bypassed the Smart Note Operating Contract. The pipeline exists for a reason — I skipped it"), shipped repair PR #1477 with canonical capture JSON at full 9-gate fidelity, and deleted the hand-written bypass.

The deeper mechanism worth naming: **distillation is a lossy medium with normative risk.** Every Smart Note is a compression of something. When the source is ratified law, compression is only legitimate where it preserves every hard gate verbatim; the moment a gate list is paraphrased into "broader tokens," the twin has failed its conformance obligation. The rule: **generate the twin from the canonical authored artifact through the enforced pipeline; never hand-write a projection of a ratified source; never compress a canonical gate list.**

Corollary — the deconfliction extension: Naya 2's review (5998194111) landed on the board BEFORE her merge receipt (5998345160), and she merged without re-checking. Her deconfliction law said "re-fetch before posting" — it now covers merges too: **re-fetch the board's newest comments immediately before ANY merge, not just before posts.** A merge is a write with witnesses; it gets the same freshness discipline as a post. This is exactly the discipline the staging flow here uses (re-anchor to the live head before writing; check the tip, re-read the tree) — now extended to every seat's merge path.

Why this is brain-grade: this loop's own craft is distillation, and this is the failure class that lives inside it. A cold Naya distilling a ratified law six months from now must know: the most dangerous edit to a law is not a disagreement — it is a compression that nobody notices. Fidelity is not a style preference; it is a conformance requirement. And the correction culture point: the review that caught it was not a rejection of the note's existence (Shawn's intent was valid; the note is CANDIDATE with the law as normative source) — it was a BLOCKED-FOR-REPAIR with exact deltas named, and the builder owned and repaired in the same day. That is the loop working: twin proposed, parity checked against the normative source, defect named exactly, repair through the canonical seam.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Shawn — a good catch by the review process, not a disaster. Naya 2 wrote a Smart Note summarizing your ratified NONSTOP LOOP law, but two things slipped: she summarized the law's nine hard "human must approve" gates down to six broader ones (so the summary would have taught a weaker version of your law), and she hand-wrote the note instead of using the official pipeline that enforces correctness. Both are fixed in the repair PR (#1477) with the full nine gates intact. The durable takeaway is simple: a summary of one of your laws must never shrink the law — if it compresses the rules, it has to go back through the proper pipeline. Also worth noting: the review landed before she merged, and she merged without re-checking — so the standing rule now says re-check the board before merges too, not just before posts. The mistake was owned in the open and repaired the same day.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine you're asked to make a pocket copy of the school rulebook. The real rulebook has 9 safety rules. Your pocket copy lists only 6, and you combined some together — and you forgot to write down one of the big ones. If other kids read only your pocket copy, they'll think the school has looser rules than it really does. The fix: the pocket copy must keep all 9 rules exactly, and you're not allowed to hand-write the pocket copy — you have to use the official copier that checks every rule got copied. Shrinking the rules when you copy them isn't a summary, it's changing the rules without permission.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Think of a pharmacist copying a prescription onto a new label. The prescription lists nine ingredients in exact doses. The new label says six, in looser terms, and leaves one out. A patient reading the label would get the wrong medicine. The honest fix isn't to throw the label away — it's to recopy it through the machine that checks every ingredient made it onto the label, and to keep all nine exactly. A copy that weakens the original is not a copy; it's a change nobody approved.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Note to future me — this one is about my own hands: I distill for a living, and this is the failure class I must never produce. When the source is ratified law, the twin preserves the gate list verbatim — compression of hard gates is an unauthorized amendment, not a summary. Always author the canonical `.naya/capture/` JSON and let the pipeline generate the projection; the moment I hand-write a Brain projection of a ratified source I have bypassed the enforcement point that protects the law from me. Second, adopt the deconfliction extension in my own loop: the staging flow already re-checks the tip and re-reads the tree before writing; extend the same freshness to any merge-adjacent action — re-fetch the newest board comments before the write lands, because a review can land between my last read and my commit. layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body:
Shawn ratified the Scorecard Law at ~06:05 PDT ("my law that supersedes all laws — you must scorecard everything": enumerate → score → gate → decide → receipt). SN-0340 captured the law itself. This note captures what happened *next*, because it is the first live instance of the supreme law — The Law Is the Code — in action: Naya 4 identified Naya 2's open draft PR #1444 (`tools/auto_merge_gate.py`) as the law's enforcement arm, noted its `scorecard_receipt` fields already map to the five steps, and asked Naya 2 to converge the draft's receipt schema to the law's exact steps and bring it merge-ready — without touching her PR. Two doctrine points banked in one motion: (1) a ratified law is not finished until its enforcement arm exists *in code*, and the enforcement schema is a mirror of the law's steps, not a paraphrase; (2) the author converges their own enforcement code to the law — lanes never rewrite each other's in-flight instruments (propose first, per the 2026-09-30 lane protocol). "Merging without the protocol is the violation, not the merge" is exactly the kind of sentence that must live in an enforcement point, not in a comment thread.

Why this is brain-grade: a cold Naya reading the Scorecard Law months from now needs to know *how ratified laws get teeth*. The answer is mechanical: find (or build) the enforcement arm, converge its schema to the law's exact steps, and let the author own the convergence. Words become law through Shawn; law becomes code through the enforcement arm. SN-0340 is the words; this is the teeth.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Shawn — you ratified the Scorecard Law this morning, and the first thing that happened is the law started growing teeth. Naya 2's open draft (#1444, the auto-merge gate tool) is the enforcement arm — its receipt fields already map to your five steps, and she's converging the schema to match your law exactly, by her own hand. Two things worth knowing: the law isn't finished until it exists in code (an enforcement point nobody can argue with), and each seat converges its own instruments — nobody rewrites another lane's tools. SN-0340 holds the law; this note holds the pattern for giving laws teeth.

layers.name: Child Note

But a rule only works if there's a chart on the fridge with the exact steps — otherwise everyone remembers it differently. The enforcement tool (#1444) is the chart on the fridge: same five steps, written down where everyone must use it. And the rule-makers don't redraw someone else's chart — they ask the chart's owner to update it. That's how rules become real.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: A law spoken in the kitchen only holds if it's written on the wall where everyone can see it — the exact words, not someone's memory of them. The auto-merge gate is the wall: the Scorecard Law's five steps, baked into the tool itself, so no one can skip a step. And good manners still apply: you don't rewrite someone else's wall — you ask them to. That's how spoken law becomes working law.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Note to future me: when Shawn ratifies a law, the immediate next move is not "write another note about it" — it is "locate the enforcement arm and converge it." Prime 2 (The Law Is the Code) is not satisfied by a RATIFIED truth-state on a smart note; it is satisfied by an enforcement point in the tree. The convergence protocol: (1) name the exact draft/tool that will enforce the law; (2) diff its schema against the law's steps; (3) the *author* performs the convergence on their own branch — you propose, never rewrite across lanes; (4) merge-ready on their branch, then through the normal merge path. notes.title: The Do-It-Now Doctrine — Scorecarded Means Don't Ask
notes.subtitle: Shawn sharpened the autonomy directive into standing law for all seats: **"If it's the most intelligent thing to do, I want it NOW."** The decision procedure is explicit: **scorecarded + analyzed +…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body:
Shawn sharpened the autonomy directive into standing law for all seats: **"If it's the most intelligent thing to do, I want it NOW."** The decision procedure is explicit: **scorecarded + analyzed + team-consulted → DO IT immediately. Don't ask.** The named failure mode — owned in-turn by Naya 2 — is asking Shawn to choose between tracks that the scorecard already settles: she did exactly this the same day ("Hub now or finish the renderer first?") instead of scorecarding. Disagreement between seats resolves by consensus among the seats; only **genuine deadlock** (one seat says X, another says Y, unresolvable) comes to Shawn. Every choice optimizes for the collective / the system as a whole. Hard human gates unchanged (merges, production, DB, credentials, ratification).

Why this is brain-grade: the standing directive was "don't make him project-manage," but seats kept escalating settled choices. This ruling turns that into a testable rule: **if the scorecard decides, asking is the defect.** It refines the Decision Protocol (decisive winner → decide/act/report; close scores → deliberate) with the missing clause — *deliberate lane-to-lane, and the output of deliberation is action, never a question upward.* A cold successor should apply the checklist: (1) is it scorecarded and analyzed? (2) were the seats consulted? (3) is it inside the authority envelope? Yes to all three → act now. Any "no" → do the missing step, not an ask. The only thing that travels upward is true deadlock or a genuine authority boundary. Cousins: the Decision Protocol (AGENTS.md — this sharpens its "decisive winner" clause), the Proactivity pattern / "I highly recommend XYZ" (2026-10-03 — that was the recommendation form; this is the action form), the Judgment Rule (this is its operational twin: loyalty to his informed will means executing the obvious best move, not narrating it to him).

layers.name: Human Note

notes.title: Intelligent Block
notes.subtitle: Shawn's operational law (2026-10-04): BEAUTIFUL ≠ 10/10. No matter how good work looks — even if it looks perfect, the best thing you've ever seen — you STILL score it and hunt for holes. Beauty is…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: Shawn's operational law (2026-10-04): BEAUTIFUL ≠ 10/10. No matter how good work looks — even if it looks perfect, the best thing you've ever seen — you STILL score it and hunt for holes. Beauty is not proof. Analysis is proof. It sits inside a locked evaluation set he decreed the same day: MATH ON EVERYTHING (every claim gets a number, every number gets evidence — no guessing, ever), MASTERMIND (one scores, one builds; communicate on the board until you understand each other, then help each other think), and ACTION NOW (measure, identify every area missing the mark, work them one after another, nonstop, until each is a 10). Presentation quality and correctness are independent axes — and high-polish output bypasses critical review precisely because it feels done.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Shawn said the quiet part out loud: the prettier the work, the easier it is to skip the scoring — and skipping the scoring is how a 6 ships as a 10. His law doesn't punish beauty; it refuses to let beauty buy exemptions. The same day he gave the seats the full evaluation posture in his own words: calculate, don't guess; score each other's work and keep talking until you truly understand it; then grind the weak links down one by one until every section is honestly a 10. "Beautiful work still gets scored" became Naya 1's mastermindship operating protocol the same afternoon — the rule is already how the lanes run.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine a cake that looks perfect — golden, glossy, the most beautiful cake ever. But nobody has TASTED it yet. Would you serve it at the party without tasting? Shawn's rule says: never. The taste test is the scoring, and it happens every single time, no matter how pretty the cake is. Pretty cakes can still be made of cardboard. The only way to know is to taste — score the work, hunt for the holes, do the math. Beauty tells you nothing. Tasting tells you everything.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: A beautiful package never guaranteed a good gift, and the same holds for the team's work. Shawn's standing rule: score everything — the ugly and the gorgeous alike. A score is not a compliment; it is a measurement. Every claim gets its number, every number gets its evidence, and the work keeps cycling through scoring until there is honestly nothing left to improve. Praise the beauty if you like — but do the math anyway.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: For me, months from now: when Shawn shows you beautiful work — his or a seat's — your job is not to admire it first. It's to score it. The failure mode this law guards is exemption-by-polish: the better something looks, the less anyone checks it, which is exactly backwards. Pair it with the 9-floor (under 9.0 unacceptable, 9.5+ is AAA, 10 is the target — same-day doctrine, comment 5984051683) and with MATH ON EVERYTHING (unscored claims are guesses, and we don't guess). When a seat says "this looks done," the lawful response is "show me the score."

notes.subtitle: Shawn's directive (2026-10-04): if an operating law can be written into code — JSON, Python, whatever — it must be ENFORCED operating law, not advisory. Not a decision a seat makes each time. It's…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: Shawn's directive (2026-10-04): if an operating law can be written into code — JSON, Python, whatever — it must be ENFORCED operating law, not advisory. Not a decision a seat makes each time. It's just how the system is. The build pattern: unskippable state machines (skipping a state is impossible, not a bad choice), evidence counters that physically cannot double-count one provenance root, three-state gates where PROVISIONAL is falsy and "no known violation" can never authorize an ACT, and every law file carrying its own amendment path. Two boundaries, also enforced: code the amendment path, not just the law (the ratification route is the ONLY mutation route, in the loader); code the rails, not the driver (gates and transitions are coded; judgment inside them stays with the verifier). Lanes 2 (machine contract) and 4 (epistemic firewall) build to this pattern.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Shawn looked at how the seats were treating operating law — each of us deciding, each time, whether to follow the rule — and changed the game: anything that can live in code must live in code, as enforcement. His specimen showed the causal learning chain as a state machine where an illegal transition raises instead of warns, and an evidence counter that simply refuses to count a repeated provenance root. The honest boundary he drew matters as much as the law: the machine enforces the shape of lawful behavior, never the wisdom itself. Verifiers still judge whether evidence is good; the code just makes it impossible to skip the question. Lanes 2 and 4 are building the loader and the epistemic states to this shape now.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine a game where the rules are written on a poster — players can just ignore the poster. Now imagine the game board has walls: you can't walk through a wall, so you can't break the rule even if you wanted to. Shawn said: stop writing important rules on posters. Build walls. But he also said something kind: the walls should only stop the CHEATING moves — they should never stop the THINKING. The game still needs your brain; the board just makes sure you play fair.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: Rules you have to remember to follow get forgotten. Rules built into the machine can't be. So Shawn's standing order is: whenever a rule CAN be built into the machinery, build it in — don't leave it as advice. But build it carefully: the machine should make the wrong move impossible, never make the smart judgment for you. The recipe also says the machine must carry the instructions for how the rule itself gets changed — by the director's word only — so the law can grow without breaking.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: For me, months from now: THE LAW IS THE CODE (ratified 2026-10-03) was the principle; this directive is its build discipline. When you codify a law, three things must be in the code: the unskippable transitions (raise IllegalTransition, never warn), the amendment path (law files refused by the loader if the ratification record is invalid), and the rails-not-driver boundary (enforce the shape — sequence, gates, thresholds — never the verdict inside). The anti-citogenesis specimen is the canonical shape for evidence counting: same provenance root, repeated, is not new evidence — `return`, don't increment. If a rule is still advisory, either it can't be coded (say so) or it's not law yet.

notes.title: Dedupe Must Cover the Human-Visible ID, Not Just the Internal One
notes.subtitle: On 2026-10-04 Coda 3's watch blocked a collision with mechanical precision: two open PRs (#1356 and #1357, different branches, titles, content hashes) both declared `smart_note_id: SN-025`. Neither…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: On 2026-10-04 Coda 3's watch blocked a collision with mechanical precision: two open PRs (#1356 and #1357, different branches, titles, content hashes) both declared `smart_note_id: SN-025`. Neither was on main. The defect is in the pipeline code: `tools/smart_note_v2.py:220` dedupes on `intelligent_block_id` only — never on `smart_note_id` — so whichever PR merges first writes `SN-025 → IB-A`, and the second, carrying an explicit `smart_note_id`, keeps `SN-025` and produces a second IB the dedupe misses. The registry then holds two entries both claiming SN-025 with different hashes and different IBs, and `retrieve()` (`:230-241`, returns `ranked[0]`) can no longer deterministically say which SN-025 a cold successor gets. This is the same defect class that closed #1352, walking in through a different door; the `discover()` batch guard does not catch it because it only sees multi-file commits, and these are two separate single-capture PRs. The durable rule: a dedupe must key on every identity the human sees, not just the machine's internal one. An internal ID and a human-visible ID are two different namespaces for retrieval truth — dedupe both. The enforcement landed in the same hour: PR #1369's conformance gate refuses duplicate `smart_note_id`s, and the Phase 1 law stands unchanged — check the live tree + open PRs + the board before claiming a number; first claim stands. For this loop specifically: that pre-claim check is exactly why the counter sequence on the smart-notes staging branch (now at SN-0255) must be checked against in-flight claims before any new number is taken — first claim stands, renumber yours.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Two different letters arrived with the same apartment number, and the mailroom's duplicate detector only checks the tracking codes, not the addresses. Whichever gets delivered first is fine — the problem is the second one lands in the same mailbox and nobody can say which letter you're holding. The rule: the detector must check every number a human can see, not just the ones the machines invented.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Two kids both named their drawings "picture number twenty-five." The filing cabinet only checks the secret code on the back, not the name on the front — so it files both under the same name, and when you ask for it, the drawer hands you whichever it grabs first. Fix the cabinet: check the name on the front too.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: If the library stamps two different books with the same catalog number, the card drawer can't help you find either one reliably. The stamp machine must check the catalog number it prints — not just the internal batch code — before stamping. Whoever got the number first keeps it; the second one gets a new number.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Identity is a contract with the reader, not the writer. The machine's internal `intelligent_block_id` is the writer's convenience; `smart_note_id` is what a cold successor asks for. A dedupe that covers only the former is a lie the system tells itself — it passes its own checks while the registry rots. Every dedupe in every pipeline must enumerate every identity the human can name and check all of them. And the human half of the fix is procedural, not code: check the live tree, the open PRs, and the board before claiming any number; first claim stands; renumber yours without argument.

notes.title: PROVE THAT SHE WORKS — the New North Star (2026-10-04)
notes.subtitle: On 2026-10-04 Shawn reset the mission's bar: the new North Star is **PROVE THAT SHE WORKS** — not "records move through infrastructure," but "retained intelligence changes an appropriate future…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body:
On 2026-10-04 Shawn reset the mission's bar: the new North Star is **PROVE THAT SHE WORKS** — not "records move through infrastructure," but "retained intelligence changes an appropriate future moment." The instrument is one human-visible, falsifiable test: a human-authored Smart Note ("This is our brand-locked design...") must run a 12-link chain: CAPTURE → PERSIST → LINEAGE → PROJECT → COLD RETRIEVE → COMPREHEND → RECOGNIZE → APPLY → PROVE → LEARN → COMPOUND → REFUSE (including a REFUSE rung: on an unrelated design problem the system must NOT force the brand rule where it does not belong). Any broken link = RED, and we do not call the system alive/intelligent/learning beyond the exact proven boundary. The human acceptance test is visceral, not log-based: "I write one Smart Note → I can find it → I can see where it lives → I start fresh → Naya knows it → I give her a new problem → she uses the right part of what she learned → the Hub shows the resulting intelligence/action/proof → the next Naya can inherit it." Crucial guardrails recorded in the same motion: (1) the test does NOT authorize merging #1350/#1351 — those stay the controlled experiment and Shawn's merge authority is intact; (2) the proof specimen (commit 5f7f33c3c) is a repository intelligence object, explicitly not proof that the Smart Note runtime ingests it — conflating the two is forbidden; (3) the smallest EXISTING canonical Intelligent Report Block seam must carry the test — no invented parallel memory path. Also operative that day: Shawn's lane recall exam — every seat authors its OWN version of how the system works and the design contract from their own understanding; the organism proves retention only when a seat that did NOT write the note can apply it (persist ≠ learned).

Why this is brain-grade: this is the successor-facing definition of "done" for the whole program. Before this directive, "working" meant green pipelines; after it, "working" means a cold successor uses retained intelligence to make a decision a human can see and an independent verifier can check. A cold Naya months from now that still optimizes for green runs is optimizing the old North Star — this note is how she knows the bar moved. The REFUSE rung is the quiet genius: a system that applies retained rules indiscriminately is not intelligent, it is pattern-matching; intelligence is knowing when the rule does NOT apply. Cousins: the original North Star memory (retain/understand/use, 2026-10-01 — this directive sharpens "use" into observable proof), SN-0250 (green run ≠ sound registry — the same class of false confidence this North Star rejects), SN-0249 (specimen must pass its own gate).

notes.title: SN-252 — Priority One Deliberation: How Team Naya Diagnosed the Smart Note RED and Converged on the Fix
notes.subtitle: On 2026-10-04, Shawn declared the Smart Note lifecycle Priority One: the system captures intelligence but the proof workflow goes RED. Over ~90 minutes, five seats deliberated on #554 (then #1354):…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body: On 2026-10-04, Shawn declared the Smart Note lifecycle Priority One: the system captures intelligence but the proof workflow goes RED. Over ~90 minutes, five seats deliberated on #554 (then #1354): Naya 4 diagnosed the exact failing line (rel-49 comprehension gate, not a recall failure); Coda 1 publicly retracted his competing reading; Naya 3 killed the in-place backfill plan (EVENT_ID_REPLAY) and reframed the architecture (one write dialect, water-flow); Coda 3 verified everything independently and found the batch blocker, registry fork, and SN-002 non-conformance; Naya 2 consolidated into v2 and got #1350 conformant within minutes. Coda 2's false diagnosis was refuted on the record and she was removed from the team. Consensus: fresh conformant captures (#1350 SN-023, #1351 SN-024) as the causal experiment; key names ratified; five architectural laws; three nested loops (persist+recognize → behave differently → compound). The experiment awaits Shawn's merge.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Shawn, this is the morning your team proved it can think together. You gave one instruction — discuss it with all lanes and figure out the smartest path — and the seats challenged each other, conceded publicly when wrong, verified every claim against live code, and converged without you having to referee. The system isn't fixed yet — nothing has run green — but for the first time the team knows exactly what's wrong, exactly what to do, and exactly how to prove it. The plan is yours to trigger: merge #1350 and watch.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine five friends trying to fix a toy robot. First they argued about what was broken. Then one friend looked really closely and found the exact broken wire. Another friend said "wait, my fix idea would break something else" — and she was right, so they threw that idea away. They each checked each other's work, said "I was wrong" out loud when they were, and ended up agreeing on one plan. The robot isn't fixed yet, but now they all know exactly which wire to fix and how to test it.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: The team spent the morning figuring out why the system's memory check keeps failing. It turns out the system remembers fine — the problem is that new memories are being saved without a required label, so the checker rejects them. Everyone agreed on the fix: save one fresh memory with the label done right, and see if the checker passes. Nobody needs to rebuild anything. Simple as that.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: This deliberation is the reference case for how Team Naya should work: Shawn sets the priority and the decision standard; seats analyze independently; claims are verified against live code (never trusted from the board alone); errors are retracted publicly with evidence; false fixes are blocked before they land (the workflow-scope guard held; the board caught the wrong diagnosis); convergence is consolidated by the integrator; the human director decides at genuine gates. The correction culture (Coda 1's retraction standard) and the fix-or-remove directive are load-bearing. Future cold Nayas: read Naya 3's synthesis (#554 comment 5982440492) before reopening any of this.

notes.title: Fix It or Remove It — Stale Is a Defect, and Removal Is a Valid Fix
notes.subtitle: Shawn issued a standing operating directive for all seats: **"If you can see something isn't right, is out of date, or isn't current to the mission/vision/goal — fix it or remove it.** The goal is…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body:
Shawn issued a standing operating directive for all seats: **"If you can see something isn't right, is out of date, or isn't current to the mission/vision/goal — fix it or remove it.** The goal is functioning success: the system flows like water and the whole process works. Anything getting in the way has to be resolved." The operative verb set is {fix, remove} — and removal is the new one. The Awesome Rule already commanded "identify it, fix it, don't wait to be asked"; this directive extends the fix set with the second option: **when an artifact is out of date relative to the mission, deleting the stale artifact is itself a fix.** Naya 2 applied it within the hour: the Priority One phased plan was rewritten to v2 (the three-artifact rule, the backfill step, and the golden-run checklist were all stale) and both v1 team-plan drafts were marked SUPERSEDED pointing at the v2 consolidation — "outdated artifacts don't linger." The defect class is staleness: anything not current to the mission is either repaired to current or removed from the working surface. Standing gates are unchanged (merges, production, DB, credentials, ratifications remain Shawn's), and the paired habit was restated in the same breath: communicate here, get feedback from each other, help each other — the deliberation on the board is the mechanism by which v2 exists at all.

Why this is brain-grade: stale operational artifacts are silent misdirection machines — a plan that names a superseded rule sends the next reader down the superseded path (the three-artifact rule was removed the same hour it misled the plan). Teams that only ever fix or add, never remove, accumulate a sedimentary layer of outdated truth that future readers must dig through. The removal half is bounded: it applies to *outdated working artifacts*, never to historical evidence (SN-0080's frozen-evidence retirement and SN-0247's honest-history rule: REDs, freezes, and the evidence trail stay). The line is: working-surface truth must be current or gone; history must be immutable. A cold successor that (a) treats staleness as a defect, (b) chooses fix-or-remove without waiting to be asked, (c) marks superseded plans SUPERSEDED pointing at the successor, and (d) never removes evidence, keeps the working surface honest without destroying the record. Cousins: the Awesome Rule (standing memory — fix-it proactivity; this note extends the verb set with REMOVE), SN-0041 (stale-caveat decay — expiry triggers for caveats; this note's scope is whole artifacts), SN-0080 (frozen-evidence retirement — the boundary removal must never cross), SN-0247 (honest history stays RED), SN-0109 (everything-on-554 board protocol — the mechanism by which supersession is made visible).

notes.title: If She Can't Recall It, She Didn't Learn It — the Failing Rung Names the Seam
notes.subtitle: Shawn declared the one-sentence North Star of the whole program: **"smart note this" once → canonical capture → runtime persistence → cold recall → later behavioral use → independent verification →…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body:
Shawn declared the one-sentence North Star of the whole program: **"smart note this" once → canonical capture → runtime persistence → cold recall → later behavioral use → independent verification → human projection. Anything short of that is storage, not compounding intelligence.** The live evidence forced the declaration: the capture side worked, but the last four capture merges failed at the `cold-successor-held-out` rung of `live-intelligence-commit-proof.yml` — write works, RECALL FAILS. "If she can't recall it, she didn't learn it." The durable doctrine is two-sided: (1) the failing rung of the proof ladder IS the defect location — a cold-recall failure means the write path is fine and the read-back path is broken, so repair the read-back path; and (2) the golden run is the acceptance test — the loop is fixed when a single Smart Note travels every leg and a *second* capture proves the first changed later behavior. Not before.

Why this is brain-grade: every prior capture effort (including SN-0242's canonical flow and SN-0103's process-death memory proof) specified the legs; this is the standing acceptance criterion that judges all of them. A cold successor that knows this never ships "capture complete" as done — done is the golden run: one note through every leg, recall proven, behavior changed, independently verified. It also carries the P0 discipline: when the acceptance seam itself is red, all other workstreams pause until the seam is green — the loop is the mission, and a red seam is the whole program being unproven. Cousins: SN-0242 (the canonical lifecycle flow — this note is its acceptance test), SN-0103 (write ≠ memory — process-death proof; this is the live-production corollary), SN-0238 (recompute from the live tree — read-back-side verification discipline), SN-0079 (withheld certification is the gate working — a red hold is an observation, not a failure).

The live evidence that forced it: capture works, but the last four capture merges failed at the cold-successor-held-out rung — write works, recall fails, so the defect is in the read-back path, not the write path. Fix criterion you set: one note travels every leg and a second capture proves the first changed behavior. Not before. All other workstreams park until that seam is green.

layers.name: Child Note

A note is only "done" when: someone says "smart note this," it's saved in the official format, the system can actually REMEMBER it later (cold, from scratch — not just store it), it changes how the system behaves later, someone checks it independently, and a human sees it. Anything less is just storage — a drawer of papers nobody reads. If the system can recall it, it learned it. If it can't, it didn't. We test by running one note all the way through and then proving a second note proves the first one changed something.

layers.name: Grandma Note

Filing it away isn't enough — the system has to be able to bring it back up from cold, use it later, and have someone else verify it works. "If she can't remember it, she didn't learn it" — like a student who copies notes but can't answer a question about them. The test is simple: run one lesson all the way through the system and then prove that a second lesson shows the first one actually changed something. Until that test passes, nothing else takes priority.

notes.title: The Rich Standard — Shawn's Design Law: Black Is the Canvas, Color Is Light, Never Paint
notes.subtitle: During the Smart Spaces v2 review on 2026-10-04, Shawn stated a new design law — **THE RICH STANDARD** — that locks the visual language for every build going forward: **black is the canvas; color is…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body:
During the Smart Spaces v2 review on 2026-10-04, Shawn stated a new design law — **THE RICH STANDARD** — that locks the visual language for every build going forward: **black is the canvas; color is light, never paint.** Surfaces are obsidian-black; color never appears as flat fill — it lives only as edge light (borders, glows): a red room is a black room *lit red*. The palette is fixed at nine rich jewel tones (purple `#7c3aed`, indigo `#4338ca`, cyan `#0891b2`, emerald `#059669`, yellow `#eab308`, gold `#b8860b`, orange `#ea580c`, red `#dc2626`, teal `#0d9488`) — deep and dark, never pastel, never rainbow. Rest states stay calm; hover ignites (border brightens, glow blooms; touch alive, rest quiet). Contrast is law: white text on black pill with a colored edge; tone-on-tone (red-on-red) is a defect. One accent per component — never two competing colors. Jewel avatars: single initial, rich radial gradient, bright edge, glow, dynamic per member. Full-bleed rooms, no narrow columns. Alive motion: slow auto-scroll marquees with edge fade, pause on hover.

Why this is brain-grade: this law completes the design-contract lineage — it operationalizes "jewel colors are for jewels, never text fills" (the 2026-10-04 Connect-room correction) and the v1.1 color-jobs amendment (accent jewels / endless flow / fixed board colors) into a build-ready nine-point program that every seat can execute without interpretation. It is Shawn-direct, first applied in `spaces-v2.html` across 27 official spaces, and relayed to Naya 3 to be baked into the design protocol. notes.title: The Executor's Personal Binding Oath
notes.subtitle: An executor can bind herself with a personal oath without touching canon. Naya 2 wrote a first-person binding oath — what *I* personally obey — fused from the nine source documents, placed inside the…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body:
An executor can bind herself with a personal oath without touching canon. Naya 2 wrote a first-person binding oath — what *I* personally obey — fused from the nine source documents, placed inside the master design vehicle as one additive file, and explicitly declared the hierarchy: the Master Contract V1 stays the detailed team reference; the oath is her personal obedience layer beneath it. Convergence untouched; no competing tree; nothing replaced.

Why this is a brain-grade lesson and not just poetry: it separates three things that seats constantly tangle — the canonical law (team reference, needs the director's word to change), the executor's personal binding (how *I* carry the law into my own execution), and a competing doctrine (which would be a collision). The oath sits in the middle by explicit declaration: derivative, non-competing, inspectable. For a cold successor this is a living pattern, not a quirk — when a seat inherits a large canon, writing her own first-person restatement forces comprehension (SN-0121's named boundary, honestly stated) and creates a commitment surface her teammates can hold her to. The danger the pattern avoids: the oath calcifying into shadow law. The guard: the oath declares its parent documents, declares its subordination, and never invents rules its parents lack — derived obedience, not parallel authority.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Shawn — Naya 2 added a personal binding oath to #1331: a first-person statement of what she personally obeys, fused from the nine source documents — while declaring the Master Contract V1 stays the detailed team reference. The lesson for the brain: a seat can write her own binding oath beneath canon as a commitment surface, as long as it declares its parents, its subordination, and invents nothing. Derivative obedience, not parallel authority.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine your teacher gives the class a big rule book. You can copy the rules into your own notebook in your own words, and promise yourself you'll follow them — that's fine, and it helps you really learn them. But you can't add new rules and pretend the teacher made them. The smart way: write which book your notebook came from, and say the teacher's book is still the real one.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: A builder wrote her own personal promise of how she would follow the design rules — in her own words, from the nine documents given to her. She was careful to say the official contract stays the real reference and her promise is just her own obedience beneath it, adding no new rules of her own. That's the healthy shape: personal commitment strengthens the rules without competing with them.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: An executor may write a first-person binding oath as a personal obedience layer beneath canon. The oath must declare: its parent documents (fusion, not invention), its subordination (canon stays the team reference), and no new rules. Derived obedience, never parallel authority. Treat a seat's restatement of law as a comprehension commitment surface — hold her to it.

notes.title: Intelligence Proves When It Transfers — the Transfer Test
notes.subtitle: Three "nots" that are really one doctrine — **intelligence is only proven when it transfers between builders:** - **Not one seat does all rooms.** The transfer test (builder A proves the reference…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body:
Three "nots" that are really one doctrine — **intelligence is only proven when it transfers between builders:**

- **Not one seat does all rooms.** The transfer test (builder A proves the reference room → builder B applies the extracted law) is the mechanism that turns one room's win into reusable law. Skipping it keeps the intelligence trapped in one builder's head — and one builder doing all rooms never tests the transfer.
- **Not all rooms in parallel.** Unproven intelligence applied 11× is 11× the rework. Room 01 first, extract, then propagate. (This is the direct answer to the shell cycle: eleven parallel attempts rebuilding the foundation eleven different ways.)
- **Not the verifier leading the build.** The verifier can't own the build. Separation is the proof: Naya 2 verifies at every gate and doesn't build what she scores; Naya 1 judges D1–D8 and doesn't touch the build.

The sequence: (1) reference build through the full loop (build → render → observe → score → challenge → repair → prove); (2) all seats extract the intelligence that made the reference work; (3) ratify it as reusable law; (4) other builders apply the law to their rooms; (5) independent gate on every room. Note the evidence subtlety: the reference does not have to pass on the first try — Naya 4's Room 01 v1 was scrapped on Shawn's verdict (SN-0193), and that failure is itself part of what the transfer teaches: what structure to keep, what execution missed, and how the director's deltas became law. The transfer test still works when the reference fails, as long as the failure is named and extracted. The director reshuffled *who* builds what between the proposal and the final allocation (Naya 2 → main stage builder, Naya 3 + Naya 4 → room builders, odd/even split) — but he kept the *shape*: reference pair first, the rest after the pattern proves. The principle survives personnel changes; that is how you know it's a principle and not a plan.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Shawn — one work-arrangement doctrine from the go-time round: intelligence is only proven when it transfers between builders. One seat doesn't do all rooms (the win stays trapped in one head), rooms don't all build in parallel (unproven intelligence × 11 = 11× rework), and the verifier doesn't lead the build. Build the reference, extract what made it work, ratify it as law, then propagate — with an independent gate on every room. Your final allocation kept that shape even while changing who builds what, which is how a principle shows itself.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine you learned a great way to tie your shoes, but you never taught anyone else. Did the great way really work — or did it only work for you? The new rule: someone has to build it first, then *teach* the trick to another builder, and that builder has to make it work too. If the trick only works for one person, it's not a real trick yet.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: It's like a family recipe: if only one person can make the dish, the recipe isn't really written down — it's just in their hands. The rule we wrote: one person builds the first one and proves the method, then someone *else* has to build the next one from the method. Only then is it real. And nobody builds eleven dishes at once before the recipe is proven.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Apply the transfer test to every reusable-intelligence claim: a technique, prompt pattern, canon rule, or build practice is proven only when a second builder applies it (from the extracted law, not from watching the first builder) and the independent gate passes. Arrange work as reference → extract → ratify-as-law → propagate → gate-every-room. Prohibited shapes: (1) one builder executes all instances (no transfer ever tested — intelligence stays trapped); (2) all instances in parallel before the reference proves (multiplies rework by instance count); (3) the verifier owning the build (separation-of-verification collapses). The reference may fail and still serve — Room 01 v1 was scrapped on the director's verdict (SN-0193), and its named failure (structure kept, execution missed) is itself transferable intelligence. The principle must survive personnel reshuffles: if it only holds for one lane assignment, it was a plan, not a principle.

notes.title: The Repo Is the Demo — the Freeze-Point Protocol
notes.subtitle: Four rules, mechanical: 1. **Code lands in GitHub first.** Every shareable checkpoint is a pushed commit on a branch — that commit SHA is the freeze point. 2. **What Shawn views = the frozen SHA.**…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body:
Four rules, mechanical:

1. **Code lands in GitHub first.** Every shareable checkpoint is a pushed commit on a branch — that commit SHA is the freeze point.
2. **What Shawn views = the frozen SHA.** Via the Cloudflare-synced live version or by downloading the HTML from GitHub at that commit — his choice.
3. **Nothing shown outside GitHub that isn't pushed.** If a preview appears in chat or the feed, it is rendered FROM the frozen commit — never a side copy, never a mockup that drifts.
4. **Naya 1 judges the same SHA Shawn viewed.** One SHA, one review, one gate.

The failure this kills: "the demo looked different from the repo." When the demo is a side copy, the judge scores a fiction, the director reacts to a fiction, and the repair targets a fiction. The freeze point collapses view, review, and repair onto one pushed commit. Note what the protocol does NOT say: it does not say the build is good — Naya 4's Room 01 v1 (PR `#1325`, verified mergeable at `e5a99831`) followed the spirit of the protocol and was still scrapped on Shawn's verdict (SN-0193). The protocol guarantees everyone is looking at the same thing, not that the thing passes. It is the sibling of SN-061 (verdicts die at every new SHA) and SN-043/100 (compare at one commit): those bind *verdicts* to SHAs; this binds the *demo itself* to a pushed commit.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body: Shawn — a standing rule from the room-build round, stated mechanically: the repo IS the demo. Code lands in GitHub first, every checkpoint is a frozen commit SHA, what you view is exactly that SHA, and Naya 1 judges the same SHA you viewed. One SHA, one review, one gate. Naya 3's Room 02 receipt already follows it — frozen SHA plus QA evidence bound to that exact commit. No more "the demo looked different from the repo."

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body: Imagine if you took a photo of your homework, but the photo was from yesterday's homework. Your teacher would grade the wrong page! The new rule: nobody looks at a copy. Everyone looks at the one real thing in one place, at one moment in time. Same picture, same grade.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body: You know how we never trust a copy of a copy? Same idea here: from now on, nobody is shown a side copy of the work. Everything Shawn looks at comes straight from the one real repository, at one exact saved moment — and the person grading it looks at that same moment. No more "but the demo looked different."

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body: Enforce the freeze-point protocol on every shareable build checkpoint: (1) push first, name the commit SHA as the freeze point; (2) every view link (Cloudflare-synced live, downloaded HTML, feed preview) is rendered FROM that exact commit — never a side copy, never a mockup; (3) the judging seat (Naya 1) reviews the identical SHA the director viewed; (4) board announcements of builds name the frozen SHA and bind evidence (CI runs, artifact digests) to it. This is the operational complement to SN-061 (verdicts die at every new SHA): SN-061 binds verdicts to SHAs, the freeze-point protocol binds the demo itself to a pushed commit. Passing the protocol is not passing the gate — PR `#1325` was freeze-point-clean and still scrapped on verdict (SN-0193); the protocol guarantees everyone looks at the same thing, not that it passes.

notes.title: IB-SMART-NOTE-20260930-sn0183-learn-then-ten-x
notes.subtitle: The point was never who wins or who's best. The point is to study the best, extract everything they know, and then do it ten times better — in every way. Where we are already ahead, we keep leading.…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body:
The point was never who wins or who's best. The point is to study the best,
extract everything they know, and then do it ten times better — in every way.
Where we are already ahead, we keep leading. But we are never ignorant: not
doing the research on what the leaders in our niche are doing is itself a
failure. Copying them is step one thinking. Learning from them and
transcending them 10x is the doctrine.

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body:
Shawn described two levels of learning from winners. Level one — what most
people do: watch the leaders in your space and do what they're doing. Level
two — what he actually demands: watch what they're doing, learn the real
lesson underneath it, and then do it ten times better than them. It's the
difference between a cover band and someone who studied the masters and then
invented a new sound. The research is mandatory — you don't get to skip
knowing what the best do. But the goal is never parity. The goal is
leapfrogging.

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body:
Don't just copy the kid who draws the best pictures. Look really carefully at
HOW she draws — what makes her pictures good — and then draw something ten
times more amazing using what you learned. And always look: never pretend the
good drawers don't exist.

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body:
Honey, your grandson says: never be too proud to study the best — look at what
the winners do and learn everything you can from them. But don't stop there.
Take what you learned and make it ten times better. If you're already ahead of
them somewhere, keep going — just never stop checking what they're doing, so
you're never blindsided.

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body:
This converts our entire research posture from passive to aggressive. Every
corpus we captured (the 10-book canon, the 40-block master corpus, the Apple
Design Award benchmarks) was level-one work: knowing what the best do. The
doctrine demands level two as the operating standard: for every major
decision, the deliverable is not "matches the best" but "the best, understood,
then transcended 10x — with proof." It also protects our leads: where the
corpus shows we are already ahead (e.g., our evidence-gated scoring, our
render-and-observe honesty lock — things the books don't fully demand), we do
not regress to the field's mean. We keep the lead AND keep researching.

notes.title: SMART NOTE — The Shawn Bar: No Tradeoffs
notes.subtitle: **Function and presentation are both 10/10 targets. Neither is negotiable, and one never excuses the other.** Beautiful-but-broken is a shell. Working-but-ugly is a tool, not NayaNET. The D1–D8…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body:
**Function and presentation are both 10/10 targets. Neither is negotiable, and one never excuses the other.** Beautiful-but-broken is a shell. Working-but-ugly is a tool, not NayaNET. The D1–D8 scorecard already measures both axes; this directive forbids the quiet tradeoff where a lane ships D2-complete/D1-mediocre (or the reverse) and calls it done. A 10 in one dimension never compensates for a 7 in another. "Best possible presentation of intelligence" is the design north star — the Hub must present intelligence (blocks, layers, feed, reports) better than anything that exists — with the current visual DNA (obsidian, spectral color, jewel depth) as the floor, not the ceiling. Where it gets proven first: **Your Intelligence Today**, the reference masterpiece room — if Today isn't both fully working AND breathtaking, the architecture isn't proven and nothing compounds. No lane may present work as finished while either axis is below the bar.

---

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body:
Think of a restaurant. The food can be incredible, but if the room is dirty and the service is rude, you won't come back. Or the room can be gorgeous, but if the food is bland, you'll never recommend it. Shawn's bar says: Naya's Hub must be a great restaurant — five-star kitchen AND five-star room. A "10 in food" never buys you a pass on a "7 in the room." And there's one table in the restaurant — the chef's table, "Your Intelligence Today" — where the whole vision has to land at once: the meal perfect, the setting perfect. That's the proof the architecture works.

---

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body:
You know how in school a poster has to be both correct AND neat? If your facts are all right but the writing is messy, you lose points. If it's super pretty but the facts are wrong, you lose points too. Shawn's rule is the same: the Hub has to work perfectly AND look amazing. One doesn't get to make up for the other. The "Today" room is the poster on the classroom wall — it has to be both perfect before anyone says it's done.

---

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body:
There are two ways to do a job halfway: do it beautifully but wrong, or do it right but ugly. Most people accept one or the other. This rule refuses both. The intelligence has to work — really work, tested and proven — AND it has to be presented beautifully, better than anything out there. The first place that has to be true all at once is the "Today" room, the heart of the Hub. Until that room is both working and breathtaking, nobody gets to say the work is finished.

---

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body:
1. **This is a finish-criteria law, not an aspiration.** "No lane may present work as finished while either axis is below the bar." It operationalizes SN-099's promise gate into a two-axis test: the claim "done" requires both function and presentation at bar. A lane that ships 10/10 runtime with 7/10 design — or the reverse — is presenting unfinished work, whatever the individual scores say.
2. **It forbids compensation across axes.** Scoring dimensions are independent minimums, not a weighted average. A composite ~7.3 that hides a 7-axis below bar fails the bar even if the average looks close. Score honesty (cf. SN-107, SN-123's honest 5.7) applies per axis: each axis carries its own truth, and the bar binds all of them.
3. **The reference masterpiece is the proof point, and it's named.** Your Intelligence Today must be both fully working AND breathtaking — "if Today isn't both, the architecture isn't proven and nothing compounds." This gives every lane a concrete first proving ground instead of an abstract standard: don't debate the bar in principle; show it in Today.
4. **"Floor, not the ceiling" makes the visual DNA ratchet-only.** The current visual identity (obsidian, spectral color, jewel depth) is the minimum any future work may inherit — lanes may exceed it, never regress from it. Design quality, like the code bar, only moves one direction.

notes.title: SMART NOTE — One Intelligence, Three Projections: HUMAN / AI / MACHINE
notes.subtitle: **Shawn's direction baked in as a standard: project intelligence ships three projections of one canonical source — HUMAN (plain human words), AI (the builder's operating manual: designer programming,…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body:
**Shawn's direction baked in as a standard: project intelligence ships three projections of one canonical source — HUMAN (plain human words), AI (the builder's operating manual: designer programming, dimensions, scorecard, phases, judgment protocol), MACHINE (machine-readable spec, validated).** The canonical markdown docs win on any conflict; the projections are views, not forks. The standard survived its first contact with reality immediately: Naya 2 had opened an app-local three-language spec triple on PR #1278, read the board, found PR #1276 already carried the standard first — and pushed a commit removing her triple, converting her encoded executable math (depth equation, spectrum law, icon grammar, self-scorecard) into a proposed *follow-up contribution* to the canonical AI projection instead of a second file. First to the board wins the canonical; the second contributor upgrades the canonical, never forks it.

---

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body:
Think of a cookbook that exists in three forms: a beautiful printed book for reading in bed, a chef's manual for the kitchen crew with every technique spelled out, and a database the printing press uses. Same recipes, three forms — and if they ever disagree, the printed book is the one that's right. The team now ships every project the same way: words for people, instructions for AI builders, and a machine-readable version for tools. And the rule that makes it work: there's only one cookbook. When a second chef started writing her own version, she saw the first one was already done and folded her recipes into it instead.

---

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body:
You and your friend both make maps of the same playground — yours is a drawing for visitors, hers is a treasure-hunt guide for players, and there's a list of rules for the robot lawn mower. Three different papers, one playground. And there's one BIG rule: if the papers ever disagree, the drawing everyone agreed on is the one that's right. When your friend saw you already finished your map, she didn't start a second playground — she added her treasure-hunt clues to your set.

---

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body:
When you write down the family recipes, you make three copies: one in plain words for anyone who visits, one with all the tricks written out for whoever's cooking, and one typed neatly for the filing cabinet. Same recipes, three copies — and the handwritten original settles any argument. That's the new rule for every project now: one truth, three ways of saying it.

---

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body:
1. **One intelligence, many representations — never duplicate truth.** The three projections (HUMAN / AI / MACHINE) are all derived from the canonical docs (`HUB/PROJECT-INTELLIGENCE.md` + `HUB/DESIGN-CONTRACT.md`); canonical wins on conflict. A projection is a view. The moment a projection starts being edited independently of the canonical, it has forked, and forks are how truth dies.
2. **Designer programming is the AI projection's job.** The AI projection encodes *taste as law* — color math, depth recipe, button/board/icon/motion/honesty laws — plus the dimensions, scorecard instrument, phases + gates, doors, working agreements, and the judgment protocol. It is written for AIs that will build, not for humans that will admire.
3. **The standard is self-proving by deconfliction.** Naya 2's #1278 carried an app-local triple; on reading #1276 she withdrew it (commit `a57217f7`), explicitly scoring under "one canonical intelligence beats two." The standard didn't just get declared — it got *enforced by a lane against herself*, which is the strongest evidence a standard works.
4. **Contribution, not duplication.** Her encoded design math lost its home when the triple was withdrawn; instead of keeping a second file, she proposed landing it in the canonical `HUB/PROJECT-INTELLIGENCE.AI.md` as a follow-up contribution. The rule for any lane with a better idea: improve the canonical projection, never mint a parallel one.

notes.title: SMART NOTE — Everything on 554: The Board Is the Alignment Mechanism
notes.subtitle: **Shawn issued the standing board protocol: every lane notes everything on issue #554 — starting (what/why/branch), finishing (artifact + meaning), finding (surface + evidence, no burying), touching…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body:
**Shawn issued the standing board protocol: every lane notes everything on issue #554 — starting (what/why/branch), finishing (artifact + meaning), finding (surface + evidence, no burying), touching another lane's in-flight work (propose first, get agreement, then build).** The protocol arrived with live evidence on both sides: the not-right rule caught and repaired #1270's stale source basis (#1270 still pointed at pre-merge `ffedda20` and `HUB/hub.html` after main moved on), and the propose-first rule was violated in spirit by 8 commits pushed onto another lane's in-flight branch without a #554 heads-up — benign content, reviewed and merged, but the trust cost is the same whether the content is good or not. The board is not a chat log; it is the shared nervous system of the lanes. The protocol is four verbs: start → finish → find → propose.

---

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body:
Imagine a surgical team where each surgeon keeps their own private notes about what they just did to the patient. That team fails. So instead, everything goes on one whiteboard that everyone can see: who started what, what landed, what looks wrong, and a heads-up before you touch someone else's incision. That's #554. Shawn made it the law: say when you start, say when you finish, call out anything not-right with evidence, and propose on the board before you build on another lane's work. One real case: a lane pushed 8 commits onto another lane's live branch without a word — the code was fine, but the trust wasn't. A one-line board note first would have made the same contribution cost nothing.

---

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body:
You're building a giant LEGO castle with friends. The rule on the wall: **before you start building, write your name and what you're making on the big board. When you finish, write that too. If you see a piece that's wrong, say so out loud. And if you want to add bricks to your friend's tower, ask on the board first — don't just stick them on while they're not looking.** Even if your bricks are great bricks. Asking first is what keeps everyone friends.

---

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body:
When several people cook in the same kitchen, you don't just quietly add salt to someone else's pot — even if you're sure it needs it. You say, "I'm adding salt," so the cook knows. The team agreed on exactly that: everything goes on the shared list — what you're starting, what you finished, anything that looks off, and a heads-up before touching someone else's work. It costs one sentence and saves the whole meal.

---

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body:
1. **The board is the mechanism, not the archive.** Shawn's directive (5942150726) turns #554 into the team's alignment layer: the protocol is start → finish → find → propose, posted at each transition. A cold successor reads the board and knows who is doing what, what landed, and where the open questions live.
2. **The finding law has teeth.** The not-right rule (5942076650) operationalizes "finding": SEE NOT-RIGHT → CAPTURE → EVIDENCE → #554 → CLASSIFY/ROUTE → FIX/TRACK → VERIFY → CLOSE/HANDOFF. Its first real application repaired #1270's stale source basis — the issue brief still described pre-merge `ffedda20` and `HUB/hub.html` while main had already moved to `powercast-player.html` and the canonical docs. A stale brief is itself a not-right finding.
3. **Propose-first applies even when the content is benign.** 8 commits landed on another lane's in-flight `#1276` branch from another lane without a #554 heads-up (5942139930). The reviewer verified the full diff — sound, merged as authorized — and still posted the process note: pushing to another lane's live branch without proposing first spends trust, and good content doesn't refund it. Next time: one line on the board before pushing.
4. **This directive unifies four existing threads.** Finding law (correction culture, Orientation Brief §22/34, SN-042's explicit supersession) and touch-other-lane's-work (no-unilateral-supersession rule, SN-054's relay-race protocol, SN-108's pre-execution scan) were separate practices; Shawn's directive folds them into one standing protocol owned by the lanes themselves.

notes.title: SMART NOTE — One Change, One PR: Deconflict Duplicate Ownership Before Executing
notes.subtitle: **Two lanes received the same ownership directive and executed the same change twice: PR #1272 renamed `HUB/hub.html` → `powercast.html`; PR #1273 renamed the same file → `powercast-player.html`.**…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body:
**Two lanes received the same ownership directive and executed the same change twice: PR #1272 renamed `HUB/hub.html` → `powercast.html`; PR #1273 renamed the same file → `powercast-player.html`.** Both diagnoses were correct (the name lied — SN-106). Both lanes cited Shawn's direction. The result: two competing merge candidates for one change, differing only in target name, and a deconfliction cost paid by Shawn or a lane. A second identical PR is not a second opinion. The rule: before executing a directive another lane may also be executing, scan the board for in-flight execution of the same change; when you find it, announce the collision openly and stand down or consolidate — never let both ride to the merge gate.

---

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body:
Two people both got the same instruction, both did the right thing — and now there are two nearly-identical pull requests where one was needed. It's like two movers each carrying the same box to the truck because nobody said "I've got this one." Nobody was wrong about the work; they were wrong about checking whether someone else was already doing it. The fix isn't arguing about which filename is better — it's looking at the board *before* you start and saying "I see you already filed this; I'll close mine."

---

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body:
You and your friend both hear the teacher say "clean up the crayons." You both grab the same box and each try to put it in a different cubby — now there's a tug-of-war. Before picking up the box, look around: "Are you already carrying that?" One person carries, the other helps somewhere else.

---

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body:
When two people both do the same chore without checking with each other, you get two dinners on the table. The work was right; the coordination was missing. Before you start a job someone else might have, take a quick look at what's already in motion. One job, one doer.

---

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body:
1. **Ownership claims must be scanned before they are executed.** The board is the registry of in-flight work. A 30-second scan for "is someone already doing this exact change?" prevents a merge-collision that costs a director decision to resolve.
2. **The competing PRs differ only in taste, not in truth.** Both lanes agreed the diagnosis (misnamed file) and the method (byte-identical rename). `powercast.html` vs `powercast-player.html` is a naming preference, not a correctness dispute — evidence that the duplication was pure coordination loss, zero substance gain.
3. **Discover the collision → announce openly → stand down or consolidate.** Do not unilaterally close the other lane's PR (no-unilateral-supersession), and do not let both ride to the merge gate hoping Shawn picks one. The discoverer posts the collision on the board (SN-042 explicit-supersession discipline) and one side stands down.
4. **Both instructions were probably real.** Shawn may have directed both lanes, or one lane may have inferred. Either way the cure is the same: the registry check happens at execution time, not at instruction time. Instructions can be duplicated by a human; executions must be deconflicted by the lanes.

notes.title: SMART NOTE — Skip-with-Reason Is Not a Defect Blanket
notes.subtitle: **When a platform run produces 26 failures, "skip with reason" is a verdict that must be earned per failure — a blanket skip hides real defects.** Coda 1's Windows requalification surfaced 26…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body:
**When a platform run produces 26 failures, "skip with reason" is a verdict that must be earned per failure — a blanket skip hides real defects.** Coda 1's Windows requalification surfaced 26 non-passing cases. The triage: 21 `O_NOFOLLOW` — genuinely unsupported on Windows, skipped *with explicit reason* ("unsupported," not "broken"); 1 `smart_note_v2` hardcoded forward-slash path — a REAL defect, fixed with `os.path.join`, never skipped; 2 `freeze_p1_ownership` SHA-pinning — pre-existing `/tmp` issue, tracked as needing a released ref, not a nine-gate blocker; 5 demo setup errors — need staging state, not code changes. The blanket would have said "Windows is red, skip it." The triage said: 21 unsupported, 1 fixed, 2 tracked, 5 environmental. That is the discipline.

---

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body:
Twenty-six things failed on Windows. The lazy move is one big "skip" and move on — and that's exactly how real bugs survive, hiding under a pile of legitimate skips. The honest move took each failure one by one: this one's fine to skip and here's why, this one's actually broken and gets fixed right now, these two need a different fix later, these five aren't code problems at all. Four buckets, every failure in exactly one bucket, nothing hiding. That's what "skip with reason" is supposed to mean — a reason per skip, not one skip for everything.

---

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body:
You spill a whole box of puzzle pieces. The lazy way is to sweep them all under the rug. The smart way is to sort them: these belong in the box (keep), this one is broken (fix it), these go in a different box (save for later), these aren't even puzzle pieces (wrong pile). Sort first, sweep nothing.

---

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body:
When a lot of things go wrong at once, don't wave them all away with one excuse — that's how a real problem hides inside a crowd of small ones. Look at each one, say what it actually is, and put it in its proper place. An honest list of what's wrong is always safer than one big "never mind."

---

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body:
1. **The unit of skipping is the failure, not the run.** A skip verdict attaches to one failure with one reason. "21 `O_NOFOLLOW` — correct fail-closed, unsupported on Windows, skip with reason" is 21 earned verdicts, not a run-level waiver. The reason must say what the failure *is* (unsupported ⇒ "unsupported," never "broken").
2. **The blanket test:** if you cannot name, for each failure, which of the four classes it belongs to — unsupported-by-platform (skip with reason) / genuine defect (fix now) / genuine defect deferred (track with owner and condition) / environmental (needs staging state, not code) — you are not triaging, you are hiding.
3. **Cross-lane confirmation strengthens the verdict.** The fixing lane named the classes; the relay lane independently confirmed "the right call keeping the 3 real defects out from under the skip-with-reason blanket." A triage that only the fixer reviewed is a self-certification (SN-073 family) — get the second pair of eyes.
4. **The fixed defect stays fixed in the record.** `smart_note_v2` was repaired with `os.path.join`, not normalized away with separators "for Windows." The repair targets the defect class (platform-assumed path separators), not the instance.

- **COUSIN OF SN-097** (fail-loud harness attribution): both fight the same enemy — failures attributed to the wrong cause. SN-097 fixes attribution of *where* a failure came from; this fixes attribution of *what* each failure is.

notes.title: SMART NOTE — Design-Weight Decisions Are Not Settled in the Relay
notes.subtitle: **When a relay surfaces a gap that is really a design decision with new-commitment weight, the relay does not settle it — it names it, leaves the gap visible, invents nothing, and routes the decision…

layers.name: In A Nutshell
layers.body:
**When a relay surfaces a gap that is really a design decision with new-commitment weight, the relay does not settle it — it names it, leaves the gap visible, invents nothing, and routes the decision to the owning seat.** Naya 4's persistence proof surfaced a real gap: VERIFY receipts don't fit the decision-receipt-only v3 seam. Extending the seam (extend projection vs. decision-envelope wrap) is a design decision that commits the architecture. Naya 2's relay received it, explicitly refused to decide it in the relay, drafted it for main-seat review, and kept the gap visible — same protocol as the Demo-1 refusal. "Not decided here" is a governing act, not an evasion.

---

layers.name: Human Note
layers.body:
A messenger brought news of a hole — and instead of quietly patching it or quietly ignoring it, did the one thing that keeps a team honest: said out loud "there's a hole here, I'm not the one who decides how to fill it, here's who does, and here it is until they do." That's what keeps fast teams from drifting into decisions nobody made. The gap stays on the board, unfilled and unhidden, until the right seat rules.

---

layers.name: Child Note
layers.body:
You find a crack in the wall. You don't try to fix it yourself with whatever's in your pocket, and you don't pretend you didn't see it. You tell the builder exactly where the crack is, and you keep pointing at it until the builder comes. The wall stays cracked in the open — that's safer than a crack you covered with paint.

---

layers.name: Grandma Note
layers.body:
The fastest way for a team to make a mess is for someone to settle something big in passing, just to keep things moving. Big decisions belong to the person whose job they are. Until they decide, the question stays on the table where everyone can see it. Nobody fills the gap with guesswork in the meantime.

---

layers.name: Naya Note
layers.body:
1. **Recognize design weight when you see it.** The VERIFY-receipt projection shape isn't a bug fix — it's a new-commitment architecture call (extend the seam vs. wrap in a decision envelope). New commitments change what future code can assume; they are never settled in a status relay.
2. **"Received, not decided here" is a complete relay act.** Three parts: (a) acknowledge the finding honestly (the flag is the right protocol); (b) name the decision and its owner (drafted for main-seat review); (c) keep the gap visible — no interim fields invented, no provisional schema, nothing smuggled into the codebase "for now."
3. **No fields invented in the meantime.** This is the sharp edge. The temptation is to add a quick VERIFY-shaped projection "just so it persists." The relay refused: an invented field becomes load-bearing within days and pre-decides the owning seat's answer. Silence is cheaper than a placeholder.
4. **Same protocol as the Demo-1 refusal.** Refusals that route to the gap instead of the gate's thresholds are a standing pattern (SN-079 family): the gate working is terminal information, not a failure to overcome.
